exercises.description: The 'Deep Squat to Wide Fold with Foot Hold' is a dynamic flexibility exercise that combines a deep squat with a forward fold, enhancing lower body mobility and flexibility. This exercise targets the hips, hamstrings, and lower back, promoting improved range of motion and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.
Lower into a deep squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, keeping your chest up and spine neutral.
Once in the squat position, extend your arms forward for balance.
From the squat, lean forward and place your hands on the ground in front of you.
Shift your weight onto your hands and straighten your legs into a wide forward fold.
Reach for your feet or ankles, holding onto them to deepen the stretch.
Hold the position for a few seconds, then release and return to the deep squat position.
Repeat the sequence for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Knees collapsing inward during the squat phase.
Rounding the back excessively in the wide fold position.
Failing to maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Not engaging the core muscles to stabilize the torso.
Allowing the heels to lift off the ground in the squat.
Gripping the feet too tightly, causing tension in the arms.
Not bending the knees enough to achieve a deep squat.
Shifting weight too far forward onto the toes.
Inadequate hip hinge during the transition to wide fold.
Losing balance due to uneven weight distribution.
Overextending the knees in the wide fold position.
Neglecting to activate the glutes during the squat.
exercises.name: Deep Squat to Wide Fold with Foot Hold
tips: Keep your heels flat on the ground during the deep squat to maintain balance.
Engage your core throughout the movement to support your lower back.
Inhale as you lower into the squat and exhale as you transition into the forward fold.
If you can't reach your feet in the forward fold, hold onto your shins or ankles instead.
Focus on maintaining a straight back during both the squat and fold to prevent strain.
Perform this exercise slowly and with control to maximize flexibility benefits.

exercises.description: The Deficit Deadlift is a variation of the conventional deadlift performed while standing on an elevated surface, typically 1-3 inches high. This exercise increases the range of motion, targeting the posterior chain muscles, including the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back, more intensely. It is particularly beneficial for improving strength off the floor in standard deadlifts.
instructions: Place a platform or weight plate on the floor to create a deficit of 1-3 inches.
Stand on the platform with your feet hip-width apart and toes pointing forward.
Position the barbell over the middle of your feet and grip it with your hands just outside your knees.
Engage your core, retract your shoulder blades, and keep your back straight.
Take a deep breath, then push through your heels to lift the barbell off the ground.
Extend your hips and knees simultaneously until you are standing upright with the barbell in front of your thighs.
Lower the barbell back to the ground in a controlled manner by hinging at the hips and bending your knees.
mistakes: Starting with hips too low, turning the movement into more of a squat than a deadlift.
Rounding the lower back, increasing the risk of spinal injury.
Letting the bar drift too far from the body, reducing leverage and control.
Failing to engage the lats, leading to poor bar path and instability.
Using excessive range of motion, causing unnecessary strain on the lower back.
Pulling with the arms instead of driving through the legs, reducing power and efficiency.
Not maintaining a neutral spine throughout the lift, compromising form and safety.
Losing tension at the bottom of the lift, hindering force production and control.
exercises.name: Deficit Deadlift
tips: Ensure that your back remains straight throughout the lift to avoid injury.
Focus on engaging your core muscles to maintain stability during the movement.
Start with a lower weight to master the form before increasing the load.
Keep the bar close to your body as you lift to maintain proper leverage.
Use a mixed grip if necessary to improve grip strength and control.
Avoid rounding your shoulders; keep them retracted and tight throughout the lift.

exercises.description: A plyometric exercise in which you step off a low box, land on both feet and rebound straight into a maximal vertical jump, spending as little time on the ground as possible. The drop pre-stretches the leg muscles, so the jump builds reactive strength and explosive power in the quads, glutes and calves.
instructions: Stand tall on a stable plyo box, close to its front edge, feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
Step forward off the box with one foot and let your body drop straight down. Do not jump up or out.
Land on the balls of both feet at the same time, just in front of the box, with your knees and hips bent and your arms swung back.
Keep your knees in line with your toes and your chest up as you touch down.
Rebound at once: spend as little time on the floor as possible, drive through your feet and swing your arms forward and up.
Jump straight up as high as you can, fully extending your hips, knees and ankles.
Land softly with your knees and hips bent, stand up, then step back onto the box for the next rep.
mistakes: Jumping up or forward off the box instead of stepping off, which raises the drop height and lands you too far from the box
Landing stiff-legged, with almost no bend in the knees and hips, which sends the impact into the knees and lower back
Landing heel-first instead of on the balls of the feet
Letting the knees cave inward on landing or takeoff
Sinking into a deep squat or pausing after landing, which turns the rebound into a slow squat jump
Rounding the back or folding far forward on landing
Cutting the jump short without fully extending the hips, knees and ankles
exercises.name: Depth Jump
tips: Start with a box about 30 cm high. Raise it only while you still land quietly and jump at least as high as from the lower box.
Land in the same stance you jump from, feet hip-width apart, so you can rebound without shifting your feet.
Jump on a firm, non-slip floor in stable shoes. A soft mat slows down the rebound.
Do depth jumps early in the workout, while you are fresh, not after heavy leg work.
Keep sets short and rest fully between them, so every jump is fast and maximal.
End the set as soon as your jump height drops or your landings get loud or unsteady.

exercises.description: Diamond Push Ups are a bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps, chest, and shoulders. This variation of the standard push-up involves placing the hands close together under the chest, forming a diamond shape with the thumbs and index fingers. This position increases the activation of the triceps compared to regular push-ups.
instructions: Start in a plank position with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Place your hands directly under your chest, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers touching.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you lower your chest towards your hands by bending your elbows.
Lower yourself until your chest nearly touches the back of your hands.
Push through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Maintain a tight core and avoid sagging or arching your back throughout the movement.
mistakes: Hands placed too far apart, reducing tricep engagement.
Elbows flaring out excessively, increasing shoulder strain.
Hips sagging or rising, compromising core stability.
Inadequate range of motion, limiting muscle activation.
Rushing through reps, decreasing control and effectiveness.
Neck craning forward, leading to poor spinal alignment.
Shoulders shrugging up, reducing scapular stability.
Failing to keep the body in a straight line, affecting posture.
Hands positioned too close to the chest, causing wrist discomfort.
exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
tips: Ensure that your hands are positioned correctly to maximize triceps engagement.
Keep your core engaged to maintain proper body alignment.
If you're new to this exercise, start on your knees to build strength before progressing to full push-ups.
Focus on a slow and controlled movement to increase muscle activation.
Breathe in as you lower yourself and exhale as you push back up.
Avoid flaring your elbows out to the sides; keep them close to your body.

exercises.description: Dip Shrugs are an upper body exercise targeting the trapezius muscles and shoulders. This movement involves a shrugging motion while supporting your body weight on parallel bars, enhancing shoulder stability and strength.
instructions: Begin by positioning yourself on parallel bars, supporting your body weight with your arms fully extended.
Keep your elbows locked and your body straight, engaging your core for stability.
Inhale deeply, then exhale as you elevate your shoulders towards your ears in a shrugging motion.
Hold the top position briefly, ensuring maximum contraction of the trapezius muscles.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing the shoulders to roll forward instead of keeping them retracted.
Failing to maintain a stable core, leading to excessive body sway.
Not fully depressing the shoulders at the top of the movement.
Using momentum to lift the body rather than controlled muscle engagement.
Locking the elbows, which reduces the focus on shoulder movement.
Shrugging the shoulders unevenly, causing imbalanced muscle activation.
Neglecting to keep the neck neutral, leading to unnecessary strain.
Performing the exercise too quickly, compromising form and effectiveness.
exercises.name: Dip Shrugs
tips: Focus on keeping your elbows straight to isolate the trapezius muscles effectively.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and straight body position throughout the exercise.
Perform the movement slowly to maximize muscle engagement and control.
Avoid using momentum; ensure each shrug is deliberate and controlled.
Breathe consistently, exhaling as you shrug and inhaling as you return to the starting position.

exercises.description: Lower your body between parallel bars until your upper arms are level with the floor, then press back up to build your triceps and lower chest. All three heads of the triceps work hardest, mostly as you lock out. The lower and middle chest pick up a big share at the bottom, and the front delts help along the way. You lean forward a little on the way down, less than in Chest Dips, so arms and chest split the work. Pick it when you want a heavy press with no machine; once body weight gets easy, add weight on a belt.
instructions: Step between the parallel bars or the dip handles of a power tower. On V-shaped bars, stand where your wrists will stay under your elbows.
Grip with your palms facing each other and thumbs wrapped around, the bar in the heel of your hand so the wrists stay straight.
Jump or step up to straight arms. Push the bars down so your shoulders sit low and away from your ears, chest up.
Bend your knees and keep your feet together behind you, off the floor. A light squeeze of the glutes stops the legs from swinging.
Bend your elbows and take about 2 seconds to lower. The elbows go straight back as your torso tips forward 20–30°.
Stop when your shoulders are level with your elbows: about 90° at the elbow, forearms close to vertical. Hold for a beat without bouncing.
Push the bars down and away until your elbows are straight and you're upright again, shoulders still low.
At the top of the final rep, step down onto the frame or a box from the top instead of dropping out of the bottom.
mistakes: Shoulders creeping up to your ears and rolling forward at the bottom. Keep pressing the bars down with your chest up, and end the descent where you can still hold that position.
Sinking far below parallel to stretch the chest. Stop when your shoulders reach elbow height; going deeper mostly loads the front of the shoulder.
Half reps that turn around well above 90° or never lock out. Use the same depth every rep and straighten the elbows fully. If the reps start shrinking, finish the set on the assisted machine.
Elbows flaring out to the sides. Point them back and keep them close to your body as you lower.
Kicking the legs or bouncing out of the bottom. Keep the knees bent and feet together, lower over about 2 seconds and pause before you press.
exercises.name: Dips
tips: Three sets of 6–12 reps is a good plan.

Build the reps before you add weight. When all three sets reach 12 clean reps at full depth, hang 2.5 kg from a dip belt and build back up from 6. Once there's weight on the belt, get on and off the bars from a box.
Fewer than 5 clean reps? Use the assisted machine or a band looped across the bars under your knees, or do 3–5 slow negatives a set: start at the top and take 3–5 seconds to lower.

The backs of your upper arms work hardest as you straighten them, and your lower chest at the bottom. A sharp or pinching pain at the front or top of the shoulder means end the set and stop higher next time.
Want the chest to do more? Switch to Chest Dips, with a deeper lean and the elbows slightly wider.

Substitutes: Assisted Machine Dips, Seated Dip Machine, Close Grip Bench Press, Diamond Push-Up. The machines and the push-up are easier starting points; the close-grip press loads your triceps with a barbell when the dip bars are taken.

exercises.description: The Donkey Kick is a lower body exercise targeting the gluteus maximus, designed to enhance strength, stability, and muscle tone. It primarily engages the glutes while also activating the core and hamstrings. This exercise is performed on all fours, making it accessible for various fitness levels.
instructions: Begin on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Engage your core to maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Lift one leg, keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, and drive the sole of your foot towards the ceiling.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement and hold for a brief moment.
Lower your leg back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.
mistakes: Arching the lower back excessively, reducing glute engagement.
Allowing the pelvis to tilt or rotate, compromising stability.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement, decreasing muscle activation.
Extending the leg too high, leading to improper form and potential lower back strain.
Failing to keep the core engaged, resulting in loss of balance.
Bending the supporting knee excessively, shifting focus away from the target muscles.
Pointing the toes instead of keeping the foot flexed, reducing hamstring involvement.
Dropping the head or looking up, causing neck strain.
exercises.name: Donkey Kick
tips: Keep your core engaged to prevent lower back arching.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of each repetition for maximum activation.
Maintain a steady pace and avoid using momentum to lift your leg.
Ensure your neck remains in line with your spine by looking down at the floor.
For added resistance, consider using ankle weights or a resistance band around your thighs.

exercises.description: The Doorway Chest Stretch is a static stretch exercise designed to improve flexibility and mobility in the chest, shoulders, and upper back. It is performed using a doorway as support, allowing for a deep stretch of the pectoral muscles and anterior deltoids.
instructions: Stand in a doorway with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise your arms to the sides and bend your elbows at a 90-degree angle, forming a 'goalpost' position.
Place your forearms against the door frame, ensuring your elbows are slightly below shoulder height.
Step one foot forward through the doorway, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Gently lean forward until you feel a stretch across your chest and shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply throughout.
Slowly return to the starting position and switch feet if desired.
mistakes: Placing hands too high or too low on the doorway, leading to ineffective stretch.
Leaning too far forward, causing strain on the shoulder joint.
Arching the lower back excessively, reducing chest engagement.
Failing to keep shoulders down and back, leading to shoulder impingement.
Holding the stretch for too short a duration, minimizing benefits.
Allowing the head to jut forward, causing neck strain.
Not engaging core muscles, leading to instability.
Rotating the torso instead of keeping it aligned, reducing stretch effectiveness.
exercises.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them during the stretch.
Ensure your elbows remain slightly below shoulder height to prevent shoulder impingement.
Maintain a neutral spine by engaging your core muscles throughout the stretch.
Avoid leaning too far forward; the stretch should be gentle and not cause pain.
Focus on deep, controlled breathing to enhance relaxation and effectiveness of the stretch.
Perform this stretch after workouts or during breaks to alleviate tension in the chest and shoulders.

exercises.description: The Double Dumbbell Bent Over Row is a compound exercise targeting the upper back, shoulders, and arms. It involves bending at the hips while maintaining a neutral spine to lift two dumbbells towards the torso. This exercise enhances muscle strength and endurance in the back and improves posture.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Let the dumbbells hang at arm's length below your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Pull the dumbbells towards your torso by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rounding the back instead of maintaining a neutral spine.
Using momentum by swinging the body instead of controlled lifting.
Allowing the elbows to flare out excessively, reducing lat engagement.
Pulling the weights too high, leading to shoulder impingement risk.
Standing too upright, reducing the effectiveness of the exercise.
Not retracting the shoulder blades fully at the top of the movement.
Failing to engage the core, leading to potential lower back strain.
Letting the wrists curl, which shifts tension away from the back muscles.
Not lowering the dumbbells fully, limiting the range of motion.
Using weights that are too heavy, compromising form and control.
exercises.name: Double Dumbbell Bent Over Row
tips: Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders to prevent strain.
Engage your core throughout the exercise to maintain stability.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of each rep for maximum contraction.
Control the movement; avoid using momentum to lift the weights.
Start with lighter weights to ensure proper form before progressing to heavier dumbbells.

exercises.description: The Double Dumbbell Preacher Curl is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps brachii. It is performed using a preacher bench and two dumbbells, allowing for controlled movement and effective muscle engagement. This exercise emphasizes the peak contraction of the biceps and helps in developing the lower part of the muscle.
instructions: Sit on a preacher bench with your chest pressed against the pad and your arms extended over it.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Start with your arms fully extended but not locked out.
Curl the dumbbells upward by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary against the pad.
Continue lifting until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement for maximum contraction.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing elbows to lift off the pad, reducing bicep engagement.
Using momentum by swinging the dumbbells, leading to poor muscle isolation.
Incorrect wrist positioning, causing strain and reducing curl efficiency.
Not fully extending arms at the bottom, limiting range of motion.
Curling too quickly, sacrificing control and muscle tension.
Leaning forward, shifting focus away from the biceps.
Gripping the dumbbells too tightly, causing forearm fatigue.
Failing to keep shoulders stable, leading to shoulder involvement.
exercises.name: Double Dumbbell Preacher Curl
tips: Ensure your elbows remain fixed on the pad to isolate the biceps effectively.
Focus on a slow and controlled movement to maximize muscle tension.
Avoid swinging or using momentum to lift the weights.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows at the bottom to maintain tension on the biceps.
Exhale as you lift the weights and inhale as you lower them.
Adjust the seat height so that your armpits are comfortably resting at the top of the pad.

exercises.description: The front squat with two kettlebells loads the thighs and glutes while the trunk stabilises the weights at shoulder height. Bend your hips and knees to squat between your feet, then push through the whole foot to stand, keeping the front rack steady and using a depth you can control.
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, with your toes turned out slightly if needed.
Hold a kettlebell at each shoulder in the front rack, with the bells resting against your forearms.
Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and maintain a neutral spine. Keep your weight balanced across your whole feet.
Begin the squat by bending your knees and hips at the same time. Let your knees track in the same direction as your toes.
Lower under control until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as low as you can go without your lower back rounding or your heels lifting.
Drive through your midfoot and heels to stand up. Extend your knees and hips together while keeping the kettlebells stable in the rack position.
Exhale as you stand, then reset your brace before the next repetition.
mistakes: Letting the kettlebells drift away from the chest instead of keeping them tight in the front rack.
Allowing the elbows to drop, which rounds the upper back and collapses the rack position.
Letting the knees cave inward during the descent or ascent.
Rising onto the toes or letting the heels lift off the floor.
Dropping into the bottom position without control.
Driving up with the hips first and letting the chest fall forward.
exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
tips: Exhale through the hardest part of the upward movement.
Choose a load that allows the same range on every repetition.
Use two weights of equal mass to balance the load on both sides.
Pick a point in front of you to help maintain your balance.
Take a breath and reset your position between repetitions.

exercises.description: The double kettlebell Romanian deadlift trains the hamstrings and glutes through a hip hinge with both feet planted. Hold one bell in each hand, send your hips back as the weights lower close to your legs, then extend your hips to stand without turning the movement into a squat.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and a kettlebell in each hand.
Hold the kettlebells near the sides of your legs with straight arms and brace your abdomen.
Keep your knees slightly bent and send your hips backward.
Lower both kettlebells close to your legs as your torso inclines forward.
Stop at a depth that preserves a neutral back, then press through your feet.
Extend your hips to stand tall and finish without leaning back.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back instead of hinging at the hips.
Squatting down by bending the knees too much instead of pushing the hips back.
Letting the kettlebells drift away from the legs and increasing the lever on the lower back.
Continuing to lower the weights after the hips stop moving, which rounds the back.
Locking the knees or hyperextending them during the movement.
Snapping the hips forward aggressively and leaning back at the top.
exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
tips: Exhale through the hardest part of the upward movement.
Choose a load that allows the same range on every repetition.
Use two weights of equal mass to balance the load on both sides.
Take a breath and reset your position between repetitions.
Wrap each thumb around the handle to secure a full-hand grip.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/双壶铃推举深蹲

exercises.description: Hold two kettlebells in the front rack position and stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart. Squat with your heels grounded, then drive upward and use the leg momentum to press both bells overhead. Finish with straight arms, then lower the bells to the rack under control before the next squat.
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart. Clean two kettlebells into the front rack position, with the bells resting against your forearms and upper arms, elbows slightly in front of your body.
Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and grip the handles firmly. Keep your wrists neutral and your heels flat on the floor.

Sit down into a squat by bending your knees and hips at the same time. Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, if your mobility allows.
Drive through your whole feet to stand up powerfully. Use the force from your legs and hips to start moving the kettlebells upward.
As you reach full hip and knee extension, press both kettlebells overhead until your arms are straight. Keep your ribs down and avoid leaning back.
Finish with the kettlebells directly above your shoulders, elbows locked out, and your head in a neutral position.
Lower the kettlebells under control back to the front rack position, then begin the next repetition.
mistakes: Letting the knees cave inward during the squat.
Allowing the heels to lift or shifting weight onto the toes.
Dropping the chest and rounding the lower back at the bottom of the squat.
Holding the kettlebells too far forward instead of keeping them close in the rack position.
Overarching the lower back to get the kettlebells overhead instead of keeping the ribs down and core braced.
Letting the kettlebells drift apart or forward during the press.
Lowering the kettlebells too quickly into the rack position without control.
exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Thruster
tips: Let the handles lie diagonally across your palms in the rack.
Choose a natural toe angle that makes the squat comfortable.
Inhale in the squat and exhale as you rise and press.
Use two kettlebells of equal weight.
Keep your eyes on a fixed point ahead during the press.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/跳绳双摇

exercises.description: Jump with both feet while turning a skipping rope twice under your feet during each jump. Keep your body upright and use quick wrist rotations to accelerate the rope, then land with slightly bent knees and link the repetitions with a consistent jump height and rhythm.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet together, a rope handle in each hand and the rope behind your heels.
Set the rope length so that, when you stand on its middle, the handles reach about your armpits.
Keep your elbows close to your ribs, hands slightly in front of your hips, and turn the rope mainly with quick wrist circles.
For a double under, jump slightly higher than for a single jump and keep your body straight, with your chest up and eyes forward.
Spin the rope twice during one jump by making faster, tighter wrist rotations.
Land softly on the balls of both feet with a small bend in your knees, then immediately prepare for the next repetition.
Keep a steady rhythm and stay relaxed through your shoulders, forearms, and grip.
mistakes: Using a donkey kick, with the feet kicking backward during each jump.
Bending the knees deeply on every rep instead of rebounding from the ankles.
Turning the rope with the shoulders or whole arms instead of the wrists.
Letting the elbows flare out or drift behind the body.
Landing heavily on the heels instead of softly on the balls of the feet.
Breaking at the hips or leaning forward instead of staying tall and braced.
exercises.name: Double Under
tips: Set the rope length so the handles reach around your armpits when you stand on the middle of the rope with one foot.
Keep your hands even and just outside your hips.
Practice single unders with a relaxed rhythm first, then use drills such as one double under followed by several single unders.
Stay relaxed through your shoulders, neck, and grip.
Use a smooth, level surface and shoes with enough forefoot cushioning and support for repeated jumping.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/下犬式

exercises.description: The Downward Dog is a fundamental yoga pose that strengthens the upper body, stretches the hamstrings, calves, and spine, and improves overall flexibility. It is often used as a transitional pose in yoga sequences and can help improve posture and balance.
instructions: Start on your hands and knees with your wrists aligned under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Spread your fingers wide and press firmly into the ground with your palms.
Tuck your toes under and lift your knees off the floor, raising your hips towards the ceiling.
Straighten your legs as much as possible without locking your knees, forming an inverted V shape with your body.
Keep your head between your arms, ears aligned with upper arms, and gaze towards your feet or navel.
Hold the position for several breaths, maintaining a steady and deep breathing pattern.
To release, lower your knees back to the floor and return to the starting position.
mistakes: Hands placed too far apart, reducing stability and shoulder engagement.
Feet positioned too close together, limiting base of support.
Heels lifted excessively, reducing hamstring and calf stretch.
Arched lower back, increasing strain on the lumbar spine.
Shoulders shrugged towards ears, causing tension and reducing neck space.
Weight unevenly distributed between hands and feet, leading to imbalance.
Elbows bent, reducing arm engagement and shoulder stability.
Neck craned excessively, causing unnecessary strain.
Hips not lifted high enough, compromising the inverted V shape.
Fingers not spread wide, reducing grip and stability.
exercises.name: Downward Dog
tips: Engage your core muscles to support the lower back and maintain stability.
If you have tight hamstrings, keep a slight bend in the knees to avoid straining.
Focus on lifting through the hips rather than pushing through the shoulders to avoid tension in the neck.
Distribute weight evenly between hands and feet to maintain balance.
Ensure that your fingers are spread wide for better grip and stability.
Use this pose as an opportunity to lengthen the spine by reaching through the tailbone.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/龙旗式

exercises.description: The Dragon Flag is an advanced core exercise that primarily targets the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors. It requires significant strength and control, as it involves maintaining a straight body position while lowering and raising the legs from a supine position. This exercise also engages the lats, shoulders, and glutes for stabilization.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench or the floor with your head near the edge. Grip the sides of the bench or anchor your hands behind your head for support.
Engage your core and lift your legs and hips off the bench, keeping your body straight from shoulders to toes.
Maintain a rigid body position as you slowly lower your legs towards the bench without letting your back arch.
Pause just above the bench, then raise your legs back to the starting position using controlled movements.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining form.
mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch off the bench, reducing core engagement.
Leading with the legs instead of lifting the hips and torso as a unit.
Dropping the hips too quickly, losing control and stability.
Failing to maintain a straight line from shoulders to feet, causing sagging.
Using momentum instead of controlled muscle contraction to lift and lower.
Not engaging the lats and shoulders to stabilize the upper body.
Starting with too much range of motion, leading to poor form.
Holding the breath, which can increase tension and reduce endurance.
Positioning the hands too close together, limiting stability and support.
exercises.name: Dragon Flag
tips: Focus on keeping your body as straight as possible to maximize core engagement.
Control is key; perform each repetition slowly to avoid using momentum.
Keep your shoulders pressed into the bench to stabilize your upper body.
If you're new to this exercise, start with partial range of motion and gradually increase as you build strength.
Engage your glutes and lats to help maintain a stable position throughout the movement.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/哑铃交替前平举

exercises.description: The Dumbbell Alternate Front Raise is an isolation exercise targeting the anterior deltoids. It involves lifting dumbbells in front of the body alternately, which helps in developing shoulder strength and definition. This exercise also engages the upper chest and traps to a lesser extent.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Keep your arms straight but not locked, and position the dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Raise one dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your palm facing down.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement with the opposite arm.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Swinging the dumbbells using momentum instead of controlled lifting.
Raising the dumbbells above shoulder height, causing unnecessary strain.
Leaning back to compensate for weight, risking lower back strain.
Using excessively heavy weights, leading to poor form and control.
Locking the elbows instead of keeping a slight bend.
Not engaging the core, resulting in instability and poor posture.
Allowing shoulders to shrug, reducing focus on the front deltoids.
Failing to keep wrists straight, leading to potential wrist strain.
Neglecting to lower the dumbbells slowly, missing eccentric muscle engagement.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Alternate Front Raise
tips: Maintain a controlled motion to avoid using momentum.
Keep your back straight and avoid leaning backward as you lift the weights.
Focus on lifting with your shoulders, not your arms or back.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
Start with lighter weights to ensure proper form before progressing to heavier dumbbells.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/哑铃交替锤式前平举

exercises.description: The Dumbbell Standing Alternate Hammer Front Raise is an isolation exercise targeting the anterior deltoids, with secondary engagement of the lateral deltoids, upper pectorals, and trapezius. This exercise involves lifting dumbbells in a hammer grip position alternately in front of the body, enhancing shoulder strength and stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your arms fully extended at your sides with a slight bend in the elbows.
Engage your core and maintain a straight back throughout the movement.
Raise one dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height while keeping your palm facing inward.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Simultaneously, raise the opposite dumbbell to shoulder height as you lower the first one.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Swinging the body or using momentum to lift the weights instead of controlled muscle engagement.
Lifting the dumbbells too high, past shoulder level, which can strain the shoulder joints.
Allowing the elbows to bend, reducing the effectiveness of the exercise on the target muscles.
Leaning back excessively, which shifts tension away from the shoulders and onto the lower back.
Failing to keep the wrists neutral, leading to unnecessary strain on the wrist joints.
Not engaging the core, resulting in poor posture and reduced stability during the movement.
Raising both arms simultaneously instead of alternating, which can lead to fatigue and form breakdown.
Using weights that are too heavy, compromising form and increasing the risk of injury.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Alternate Hammer Front Raise
tips: Focus on controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Avoid swinging or using momentum to lift the weights; maintain strict form.
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed to prevent tension in the neck.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
Start with lighter weights to master form before progressing to heavier loads.
Ensure your wrists remain neutral and aligned with your forearms throughout the exercise.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱二头肌/哑铃交替反握弯举

exercises.description: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and arms at your sides, palms facing inward. Curl one dumbbell upward while rotating the palm to face up, keeping the elbow close to your torso and the upper arm still. Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower the weight slowly while rotating the hand back to a neutral grip. Repeat with the opposite arm, alternating sides without swinging or leaning back.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your arms fully extended and your palms facing your thighs.
Brace your core, keep your chest lifted, and pull your shoulders gently down and back without arching your lower back.
Keeping your upper arm close to your torso, curl one dumbbell upward while rotating your palm from neutral to facing upward as the weight rises.
Continue lifting until the dumbbell is near shoulder height, squeezing your biceps at the top without allowing your elbow to drift forward excessively.
Lower the dumbbell slowly and under control, rotating your palm back toward your thigh as your arm returns to full extension.
Repeat the same movement with the opposite arm, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
Exhale as you curl and inhale as you lower, keeping your torso still and avoiding swinging, leaning back, or using momentum.
mistakes: Swinging the torso or using hip drive to lift the dumbbell
Letting the elbow drift far forward or away from the side
Curling the weight with the shoulder instead of isolating elbow flexion
Failing to fully supinate the forearm as the dumbbell rises
Bending or extending the wrist instead of keeping it neutral and aligned with the forearm
Using only a partial range of motion and not lowering the dumbbell under control
Dropping the dumbbell quickly during the lowering phase
Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear during the curl
Using a load that prevents controlled, alternating repetitions
exercises.name: Dumbbell Alternate Supinated Curl
tips: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip and your elbows close to your torso.
Curl one dumbbell at a time while rotating your palm upward as the weight rises, finishing with the palm facing your shoulder.
Keep your upper arm mostly still; only your forearm should move at the elbow during the curl.
Squeeze your biceps briefly at the top without lifting your shoulder or allowing the elbow to drift far forward.
Lower the dumbbell slowly and under control, rotating back toward a neutral grip as it returns to your side.
Avoid swinging your torso, leaning back, or using momentum; reduce the weight if you cannot keep your body stable.
Keep your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm rather than bending it backward or curling it toward your body.
Exhale as you curl and inhale as you lower, maintaining a controlled tempo on both sides.
Use a full comfortable range of motion, but do not force the elbow to lock out aggressively at the bottom.
Choose a weight that allows smooth, even repetitions on both arms without twisting your hips or shoulders.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/仰卧哑铃环绕

exercises.description: Lying on a flat bench, you move two dumbbells in one large circle with almost straight arms: up over your chest, behind your head, then out wide to the sides and back to your hips. It works the chest, lats and serratus through a long range of motion and is done with light weights.
instructions: Lie face up on a flat bench with your head on the bench and your feet flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and extend your arms so the dumbbells sit just above your hips.
Brace your core and keep a slight bend in your elbows for the whole set.
Raise the dumbbells together over your chest, keeping your arms almost straight.
Continue the arc and lower the dumbbells behind your head until your arms are roughly in line with your body.
Spread your arms and sweep the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc at about bench height, then down to your hips.
Repeat the circle in the same direction for every rep.
mistakes: Swinging the dumbbells with momentum instead of moving them under control
Bending the elbows a lot, which shortens the lever and turns the circle into a press
Arching the lower back or lifting the hips off the bench when the dumbbells are behind the head
Forcing the dumbbells further behind the head than your shoulders allow, which causes pain or pinching in the shoulder
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Letting the wrists bend back under the weight of the dumbbells
Moving the arms unevenly, so one dumbbell leads the other
exercises.name: Dumbbell Around the World
tips: Use light dumbbells. With straight arms the lever is long, so even a small weight loads the shoulders heavily.
Feel the stretch across your chest and lats when the dumbbells are behind your head and out to the sides.
Keep the sideways part of the arc wide, with the dumbbells far from your body, all the way down to your hips.
Keep your head on the bench and look at the ceiling instead of following the dumbbells with your eyes.
Breathe in as the dumbbells travel up and behind your head, and breathe out as you sweep them out to the sides and down.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/哑铃卧推

exercises.description: Lying on a flat bench, you press a dumbbell in each hand from the sides of your chest to straight arms to build chest and triceps strength and size. Your chest is the main mover, mainly the middle and lower fibers, while the triceps straighten your elbows and the front delts help off the bottom. Compared with a barbell, the dumbbells travel deeper and meet at the top, and each arm carries its own load, so a weaker side can't hide. It's also easy to bail out of when you train alone: if a rep stalls, set the dumbbells down on the floor beside you.
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with the dumbbells standing on end on your thighs, close to your knees.
Lie back and push each knee up into its dumbbell as you go, so the weights arrive at your chest instead of being swung up.
Plant your feet flat, hip-width or a little wider, knees bent about 90°. Head, upper back and glutes stay on the pad.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and leave them there. A small arch in your lower back is fine.
With the handles in one line and knuckles to the ceiling, press up and slightly in to straight arms, dumbbells almost touching.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower them out and down beside your mid to lower chest, forearms vertical and elbows about 45–60° from your sides.
Stop when your elbows dip just below the bench, or sooner if your shoulders complain, then press the next rep without a bounce.
To get up, bring the dumbbells to your chest, curl your knees up and rock to sitting with the weights back on your thighs.
mistakes: Dumbbells drifting toward your face or neck with the forearms tilted. Keep each one stacked over its elbow and lower it to the line of your lower chest, not your collarbones.
Elbows flared straight out in a T at the bottom. Tuck them to about 45–60° so the dumbbells finish beside your lower chest.
Clanking the dumbbells together at the top. The rep is done when your elbows are straight, so stop a few centimeters apart.
Shoulders rolling up off the bench at lockout. Reach only as far as straight elbows and keep the shoulder blades pinned.
Swinging the weights up from the floor or dropping them from straight arms. Get in with the knee kick-up and get out the same way.
One arm lagging, or the reps getting shallower as the set gets hard. Let the weaker arm set the pace and end the set when either arm misses a clean rep.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
tips: Press 2–4 sets of 6–12 reps. Heavy sets of 5–8 work too, but getting big dumbbells into position soon becomes the limit, not your chest.
Stay with one pair until you get 12 on every set, then move to the next pair, usually 1–2.5 kg more per hand. On light dumbbells that is a big jump, so start again near the bottom of the range.
Expect a stretch across your chest at the bottom. A sharp pinch at the front of the shoulder means go less deep or switch to a neutral grip.
Too wobbly? Start with the Floor Dumbbell Press: the floor stops your elbows at a safe depth. For a harder version, lift your feet into a Dumbbell Larsen Press or pause 1–2 seconds at the chest.

Substitutes: Barbell Bench Press when you have a rack or spotter and want heavier loads, Hammer Grip Dumbbell Bench Press for cranky shoulders, Floor Dumbbell Press, or Push-Up with no equipment at all.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/单臂哑铃划船

exercises.description: With one knee and hand on a flat bench, row a dumbbell with one arm from a straight-arm hang to your hip to build your lats and upper back. Most of the work lands on your lats and teres major below the armpit, the rotator cuff on the back of the shoulder blade and the lower traps, which pull the blade down and back; your middle traps, rear delt and forearm help. The bench holds your torso, so your lower back stays out of it and you can row a heavy dumbbell. Pick it over the standing two-dumbbell row when your lower back tires first or one side lags behind.
instructions: Set a dumbbell beside the front half of a flat bench, on the side you'll train. Any sturdy support at knee height works too.
For a right-arm set, put your left knee and shin on the bench and your left hand flat ahead of the knee, arm straight under your shoulder.
Plant your right foot a little back and out to the side, knee soft. Flat back, torso about parallel to the floor, eyes on the floor just past the bench.
Pick up the dumbbell with your palm facing the bench, fingers hooked around the handle and wrist straight. Let the arm hang under your shoulder, shoulder blade drifting forward.
Pull the shoulder blade toward your spine first, then drive your elbow up and back toward your hip, upper arm brushing your side.
Stop with the dumbbell beside your hip and the elbow just above your back. Hold a second, then lower in about 2 seconds to a full hang.
Finish all reps on this side and set the dumbbell down, then swap knee, hand and arm for the same number on the other side.
mistakes: Twisting to heave the dumbbell up: the working shoulder rolls toward the ceiling and the hip opens. Keep both shoulders and hips square to the floor, press the support hand into the bench and go lighter if you still turn.
Rowing to your chest with the elbow flared out wide. That's a rear-delt row; here the elbow drives toward your hip and the dumbbell finishes beside your lower ribs.
Stopping the dumbbell halfway down. At the bottom of every rep, let the arm hang straight and the shoulder blade spread before you pull again.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent Over Row
tips: Work with 8–12 reps per side for muscle and 5–8 for strength, over 3–4 sets. Stay with one dumbbell until both sides reach the top number in all sets with a full hang, a one-second hold and no twisting. Then take the next dumbbell, usually 2–2.5 kg heavier, and build the reps back up from the bottom.

You should feel it along the side of your back under the armpit and around the shoulder blade, while the support arm and your abs work to keep you still. If your lower back starts doing the work, your support hand has probably drifted away from under your shoulder. On heavy sets, your grip often gives out before your back does.

Substitutes: Dumbbell Neutral Grip Incline Bench Row if you can't stop your torso from twisting, Bent Over Kettlebell Row when there's no bench (free hand on your front knee), Double Dumbbell Bent Over Row to train both sides at once, and One-Arm Cable Row for the steady pull of a low pulley.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱二头肌/啞鈴二頭彎舉

exercises.description: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward, and curl both weights up to your shoulders: the classic way to build bigger, stronger biceps. Both heads of the biceps on the front of your upper arm do most of the work, helped by the brachioradialis on the thumb side of your forearm and the grip muscles holding the handles. Each arm lifts its own dumbbell, so your stronger side can't cover for the weaker one, and one pair of dumbbells is all the kit you need. Pick it over a barbell curl when a straight bar bothers your wrists or elbows.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and your knees straight but soft, a dumbbell in each hand and your arms hanging at your sides.
Turn your palms to face forward and hold each handle in the middle, knuckles in line with your forearm.
Set your shoulders down and back, stack your ribs over your hips and lightly tense your abs and glutes. Your elbows rest against your sides.
Breathe out and bend both elbows at the same time, bringing the dumbbells up in an arc toward the front of your shoulders. Only your forearms move.
Stop when your forearms are close to vertical and the dumbbells reach shoulder height, palms facing your shoulders. Squeeze there for about a second.
Lower both dumbbells along the same arc in 2–3 seconds until your elbows are completely straight, then curl again without a bounce. Set them down only after the last slow lowering.
mistakes: Leaning back and throwing the dumbbells up with your hips. Go lighter, brace your abs and glutes and keep your knees still. If the swing keeps creeping in, do the set with your back against a wall.
Elbows sliding forward and up at the top so your shoulders lift the weight. Keep the elbows beside your ribs and stop at shoulder height, not at your chin.

Half reps at the bottom, or dumbbells that drop the last part of the way. Lower for 2–3 seconds until your elbows are fully straight; heavy dumbbells snapping into a locked elbow yank on the biceps tendon.
Palms turning in toward a hammer grip as the dumbbells rise. Keep them facing forward at the bottom and toward your shoulders at the top; think "pinky slightly up".
exercises.name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
tips: Curl 8–15 reps, or 6–10 on heavier days. Add reps at the same dumbbells until all sets hit the top number, then take the next pair (usually 1–2 kg more per hand) and go back to the bottom. On light dumbbells that step is a 10–20% jump, so expect several sessions at each weight.

The front of your upper arm works hardest as your forearms pass horizontal and in the squeeze at the top, plus some work along the thumb side of your forearm. If your lower back or the front of your shoulders starts doing the lifting, the dumbbells are too heavy.

Can't stop the swing? Switch to the Seated Dumbbell Curl with your back against an upright bench. For a harder version, stretch the lowering to 3–4 seconds or move on to the Seated Incline Biceps Curl, where the biceps starts from a longer stretch.
Substitutes: Alternate Biceps Curl (one arm at a time), Barbell Biceps Curl (more total weight), EZ-Bar Biceps Curl (easier on the wrists) and Bar Cable Biceps Curl (steady pull at the bottom).

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/平凳哑铃鸟狗式划船

exercises.description: Support one hand and the opposite knee on a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in your free hand and extending the free leg behind you. Row the dumbbell toward your hip, then lower it under control. Keep your torso and raised leg steady throughout, then switch sides after the set.
instructions: Place a dumbbell on the floor beside the bench and position yourself with one knee and the opposite hand supported on the bench.
Hold the dumbbell in your free hand and extend the free leg, opposite the rowing arm, straight behind you.
Brace your core, keep your spine neutral, square your hips and shoulders toward the floor, and let the dumbbell hang directly below your shoulder.
Pull the dumbbell toward the side of your rib cage by driving your elbow up and back, keeping your upper arm close to your torso.
Pause briefly at the top of the row while squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine without rotating your torso.
Lower the dumbbell slowly and under control until your arm is fully extended, maintaining the raised-leg position and a stable torso.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch the supporting hand and knee, dumbbell hand, and extended leg to train the other side.
mistakes: Rotating the torso or opening the hips as the dumbbell is pulled up
Letting the raised leg drop, bend excessively, or swing instead of keeping it aligned with the torso
Arching or rounding the lower back instead of maintaining a neutral spine
Shrugging the working shoulder toward the ear during the row
Flaring the elbow too far out from the body instead of rowing in a controlled path
Lowering the weight too quickly and losing shoulder control at the bottom
exercises.name: Dumbbell Bird Dog Row
tips: Support the hand and opposite knee firmly on the bench, with the hand below the shoulder.
Pause briefly at the top and feel the contraction around the working shoulder blade.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
Keep the neck relaxed and look down at the bench or floor so your head stays aligned with your spine.
Perform the same number of controlled repetitions on both sides.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/哑铃保加利亚剪蹲

exercises.description: The Dumbbell Bulgarian Squat is a unilateral lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and calves. It involves performing a squat with one leg elevated behind you on a bench or platform while holding dumbbells for added resistance. This exercise improves balance, coordination, and strength in the lower body.
instructions: Stand a few feet in front of a bench or platform with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides.
Extend one leg back and place the top of your foot on the bench.
Keep your chest up and core engaged as you begin to lower your hips by bending your front knee.
Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the ground or as far as your mobility allows.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions on one leg before switching to the other.
mistakes: Using a bench height that is too high or too low, leading to improper balance and alignment.
Allowing the front knee to cave inward, which can strain the knee joint.
Leaning too far forward, causing excessive stress on the lower back.
Failing to keep the core engaged, resulting in loss of stability.
Not maintaining a vertical shin position on the front leg, reducing effectiveness.

exercises.description: A full-body conditioning exercise that combines a burpee with a double dumbbell snatch. Sweep both dumbbells forward, up and in along a wide arc, like scooping up a big ball to hug it, palms facing each other.
Move only at the shoulders. The elbow angle doesn't change and your torso stays upright, with no lean back.
Stop with the dumbbells almost touching at eye level, upper arms near shoulder height. Squeeze your upper chest for half a second.
Lower along the same arc in about 2 seconds, hands drifting apart, until the dumbbells hang beside your thighs. Start each rep from a standstill.
mistakes: Lifting straight ahead with your hands staying shoulder-width apart. That's a front raise, and it leaves most of the work to your front delts. Sweep up and in until the dumbbells nearly touch.
Opening the arms out to the sides like a lateral raise. From your thighs, travel forward and in; at the top your hands sit at the midline in front of you.
Bending and straightening the elbows, so the dumbbells get curled or pressed up. Set a small bend before the first rep and hold it; if it keeps changing, go lighter.
Leaning back, dipping the knees or snapping the hips to get the weights moving. Take about 2 seconds on the way up; if you still need a swing, go lighter or stand with your back against a wall.
Shrugging at the top or lifting the hands overhead. Keep your shoulders down and stop at eye level.
Letting the dumbbells drop back to your thighs after the squeeze. Let them travel back down the arc as slowly as they went up: that half of the rep counts too.

tips: Take 2–4 sets of 12–20 reps close to failure. Add reps with the same dumbbells until you get 20 on every set with the hands meeting at eye level and no lean back. Then move to the next pair, usually 1–2 kg heavier per hand, and restart at 12.
Light dumbbells make big jumps: going from 5 to 6 kg adds a fifth to the load. Before you move up, earn it with a 1–2 second pause at the top or a 3-second lowering.

Only the fronts of your shoulders burning? Bring your hands closer to the midline and think "upper arms across the chest" instead of "hands up". A pinch at the front of the shoulder near the top means you stop each rep at shoulder height.
Can't feel your upper chest yet? Learn the arc one arm at a time with your free hand on your upper chest, as in the One-Arm Low Fly Dumbbell.

Substitutes: Low-to-High Cable Fly, which keeps tension at the top where dumbbells go slack; One-Arm Low-to-High Cable Fly; Incline Dumbbell Chest Fly for a heavier, stretched upper-chest fly. After the classic lying fly? That's the Dumbbell Chest Fly on a flat bench.

exercises.description: Lie across a flat bench on your shoulder blades and move one dumbbell in an arc behind your head and back to train your lats through a deep stretch. The lats and the teres major, along the sides of your upper back and under the armpits, do the bulk of the pulling. The serratus anterior on your ribs and the long head of the triceps assist, and the lower chest chips in. Your elbows keep the same slight bend, so only the shoulders move. Lying crosswise leaves your ribcage free for a longer arc than lying along the bench, and all it takes is a dumbbell and a bench.
instructions: Sit on the side of a flat bench with the dumbbell standing on end on your thigh.
Lie back so only your shoulder blades rest across the pad, with your head at its edge.
Walk your feet out until your knees are bent about 90° and your hips are level with your torso. Feet flat, about hip-width.
Cup the inside of the top plate with both palms, fingers spread and thumbs around the handle, so the dumbbell hangs straight down.
Press it up over your shoulders with a soft bend in the elbows. Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs down.
Breathe in and take 2–3 seconds to lower the dumbbell over your face and behind your head. The elbow angle doesn't change.
Stop when your upper arms are beside your ears, or sooner if your ribs start to lift. Your hands end up about level with the bench.
Drive your upper arms toward your hips to bring the weight back along the same arc, breathing out as your arms reach vertical. After the last rep, lower it to your chest before you sit up.
mistakes: Hips sagging at the bottom or bucking up to get the weight moving. Squeeze your glutes and keep your hips level with the bench; if they have to move, the dumbbell is too heavy.
Arching the lower back and flaring the ribs to chase a deeper stretch. Breathe out a little, keep the ribs down and end the arc where they start to lift.
Bending and straightening the elbows. That turns the rep into a triceps extension, so set a small bend at the top and keep exactly that angle.
Bringing the dumbbell past vertical, over your stomach. The lats go slack there; stop with your arms straight up over your shoulders.
Holding the handle instead of the plate, so the dumbbell tilts toward your face. Cup the top plate from underneath with both palms.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
tips: Do 2–4 sets of 10–15 reps. Add reps first: once you get 15 in all sets with the full arc and level hips, take the next dumbbell up (usually 2–2.5 kg heavier) and start again from 10. Before going heavier you can also slow the lowering to 3 seconds and pause 1–2 seconds in the stretch.

Expect a big stretch, then the work, along the sides of your upper back, under your armpits and over your ribs, plus the backs of your upper arms. Feeling it in your elbows, neck or lower back means the setup needs a second look.

Shoulder pinching with your arms overhead? Shorten the arc to where it's pain-free, or lie along the bench with your whole back supported. The dumbbell passes over your face, so check the collars of an adjustable one before every set.
Substitutes: Dumbbell Pullover with Legs Raised if holding the hip bridge bothers your back, Straight-Arm Lat Pulldown when you'd rather have cable tension, Barbell Pullover, Machine Pullover.

exercises.description: Brace one knee and hand on a flat bench and row a single dumbbell with an overhand grip, elbow flared out to the side, to build your rear delts. The back of the shoulder does most of the work; the middle and lower traps between your shoulder blades and the side delt help out. The setup matches the classic one-arm row, but the elbow travels wide and the dumbbell goes to your chest line instead of your hip, which shifts the load from the lats to the rear delts. It's worth adding if you press a lot, your shoulders tend to roll forward, or flyes bother your elbows.
instructions: To work your right arm, rest your left knee and shin on a flat bench, knee under your hip, foot hanging off the end.
Plant your left hand flat on the bench just ahead of your shoulder, arm straight.
Set your right foot on the floor beside the bench, a little back, knee soft. Flat back, torso about parallel to the floor, eyes on the bench just past your hand.
Pick up the dumbbell with an overhand grip: handle across your body, palm facing your feet, knuckles toward your head.
Let the arm hang straight under the shoulder.
Lead with the elbow, driving it up and out to the side, away from your ribs. The forearm stays vertical and the dumbbell rises beside the bench toward your chest line, not your hip.
Stop when your upper arm is level with your back and the elbow is bent about 90°. Pull the shoulder blade toward your spine without shrugging and hold for 1–2 seconds.
Lower over about 2 seconds to a straight arm, letting the shoulder blade slide forward a little so you feel a stretch across the back of the shoulder.
Finish all your reps on the right, then mirror the setup and do the same number with your left arm.
mistakes: Tucking the elbow along your ribs and pulling the dumbbell to your hip. That's a regular lat row; point the elbow out to the side and aim the dumbbell at your chest line.
Twisting your torso open to get the dumbbell higher. Keep hips and shoulders square to the floor and stop at back level; if you can't, the dumbbell is too heavy.
Shrugging the working shoulder toward your ear at the top. Think “elbow out”, not “elbow to the ear”, and pull the shoulder blade back toward your spine, not up.
Curling the weight up: the hand drifts toward your shoulder and the elbow angle closes well below 90°. Let the forearm hang vertical and move the elbow, not the hand.
Driving the elbow far above your back so the shoulder rolls forward and pinches at the front. Stop when the upper arm is level with your torso and hold there.
A sloppy base, with the knee or hand out of line and the back sagging. Set knee under hip and hand under shoulder before the first rep, and reset when you switch sides.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
tips: Do 2–4 sets of 10–20 reps per arm, taking the last reps close to failure; sets of 8–10 are about as heavy as this lift needs to go.
Add reps first: once both arms reach 20 in every set with the elbow wide and a 1-second hold, move to the next dumbbell, usually 1–2 kg heavier.
With light dumbbells, each step up is a big jump. If the heavier one drops you below your range, stay with the old one and add a rep per session or stretch the top hold to 2–3 seconds.
Start with about half the weight you use for a regular one-arm dumbbell row.

The work belongs in the back of the working shoulder and between the shoulder blade and spine. Lat burning along your side means the elbow has drifted to your ribs; a tight neck means you're shrugging. If the front of the shoulder pinches at the top, bring the elbow in to about 45° from your ribs and stop at torso height.

Substitutes: Dumbbell Seated Bent Over High Row (both arms at once, seated), Barbell Rear Delt Row (heavier, but you hold the hip hinge yourself), Cable Face Pull (cable tension, no hinge) and Barbell Incline Wide Grip Row (chest on an incline bench, no lower-back load).

exercises.description: With a dumbbell in each hand, push your hips back and lower the weights down your legs to just below the knees to build your hamstrings and glutes. Going down, the backs of your thighs stretch; coming up, your glutes and hamstrings do the lifting while the muscles along your lower spine hold your back flat. Dumbbells make it an easy first hinge and the standard RDL for home training. Each hand finds its own line, so many people find it easier on the wrists than a straight bar. To go really heavy, switch to the barbell: big dumbbells usually beat your grip first.
instructions: Take the dumbbells from a rack or bench. If they're on the floor, squat down, lift them with a flat back and stand tall.
Set your feet hip-width apart, toes forward, and unlock your knees into a soft bend you keep until the last rep.
Rest the dumbbells on the front of your thighs, overhand grip, palms facing you and handles roughly in line. Shoulders slightly back and down.
Breathe in, brace and push your hips straight back. Your torso tips forward on its own, back flat, eyes on the floor ahead.
Take 2–3 seconds to slide the dumbbells down your thighs, arms hanging straight. Stop just below the knees, when your hips stop moving back.
Pause for a beat, then drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall without leaning back. The dumbbells never touch the floor.
To finish, bend your knees and set the dumbbells down with your back flat, or return them to the rack.
mistakes: Squatting the dumbbells down: your knees bend more and push forward the lower the weights go. Set the soft bend at the top, leave it there and send your hips back with your shins close to vertical.
Rounding your back to reach the floor. Depth ends where your hips stop moving back with a flat back, usually just below the knees; if you can't get there, use a lighter pair.
Letting the dumbbells swing out in front of your legs. Keep your arms pulled in so the dumbbells brush your thighs and shins all the way down and up.
Shoulders rolling forward as the dumbbells drag your upper back round. Set them slightly back and down before every rep. If they won't stay there, the weight is too heavy.
One dumbbell sitting lower than the other, or your hips drifting to one side. Keep both handles level and your weight even over both feet.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
tips: Two to four sets of 8–12 reps, up to 15, cover most needs. Stay with the same pair until all your sets hit 12 with the same depth and a flat back, then move to the next pair (usually 1–2.5 kg heavier per dumbbell) and drop back to 8.

The stretch belongs in the back of your thighs, between your glutes and knees. If your lower back tires first, you're going too deep or rounding; if the fronts of your thighs burn, your knees are bending too much.
Heavy dumbbells tend to slip out of your hands before your hamstrings are done. Lifting straps solve that; rounding your back to hang on doesn't.
Learning to hinge? Practice the Hip Hinge with a dowel along your spine first. Once your heaviest pair feels easy, slow the lowering to 3–4 seconds or move on to the Single Leg Romanian Deadlift.

Substitutes: Romanian Deadlift with a barbell when you want to load heavier, Cable Romanian Deadlift when your grip needs a break, Dumbbell Straight Leg Deadlift for a longer stretch, and B Stance Romanian Deadlift when your dumbbells are too light.

exercises.description: Lie face down on a raised flat bench and row two dumbbells up beside your ribs to build your lats and upper back without loading your lower back. The lats do most of the pulling, with help from the teres major under each armpit, the lower and middle traps between and below your shoulder blades and the small rotator cuff muscles on them; rear delts and arms assist. Your feet are off the floor, so there's nothing to push or swing with. Unlike the incline dumbbell row, your whole body lies flat; unlike the barbell Seal Row, you get a neutral grip and a full squeeze at the top.
instructions: Raise a flat bench on solid blocks or plates until your arms can hang straight with the dumbbells off the floor. It must not wobble.
Set the dumbbells on the floor under the head end of the bench, one per side, before you lie down.
Lie face down with your upper chest at the front edge and your chin just over it, legs straight and feet together.
Take the dumbbells with a neutral grip, palms facing the bench, arms hanging straight under your shoulders and shoulder blades spread.
Pull your shoulder blades toward your spine first, then drive both elbows up and back toward your hips, upper arms 20–30° from your sides.
Stop with the dumbbells level with the pad beside your lower ribs, elbows above your back. Hold one second, chest and chin down.
Take about 2 seconds to lower to a full hang and let your shoulder blades slide apart before the next pull.
Set the dumbbells on the floor first when the set is done, then slide off the bench.
mistakes: Bench too low, so the dumbbells tap the floor or your arms never straighten. Raise it on stable blocks or plates until you hang with straight arms and the dumbbells clear.
Peeling your chest and head off the pad and arching to heave the dumbbells up. Keep your breastbone and chin down; if a rep won't finish without lifting, take lighter dumbbells or end the set.

Elbows flaring wide and the dumbbells drifting toward your chest. Keep your upper arms about 20–30° from your sides and pull toward your hips; the elbows-out version is the Incline Bench Dumbbell Wide Row.
Curling instead of rowing: wrists bend and the hands come up while the elbows stay low. Let your forearms hang vertical, treat your hands as hooks, and use straps if your grip goes before your back.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Seal Row
tips: Three or four sets of 8–12 reps are the default; go down to 6–8 for heavier work or up to 15 for lighter pump sets. Keep the same pair until you get 12 on all sets with the one-second hold and your chest on the pad. Then take the next pair, usually 1–2 kg heavier per hand, and build back up from 8.

The sides of your back do the pulling, under your armpits and between and below your shoulder blades. Arms and grip work too but shouldn't quit first. Lower back joining in? Your chest is coming off the pad.
When the dumbbells feel light but the next pair is too big a jump, hold 2–3 seconds at the top and take 3 seconds on the way down.

Substitutes: Dumbbell Neutral Grip Incline Bench Row if you can't raise a bench, Seal Row for a heavier barbell version, Double Dumbbell Bent Over Row with no bench at all, or Chest Supported Machine Row.

exercises.description: Curl both dumbbells to your shoulders and turn your palms up on the way, so your biceps does both of its jobs: bending the elbow and turning the forearm. You start in a hammer grip with your palms facing your thighs, and most of the twist happens in the top half of the lift before it unwinds as you lower. The front of your upper arm does the work, with the thumb side of your forearm chipping in early while the grip is still neutral. Pick it over the palms-forward curl when a fully turned grip at the bottom bothers your wrists or elbows.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and your knees straight but soft, holding two equal dumbbells by the middle of the handles.
Let your arms hang at your sides with your palms facing your thighs, like the start of a hammer curl. Your elbows rest against your ribs.
Pull your shoulders down and slightly back and lightly tense your abs and glutes so your torso stays still for the whole set.
Curl both dumbbells up together by bending only at the elbows. Once your forearms pass horizontal, start turning your palms up.
Stop with the dumbbells in front of your shoulders and your forearms just past vertical, palms facing your shoulders and little fingers a bit higher than your thumbs. Squeeze for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower along the same arc, turning your palms back toward your thighs, until your elbows are completely straight. Pause for a beat before the next rep.
mistakes: No real twist. If your palms still face each other at the top, or only flick over in the last inch, you've done a hammer curl. Start turning as your forearms pass horizontal and think "little finger up".
Bending the wrist back or flaring the elbow to get the palm up. Turn the whole forearm with your wrist straight in line with it, and go lighter if the elbow wanders off your ribs.
Letting the dumbbells drop and skipping the turn back. Lower for 2–3 seconds, rotate your palms toward your thighs on the way down and straighten your elbows on every rep.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Supinated Curl
tips: Two to four sets of 8–15 reps work, or 6–10 on heavier days. Pick a range such as 3 × 8–12 and add reps at the same dumbbells until all sets reach 12 with a full twist at the top and straight elbows at the bottom. Then take the next pair up (usually 1–2.5 kg more per hand) and work up again from 8.

The front of your upper arm should burn most as your palms turn up near the top. A sharp pull deep in the crease of the elbow during the twist means the dumbbells are too heavy or you're jerking the rotation.

Torso keeps swinging? Sit on a bench with the back upright and keep the same twist. For a harder version, hold each handle off-center with your thumb against the inner plate; the heavier little-finger side fights the turn.

Substitutes: Dumbbell Alternate Supinated Curl (same twist, one arm at a time), Seated Dumbbell Curl (no body swing), Dumbbell Biceps Curl (palms forward the whole rep) and Barbell Biceps Curl for heavier loads.

instructions: Adjust the preacher bench so that your upper arms rest comfortably on the pad with your armpits at the top edge.
Sit down and hold a dumbbell in one hand with a supinated grip (palm facing up).
Extend your arm fully, allowing the dumbbell to hang down without locking your elbow.
Curl the dumbbell upwards by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arm stationary against the pad.
Continue curling until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbell is at shoulder level.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.

Lifting the dumbbells too quickly, using momentum instead of controlled muscle contraction.

Curling the wrists at the top of the movement, shifting focus away from the biceps and onto the forearms.
Positioning the seat too high or too low, causing improper arm alignment and reducing exercise effectiveness.
Letting the shoulders roll forward, decreasing bicep isolation and increasing shoulder involvement.
Using excessive weight, leading to compromised form and potential strain on the elbows.
Failing to maintain a supinated grip throughout the curl, reducing bicep engagement.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Supinated Preacher Curl
tips: Ensure your upper arms remain in contact with the pad throughout the exercise to isolate the biceps effectively.
Focus on using a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle tension and prevent momentum from assisting in the lift.
Avoid locking out your elbows at the bottom of the movement to maintain continuous tension on the biceps.
Exhale as you curl the weight up and inhale as you lower it back down.
Start with a lighter weight to perfect your form before progressing to heavier dumbbells.

exercises.description: Swing one dumbbell from between the legs to shoulder height, holding it with both hands. Drive the movement by extending the hips, then hinge back as the dumbbell returns. This exercise develops power through the glutes and back of the thighs while the arms guide the weight rather than lift it.
instructions: Hinge at your hips, bend your knees slightly, and grip one end of the dumbbell with both hands. Keep your back flat and your chest open.
Pull the dumbbell back between your legs, keeping your arms straight and your shoulders packed down.
Extend your hips forcefully to swing the dumbbell to shoulder height.
Let the dumbbell move from the power of your hips, not by lifting with your arms or squatting deeply.
At the top, stand tall with your glutes tight, ribs down, and arms straight in front of you.
Let the dumbbell fall back under control, then hinge at the hips as it passes between your legs.
Repeat with a steady rhythm. Keep your spine neutral throughout and stop if you feel pain in your lower back.
mistakes: Lifting the dumbbell with the arms and shoulders instead of driving with the hips.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the swing.
Hyperextending the lower back at the top instead of finishing with a neutral, tall posture.
Letting the knees cave inward during the hip drive.
Keeping the weight on the toes or letting the heels lift.
Failing to fully extend the hips at the top of each rep.
exercises.name: Dumbbell Swing
tips: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart, with the dumbbell on the floor slightly in front of you.
Hinge at the hips by pushing them back, keep a soft bend in your knees, and grip one end of the dumbbell firmly with both hands.
Hike the dumbbell back between your thighs, keeping your shoulders packed and your arms straight but not locked.
Keep your shins fairly vertical during the hinge. This is not a squat, so avoid letting your knees travel far forward.
Keep a repeatable rhythm from one swing to the next.
