exercises.description: The High Low Cable Chest Fly is an isolation exercise targeting the pectoral muscles. It involves using a cable machine to perform a fly motion, starting with the cables positioned high above the shoulders and pulling them downwards in an arc towards the midline of the body. This movement emphasizes the lower portion of the chest.
instructions: Set the pulleys on a cable machine to a high position above shoulder height.
Attach D-handle attachments to each pulley.
Stand in the center of the machine with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand.
Step forward slightly to create tension in the cables, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Position your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Exhale and bring your hands together in front of your body in a wide arc, maintaining the bend in your elbows.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Inhale and slowly return to the starting position, controlling the weight throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Starting with the cables too high or too low, leading to improper targeting of the chest muscles.
Allowing the elbows to bend excessively, which shifts focus away from the chest to the arms.
Using momentum to swing the cables instead of controlled movements, reducing muscle engagement.
Failing to maintain a slight bend in the elbows, increasing strain on the shoulder joints.
Overextending the arms at the end of the motion, risking shoulder injury.
Not retracting the shoulder blades, which can lead to poor posture and ineffective chest activation.
Setting the weight too heavy, causing form breakdown and reduced range of motion.
Leaning too far forward or backward, compromising balance and targeting the wrong muscle groups.
Not aligning the wrists with the forearms, leading to wrist strain.
Neglecting to engage the core, which can result in instability and poor form.
exercises.name: High Low Cable Chest Fly
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability.
Avoid locking out your elbows; maintain a slight bend to protect your joints.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your hands together.
Control the movement on both the concentric (bringing hands together) and eccentric (returning to start) phases.
Adjust the weight so that you can perform each repetition with proper form without straining.
Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle engagement.

exercises.description: A static hold at the top of a push-up: arms straight, hands under the shoulders and the body in one line from head to heels, supported on the toes. It works the abs and the shoulder stabilizers. Brace your core, squeeze your glutes and push the floor away while you hold for time and breathe steadily.
instructions: Kneel on all fours with your hands on the floor directly under your shoulders and your fingers spread.
Step your feet back one at a time and straighten your legs so you are supported only on your hands and toes.
Straighten your arms and keep your shoulders stacked over your wrists.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your body forms one straight line from head to heels.
Push the floor away with your palms to keep your shoulder blades spread apart.
Keep your neck neutral and look at the floor just ahead of your hands.
Hold for the planned time while breathing steadily, then lower your knees to the floor to finish.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag so the lower back arches
Piking the hips higher than the shoulders
Placing the hands in front of the shoulders instead of directly under them
Letting the chest sink between the shoulder blades instead of pushing the floor away
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Dropping the head or lifting it to look forward
Holding the breath
Hyperextending the elbows and hanging on the joints
exercises.name: High Plank
tips: Spread your fingers and press through the whole hand, especially the base of the index finger, to take pressure off your wrists.
Tighten your quads and push your heels back so your legs help hold the position.
Draw your ribs toward your pelvis and tuck your pelvis slightly to keep your lower back neutral.
If you cannot hold a straight line for 20 seconds, rest your knees on the floor and build up the time from there.
End the set as soon as your hips start to drop instead of chasing a longer time with poor form.
Add 5 to 10 seconds at a time once you can hold the current duration with clean form.

exercises.description: Facing away from a high pulley and leaning well forward, you push a rope from behind your head out to arm's length to train your triceps in the stretch. Unlike a pushdown, your upper arms stay beside your ears, not at your sides. All three heads of the triceps work, and the long head, which runs up the back of the arm toward the armpit, gets the deepest stretch. The cable pulls hardest with your hands behind your head. Because you take the rope from above and step out, setup stays easy with a heavy stack, and your lower back doesn't arch the way it can in the low-pulley version.
instructions: Set the pulley at the very top of a cable station or lat pulldown tower and clip on a triceps rope.
Hold one rope end in each hand, palms facing each other, with your fists right on top of the knobs.
Turn your back to the stack and bring the rope over your head: hands behind your head, elbows pointing forward beside your ears.
Take a long step out into a split stance, front knee bent and back heel up, far enough that the plates stay lifted at the bottom.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is well past 45° from upright, back flat, abs braced and head between your arms.
From the stretch, straighten your elbows and push your hands forward until your arms line up with your torso, not up toward the ceiling.
Squeeze for a second with your fists together, then take 2–3 seconds to bend your elbows until your hands are back behind your head.
When you're finished, walk back toward the stack until the weight sets down, then lift the rope off over your head.
mistakes: Standing upright with your feet together. The cable pulls you backward and your lower back arches; take a long split stance and hinge until the cable runs over your upper back.
Elbows dropping toward the floor as you push, so your lats turn the rep into a pullover. Keep your elbows by your ears and move only your forearms. If they keep drifting, go lighter.
Flaring the elbows and pulling the rope apart. Point your elbows forward, no wider than your shoulders, and keep your fists together from start to finish.
Turning around when your forearms are about level with the floor. Let your hands travel all the way behind your head; if you can't get there, the weight is too heavy.
Letting the stack yank your arms back, so your shoulders hike up or the plates clank between reps. Lower over 2–3 seconds and stand far enough out that the weight never touches down.
exercises.name: High Pulley Overhead Triceps Extension
tips: Do 2–4 sets of 10–15 reps; for strength, 6–10. Chase reps before weight. When you get 15 on all sets with your body still, move the pin down one plate. A whole plate is a big jump on this lift, so use the stack's add-on weight or a small magnetic plate if your gym has one.

Expect a strong stretch along the back of your upper arm, up toward the armpit, while your hands are behind your head. Feeling it mostly in your lats means your shoulders are moving. Pain at the front of the shoulder or inside the elbow means shorten the stretch or go lighter.
Warm up with one or two light sets. Once the standard version feels easy, pause 1–2 seconds in the stretch or lower over 3–4 seconds. If your lower back tires before your triceps, lean a little less.

Substitutes: Cable Overhead Triceps Extension when you only have a low pulley or the lean bothers your back, Dumbbell Seated Triceps Extension if you'd rather have a backrest, and Standing One Dumbbell French Press when all you have is one dumbbell. If every overhead position hurts your shoulders, do pushdowns instead.

exercises.description: The High To Low Band Woodchopper is a dynamic exercise targeting the core, specifically the obliques, while also engaging the shoulders and hips. It mimics the motion of chopping wood, using a resistance band to provide tension throughout the movement. This exercise helps improve rotational strength and stability.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at a high point above your head.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, perpendicular to the anchor point.
Grasp the band with both hands, arms fully extended above one shoulder.
Engage your core and rotate your torso as you pull the band diagonally across your body.
Finish the movement by bringing your hands down towards the opposite knee, keeping arms straight.
Slowly return to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
mistakes: Using too much resistance, leading to compromised form and control.
Rotating the hips instead of keeping them stable and engaging the core.
Pulling with the arms instead of initiating the movement from the core.
Allowing the knees to collapse inward, reducing stability.
Not maintaining a neutral spine, causing undue stress on the back.
Failing to fully extend the arms during the chopping motion.
Moving too quickly, sacrificing control and precision.
Not aligning the band anchor point correctly, affecting the movement path.
Neglecting to engage the obliques, reducing effectiveness.
Standing too far from or too close to the anchor, altering resistance and range of motion.
exercises.name: High To Low Band Woodchopper
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better stability.
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement to protect your lower back.
Focus on using your core to drive the movement rather than relying on your arms.
Exhale as you pull the band down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Ensure that your movements are controlled to maximize muscle engagement and avoid injury.
Adjust the resistance of the band if needed to ensure proper form and effectiveness.

exercises.description: The Highbar Squat is a compound lower body exercise that primarily targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. It involves placing the barbell on the upper traps, maintaining an upright torso, and descending into a squat position while keeping the knees aligned with the toes.
instructions: Position a barbell on a squat rack at shoulder height.
Step under the bar and place it on your upper traps, ensuring it is centered.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and lift your elbows to create a stable shelf.
Unrack the bar by standing up straight and take a step back.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes slightly pointed out.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Initiate the squat by bending at the hips and knees simultaneously.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below.
Ensure your knees track over your toes throughout the movement.
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees.
mistakes: Knees caving inward during the ascent.
Heels lifting off the ground.
Bar placed too high on the neck.
Hips rising faster than the chest.
Not reaching full depth with thighs parallel to the ground.
Allowing the lower back to round.
Feet positioned too narrowly or too widely.
Failing to engage the core for stability.
Leaning too far forward, causing excessive forward tilt.
Not maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
exercises.name: High-Bar Squat
tips: Keep your core tight to maintain stability and prevent lower back strain.
Focus on keeping an upright torso to emphasize quadriceps engagement.
Ensure your knees do not cave inward; they should align with your toes.
Control the descent to maintain balance and prevent injury.
Use a full range of motion for maximum muscle activation.
Warm up properly before performing heavy squats to prepare your muscles and joints.
Start with lighter weights to perfect form before progressing to heavier loads.

instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place your hands on your hips.
Engage your core muscles to maintain balance and stability.
Begin by slowly rotating your hips in a clockwise direction, making large circles.
Complete 10-15 rotations, then switch to a counterclockwise direction for another 10-15 rotations.
Keep your upper body stable and focus on moving only your hips.

Allowing the torso to move excessively, reducing the focus on the hip joint.

Performing circles that are too large, leading to improper form and reduced control.

exercises.name: Hip Circles

Focus on controlled movements; avoid rushing through the rotations.
Keep your knees slightly bent to reduce pressure on the joints.
Perform hip circles as part of your warm-up routine to enhance joint mobility before engaging in more strenuous exercises.

exercises.description: The hip hinge is a fundamental movement pattern essential for exercises like deadlifts and kettlebell swings. It involves bending at the hips while maintaining a neutral spine, allowing for efficient load transfer and minimizing stress on the lower back.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Engage your core to stabilize your spine.
Begin the movement by pushing your hips back as if reaching them toward a wall behind you.
Keep your knees slightly bent and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Lower your torso until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your chest open and shoulders back.
Reverse the motion by driving through your heels and extending your hips to return to the starting position.

Rounding the lower back instead of keeping a neutral spine.
Allowing the shoulders to slump forward instead of maintaining a broad chest.
Initiating the movement from the knees rather than the hips.
Not engaging the core, leading to instability and poor control.
Hyperextending the neck by looking too far forward.
Failing to keep the weight on the heels, shifting it to the toes.
Not maintaining a straight line from the head to the tailbone.
Moving too quickly, sacrificing control and precision.
Allowing the hips to sway side-to-side instead of moving straight back.
exercises.name: Hip Hinge
tips: Focus on moving from the hips rather than bending at the waist.
Keep your weight balanced over your midfoot to heels to maintain stability.
Ensure your back remains flat and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Practice in front of a mirror to monitor form and alignment.
Start with bodyweight to master the technique before adding resistance.

Brace your core and drive through your heels to lift your hips upward, extending them fully while keeping your chin tucked.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement and hold for a moment.
Lower your hips back down in a controlled manner to return to the starting position.

Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and prevent hyperextension of the lower back.

Control the descent of the bar to prevent it from dropping too quickly, which can reduce effectiveness and increase injury risk.

Lift your shoulders and legs off the ground simultaneously, keeping your lower back pressed into the mat.
Maintain a slight curve in your lower back without arching.
Hold this position, keeping your arms and legs straight and close to the floor without touching it.
Breathe steadily throughout the hold, maintaining tension in your core.

Allowing the ribs to flare out, reducing core stability.
Holding the position without breathing, leading to tension and fatigue.
Starting with an advanced position without mastering the basic form.
exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold

Start with shorter holds and gradually increase duration as you build strength.
Focus on keeping your body as tight as possible, minimizing any movement.
If you experience lower back discomfort, raise your legs higher to reduce strain.
Keep your head in a neutral position to avoid neck tension.

Lift your shoulders, arms and legs slightly off the floor, keeping your body in a curved hollow position.
Keep your ribs pulled down, your chin slightly tucked and your legs together.
Rock smoothly from your upper back toward your hips, using your core to control the movement.

Starting the rock by swinging the arms or legs rather than rocking as one rigid unit.

Using a large, uncontrolled rocking range.
Relaxing at either end of the rock.

Keep your arms closer to your torso to make the exercise easier.

Focus on lifting your knees high to maximize the engagement of your lower body muscles.
Maintain a steady breathing pattern; exhale as you lift each knee.
Start at a slow pace to master the movement, then gradually increase speed as you become more comfortable.
Ensure that each hop is light and controlled to reduce impact on the joints.

exercises.description: A lying core exercise in which both straight legs, held about 30 to 45 degrees off the floor, move side to side: they open wide, then cross over each other, with the top leg switching every rep. The hands rest under the hips and the head stays down. It trains the abs and hip flexors, and the inner and outer thighs work as the legs open and close.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight and together, and slide your hands palms down under your hips.
Rest your head on the floor and relax your shoulders.
Brace your abs and press your lower back into the floor.
Raise both straight legs to about 30 to 45 degrees off the floor and point your toes.
Open your legs wide to the sides, keeping both at the same height.
Bring them back toward the center and cross one leg over the other.
Open again and cross with the other leg on top. Keep alternating for the whole set, then lower your legs to the floor with control.
mistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the floor, which moves the strain from the abs to the lumbar spine
Bending the knees, which shortens the lever and takes work off the abs
Letting the legs rise or drop as they open and cross instead of keeping them at one height
Swinging the legs fast with momentum instead of controlling each opening and cross
Making the movement so small that the legs never open wide or fully cross
Always crossing with the same leg on top
Lifting the head and straining the neck instead of resting it on the floor
exercises.name: Horizontal Scissor Kicks
tips: Raise your legs higher to make the exercise easier, or lower them toward the floor to make it harder.
Press your palms lightly into the floor under your hips to keep your pelvis steady.
Point your toes and reach your legs long away from you to keep tension through the whole leg.
Exhale as your legs cross and inhale as they open.
Count each cross as one rep. Start with 10 to 20 per set and add more as your control improves.

exercises.description: From standing, fold forward and walk your hands along the floor until you reach a high plank, keeping your feet in place. Perform one push-up, then walk your hands back toward your feet and return to standing, linking the hip hinge with controlled upper-body support.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and brace your core.
Hinge at your hips and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet, bending your knees slightly if needed.
Walk your hands forward until you reach a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping your body rigid and your elbows angled slightly back.
Press through your palms to return to the high plank.
Keep your feet in place, walk your hands back toward them and stand up.
Repeat the movement smoothly, keeping your hips from sagging during the plank and push-up.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike up in the plank position.
Walking the hands out too far and losing a strong plank before the push-up.
Placing the hands too wide or too far forward for the push-up.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides during the push-up.
Dropping the chest only partway instead of using a controlled full range of motion.
Allowing the hips to drop before the chest during the push-up.
exercises.name: Inchworm Push-Up
tips: Start standing with feet about hip-width apart.
Spread your fingers to give the moving hands a wider base of support.
Take short backward hand steps on the return so the hips can rise gradually.
Stand up by driving through your feet and extending your hips, then begin the next repetition with control.
Use short sets so the hand-walking rhythm stays consistent from start to finish.

exercises.description: The Incline Barbell Bench Press is a compound upper body exercise that primarily targets the upper portion of the pectoral muscles, with secondary emphasis on the shoulders and triceps. It is performed on an incline bench set at a 15-30 degree angle, which shifts more focus to the upper chest compared to the flat bench press.
instructions: Set an incline bench at a 15-30 degree angle and position it under a barbell rack.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor for stability.
Grip the barbell with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and hold it directly above your chest with arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly to your upper chest, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly when the barbell is near your chest, then press it back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.
mistakes: Arching the lower back excessively, reducing chest engagement.
Lowering the bar too high on the chest, increasing shoulder strain.
Flaring elbows out too wide, risking shoulder impingement.
Bouncing the bar off the chest, leading to poor muscle control.
Failing to maintain a stable wrist position, risking wrist strain.
Not using a full range of motion, limiting muscle activation.
Lifting hips off the bench, compromising stability.
Allowing the bar to drift forward, reducing chest activation.
Using too much weight, sacrificing form for load.
Neglecting to engage the core, leading to reduced stability.
exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
tips: Ensure your back remains firmly pressed against the bench throughout the exercise to maintain proper form.
Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body and prevent arching of the lower back.
Focus on controlled movements; avoid bouncing the bar off your chest to reduce injury risk.
Adjust the bench angle if you feel excessive strain on your shoulders; a lower angle can reduce this stress.
Use a spotter for safety, especially when lifting heavy weights or approaching muscle fatigue.

exercises.description: The Incline Barbell Triceps Extension is a strength training exercise targeting the triceps brachii. It is performed on an incline bench, which emphasizes the long head of the triceps due to the angle of the arms. This exercise helps in building mass and strength in the upper arm.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight above your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the barbell slowly towards your forehead by bending your elbows.
Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your head throughout the movement.
Pause briefly when the barbell is just above your forehead.
Press the barbell back to the starting position by extending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing elbows to flare out excessively, reducing triceps engagement.
Lowering the barbell too far behind the head, causing shoulder strain.
Using momentum to lift the barbell instead of controlled movements.
Failing to keep the wrists straight, leading to strain and reduced control.
Positioning the bench at too steep of an incline, shifting focus away from the triceps.
Not fully extending the arms at the top of the movement, limiting triceps contraction.
Arching the back excessively, compromising stability and form.
Gripping the barbell too wide, reducing leverage and triceps activation.
exercises.name: Incline Barbell Triceps Extension
tips: Ensure your elbows remain stationary and do not flare out during the movement.
Maintain a controlled motion to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
Start with a lighter weight to perfect form before increasing resistance.
Focus on squeezing the triceps at the top of the movement for maximum contraction.
Keep your core engaged to maintain stability on the incline bench.

exercises.description: The Incline Cable Fly is an isolation exercise targeting the upper portion of the pectoral muscles. It involves using a cable machine with an adjustable bench set to an incline position. This exercise helps in developing chest definition and strength, emphasizing the upper chest fibers.
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 30-45 degree incline and position it between two cable pulleys.
Attach D-handle attachments to the low pulleys.
Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor, and grasp each handle with a neutral grip.
Lean back against the bench, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Extend your arms above your chest with a slight bend in your elbows, palms facing each other.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale and bring your arms back to the starting position, squeezing your chest muscles at the top of the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing elbows to bend excessively, turning the fly into a press.
Setting the bench at too steep an incline, shifting focus from chest to shoulders.
Failing to maintain a slight bend in the elbows, increasing strain on the joints.
Letting the cables pull arms too far back, risking shoulder strain.
Not retracting shoulder blades, reducing chest engagement.
Using momentum rather than controlled movements, decreasing effectiveness.
Bringing handles too close together, losing tension in the chest.
Arching the back excessively, compromising form and stability.
Not keeping wrists neutral, leading to potential wrist strain.
exercises.name: Incline Bench Cable Fly
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to reduce stress on the joints.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles at the top of the movement for maximum contraction.
Keep your movements controlled and avoid letting the weights pull your arms too far back to prevent shoulder strain.
Ensure that your shoulders remain down and back, avoiding any shrugging during the exercise.
Adjust the bench angle if needed to target different areas of the chest more effectively.

exercises.description: The Incline Bench Dumbbell Wide Row is an upper body exercise targeting the upper back, shoulders, and biceps. It involves pulling dumbbells towards your torso while lying face down on an incline bench, emphasizing the rear deltoids, rhomboids, and trapezius muscles. This exercise helps improve posture and upper back strength.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Lie face down on the bench with your chest supported and feet firmly on the ground.
Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Engage your core and keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Pull the dumbbells up towards your sides by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using too much weight, compromising form and control.
Allowing the elbows to drop below the back, reducing muscle engagement.
Arching the back excessively, leading to poor spine alignment.
Failing to retract the shoulder blades, limiting upper back activation.
Swinging the dumbbells, using momentum instead of muscle control.
Not maintaining a stable core, causing body sway.
Incorrect bench angle, affecting the range of motion.
Gripping the dumbbells too tightly, causing forearm fatigue.
Lifting the head, straining the neck.
exercises.name: Incline Bench Dumbbell Wide Row
tips: Ensure the bench is stable and set at a comfortable angle for your body.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid strain.
Use a controlled motion to prevent using momentum, which can reduce effectiveness and increase injury risk.
Start with lighter weights to master form before progressing to heavier dumbbells.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to protect your joints.

Keep your legs straight and together, then lift them towards your chest by flexing at the hips.
Raise your legs until they are perpendicular to your torso, or as high as you comfortably can.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position without letting them touch the ground.

Raising legs too high, shifting focus away from the lower abs.
Not keeping the legs straight, decreasing tension on the core.
Gripping the bench too tightly, causing unnecessary upper body tension.
Failing to engage the core muscles throughout the movement.
Using the hip flexors instead of the abs to lift the legs.
Not maintaining a consistent breathing pattern, reducing efficiency.

tips: Ensure your lower back remains in contact with the bench throughout the movement to prevent strain.
Control the movement both when raising and lowering your legs to maximize muscle engagement.
Exhale as you lift your legs and inhale as you lower them to maintain proper breathing rhythm.
If you find it difficult to keep your legs straight, you can slightly bend your knees.
Start with a moderate incline and adjust as needed to increase or decrease difficulty.

Sit on the incline bench with your back firmly against it and feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, and arms fully extended.
Keep your elbows close to your body and stationary as you curl the bar upwards towards your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.
Maintain control throughout the exercise and avoid using momentum.

Use a full range of motion to ensure maximum muscle activation.

exercises.description: Lie chest-down on a 45-degree incline bench and row a barbell from straight arms up to the pad, training your upper back while your lower back rests. The middle and lower traps between your shoulder blades, the rear delts and the small muscles over the shoulder blades (infraspinatus and teres minor) do most of the pulling, and the lats chip in along the sides. The pad holds your torso, so there's no hinge to hold and nothing to swing. Use it after heavy squats or deadlifts, or when your lower back limits your bent-over rows.
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to about 45 degrees (30–45 works) and lay a loaded barbell on the floor under the top of the backrest.
Straddle the seat and lean onto the backrest, chest and stomach on the pad, its top edge at your upper chest, chin just above it.
Plant both feet with your knees bent, one foot a little further back. Your hips sit at the bottom of the backrest, not on the seat.
Take an overhand grip about shoulder-width, hands just outside the pad, and lift the bar a couple of inches so it hangs from straight arms.
Draw your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows back and up, about 30–45 degrees from your sides.
Pull the bar almost straight up until it touches the underside of the pad at your lower chest or upper stomach, and hold for a second.
Lower it over 1–2 seconds to straight arms and let your shoulder blades spread. The plates stay off the floor between reps.
Set the bar down on the floor at the end of the set before you climb off the bench.
mistakes: Peeling your chest off the pad and heaving the bar up with your torso. Keep your breastbone on the pad until the last rep; if you can't, take weight off.
Half reps: the arms never straighten at the bottom, or the bar stops well short of the pad. Start every rep from a full hang and pull until the bar meets the pad.
Cranking your head up to look forward. Tuck your chin slightly and look at the floor just ahead of the bench.
Plates tapping or bouncing off the floor at the bottom. Raise the backrest a notch, set the bench on plates or blocks, or switch to smaller plates.
exercises.name: Incline Chest Supported Barbell Row
tips: Row 3–4 sets of 8–15 reps for muscle, or 6–8 reps for strength. Pick a range such as 8–12 and add reps at the same weight until you get 12 on all sets with your chest on the pad and a one-second hold. Then add 2.5 kg in total (1.25 kg per side) and go back to 8.

The work sits between and under your shoulder blades, at the backs of your shoulders and along the sides of your back, while your lower back stays quiet. A burning neck means you're shrugging. If your chest grinds into the pad and your legs start pushing, the weight is too heavy.

Ready for more? Pause 2 seconds with the bar against the pad, or move to the Seal Row, lying flat on a high bench where your legs can't help. Struggling with the setup? Use an empty bar or an EZ bar until the groove feels natural.
A light adjustable bench can slide or tip forward when you lean onto a steep backrest. Check that it stands firm before every set.

Substitutes: Incline Bench Dumbbell Wide Row (same bench, dumbbells), Chest Supported Machine Row (fixed path, nothing to pick up off the floor) and Barbell Bent Over Row (no bench, your lower back holds the hinge).

exercises.description: The Incline Close Grip Push Up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps, chest, and shoulders. It involves performing a push-up with hands placed closer together than shoulder-width on an elevated surface, such as a bench or step, to increase the emphasis on the triceps.
instructions: Position yourself in front of an elevated surface like a bench or step.
Place your hands on the edge of the surface, closer than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your legs behind you, balancing on your toes, forming a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and keep your body rigid.
Lower your chest towards the surface by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Hands placed too wide, reducing triceps engagement.
Elbows flaring out, causing shoulder strain.
Hips sagging, leading to lower back stress.
Inadequate core engagement, compromising stability.
Lowering body too quickly, losing control.
Not lowering chest fully to the incline, limiting range of motion.
Neck craned forward, causing neck strain.
Feet positioned too close, reducing balance.
Wrists bent excessively, increasing wrist strain.
exercises.name: Incline Close Grip Push-Up
tips: Keep your elbows tucked in close to your body throughout the movement to maximize tricep engagement.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels; avoid sagging or arching your back.
Control the movement speed; lower yourself slowly and push up with power.
Breathe in as you lower down and exhale as you push back up.
Adjust the incline height to modify difficulty; higher inclines are easier, lower inclines are more challenging.

exercises.description: Press two dumbbells from beside your upper chest to straight arms while lying on a bench set to 30–45°, to build the upper part of your chest. You feel a deep stretch just below the collarbones at the bottom; your front delts and triceps help, the triceps mostly near lockout. Compared with the flat dumbbell press, the incline shifts work toward the upper chest and shoulders, so most people use lighter dumbbells. Go for it instead of the incline barbell press when you train without a spotter or want each arm working on its own.
instructions: Set the backrest to 30–45° and leave the seat flat. If you slide down the bench, raise the seat one notch.
Sit with the dumbbells standing on your thighs near the knees, then lie back and kick them up to your shoulders with your knees.
Plant your feet flat, wider than your hips, knees bent about 90°. Glutes, upper back and head stay on the pads.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the backrest. A small natural arch in your lower back is fine.
Start with the dumbbells beside your upper chest, palms facing your feet, handles in one line and forearms vertical.
Press up and slightly in until your arms are straight over your shoulders. Stop with the dumbbells a few centimeters apart instead of clanging them.
Lower over about 2 seconds along the same arc until the handles reach your upper chest, elbows about 45–60° from your torso.
To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest, then onto your thighs as you sit up. Never drop them from straight arms.
mistakes: Backrest at 60° or steeper. At that angle your shoulders do most of the pressing; drop it to 30–45° and you'll feel the upper chest again.
Elbows flared out to 90° with the dumbbells drifting toward your neck at the bottom. Keep the dumbbells beside your upper chest and the elbows about 45–60° from your torso.
Hips leaving the seat, or an arch so big that the incline turns into a flat press. Glutes down, feet pushing into the floor, ribs down.
Wrists bent back and dumbbells drifting toward your face. Stack the handle over the wrist and the wrist over the elbow.
exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
tips: Press 3–4 sets of 8–12 reps for muscle, or 5–8 for strength.

Keep the same pair until all your sets hit the top of the range, then move to the next pair (usually 1–2.5 kg more per dumbbell) and build the reps back up. With light dumbbells that jump is big, so expect to lose 2–4 reps at first.
A pinch at the front of the shoulder means the bottom is too deep for you today: stop a little higher, lower the backrest or switch to a neutral grip.
Dumbbells wobbling all over the place? Start on the Smith machine, or use lighter dumbbells at about 15–30°. Once the path feels solid, add a 2-second pause at the bottom or try the one-arm version.
Substitutes: Incline Barbell Bench Press, Incline Neutral Grip Dumbbell Press, Smith Incline Chest Press.

Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Focus on a controlled motion; avoid using momentum to lift the weights.
Exhale as you press the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them down.
Adjust the bench angle if you feel discomfort in your shoulders; a lower incline may reduce strain.
Start with lighter weights to perfect your form before progressing to heavier loads.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/上斜坡尔抬举

exercises.description: The Incline Powell Raise is an isolation exercise targeting the rear deltoids, upper back, and rotator cuff muscles. It is performed on an incline bench to enhance the range of motion and muscle engagement. This exercise helps improve shoulder stability and posture.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Lie face down on the bench with your chest and stomach supported, feet firmly planted on the ground.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Extend your arms straight down towards the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise the dumbbells outward and upward in a wide arc until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Lifting the weight too high, causing shoulder impingement.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement, reducing muscle engagement.
Allowing the torso to rotate, reducing focus on the target muscles.
Incorrect bench angle, leading to ineffective muscle activation.
Gripping the weights too tightly, causing unnecessary tension in the arms.
Not maintaining a neutral spine, increasing the risk of lower back strain.
Failing to retract the shoulder blades, limiting scapular movement.
Raising the arms too quickly and lowering too slowly, disrupting proper muscle contraction.
Allowing the elbows to flare out excessively, altering the intended movement path.
exercises.name: Incline Powell Raise
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability.
Avoid using momentum; focus on controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement.
Ensure your head remains in a neutral position, aligned with your spine.
Start with lighter weights to perfect your form before progressing to heavier loads.
Breathe out as you lift the weights and inhale as you lower them.
If you feel strain in your neck or lower back, adjust your position or reduce the weight.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/上斜俯卧撑

exercises.description: The incline push-up is a bodyweight exercise that targets the upper chest, shoulders, and triceps. It is performed with the hands elevated on a stable surface, such as a bench or step, which decreases the resistance compared to a standard push-up. This exercise is suitable for beginners and those looking to focus more on the upper part of the pectoral muscles.
instructions: Position your hands shoulder-width apart on an elevated surface, such as a bench or step.
Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your body.
Lower your chest towards the elevated surface by bending your elbows.
Pause briefly when your chest is just above the surface.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Hands placed too wide, reducing chest engagement.
Elbows flaring out excessively, increasing shoulder strain.
Hips sagging, leading to lower back stress.
Neck craned forward, causing neck discomfort.
Inadequate core engagement, resulting in unstable form.
Inconsistent range of motion, limiting muscle activation.
Rushing through reps, compromising control and effectiveness.
Feet positioned too close to the incline, reducing leverage.
exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
tips: Ensure that the surface you use is stable and can support your weight.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement to engage your core effectively.
Keep your elbows at about a 45-degree angle from your body to protect your shoulders.
Focus on controlled movements rather than speed to maximize muscle engagement.
Breathe in as you lower yourself and exhale as you push back up.
Adjust the height of the incline to increase or decrease difficulty as needed.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/上斜扭转仰卧起坐

exercises.description: The Incline Twisting Sit Up is an advanced core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the obliques. It involves performing a sit-up on an incline bench while incorporating a twisting motion to engage the side muscles of the abdomen.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a moderate angle, typically between 30 to 45 degrees.
Sit on the bench and secure your feet under the foot pads.
Lie back with your hands placed behind your head or crossed over your chest.
Engage your core and lift your upper body off the bench, twisting your torso to one side as you ascend.
Reach the top of the movement with your elbow pointing towards the opposite knee.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat the movement, alternating sides with each repetition.
mistakes: Failing to keep the core engaged throughout the movement, leading to reduced effectiveness.
Using momentum to lift the torso instead of controlled muscle engagement.
Allowing the lower back to arch excessively, which can strain the spine.
Twisting the torso without proper alignment, causing uneven muscle activation.
Not maintaining a consistent breathing pattern, leading to reduced performance.
Rushing the movement, which compromises form and control.
Neglecting to return to the starting position fully, limiting the range of motion.
Letting the feet lift off the incline, reducing stability and core engagement.
exercises.name: Incline Twisting Sit Up
tips: Focus on controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and reduce injury risk.
Keep your core tight throughout the exercise to maintain stability and effectiveness.
Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands; instead, use your core muscles to lift.
Exhale as you twist up and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Start with a lower incline if you're new to this exercise and gradually increase as you build strength.
Ensure your movements are smooth and deliberate, avoiding any jerking motions.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/反向划船

exercises.description: The Inverted Row, also known as the Australian Pull-Up, is a bodyweight exercise that targets the upper back, shoulders, and biceps. It involves pulling your chest towards a bar while your body is suspended horizontally beneath it. This exercise is effective for building strength and improving posture.
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at waist height or use a Smith machine bar.
Lie under the bar with your chest directly below it and extend your legs straight out.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and glutes to keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Pull your chest towards the bar by retracting your shoulder blades and bending your elbows.
Pause at the top when your chest nearly touches the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Sagging hips due to lack of core engagement, leading to improper alignment.
Pulling with the arms instead of engaging the back muscles, reducing effectiveness.
Flaring elbows out excessively, which can strain the shoulders.
Not pulling the chest to the bar, limiting range of motion.
Using momentum to complete the movement instead of controlled motion.
Allowing the shoulders to round forward, compromising posture.
Positioning the feet too close, reducing stability and range of motion.
Not maintaining a straight line from head to heels, affecting form.
Failing to retract the scapulae, decreasing back muscle activation.
Overarching the lower back, which can lead to discomfort.
exercises.name: Inverted Row
tips: Keep your body rigid and avoid sagging hips to maintain proper form.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Adjust the height of the bar to increase or decrease difficulty; lower bars make it harder.
Ensure your head remains in a neutral position throughout the exercise.
Breathe out as you pull up and inhale as you lower down.
If you find it too challenging, bend your knees and place feet flat on the ground for support.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/倒置耸肩

exercises.description: The Inverted Shrug is an exercise primarily targeting the trapezius muscles, particularly the lower traps. It involves hanging from a bar and using shoulder depression to lift your body slightly, engaging the upper back and shoulders. This exercise helps improve shoulder stability and posture.
instructions: Begin by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body straight, avoiding any swinging.
Depress your shoulders by pulling them down away from your ears, lifting your body slightly upward.
Hold the top position for a moment, focusing on squeezing the lower trapezius muscles.
Slowly relax your shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing the shoulders to roll forward instead of keeping them retracted.
Failing to maintain a straight body line from head to heels.
Using momentum to lift the shoulders instead of controlled muscle engagement.
Not fully depressing the scapulae, limiting the range of motion.
Engaging the arms instead of focusing on the shoulder girdle.
Letting the hips sag, which compromises body alignment.
Neglecting to breathe steadily, leading to tension and reduced control.
Rushing the movement, which reduces effectiveness and control.
exercises.name: Inverted Shrug
tips: Ensure your grip is secure on the bar to maintain stability throughout the exercise.
Focus on moving only at the shoulders; avoid bending your elbows or using momentum.
Keep your core engaged to prevent swinging and maintain proper form.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you depress your shoulders and inhaling as you return to the start.
Start with a few repetitions to master the form before increasing volume.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/开合俯卧撑

exercises.description: The Push Up Jack is a dynamic exercise that combines the traditional push-up with a jumping jack motion. It targets the chest, shoulders, triceps, and core muscles while also providing cardiovascular benefits. This exercise enhances upper body strength, endurance, and coordination.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at about a 45-degree angle to your body.
As you push back up to the starting position, jump your feet out to the sides wider than hip-width apart.
Immediately jump your feet back together as you lower into the next push-up repetition.
Continue alternating between push-ups and jumping jack motions for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Failing to maintain a straight line from head to heels, causing the hips to sag or pike.
Allowing the elbows to flare out excessively, increasing shoulder strain.
Not engaging the core, leading to instability and reduced effectiveness.
Performing the jumping jack movement too quickly, compromising form and control.
Placing hands too far forward or backward, disrupting balance and alignment.
Neglecting to lower the chest fully to the ground, reducing range of motion.
Landing heavily on the toes during the jumping jack, increasing impact on the joints.
Rushing through the push-up phase, diminishing muscle engagement and control.
exercises.name: Jack Push-Up
tips: Maintain a strong core throughout the exercise to prevent sagging hips.
Focus on controlled movements rather than speed to ensure proper form.
Keep your elbows slightly tucked in during the push-up to protect your shoulders.
Breathe out as you push up and jump, and inhale as you lower down.
If you're new to this exercise, start with modified push-ups on your knees before progressing to full push-up jacks.
Ensure that your hands are positioned correctly to avoid wrist strain.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/詹达仰卧起坐

exercises.description: The Janda Sit Up is an advanced core exercise designed to isolate the abdominal muscles by minimizing the involvement of the hip flexors. This exercise emphasizes the contraction of the rectus abdominis and obliques, providing a more intense abdominal workout.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent at a 90-degree angle and feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands behind your head, keeping your elbows wide.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings by having a partner hold your ankles or using a resistance band around them to create tension.
Exhale and slowly curl your torso up towards your knees, focusing on contracting your abdominal muscles.
Pause at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the abs.
Inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the descent.
mistakes: Engaging hip flexors instead of isolating the abs.
Failing to maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Using momentum rather than controlled muscle contraction.
Lifting the lower back off the ground at the start.
Not fully engaging the glutes and hamstrings to stabilize the pelvis.
Allowing the feet to lift off the ground during the sit-up.
Rushing the movement, leading to poor form and reduced effectiveness.
Incorrectly positioning the hands, causing neck strain.
Not exhaling fully on the way up, reducing core engagement.
Overextending the neck by pulling on the head with the hands.
exercises.name: Janda Sit Up
tips: Focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift your torso rather than pulling with your neck or arms.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor as you lift to avoid engaging the hip flexors.
Maintain a slow and controlled movement to maximize muscle engagement and reduce momentum.
Ensure that your breathing is synchronized with the movement: exhale on the way up and inhale on the way down.
If you feel strain in your neck or lower back, reassess your form and ensure proper engagement of the core muscles.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/杰斐逊弯曲

exercises.description: The Jefferson Curl is a mobility and flexibility exercise targeting the posterior chain, particularly the hamstrings, lower back, and spinal erectors. It involves a controlled, weighted spinal flexion from a standing position, promoting spinal articulation and flexibility.
instructions: Begin by standing on an elevated surface with feet hip-width apart, holding a light barbell or dumbbell with both hands.
Keep your arms straight and let the weight hang in front of you.
Slowly tuck your chin to your chest and begin to roll down through your spine, vertebra by vertebra.
Allow your upper back to round as you continue to lower the weight towards the floor.
Keep your knees slightly bent and focus on maintaining control throughout the movement.
Once you reach your maximum comfortable range of motion, pause briefly.
Reverse the movement by slowly rolling up through your spine, vertebra by vertebra, until you return to the starting position.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back excessively instead of maintaining a controlled curve throughout the spine.
Bending the knees too much, reducing the stretch on the posterior chain.
Not engaging the core, leading to a lack of stability and control.
Allowing the shoulders to slump forward instead of keeping them retracted.
Using too much weight, compromising form and increasing injury risk.
Moving too quickly, which limits the effectiveness of the stretch and control.
Not maintaining a neutral neck position, causing strain on the cervical spine.
Failing to hinge at the hips, reducing the stretch on the hamstrings and lower back.
Not descending fully, limiting the range of motion and stretch benefits.
exercises.name: Jefferson Curl
tips: Start with a very light weight to ensure proper form and control.
Focus on moving slowly and deliberately to maximize spinal articulation.
Maintain a slight bend in the knees to reduce strain on the lower back.
Engage your core throughout the movement for stability.
Breathe steadily; exhale as you roll down and inhale as you roll up.
Avoid forcing the range of motion; only go as far as is comfortable.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱三头肌/jm推举

exercises.description: The JM Press is a hybrid exercise combining elements of the close-grip bench press and triceps extension, primarily targeting the triceps brachii while also engaging the chest and shoulders. To perform, lie on a flat bench holding a barbell with a narrow grip, lower the bar to your chest, then press it upward while keeping the elbows tucked close to your body. This movement emphasizes triceps activation by minimizing shoulder involvement, making it effective for building arm strength and size. Maintain controlled form to avoid elbow strain and ensure optimal muscle engagement.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with a barbell positioned above your chest, using a grip slightly narrower than shoulder-width.
Unrack the barbell and hold it steady with your arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly towards the middle of your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body to engage the triceps.
Pause briefly when the barbell is just above your chest, maintaining control and tension.
Press the barbell upward by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straightened again.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining proper form throughout.
After completing your set, carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench supports.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to flare out excessively, reducing triceps engagement and increasing shoulder strain
Lowering the bar too far behind the head, causing undue stress on the shoulder joint
Using a grip that is too wide, which shifts focus away from the triceps and compromises control
Failing to keep the wrists straight, leading to unnecessary wrist strain
Dropping the bar quickly instead of controlling the descent, reducing muscle activation and increasing injury risk
Not maintaining a stable scapular position, which decreases pressing power and shoulder stability
Extending the elbows too early during the lowering phase, reducing tension on the triceps
Allowing the bar path to drift forward or backward, compromising joint alignment and muscle engagement
Using excessive weight that compromises form and control throughout the movement
exercises.name: JM Press
tips: Lie flat on a bench with a barbell or EZ curl bar, gripping it with hands shoulder-width apart.
Start by lowering the bar slowly towards your chest, aiming to touch the area between your chest and triceps.
Keep your elbows close to your body throughout the movement to emphasize triceps engagement.
Press the bar upward by extending your arms, focusing on using your triceps rather than your chest.
Maintain a controlled tempo, avoiding any bouncing or jerking motions to reduce injury risk.
Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms to prevent strain.
Ensure your feet are firmly planted on the floor to provide stability during the lift.
Breathe in while lowering the bar and exhale as you press it back up.
Start with lighter weights to master the form before progressing to heavier loads.
Use a spotter or safety equipment when lifting heavy to ensure safe execution.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱三头肌/史密斯机窄距卧推

exercises.description: Set the Smith bar just below chest height and lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar. Use a close, overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder width. Unrack the bar and lower it under control toward the upper chest or chin area by bending the elbows while keeping them angled forward. Stop when the forearms approach the biceps, then extend the elbows to press the bar back to the start. Keep your shoulders pinned to the bench, wrists neutral, and avoid flaring the elbows.
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar just below chest level and position a flat bench underneath it so the bar will travel over your upper chest and lower face area.
Lie flat on the bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor, your head supported, and your upper back and glutes in contact with the bench.
Grip the bar with a shoulder-width or slightly narrower overhand grip, keeping your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms.
Unrack the bar and hold it above your upper chest with your elbows angled forward rather than flared directly to the sides.
Lower the bar slowly by bending your elbows and allowing them to travel forward, bringing the bar toward the area between your upper chest and chin.
Keep your upper arms relatively close to your torso and stop the descent when your forearms are near vertical and you feel a strong triceps stretch without shoulder discomfort.
Press the bar back up by extending your elbows, following the Smith machine’s fixed path while keeping your wrists neutral and elbows controlled.
Finish with your arms nearly straight without aggressively locking the elbows, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
After the final repetition, fully extend your arms and rotate the bar into the Smith machine safety hooks before releasing your grip.
mistakes: Setting the bench too far forward or backward so the bar path does not align over the upper chest and shoulders
Using a grip that is too wide, turning the movement into a standard bench press
Flaring the elbows out to the sides instead of keeping them slightly tucked and pointed forward
Lowering the bar to the mid-chest or abdomen rather than toward the upper chest and chin area
Letting the elbows drift too far behind the bar at the bottom, reducing triceps tension
Turning the movement into a pure skull crusher by bending the elbows excessively while keeping the upper arms fixed
Dropping the bar quickly and bouncing it off the chest
Losing wrist alignment and allowing the wrists to bend backward under the bar
Lifting the shoulders off the bench or shrugging them forward during the press
Using excessive load that shortens the range of motion and causes the elbows to flare
Locking out aggressively and losing control of the bar at the top
Allowing the hips to rise off the bench to compensate for insufficient triceps strength
exercises.name: JM Press on Smith
tips: Set the Smith bar just below arm’s length when lying on the bench, and position the bench so the bar travels over your upper chest and chin area rather than directly over your forehead.
Use a close, comfortable grip with hands roughly shoulder-width apart or slightly narrower; avoid an extremely narrow grip that causes wrist discomfort.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down against the bench, maintain a small natural arch in the lower back, and keep both feet firmly planted on the floor.
Start with the bar above the upper chest with elbows nearly locked, then bend mainly at the elbows while allowing them to travel slightly forward rather than flaring wide to the sides.
Lower the bar in a controlled path toward the area between your upper chest and chin, aiming to create a deep triceps stretch without letting the shoulders roll forward.
Keep your wrists stacked over your forearms and avoid letting the hands bend backward under the bar.
Press the bar back up by extending the elbows and contracting the triceps, while keeping the upper arms relatively fixed and avoiding a large chest press motion.
Do not bounce the bar off the chest or lower it onto the neck; use a smooth, deliberate tempo and stop the descent if shoulder, elbow, or wrist pain appears.
Use the Smith machine safety stops at an appropriate height, especially when learning the movement or training close to failure.
Begin with a lighter load than you would use for a close-grip bench press, as the JM press places substantial stress on the elbows and requires precise control.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/原地慢跑

exercises.description: Jog lightly on the spot with low knee lifts and small alternating steps. Keep your torso upright and swing your bent arms naturally beside your body as each foot lands softly on the forefoot. Maintain an even rhythm and steady breathing for the planned time, then slow down to finish.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed by your sides, and your gaze forward.
Increase your pace into a light jog, landing softly on the balls of your feet and keeping your steps quick and controlled.
Keep your chest lifted, shoulders relaxed, and core gently braced so your torso stays upright without leaning forward or backward.
Lift your knees only slightly, keeping the steps small.
Swing your arms close to your body, with your elbows bent, to help maintain rhythm and balance.
Breathe steadily throughout the movement, using a pace that allows you to stay in control.
Continue for the planned time, then slow to a march before stopping.
mistakes: Letting the knees collapse inward while lifting or landing
Leaning too far forward or backward instead of keeping the torso tall
Lifting the knees too high and turning the movement into high knees
Barely lifting the feet and shuffling instead of using a light running motion
Looking down and rounding the upper back
Letting the hips drop or the core relax, causing excessive side-to-side movement
Moving too fast before establishing a controlled rhythm
exercises.name: Jogging in Place
tips: Swing your arms naturally at your sides, with elbows bent around 90 degrees.
Land softly with quiet steps and let your heels lower naturally if that feels comfortable.
Start with short intervals and increase their duration gradually.
Breathe steadily, using a rhythm you can maintain without tightening your shoulders or holding your breath.
Use a stable, clear surface and wear supportive shoes, especially for longer intervals.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/跳绳

exercises.description: Jump rope is a cardiovascular exercise that involves jumping over a swinging rope. It enhances coordination, agility, and cardiovascular endurance. This exercise can be performed at varying intensities and is effective for burning calories and improving overall fitness.
instructions: Choose a rope of appropriate length; when you stand on the middle of the rope, the handles should reach your armpits.
Hold the handles with a firm grip, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Stand with your feet together on a flat surface, maintaining an upright posture.
Swing the rope over your head using your wrists, not your arms.
Jump off the ground just enough to clear the rope, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Maintain a steady rhythm and keep your jumps consistent in height and speed.
mistakes: Jumping too high, leading to unnecessary fatigue and reduced control.
Using arms excessively instead of wrists to turn the rope.
Keeping shoulders tense, causing fatigue and inefficient movement.
Landing heavily on heels instead of the balls of the feet.
Failing to maintain a consistent rhythm, disrupting coordination.
Holding the rope handles too tightly, causing tension in arms.
Not engaging core muscles, leading to poor posture and balance.
Allowing the rope to hit the ground too far in front or behind.
Jumping with knees locked, increasing impact and injury risk.
Looking down at feet, causing neck strain and poor alignment.
exercises.name: Jump Rope
tips: Start with short sessions to build endurance and gradually increase duration as you become more comfortable.
Focus on wrist movement rather than arm movement to conserve energy and maintain control.
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Wear supportive athletic shoes to cushion your feet and reduce impact stress.
Practice different footwork patterns like alternating feet or high knees to add variety and challenge.
Ensure you have enough space around you to avoid tripping or hitting obstacles with the rope.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/跳跃深蹲

exercises.description: A bodyweight squat that ends in a jump: you squat down, then drive up explosively so your feet leave the floor. It builds power in the quads, glutes and calves and raises your heart rate, so it works both as a plyometric drill and as conditioning.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Push your hips back and bend your knees until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Keep your chest up and your knees in line with your toes.
From the bottom, drive through your feet and extend your hips, knees and ankles to jump straight up.
Let your arms swing down to your sides as you leave the floor.
Land softly from the balls of your feet to your heels, with your knees bent to absorb the impact.
Bring your hands back to your chest and sink straight into the next squat.
mistakes: Landing with knees caving inward, increasing knee joint stress.
Not keeping the chest up, leading to poor posture and potential lower back strain.
Failing to engage core muscles, reducing stability and control.
Jumping without fully extending the hips, limiting power output.
Landing on toes instead of the whole foot, decreasing balance and increasing ankle strain.
Not bending knees enough during the squat phase, reducing range of motion.
Allowing heels to lift off the ground during the squat, leading to instability.
Using momentum instead of controlled muscle engagement, reducing effectiveness.
exercises.name: Jump Squat
tips: Warm up your ankles, knees and hips before you start jumping.
Land as quietly as you can. A loud landing means your legs are not absorbing the impact.
Keep your gaze forward and your chest up through the whole rep.
Jump straight up so you land on the same spot you took off from.
Use the arm swing to add height to the jump.
If you're new to jumping, start with small jumps and a short reset between reps.
End the set when your jumps get noticeably lower or your landings get sloppy.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/开合跳

exercises.description: Jumping Jacks are a full-body cardiovascular exercise that increases heart rate, improves endurance, and enhances coordination. This plyometric movement involves jumping to a position with legs spread wide and arms raised overhead, then returning to the starting position.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet together and arms at your sides.
Bend your knees slightly and jump into the air.
As you jump, spread your legs shoulder-width apart and raise your arms above your head.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent to absorb impact.
Quickly jump back to the starting position by bringing your feet together and lowering your arms to your sides.
Repeat the movement continuously at a steady pace.
mistakes: Feet landing too far apart or too close together, disrupting balance.
Arms not fully extending overhead, reducing shoulder engagement.
Bouncing on toes instead of landing softly on the entire foot, increasing impact.
Knees not slightly bent upon landing, leading to joint stress.
Arms crossing in front of the body, causing shoulder strain.
Core not engaged, resulting in poor posture and stability.
Head and neck jutting forward, leading to potential neck strain.
Inconsistent rhythm, affecting coordination and control.
exercises.name: Jumping Jacks
tips: Maintain a consistent pace to keep your heart rate elevated.
Engage your core throughout the exercise for better stability.
Land softly to reduce impact on your joints.
Keep your knees slightly bent during landings to avoid injury.
Focus on controlled breathing: inhale as you jump out, exhale as you return.
Use a mirror or video yourself to ensure proper form and alignment.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/跳跃弓步蹲

exercises.description: A bodyweight plyometric lunge. From a split stance you jump straight up, switch legs in the air and land in a lunge with the other foot in front, then go straight into the next jump. It builds power in the quadriceps, glutes and calves and trains balance and landing control.
instructions: Stand in a split stance with one foot forward and the back heel raised, feet about hip-width apart side to side. Brace your core.
Lower until your back knee is just above the floor and your front thigh is about parallel to it. Keep your torso upright.
Push hard through the whole front foot and the ball of the back foot and jump straight up, swinging your arms in opposition.
Switch legs in the air so the back foot comes forward and the front foot goes back.
Land softly in a lunge with the other foot in front, bending both knees to absorb the impact.
Go straight into the next jump and keep alternating legs until the set is done.
mistakes: Letting the front knee cave inward on landing or takeoff.
Landing on stiff, straight legs instead of bending the knees to absorb the impact.
Jumping forward and drifting across the floor instead of straight up.
Dipping only slightly between jumps, with the back knee far from the floor.
Letting the front heel lift in the bottom position, which shifts the load onto the knee.
Leaning the torso far forward or arching the lower back.
Twisting the hips or letting one hip drop as the legs switch.
exercises.name: Jumping Lunge
tips: Swing your arms in opposition to your legs, as when running, to gain height and keep the rhythm.
Treat each landing as the start of the next rep: absorb it in the lunge and jump again without a pause.
Keep your feet about hip-width apart side to side on every landing, as if on two rails, not on one line.
Start with low jumps at a slower pace and add height and speed only when every landing is stable.
If you cannot control the landing yet, build up with regular lunges or split squats first.
Breathe out as you jump and breathe in as you sink into the lunge.

exercises.description: The KAS Glute Bridge is an exercise focused on strengthening the gluteal muscles. It differs from the hip thrust mainly in the range of motion and execution technique. In the KAS Glute Bridge, the movement is more controlled and limited, allowing for greater focus on glute activation. The exercise is performed on an elevated surface, similar to the hip thrust, but with a smaller range of motion. The name 'KAS' comes from Kasemira 'Kass' Loxley, a personal trainer who popularized this version of the glute bridge.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your back against a bench or elevated surface, knees bent, feet flat on the ground.
Place a barbell over your hips, holding it with both hands.
Engage your glutes and lift your hips upward until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Pause at the top for a moment, focusing on squeezing your glutes.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position, controlling the movement.
mistakes: Feet placed too far from the glutes, reducing activation and engagement.
Allowing the knees to collapse inward, leading to poor alignment and reduced glute activation.
Hyperextending the lower back instead of lifting through the hips, increasing the risk of lower back strain.
Not maintaining a neutral spine, which can lead to unnecessary stress on the back.
Raising the hips too high, causing the lower back to arch excessively.
Failing to engage the core, resulting in instability and reduced effectiveness.
Using momentum to lift the hips instead of controlled muscle engagement.
Not squeezing the glutes at the top of the movement, minimizing activation.
Feet positioned too wide apart, which can reduce glute engagement.
Allowing the head and neck to lift off the ground, causing strain.
exercises.name: KAS Glute Bridge
tips: Ensure your feet are hip-width apart to maintain stability.
Control the movement during both lifting and lowering phases to maximize glute engagement.
Avoid lifting hips too high. Focus on muscle tension rather than height.
Breathe regularly: inhale while lowering and exhale while lifting your hips.
If you're a beginner, start without added weight to master the technique.
Focus on keeping your shoulder blades stable on the elevated surface throughout the exercise.
Avoid excessive arching of the lower back. Keep your spine in a neutral position.

exercises.description: The Katana Triceps Extension is an isolation exercise targeting the triceps brachii, particularly focusing on the long head. This exercise is performed using a cable machine with a rope attachment, allowing for a full range of motion and continuous tension on the triceps.
instructions: Attach a rope handle to the high pulley of a cable machine.
Stand facing away from the machine, holding the rope with both hands above your head, elbows bent and close to your ears.
Step forward slightly to create tension in the cable.
Extend your arms fully by straightening your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out instead of staying close to the head, reducing triceps engagement.
Using momentum to swing the weights instead of controlled movements, leading to poor muscle activation.
Arching the lower back excessively, which can strain the spine.
Allowing the wrists to bend, causing unnecessary stress on the joints.
Not extending the arms fully, limiting the range of motion and effectiveness.
Failing to keep the core engaged, leading to instability and reduced power.
Rushing through repetitions, which compromises form and control.
exercises.name: Katana Triceps Extension
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and prevent arching of the lower back.
Focus on moving only your forearms; keep your upper arms stationary throughout the exercise.
Use a controlled motion to avoid using momentum, which reduces effectiveness.
Ensure that your elbows remain close to your head during the entire movement.
Start with a lighter weight to perfect your form before increasing resistance.
Exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you return to the starting position.

exercises.description: The Kettlebell Around the Head Rotation is a dynamic exercise that targets the shoulders, core, and upper back. It involves rotating a kettlebell around your head in a controlled manner, enhancing shoulder mobility and stability while engaging the core muscles.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell with both hands in front of you at chest level.
Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Lift the kettlebell over your head, starting to rotate it around your head in a clockwise direction.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled, ensuring the kettlebell stays close to your head.
Complete the rotation by bringing the kettlebell back to the starting position in front of your chest.
Repeat the movement in a counterclockwise direction.
Perform the desired number of repetitions for each direction.
mistakes: Using too heavy a kettlebell, compromising control and form.
Allowing the elbows to flare out excessively, reducing shoulder engagement.
Failing to keep the core engaged, leading to unnecessary lower back strain.
Rotating the head instead of the kettlebell, reducing exercise effectiveness.
Not maintaining a steady pace, causing jerky and uncontrolled movements.
Holding the kettlebell too far from the head, increasing shoulder strain.
Neglecting to keep a neutral spine, risking neck and back discomfort.
Rushing through the movement, reducing focus on muscle engagement.
Gripping the kettlebell too tightly, causing forearm fatigue.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Around the Head Rotation
tips: Maintain a tight core throughout the exercise to stabilize your body.
Keep your elbows slightly bent to reduce strain on the joints.
Focus on smooth, controlled movements rather than speed.
Ensure that the kettlebell remains close to your head to maximize shoulder engagement.
Breathe steadily and avoid holding your breath during the rotation.
Start with a lighter kettlebell to master the technique before progressing to heavier weights.
