exercises.description: The Kettlebell Biceps Curl is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps brachii. It involves lifting a kettlebell with a controlled motion to engage the biceps, promoting muscle strength and hypertrophy. This exercise can be performed standing or seated and is suitable for various fitness levels.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your palms facing forward.
Exhale as you curl the kettlebells upward by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue lifting until the kettlebells are at shoulder level and your biceps are fully contracted.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then inhale as you slowly lower the kettlebells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using excessive weight, leading to poor form and momentum-driven lifts.
Swinging the kettlebell instead of maintaining controlled, smooth movements.
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom of the curl, limiting the range of motion.
Curling the wrists at the top of the movement, causing unnecessary strain.
Engaging the shoulders and upper back instead of isolating the biceps.
Leaning back or using the lower back to assist the lift, risking strain.
Allowing the elbows to drift forward, reducing biceps activation.
Rushing through the exercise, compromising muscle engagement and control.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Biceps Curl
tips: Maintain a straight posture throughout the exercise to avoid using momentum.
Focus on squeezing the biceps at the top of the curl for maximum contraction.
Control the descent of the kettlebells to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid swinging or using your back to lift the weights; keep the movement isolated to your arms.
Start with a lighter weight to perfect your form before progressing to heavier kettlebells.

exercises.description: The Kettlebell Clean is a dynamic exercise that involves lifting a kettlebell from the ground to the rack position in one fluid motion. It is designed to improve strength, power, and coordination, primarily targeting the posterior chain, shoulders, and core muscles.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a kettlebell between your feet.
Bend at the hips and knees to grip the kettlebell handle with one hand, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Engage your core and drive through your heels to lift the kettlebell off the ground.
As the kettlebell rises, pull it close to your body by bending your elbow and rotating your wrist.
Quickly tuck your elbow into your side and allow the kettlebell to rotate around your forearm into the rack position.
Stand tall with the kettlebell resting on the outside of your forearm, elbow close to your body.
Reverse the motion to lower the kettlebell back to the starting position.
mistakes: Swinging the kettlebell out and away from the body, causing an uncontrolled arc.
Over-gripping the handle, leading to excessive wrist flexion and strain.
Failing to keep the elbow close to the body during the clean, resulting in inefficient movement.
Allowing the kettlebell to crash onto the forearm, causing discomfort and potential bruising.
Not engaging the core, leading to instability and poor control of the movement.
Using the arms to lift the kettlebell instead of driving through the hips and legs.
Standing too upright during the initial pull, reducing power generation.
Neglecting to align the wrist in a neutral position at the rack, causing joint stress.
Rushing the transition phase, leading to a lack of control and precision.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the movement to maintain stability.
Use a smooth, controlled motion to bring the kettlebell into the rack position.
Avoid swinging the kettlebell away from your body; keep it close during the lift.
Practice with a lighter weight to master form before progressing to heavier kettlebells.
Ensure that your wrist remains neutral in the rack position to prevent strain.
Focus on driving through your heels during the initial lift for maximum power.

exercises.description: The Kettlebell Clean and Jerk is a dynamic, full-body exercise that combines strength, power, and endurance. It involves lifting a kettlebell from the ground to the shoulder (clean) and then pressing it overhead (jerk). This exercise targets multiple muscle groups including the shoulders, legs, core, and back, making it an effective compound movement for building functional strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a kettlebell between your feet.
Bend at the hips and knees to grip the kettlebell with one hand, keeping your back straight.
Drive through your heels to lift the kettlebell off the ground, extending your hips and knees explosively.
As the kettlebell rises, pull it close to your body and rotate your wrist to bring it to shoulder height in a rack position.
Once stabilized, dip slightly by bending your knees and then drive through your legs to press the kettlebell overhead.
Lock out your arm at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbow is straight and bicep is close to your ear.
Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position at your shoulder before returning it to the ground with control.
mistakes: Using too much arm strength instead of driving with the hips.
Failing to keep the kettlebell close to the body during the clean.
Allowing the kettlebell to crash onto the forearm during the catch.
Not fully extending the hips and knees during the drive phase.
Pressing the kettlebell overhead with a bent elbow.
Not engaging the core to stabilize the movement.
Overarching the lower back during the jerk phase.
Allowing the knees to cave in during the dip and drive.
Not maintaining a neutral wrist position when holding the kettlebell.
Rushing the transition between the clean and jerk phases.
Losing balance by not distributing weight evenly on the feet.
Failing to lock out the elbow and shoulder at the top of the jerk.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean and Jerk
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the movement to maintain stability and protect your lower back.
Focus on using your hips for power during the clean phase rather than relying solely on your arm strength.
Ensure a smooth transition from clean to jerk by maintaining balance and control in the rack position.
Practice proper breathing: inhale before lifting, exhale during exertion as you press overhead.
Start with a lighter kettlebell to master technique before progressing to heavier weights.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the exercise to prevent injury.

exercises.description: The Kettlebell Deadlift is a compound exercise targeting the posterior chain, including the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back. It involves lifting a kettlebell from the ground to a standing position using proper hip hinge mechanics.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and place a kettlebell between your feet.
Hinge at the hips by pushing them back while keeping your back straight and chest up.
Grip the kettlebell handle with both hands, ensuring your shoulders are above or slightly in front of the kettlebell.
Engage your core and drive through your heels to lift the kettlebell, extending your hips and knees simultaneously.
Stand fully upright with the kettlebell in front of your thighs, keeping your shoulders back and chest proud.
Reverse the movement by hinging at the hips and lowering the kettlebell back to the ground with control.
mistakes: Rounding the back instead of maintaining a neutral spine.
Allowing the knees to cave inward during the lift.
Starting with the kettlebell too far from the body.
Lifting with the arms instead of driving through the hips.
Not engaging the core throughout the movement.
Pulling the kettlebell up with the shoulders instead of using hip extension.
Standing too narrow or too wide, affecting balance and power.
Bending the knees excessively, turning the deadlift into a squat.
Failing to lock out the hips at the top of the lift.
Dropping the kettlebell instead of controlling the descent.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Deadlift
tips: Keep your spine neutral throughout the movement to avoid injury.
Focus on driving through your heels to engage the posterior chain effectively.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees but avoid excessive squatting motion.
Ensure the kettlebell stays close to your body during the lift for better leverage.
Practice with lighter weights initially to master form before progressing to heavier loads.
Breathe in as you lower the kettlebell and exhale as you lift it.

exercises.description: The Kettlebell Sumo Squat is a lower-body exercise targeting the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and inner thighs. It involves holding a kettlebell with both hands while performing a squat with a wide stance, similar to a sumo wrestler's stance. This exercise helps improve strength, stability, and flexibility in the lower body.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and toes slightly pointed out.
Hold a kettlebell with both hands in front of you, allowing it to hang between your legs.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to lower your body by bending at the hips and knees.
Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as your flexibility allows.
Ensure your knees are tracking over your toes and not caving inward.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, straightening your legs and keeping your back upright.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Holding the kettlebell too far from the chest, causing instability.
Allowing knees to collapse inward during the squat, leading to poor alignment.
Squatting too shallow, not reaching a parallel or deeper position.
Rounding the back instead of maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Failing to engage the core, resulting in loss of control and balance.
Rising onto the toes instead of keeping heels grounded.
Letting the elbows flare out excessively, reducing upper body engagement.
Dropping the kettlebell too low, which can affect posture and balance.
Not controlling the descent, leading to a rapid drop and potential strain.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders during the squat.
Focus on engaging your core throughout the movement for better stability.
Make sure to keep the weight distributed evenly across both feet.
Control the movement on the way down to prevent dropping too quickly into the squat.
Breathe in as you lower into the squat and exhale as you push back up to standing.
Adjust the width of your stance if necessary to ensure comfort and proper form.

exercises.description: Stand over two kettlebells in a wide stance and hinge forward with your knees slightly bent. Row one bell toward your hip while the other stays on the floor to support you, then lower it and switch arms. Keep your torso steady and maintain the bent-over position as you alternate sides.
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the floor between your feet. Stand with a wide stance, toes slightly turned out.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees until you can reach both kettlebell handles. Keep your chest open, spine neutral, and neck in line with your back.
Grip both handles with your arms straight. Brace your core and keep your weight balanced through your whole feet.
Pull one kettlebell toward the side of your ribcage by driving your elbow back. Keep your shoulder down and avoid twisting your torso.
Lower the kettlebell under control until your arm is straight again.
Row the other kettlebell to your ribcage in the same way.
Continue alternating sides while maintaining a stable hip hinge, a flat back, and controlled movement. Finish the set by placing both kettlebells on the floor before standing up.
mistakes: Letting the hips rotate or shift side to side as one kettlebell is pulled.
Shrugging the working shoulder toward the ear instead of keeping it down and back.
Flaring the elbow far out to the side instead of rowing it close to the ribs.
Using momentum or twisting the torso to lift the kettlebell.
Letting the non-working kettlebell hang without control or losing tension through the supporting side.
Dropping the kettlebell quickly instead of lowering it under control.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Gorilla Row
tips: Set two kettlebells on the floor between your feet. Stand with a wide stance, hinge at the hips, and bend your knees enough to reach the handles without rounding your lower back.
Keep your chest long, spine neutral, and neck in line with your back. Look slightly ahead of your hands rather than cranking your head up.
Brace your abs before each pull as if preparing to take a punch. Maintain this brace throughout the set.
Pause briefly at the top and feel the upper back contract.
Use two kettlebells of equal weight so both arms work with the same load.

instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a kettlebell in one hand with an overhand grip, positioning it close to your chest.
Extend your free arm out to the side for balance.
Press the kettlebell upward until your arm is fully extended, keeping your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your shoulder remains stable.
Slowly lower the kettlebell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.
mistakes: Allowing the shoulder to lift off the floor, reducing stability and control.
Failing to keep the wrist straight, leading to loss of control over the kettlebell.
Not engaging the core, resulting in a lack of support and potential imbalance.
Using too heavy a kettlebell, compromising form and increasing strain on the shoulder.
Allowing the elbow to flare out excessively, putting undue stress on the shoulder joint.
Not maintaining a neutral spine, which can lead to poor posture and reduced effectiveness.
Rushing through the movement, sacrificing control and precision.
Neglecting to keep the feet planted firmly on the floor, reducing overall stability.
Lowering the kettlebell too quickly, risking loss of control and potential injury.
exercises.name: Kettlebell One Arm Floor Press
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability.
Ensure your elbow is at a 45-degree angle to your body during the press to protect your shoulder joint.
Focus on a controlled movement, especially during the lowering phase, to maximize muscle engagement.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form for all repetitions.
If you're new to this exercise, start with a lighter kettlebell to master the technique before increasing weight.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain and ensure effective force transfer.

exercises.description: The Kettlebell Rear Lunge is a compound exercise that targets the lower body, particularly the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and calves. It also engages the core for stability. This exercise involves stepping backward into a lunge position while holding a kettlebell, which adds resistance and challenges balance.
instructions: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height or with both hands in front of your chest.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Step back with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees. The front knee should be directly above the ankle.
Ensure the back knee hovers just above the ground without touching it.
Push through the heel of the front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
mistakes: Allowing the front knee to cave inward, reducing stability and increasing stress on the knee joint.
Holding the kettlebell too far from the body, causing imbalance and unnecessary strain on the shoulders.
Stepping back too shallow, limiting range of motion and muscle engagement.
Failing to keep the chest up, leading to a rounded back and poor posture.
Not engaging the core, resulting in a lack of stability and control.
Letting the back knee touch the ground, which can lead to loss of control and potential injury.
Pushing off the toes of the back foot instead of using the heel of the front foot, reducing power and effectiveness.
Rushing through the movement without proper control, increasing the risk of losing balance.
Allowing the kettlebell to swing excessively, which can disrupt balance and form.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Rear Lunge
tips: Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement to protect your lower back.
Focus on keeping your core engaged to improve balance and stability.
Ensure that your front knee does not extend past your toes to prevent strain on the knee joint.
Use a controlled motion when stepping back and returning to the starting position to maximize muscle engagement.
Start with a lighter kettlebell if you're new to this exercise to master proper form before increasing weight.

exercises.description: The Kettlebell Renegade Row is a compound exercise that targets the back, shoulders, arms, and core. It combines a plank position with a rowing motion, enhancing stability and strength. This exercise is effective for improving balance and coordination while building upper body and core strength.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with a kettlebell in each hand, wrists aligned under your shoulders, and feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart for stability.
Engage your core to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Shift your weight slightly to one side and row the kettlebell on the opposite side towards your hip, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Lower the kettlebell back to the ground with control.
Repeat the movement on the other side, alternating rows while maintaining plank position throughout.
mistakes: Allowing the hips to sag or rotate, losing core stability.
Rowing the kettlebell with the shoulder instead of engaging the back muscles.
Not maintaining a neutral spine, leading to excessive arching or rounding.
Using momentum to lift the kettlebell instead of controlled muscle engagement.
Feet positioned too close together, reducing balance and stability.
Failing to keep the wrist straight, causing strain on the joint.
Not fully extending the arm during the row, limiting range of motion.
Letting the elbow flare out instead of keeping it close to the body.
Rushing the movement, compromising form and control.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Renegade Row
tips: Keep your hips as stable as possible to avoid rocking side to side during the row.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the row for maximum engagement.
Maintain a neutral spine by keeping your head in line with your body and avoiding arching or rounding your back.
If you're new to this exercise, start with lighter kettlebells to ensure proper form before progressing to heavier weights.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you row the kettlebell up and inhaling as you lower it down.

exercises.description: The kettlebell snatch is a one-arm ballistic lift that takes the bell from a backswing between your legs to lockout overhead in one continuous movement. A hard hip drive does most of the work while the arm guides the bell close to your body. It trains the glutes, hamstrings, back and shoulders and builds power and conditioning.
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and the kettlebell on the floor a short step in front of you.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back, grip the handle with one hand and hike the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward and stand up hard so the kettlebell floats up close to your body.
As it rises, let your elbow bend and travel up, then punch your hand through the handle at head height so the bell rolls onto the back of your forearm.
Lock out with your arm straight overhead, biceps by your ear, wrist straight and the bell over your shoulder.
Hold for a moment with your ribs down and glutes tight, keeping the free arm relaxed at your side.
Let the bell fall in front of you, close to your body, and hinge only when it reaches your hips, swinging it back between your legs.
Go straight into the next rep, finish the set, then switch arms.
mistakes: Squatting the kettlebell down instead of hinging at the hips.
Lifting the bell with your arm instead of driving it up with the hips.
Swinging the bell out in a wide arc instead of keeping it close to your body.
Letting the bell flip over and bang into your forearm at the top.
Finishing with a bent elbow or with the bell in front of your head instead of over your shoulder.
Bending the wrist back under the bell at lockout.
Leaning back and arching the lower back at the top.
Rounding your back in the backswing.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Snatch
tips: Learn the one-arm swing and the high pull first, then combine them into the snatch.
Pick a kettlebell you can lock out overhead without having to press it up at the end.
Exhale sharply as your hips snap forward and breathe in as the bell drops.
Keep your grip relaxed in the fingers on the way up and down and squeeze only at the top to spare the skin on your palm.
At the top, pull your shoulder down and away from your ear.
Clear the space around and above you before the set.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/壶铃摆动

exercises.description: The kettlebell swing is a dynamic, full-body exercise that primarily targets the posterior chain, including the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back. It also engages the core and shoulders, providing both strength and cardiovascular benefits. This exercise involves swinging a kettlebell from between the legs to shoulder height using a hip hinge motion.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out, and a kettlebell placed about a foot in front of you.
Hinge at the hips by pushing your butt back while maintaining a slight bend in the knees. Keep your back straight and chest up.
Grip the kettlebell handle with both hands using an overhand grip.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs, keeping it close to your groin.
Drive your hips forward explosively to swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height. Your arms should remain straight but relaxed.
Let the kettlebell fall back down naturally as you hinge at the hips again to repeat the motion.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout.
mistakes: Using the arms to lift the kettlebell instead of driving the movement with the hips.
Rounding the back instead of maintaining a neutral spine throughout the swing.
Squatting instead of hinging at the hips, which reduces power and can strain the knees.
Letting the kettlebell swing too low or too high, leading to loss of control and balance.
Failing to engage the core, resulting in reduced stability and potential lower back strain.
Standing too upright at the top of the swing, preventing full hip extension.
Allowing the knees to cave inwards, which can lead to knee discomfort or injury.
Gripping the kettlebell too tightly, causing unnecessary tension in the forearms.
Not using the glutes to drive the movement, leading to decreased power and efficiency.
exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
tips: Focus on using your hips to generate power rather than lifting with your arms.
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement to protect your lower back.
Ensure that your shoulders remain relaxed and do not shrug during the swing.
Maintain a neutral spine position to avoid rounding your back.
Breathe out as you swing the kettlebell up and inhale as it comes down.
Start with a lighter kettlebell to master form before progressing to heavier weights.
Keep your eyes forward and avoid looking down to maintain proper posture.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/壶铃风车式

exercises.description: The Kettlebell Windmill is a compound exercise that targets the core, shoulders, and hips. It enhances flexibility, stability, and strength, particularly in the obliques and shoulder girdle. This exercise requires balance and coordination, making it effective for improving overall functional fitness.
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Hold a kettlebell in one hand and press it overhead, keeping your arm straight.
Turn your feet approximately 45 degrees away from the arm holding the kettlebell.
Shift your weight onto the leg opposite the kettlebell and push your hip out to the side.
Keeping your eyes on the kettlebell, slowly lower your torso by bending at the hips. Your free hand should slide down your leg towards the floor.
Continue lowering until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings or until your hand reaches the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom position, then engage your core and glutes to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
mistakes: Rotating the torso instead of hinging at the hips, leading to poor form and reduced muscle engagement.
Failing to keep the kettlebell arm fully extended, which can compromise shoulder stability.
Allowing the knees to bend excessively, reducing the stretch in the hamstrings and obliques.
Not keeping the eyes on the kettlebell, which can destabilize the shoulder and affect balance.
Leaning forward instead of laterally, causing improper weight distribution and potential back strain.
Using too heavy a kettlebell, leading to compromised form and increased injury risk.
Neglecting to engage the core, resulting in a lack of stability and control throughout the movement.

exercises.description: Kneel on the ab coaster's moving pad, forearms on the arm rests, and drive your knees up toward your chest to train your lower abs against a load. You feel it most below the navel, with the whole front of your stomach and your obliques squeezed hard at the top. Your hip flexors help bring the knees through. Your torso rests on your forearms and the plate rides on the lever, so there's nothing to swing with and weight goes up in small steps. Pick it over captain's chair or hanging knee raises when you want to add load, or when your grip and shoulders quit before your abs.
instructions: Load the plate, or set the pin, while the platform rests at the bottom. Start light: the long lever makes even one plate feel heavy.
Kneel on the platform facing the arm pads, shins flat and knees at the front edge, with your feet hanging off the back.
Lean forward and lay your forearms along the pads, elbows at the back end under your shoulders, hands on the handles with palms facing in. Your torso ends up about 45° forward.
Press your forearms lightly into the pads, pull your shoulders away from your ears and keep your ribs down.
Breathe out and tuck your tailbone under first, then drive your knees forward and up toward your chest. The platform swings up with you.
Stop when your thighs are about level with your hips and your lower back has rounded. Hold for a second and squeeze your lower stomach.
Take 2–3 seconds to lower the platform to the start without letting the plate bang. After the last rep, let it settle at the bottom before you climb off.
mistakes: Throwing your knees forward from the hips and letting the plate carry the platform up. Start each rep from a dead stop at the bottom, tuck the pelvis first and take 1–2 seconds to lift.

Moving only the legs: the knees come forward but your pelvis never curls and your lower back stays arched. Think tailbone under, pubic bone toward the ribs. The rep ends when your lower back rounds, not when your knees stop.
Letting the plate drop and bounce at the bottom, or pull your thighs so far back that your lower back arches. Lower in 2–3 seconds, stop as the platform touches the rest and keep your ribs down.
Pulling on the handles and shrugging until your shoulders and arms tire before your abs. Push your forearms down into the pads and hold the handles just firmly enough to stay put.
Kneeling too far back, so your knees slide or your shins lift off the pad. Set your knees at the front edge with your shins flat before the first rep.
exercises.name: Knee Raise Ab Coaster
tips: Near the end of a session, 2–4 sets of 12–20 reps work well, or 8–12 heavier reps with a full one-second hold at the top. Add reps first: once you get 20 on all sets with a full tuck and a 2–3 second lowering, add the smallest plate (usually 2.5 kg) or one stack plate, then build the reps back up.

Because the lever is long, one small plate can feel like a big jump. If your reps fall by more than 3–4, slow the lowering or add a 2-second pause at the top before adding weight. Too hard even with no plates? Stop when your knees are about halfway to hip height, and lengthen the range as you get stronger.

Most of the work should land below your navel. If it's mostly the front of your hips or your lower back, you're swinging the knees without curling the pelvis; if it's your shoulders or arms, you're pulling on the handles.

Substitutes: Captains Chair Knee Raises (same forearm support, bodyweight only, and kinder to knees that dislike kneeling under load), Hanging Knee Raises (much harder to keep still), Reverse Crunches (on the floor, the easiest way to learn the tuck) and Weighted Hanging Leg Raise (a big step up).

Release the right knee and return to the starting position.

tips: Ensure your head and shoulders remain relaxed on the mat throughout the stretch.
Avoid pulling too hard; the movement should be gentle to prevent strain.
Focus on maintaining a steady breathing pattern to enhance relaxation.
If you feel discomfort in your lower back, reduce the range of motion.
Perform this stretch after workouts to aid in recovery and flexibility.

instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and arms at your sides.
Place your hands lightly behind your head for support, keeping elbows wide.
Engage your core by drawing your belly button towards your spine.
Simultaneously lift your knees towards your chest while curling your upper body off the ground.
Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your abs tightly.
Slowly lower back to the starting position, keeping control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Using momentum to swing the legs instead of controlled movement.
Failing to fully extend the legs out before tucking them back in.
Not keeping the chin slightly tucked, leading to neck strain.

Allowing the shoulders to remain on the ground, minimizing the crunch effect.
Holding the breath instead of maintaining a steady breathing pattern.

Keep your lower back pressed against the mat to prevent strain and ensure proper form.
Exhale as you crunch up and inhale as you return to the starting position.

Extend your left arm out in front of you, resting it on the floor for support.
Inhale deeply, then exhale as you rotate your upper body to the right, bringing your right elbow up towards the ceiling.

Inhale as you return to the starting position, then repeat on the opposite side.

exercises.description: A static hip flexor stretch in a half-kneeling position, with the back knee on the floor, the front foot planted well ahead and the hands clasped on the front knee. Relaxing the glute of the kneeling leg and letting the pelvis tip forward, which takes the stretch off the hip flexors.
Leaning the torso forward instead of keeping it upright over the hips.
Setting the front foot too close to the back knee, which leaves no room to move the hips forward.
Letting the front knee cave inward.
Twisting the pelvis or letting one hip drop instead of keeping both hips facing forward.
Bouncing or forcing the hips forward instead of settling into a steady hold.
exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
tips: Put a folded mat or pad under the back knee if the floor is hard.
Set the back knee and front foot about hip-width apart, not on one line, so you stay balanced.
Your clasped hands on the front knee give you support, so you can focus on your hips.
Move your hips forward only a little. With the pelvis tucked, a short shift is enough to feel the stretch.
Breathe out slowly and let the hip ease a little further forward with each exhale.
If you feel pinching at the front of the hip, reduce the depth and tuck the pelvis more.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/臀部/跪姿髋推

exercises.description: The kneeling hip thrust trains the glutes by moving the hips between a seated-back position and tall kneeling without added weight. Keep your hands at your chest, send your hips toward your heels with a forward torso incline, then extend your hips to return upright without leaning back.
instructions: Kneel with your knees about hip-width apart and hold your hands together in front of your chest.
Start with your hips fully extended, glutes lightly squeezed, and ribs stacked over your pelvis. Keep your head and neck neutral.
Send your hips back toward your heels, bending at the hips and allowing your torso to incline forward with a neutral spine.
Lower only as far as you can control while keeping your knees planted and your spine neutral.
Drive your hips forward by squeezing your glutes, returning to the tall kneeling position.
Finish with your hips fully extended and glutes contracted, without leaning back or arching your lower back. Repeat for the planned number of repetitions.
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of extending the hips with the glutes.
Letting the ribs flare and losing a stacked ribcage-over-pelvis position.
Failing to squeeze the glutes fully at the top.
Allowing the knees to drift apart or cave inward during the movement.
Using momentum instead of controlling the hip drive and return.
Leaning backward with a rigid torso instead of bending at the hips to sit back.
exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Thrust
tips: Exhale through the hardest part of the upward movement.
Use a mat or folded towel for comfortable support on the floor.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest as a position cue.
Use short sets that let you repeat the same movement pattern.
Rest the tops of your feet on the floor to support the kneeling base.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/跪姿背阔肌拉伸

exercises.description: This floor stretch lengthens one lat at a time with the hips above the knees and one hand supporting your weight. From all fours, slide the other hand forward and lower your chest toward the floor, then breathe into the reaching side before returning and changing arms.
instructions: Start on all fours with your knees under your hips and hands under your shoulders.
Keep one hand in place and slide the other forward along the floor.
Keep the reaching elbow straight and your hips above your knees.
Lower your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch along the reaching side.
Breathe slowly while holding a comfortable stretch.
Slide your hand back under your shoulder and repeat on the other side.
mistakes: Bending the reaching elbow and shortening the stretch.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears instead of reaching through the arms.
Letting the ribs flare and over-arching the lower back.
Rotating the torso instead of keeping both sides of the pelvis and shoulders square.
Forcing the chest too low and turning the stretch into lower-back extension.
Bouncing or repeatedly forcing deeper range instead of breathing and holding a controlled stretch.
exercises.name: Kneeling Lat Stretch
tips: Use a mat or folded towel for comfortable support on the floor.
Breathe into the ribs on the side of the reaching arm.
Keep the supporting hand under its shoulder to support your weight.
Give each side the same amount of practice.
Let the reaching hand slide rather than lifting it from the floor.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/跪姿平板支撑

exercises.description: The kneeling plank is a forearm hold with the knees on the floor and the feet lifted. Keep the shoulders, hips and knees in one line while the abdominal and glute muscles stabilize the trunk, maintaining steady breathing and a relaxed neck throughout the hold.
instructions: Kneel on the floor and place your forearms down with your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Lift your feet off the floor, keeping the knees supported.
Walk your knees back until your body forms a straight line from your head through your hips to your knees.
Tuck your pelvis slightly and squeeze your glutes to prevent your lower back from arching.
Brace your abdominal muscles as if preparing for a light punch, while keeping your ribs pulled down.
Keep your neck neutral and look at the floor slightly in front of your hands.
Hold with steady breathing, then shift your hips back to leave the position.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag below the shoulders instead of keeping a straight line from head to knees
Piking the hips too high and turning the movement into a bent-over position
Setting the elbows too far in front of or behind the shoulders
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears instead of pressing the floor away
Dropping or lifting the head instead of keeping the neck neutral
Failing to brace the abs, causing the lower back to arch
exercises.name: Kneeling Plank
tips: Use a mat or a folded towel under the knees.
Spread pressure along the forearms, not just through the elbows.
Keep the feet relaxed above the floor.
Breathe slowly in and out during the hold.
Begin with short holds and extend them as control improves.

aliases: Resistance Band Kickback on All Fours

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/臀部/跪姿弹力带臀部后踢

exercises.description: On all fours, with a loop band running from one foot to the hand on the same side, you kick that leg straight back to build your glute one side at a time. The gluteus maximus of the kicking leg does most of the work; your hamstrings help as the knee straightens, and the gluteus medius keeps your pelvis level. Unlike the Donkey Kick, the knee goes from bent to fully straight on every rep, and the band pulls hardest at the top, right where you squeeze. All you need is the band, so it works at home, as a warm-up before squats or as a high-rep finisher.
instructions: Pick a long loop band, light or medium to start. A mini band is too short to reach from your foot to your hand.
Get on all fours: hands flat under your shoulders, arms straight, knees under your hips, back flat, eyes on the floor just ahead of your hands.
Hook one end of the band around the sole of your working foot, across the arch just in front of the heel.
Pin the other end to the floor under the heel of your palm on the same side.
Slide that hand forward or back until the band is just taut with your knee down.
Brace your stomach lightly, ribs down. Lift the working knee just off the floor and drive the foot straight back as the knee straightens.
Stop when the leg is straight and in line with your body: foot at about hip height, toes pointing down, heel pushing back.
Squeeze the glute and hold for a second. Your hips stay level and square to the floor, and your lower back doesn't move.
Take about 2 seconds to bend the knee and bring it back under your hip, tap the floor lightly and go again. Finish every rep on one leg, then switch.
mistakes: Arching your lower back to get the foot higher than your body. Stop when the leg is in line with your torso, ribs down, and switch to a lighter band if the arch keeps coming back.
The hip on the working side lifts and your pelvis turns open. Keep both hip bones pointing at the floor and kick straight back, not up and out.
Finishing with a bent knee, so the band never fully stretches. Straighten the knee all the way, push the heel back and hold for a second before you return.
Letting the band snap your leg back in. Take about 2 seconds on the way back and set the knee down softly; if you can't, the band is too heavy.
Rocking your whole body back and forth to help the leg. Shoulders stay over your hands and the supporting knee under your hip; only the working leg moves.
The band slips off your foot or out from under your hand. Keep the foot flexed so the band sits across the arch, and press down with the heel of your palm, not your fingers.
exercises.name: Kneeling Resistance Band Glute Kickback
tips: Aim for 2–4 sets of 12–20 reps per leg with a one-second squeeze at the top; as a warm-up, 1–2 easy sets of 10–15 are plenty. Once both legs make 20 on every set with a locked knee and a clean hold, move to the next band and build the reps back up.
Not ready for the next band? Place the anchoring hand 5–10 cm farther forward so the band stretches more at the top, or hold the top for 2–3 seconds.
Expect the burn in the glute of the kicking leg, most during the hold, plus some work in the back of the thigh as the knee straightens. If your lower back takes over, the leg is going too high.

Sore wrists? Rest on your fists with the band pinned under them. Kneel on a mat or folded towel, and check the band for nicks before each session, because a band that tears snaps back toward your hand and arm.

Substitutes: Donkey Kick (no band, knee stays bent), Glute Cable Kickback (load you can measure and add in small steps), Band Standing Balance Glute Kickback (if kneeling bothers you), Glute Machine Kickback (for heavier loading).

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/跪姿环形俯卧撑

exercises.description: Kneeling Ring Push Ups are a bodyweight exercise that targets the chest, triceps, and shoulders. This variation uses gymnastic rings to increase instability, engaging core muscles for stabilization. Performing the exercise on your knees reduces the load, making it suitable for beginners or those focusing on form and control.
instructions: Adjust the rings so they hang just above the floor.
Kneel on a mat with your knees hip-width apart.
Grip the rings firmly with palms facing each other.
Lean forward slightly, keeping a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Lower your chest towards the rings by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
mistakes: Allowing the hips to sag, causing a loss of core engagement and improper alignment.
Flared elbows, which can lead to shoulder strain and reduced effectiveness.
Rings set too wide, resulting in excessive shoulder stress and decreased stability.
Failing to maintain a neutral spine, leading to potential back discomfort.
Inadequate range of motion by not lowering the chest close enough to the rings.
Lack of control during the descent, causing instability and poor muscle activation.
Neglecting to keep wrists neutral, increasing strain on the wrists and forearms.
Rushing the movement, which reduces time under tension and muscle engagement.
exercises.name: Kneeling Ring Push-Up
tips: Ensure the rings are stable and securely fastened before starting.
Focus on maintaining a straight line from shoulders to knees throughout the movement.
Engage your core to prevent sagging or arching of the lower back.
Keep your elbows close to your body to maximize tricep engagement.
Control the movement speed, especially when lowering yourself, to increase muscle activation.
Breathe in as you lower yourself and exhale as you push back up.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/跪姿宽距俯卧撑

exercises.description: The Kneeling Wide Hand Push Up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the chest, shoulders, and triceps. By performing this exercise on your knees with a wide hand placement, it reduces the load compared to a standard push-up, making it suitable for beginners or as a warm-up for more advanced athletes.
instructions: Start by kneeling on the floor with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your body straight from your knees to your head, engaging your core.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows outwards.
Stop when your chest is just above the ground, then push back up to the starting position.
Maintain a steady pace and controlled movement throughout the exercise.
mistakes: Hands placed too wide, reducing range of motion and increasing shoulder strain.
Elbows flaring out excessively, leading to poor shoulder engagement.
Hips sagging towards the floor, causing lower back strain.
Failing to maintain a straight line from head to knees, compromising core stability.
Not lowering the chest close enough to the ground, limiting muscle activation.
Rushing the movement, reducing control and effectiveness.
Allowing the head to drop, causing neck strain.
Neglecting to engage the core, leading to a loss of balance and form.
Pushing through the wrists instead of distributing weight evenly through the hands.
exercises.name: Kneeling Wide Push-Up
tips: Ensure your hands are placed wider than shoulder-width to target the chest effectively.
Engage your core to maintain a straight line from knees to head.
Focus on controlled movements; avoid letting gravity do the work during the descent.
Keep elbows slightly bent at the top of the movement to maintain tension in the muscles.
Breathe in as you lower your body and exhale as you push back up.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/拳面俯卧撑

exercises.description: Knuckle Push Ups are a variation of the traditional push-up performed on the knuckles instead of the palms. This exercise targets the chest, triceps, shoulders, and core while also strengthening the wrists and forearms. It is often used in martial arts training to improve punching power and wrist stability.
instructions: Begin in a standard push-up position with your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Place your fists on the ground shoulder-width apart, with your knuckles facing down.
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your body as you lower yourself towards the ground.
Lower your chest until it is just above the ground, keeping your body straight.
Push through your knuckles to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing the wrists to collapse inward or outward, compromising stability and increasing strain on the joints.
Failing to maintain a straight line from head to heels, leading to sagging hips or a raised rear, which reduces core engagement.
Positioning the hands too wide or too narrow, affecting shoulder and chest muscle activation.
Not fully extending the elbows at the top of the movement, limiting the range of motion and muscle engagement.
Dropping the head, which strains the neck and disrupts spinal alignment.
Rushing through repetitions, sacrificing form and control for speed.
Neglecting to engage the core, resulting in a lack of stability and increased risk of lower back strain.
Bending the fingers instead of keeping them straight, reducing the effectiveness of the exercise.
exercises.name: Knuckle Push-Up
tips: Ensure that your wrists are aligned with your forearms to avoid strain.
Keep your core tight throughout the movement to maintain proper form.
If you're new to this exercise, start on a softer surface to reduce stress on the knuckles.
Focus on controlled movements rather than speed to maximize muscle engagement.
Breathe in as you lower yourself and exhale as you push back up.
If you experience discomfort in your wrists, try adjusting the position of your fists or consider using push-up bars.

exercises.description: The Korean Dip is an advanced bodyweight exercise that targets the triceps, shoulders, and chest. It involves a unique movement pattern that requires significant upper body strength and stability. This exercise is typically performed on parallel bars and is known for its dynamic transition from a dip to a horizontal hold.
instructions: Begin by positioning yourself between parallel bars, gripping them firmly with your palms facing inward.
Lift your body off the ground by straightening your arms, ensuring your shoulders are directly above your wrists.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
As you reach the bottom of the dip, lean forward and extend your legs behind you, transitioning into a horizontal position.
Hold this position briefly, engaging your core and maintaining a straight line from head to heels.
Return to the starting position by reversing the movement, bringing your legs back under you and pushing up through your arms.
mistakes: Failing to maintain a straight body line, leading to excessive arching or sagging.
Allowing the shoulders to roll forward, reducing scapular engagement.
Dropping too quickly into the dip without controlled descent.
Not achieving full range of motion by stopping too high or going too low.
Neglecting to keep elbows close to the body, causing flaring.
Using momentum instead of muscle strength to push back up.
Inadequate core engagement, leading to instability.
Overextending the neck by looking up or down instead of keeping it neutral.
exercises.name: Korean Dip
tips: Focus on maintaining control throughout the movement to prevent swinging.
Engage your core muscles to stabilize your body during the transition phase.
Keep your elbows close to your body to maximize tricep engagement.
Practice on lower bars initially if you're new to this exercise to build confidence and strength.
Ensure proper warm-up of shoulders and wrists before attempting the Korean Dip to reduce injury risk.

exercises.description: The L Pull-Up is an advanced bodyweight exercise that combines a pull-up with an isometric hold in an L-sit position. This exercise targets the upper back, biceps, core, and hip flexors, demanding significant strength and stability.
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and lift your legs to form a 90-degree angle at the hips, creating an 'L' shape with your body.
Keep your legs straight and parallel to the ground throughout the movement.
Pull yourself up by engaging your back and biceps until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner while maintaining the L-sit position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Swinging the legs instead of maintaining a static L position, reducing core engagement.
Failing to keep the legs parallel to the ground, compromising the L shape.
Using momentum to initiate the pull, leading to less muscle activation.
Allowing the shoulders to shrug, which can strain the neck and upper back.
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom, limiting range of motion.
Arching the back excessively, which can lead to improper form and potential lower back strain.
Pulling with the arms only and not engaging the back muscles effectively.
Neglecting to keep the core tight, resulting in a loss of stability and control.
exercises.name: L Pull-Up
tips: Ensure your core is engaged throughout to maintain the L-sit position.
Focus on controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and reduce injury risk.
If you struggle with the L-sit position, practice leg raises separately to build strength.
Keep your shoulders down and back to avoid unnecessary strain on the neck.
Breath steadily; exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower down.
Start with fewer reps or use assistance bands if needed, gradually increasing difficulty as you gain strength.

exercises.description: The L-Sit is a challenging isometric exercise that targets the core, hip flexors, and shoulders. It involves holding your body off the ground while maintaining a seated position with legs extended straight out in front of you. This exercise requires significant strength and stability, making it ideal for building core endurance and improving overall body control.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and your hands placed on the ground beside your hips.
Engage your core muscles and press your hands firmly into the ground to lift your body off the floor.
Keep your legs straight and parallel to the ground, forming an 'L' shape with your body.
Hold this position for as long as possible, maintaining steady breathing throughout.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
mistakes: Leaning too far forward, causing excessive strain on shoulders and wrists.
Allowing hips to sag, reducing core engagement and effectiveness.
Failing to keep legs straight, compromising form and muscle activation.
Rounding the back, leading to poor posture and potential back strain.
Neglecting to fully engage the core, resulting in decreased stability.
Placing hands too far apart, which can destabilize the position.
Holding breath, which can lead to increased tension and reduced endurance.
Not keeping shoulders depressed, causing unnecessary tension in the neck.
Using momentum to lift legs instead of controlled strength, reducing effectiveness.
exercises.name: L-Sit
tips: Ensure your hands are placed firmly on the ground for maximum stability.
Focus on engaging your core and hip flexors to maintain leg elevation.
Start by practicing with bent knees if full leg extension is too challenging.
Gradually increase hold time as you build strength and endurance.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears to prevent tension.

exercises.description: The Landmine Lateral Raise is an effective shoulder exercise that targets the lateral deltoids. It utilizes a landmine setup, which involves anchoring one end of a barbell to the ground, allowing for a unique range of motion and stability. This exercise helps in building shoulder strength and size, while also engaging the core for stabilization.
instructions: Position a barbell in a landmine attachment or securely anchor one end in a corner.
Stand perpendicular to the barbell with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the end of the barbell with one hand, keeping your arm straight and at your side.
Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your knees.
Lift the barbell laterally by raising your arm to shoulder height, keeping your elbow slightly bent.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring control and stability.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.
mistakes: Using too much weight, leading to loss of control and poor form.
Raising the bar too high, causing shoulder impingement.
Leaning the torso excessively, reducing lateral deltoid engagement.
Swinging the barbell, using momentum instead of muscle activation.
Not maintaining a slight bend in the elbow, straining the joints.
Allowing the wrist to bend, reducing power and control.
Failing to keep the core engaged, leading to instability.
Not keeping the feet firmly planted, affecting balance and control.
exercises.name: Landmine Lateral Raise
tips: Focus on using your shoulder muscles to lift the weight, avoiding momentum or swinging.
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain balance and support.
Start with a lighter weight to master form and technique before increasing resistance.
Ensure that your movements are controlled and deliberate, especially during the lowering phase.
Maintain a neutral spine and avoid leaning excessively to either side.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/臀部/杠铃地雷管罗马尼亚硬拉

exercises.description: Straddle the landmine bar facing away from its anchor and hold the loaded end with both hands. With your knees slightly bent, push your hips back to lower the bar while keeping your back neutral. Extend your hips to stand, letting the straight arms hold the load without pulling it upward.
instructions: Straddle the bar facing away from the landmine anchor, with your feet hip-width apart and the loaded end in front of you.
Grip the sleeve or the end of the barbell with both hands, straighten your arms, and stand tall with your chest up, shoulders pulled down and back, and core braced.
Begin the repetition by pushing your hips backward while keeping a slight bend in your knees and maintaining a neutral spine.
Allow the bar to travel downward close to your body as your torso leans forward, keeping your arms straight and your weight balanced through your mid-foot and heels.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings while maintaining a flat back and controlled position; do not round your lower back or force excessive depth.
Drive your hips forward and press through your feet to return to standing, squeezing your glutes as you finish with your hips fully extended.
Keep the movement controlled throughout the set, avoiding jerking the bar, squatting deeply, or leaning backward at the top.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back instead of maintaining a neutral spine
Turning the movement into a squat by bending the knees too much
Locking the knees completely instead of keeping a soft knee bend
Allowing the bar to move away from the body instead of keeping it close to the legs
Shifting weight onto the toes instead of keeping pressure through the midfoot and heels
Using momentum or bouncing out of the bottom position
Hyperextending the lower back by leaning back at the top
exercises.name: Landmine Romanian Deadlift
tips: Straddle the bar facing away from the landmine anchor, with your feet hip-width apart and the loaded end in front of you.
Look a short distance ahead on the floor to keep the neck relaxed.
Use the stretch in the back of your thighs to judge your lowering depth.
Use your arms as hooks rather than pulling with them; the movement should be driven primarily by your hips, hamstrings, and glutes.
Begin with a light load and increase resistance gradually as the hinge becomes familiar.
