exercises.description: Lie face up on a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor, positioned in line with a low cable pulley behind your head. Hold the cable attachment with an underhand grip and start with your arms extended toward the pulley. Keeping your upper arms still and elbows close to your body, curl the handle toward your shoulders by contracting your biceps. Pause briefly at the top, then slowly extend your elbows to return to the starting position. Avoid lifting your shoulders, arching your back, or using momentum.
instructions: Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a straight bar or EZ-curl bar.
Place a flat bench in line with the cable stack, with the head end closest to the low pulley.
Lie on your back on the bench with your head nearest the cable, plant your feet firmly on the floor, and reach overhead to grip the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Begin with your arms extended toward the pulley, keeping a slight bend in the elbows and maintaining tension on the cable.
Keep your upper arms as still as possible and curl the bar by bending your elbows, bringing it toward your forehead or just above the top of your head.
Squeeze your biceps briefly at the top without allowing your elbows to flare excessively or your shoulders to lift off the bench.
Slowly extend your elbows to return the bar toward the starting position, controlling the resistance and keeping tension in your biceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your wrists neutral and avoiding momentum throughout the movement.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to drift backward or forward instead of keeping them fixed relative to the torso
Lifting the shoulders off the bench or shrugging to help pull the cable
Using momentum by jerking the handles at the start of the curl
Letting the wrists bend back or curl forward instead of keeping them neutral
Failing to fully extend the elbows under control at the bottom
Stopping the curl short and not bringing the hands toward the shoulders through a comfortable full range
Letting the upper arms flare outward rather than keeping them stable and aligned
Arching the lower back or losing full contact with the bench to create leverage
Using excessive load that turns the movement into a partial-range, body-assisted curl
Dropping the weight too quickly and losing tension during the lowering phase
Relaxing at the bottom so the cable goes slack instead of maintaining controlled tension
Rotating the forearms excessively or changing grip position during the curl
exercises.name: Lying Cable Biceps Curl
tips: Set the bench so the cable provides tension from the bottom position and remains aligned with your forearms throughout the curl.
Lie flat with your head, upper back, and hips supported on the bench, keeping your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Grip the cable attachment with an underhand grip and begin with your elbows extended but not locked, maintaining tension on the cable.
Keep your upper arms as still as possible and curl by bending only at the elbows rather than pulling with the shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the repetition without allowing your elbows to flare excessively or your wrists to bend back.
Lower the handle slowly and under control until your elbows are nearly straight, avoiding a sudden drop or loss of cable tension.
Use a load that allows a full range of motion without arching your back, lifting your shoulders, or swinging the arms.
Keep your wrists neutral and choose an attachment that feels comfortable for your elbows, such as a straight bar, EZ-bar, or individual handles.

exercises.description: Lie face up on a bench under a high pulley and pull a rope down to your forehead to train your rear delts and the muscles between your shoulder blades. The rear delts do most of the work. Your middle traps pull the shoulder blades together, the infraspinatus (a rotator cuff muscle) turns your arms out as your hands finish beside your head, and the upper traps help a little. The bench holds your torso, so you can't lean back or sway as on a standing face pull. Use it as a warm-up before pressing, or when you rock on the standing version.
instructions: Clip a rope to the top pulley of a cable column (a lat pulldown station works).
Set a flat bench lengthwise in front, one end against the column.
Lie face up with your head at the column end so the rope hangs straight down over your face. Knees bent, feet flat on the floor.
Reach up and take one rope end in each hand just above the stoppers: palms facing each other, thumbs toward the pulley, wrists straight.
Start with your arms straight up above your shoulders and the plates lifted off the stack. If they touch down, slide the bench or use a higher pulley.
Press your shoulders down, away from your ears, then pull the rope toward your forehead as your elbows bend and travel out to the sides, down toward the floor.
As the rope reaches your face, pull the ends apart until your hands sit beside your temples, upper arms level with your shoulders and elbows bent about 90°.
Squeeze your shoulder blades into the bench for a second, then take 2–3 seconds to return along the same path to straight arms, plates still off the stack.
After the last rep, let the stack down with your arms straight before you let go or sit up. Let go early and the rope whips up past your face.
mistakes: Bench in the wrong spot. If the rope comes from behind your head, the pull turns into a pullover; from over your hips, it turns into a row. Slide the bench until the rope hangs straight over your face with your arms vertical.

Rowing the rope to your chin or chest: the elbows drift toward your hips and your lats and biceps take over. Aim the middle of the rope at your forehead and keep your upper arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Lifting your head off the bench to meet the rope. The back of your head stays down; stop the rope just above your forehead.
Stopping with your hands in front of your face and the rope ends still together. Pull the ends apart until your hands sit beside your temples, forearms angled toward the top of your head.
exercises.name: Lying Cable Face Pull
tips: Sets of 12–20 reps, 2–4 of them, suit this lift; stop 1–3 reps short of failure, or as soon as the hands no longer reach the spot beside the head. Add reps before weight: once you hit 20 on all sets with a one-second hold and your head still down, go up one step on the stack (usually 2.5–5 kg) and restart at 12. One plate can mean 10–20% more here, so expect a few sessions at each weight.

Most of the burn sits at the back of your shoulders and between your shoulder blades, right where they press into the bench, and on the back of the shoulder blade as your hands turn out. A pinch at the front of the shoulder at the finish means you should stop with your hands slightly in front of your ears and take some weight off.

As a warm-up before pressing or pulling, 1–2 light sets of 15–25 are enough. Can't reach the full finish yet? Stop with your hands just above your forehead. Too easy? Hold the finish for 2 seconds and take 3 seconds on the way up before you add load.

Substitutes: Cable Face Pull, standing at a head-height pulley, when no bench is free under a high pulley; Seated Face Pull on the floor, which also keeps your body out of it; Banded Face Pull at home or as the easier version; Machine Reverse Flyes for the rear delts with your chest on a pad, straight arms and no rotation.

exercises.description: The Lying Cable Fly is an isolation exercise targeting the pectoral muscles. It involves lying on a flat bench and using cables to perform a fly motion, which helps in developing the chest by focusing on the inner and outer portions of the pectorals. This exercise also engages the shoulders and triceps as secondary muscles.
instructions: Set the pulleys on a cable machine to the lowest position and attach single handle grips.
Lie flat on a bench positioned between the cable stacks, ensuring your feet are flat on the floor.
Grasp each handle with an overhand grip, palms facing each other, and extend your arms straight up above your chest.
With a slight bend in your elbows, slowly lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then bring your arms back to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the motion.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to drop too low, reducing chest engagement and increasing shoulder strain.
Using too much weight, leading to uncontrolled movements and poor form.
Failing to maintain a slight bend in the elbows, which can stress the elbow joints.
Not keeping the shoulders retracted, causing the shoulders to take over the movement.
Bringing the cables too close together, losing tension on the chest muscles.
Arching the lower back excessively, which can lead to improper core engagement.
Lifting the head off the bench, causing neck strain and misalignment.
Moving the arms too quickly, reducing time under tension and control.
exercises.name: Lying Cable Fly
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to reduce stress on the joints.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your arms back together to maximize muscle engagement.
Maintain a controlled motion; avoid letting the weights pull your arms back too quickly.
Ensure that your shoulder blades remain in contact with the bench to stabilize your upper body.
Breathe out as you bring your arms together and inhale as you lower them back down.

exercises.description: Lie flat on a bench facing away from a low cable pulley, holding the cable attachment with an overhand grip above your chest. Keep your upper arms still and perpendicular to the floor as you bend your elbows to lower the handle toward your forehead. Extend your elbows to straighten your arms and contract the triceps, then repeat with controlled movement. Keep your wrists neutral, avoid flaring the elbows excessively, and do not use momentum.
instructions: Set a flat bench in front of a low cable pulley so that your head will be closest to the pulley when lying down.
Attach a straight bar, EZ-bar attachment, or rope to the low pulley and select a manageable weight.
Lie flat on the bench with your feet firmly on the floor, then hold the attachment with an overhand grip and position your arms vertically above your chest or slightly back toward the pulley.
Keep your upper arms mostly fixed, elbows pointing upward, and brace your core to keep your lower back and shoulders stable on the bench.
Inhale and slowly bend only at the elbows, lowering the attachment toward your forehead or just behind the top of your head.
Pause briefly when your elbows are deeply bent and you feel a stretch in your triceps, without allowing your elbows to flare excessively.
Exhale and extend your elbows to press the attachment back to the starting position, squeezing your triceps at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions using controlled movement, keeping tension on the cable and avoiding shoulder movement or swinging.
mistakes: Letting the elbows flare outward instead of keeping them fixed and shoulder-width apart
Moving the upper arms during the rep instead of hinging mainly at the elbows
Using the shoulders to pull the cable rather than isolating elbow extension
Lowering the handle toward the chest or face instead of bending the elbows under control
Cutting the range of motion short and not fully extending the elbows at the top
Locking the elbows aggressively at the top instead of finishing with controlled extension
Allowing the wrists to bend back or forward instead of keeping them neutral
Using excessive weight and turning the movement into a press or pullover
Lowering the cable too quickly and losing tension or control at the bottom
Arching the lower back or lifting the hips off the bench to create momentum
Letting the elbows drift behind the head excessively, shifting tension away from the triceps
Relaxing the triceps at the bottom instead of maintaining control through the transition
exercises.name: Lying Cable Skull Crusher
tips: Set a flat bench in front of a low cable pulley and attach a straight bar, EZ-bar, or rope handle securely before starting.
Lie with your head closest to the pulley so the cable provides tension throughout the movement, then hold the attachment above your forehead with an overhand or neutral grip.
Keep your upper arms mostly fixed and angled slightly back toward the pulley; the movement should come from bending and straightening the elbows, not from pressing with the shoulders.
Lower the handle under control toward the forehead or just behind the head, choosing the path that feels comfortable for your elbows and allows a full triceps stretch.
Extend your elbows until your arms are nearly straight, then squeeze the triceps without aggressively locking or hyperextending the elbows.
Keep your wrists neutral and grip the attachment firmly so the wrists do not bend backward as the cable pulls toward the pulley.
Avoid letting the elbows flare excessively; keep them roughly shoulder-width apart and use a load that lets you maintain this position.
Keep your head, upper back, and hips stable on the bench, and avoid using momentum or turning the exercise into a pullover or chest press.
Use a lighter weight than you might use for free-weight skull crushers at first, as cable tension can feel challenging in different parts of the range of motion.
Finish each set carefully by returning the handle toward the pulley under control rather than releasing cable tension suddenly.

exercises.description: Lie on a lever machine's flat pad and press two handles from your chest to nearly straight arms: a bench press for your chest with no bar to balance. The muscles worked are mainly the chest, its middle part most, with the triceps taking over in the top third and the front delts helping off the bottom. The handles rest on stops, so a missed rep needs no rack or spotter. That suits training alone, sets close to failure and shoulders that prefer a neutral grip to a barbell. Unlike the seated chest press, you keep the bench-press position: shoulder blades pinned, feet driving into the floor.
instructions: Load the same plates on both weight horns, then lie back on the pad with your head toward the frame.
Slide up or down until the resting handles sit beside your mid-chest, around the nipple line, not at your neck or over your stomach.
Plant your feet flat and wider than your hips, knees bent about 90°. Hips, upper back and head stay on the pad.
Take the handles with your palms facing each other and thumbs toward your head, wrists straight over vertical forearms.
Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the pad. A small natural arch in your lower back is fine; a big bridge is not.
Exhale and press both handles up until your arms are nearly straight over your shoulders. The levers' arc carries your hands slightly toward your head.
Lower for about 2 seconds along the same arc, elbows 30–45° from your sides, until the handles are back beside your chest and you feel a stretch.
Touch lightly and press again before the plates settle on the stops. After the last rep, set both handles down on the stops, then let go.
mistakes: Starting with the handles at your neck or collarbones, so your shoulders take over. Before the set, shift toward the frame until the resting handles sit beside your mid-chest.
Reaching the handles higher at the top until your shoulder blades peel off the pad. Stop at almost straight arms with the blades still pinned.
Elbows flaring straight out to the sides. Keep your forearms vertical under the handles and your elbows 30–45° from your torso.
Parking the plates on the stops, or bouncing off them, between reps. Lower over about 2 seconds, touch lightly and press straight back up.
One handle running ahead of the other while the stronger arm does more of the work. Keep them level; if one arm keeps lagging, end the set when it slows and add a few one-arm sets for that side.
exercises.name: Lying Chest Press
tips: Take 3–4 sets of 6–12 reps close to failure, because a missed rep just ends on the stops.
Add reps before weight: once you hit 12 on all sets with your shoulder blades still down, add the smallest plate to each side (usually 1.25 or 2.5 kg) and build the reps back up.
Log the plates per side. The levers change the real resistance, so the plate total won't match what you bench with a bar.

Most of it should land across your chest, with the triceps kicking in near the top. If the front of your shoulders does most of the work, the handles start too close to your neck: shift toward the frame until they sit at mid-chest.

New to pressing? Use lighter plates and stop a little short at the bottom, or start on the seated Machine Chest Press. To make it harder, lower for 3–4 seconds, pause 1–2 seconds at your chest, or press one arm at a time on the independent levers.
Substitutes: Hammer Grip Dumbbell Bench Press for the same neutral grip on free weights, Barbell Bench Press for heavy low-rep work, Smith Bench Press when no lever machine is free.

exercises.description: The Lying Cross Lateral Cable Fly is an isolation exercise targeting the pectoral muscles, particularly the sternal head of the pectoralis major. It involves lying on a flat bench positioned between two cable machines, using the cables to perform a fly motion that emphasizes the chest muscles while minimizing involvement of the shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Position a flat bench in the center of a cable crossover machine.
Attach D-handle attachments to the low pulleys on each side.
Lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the floor and grasp each handle with an overhand grip.
Extend your arms straight up above your chest, palms facing each other, with a slight bend in your elbows.
Inhale and slowly lower your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Exhale and bring your arms back to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping the movement controlled.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Arching the back excessively, reducing core engagement and stability.
Allowing the cables to pull the arms too far back, risking shoulder strain.
Bending the elbows too much, turning the exercise into a press rather than a fly.
Not maintaining a controlled motion, leading to momentum-based swings.
Failing to align the cables with the chest, compromising muscle activation.
Lifting the head off the bench, causing neck strain.
Dropping the arms too low, placing unnecessary stress on the shoulder joints.
Rushing through the movement, diminishing muscle tension and control.
exercises.name: Lying Cross Lateral Cable Fly
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to reduce stress on the joints.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles at the top of the movement for maximum contraction.
Keep your back flat against the bench and avoid arching to maintain proper form.
Control the movement speed; avoid letting gravity pull your arms down too quickly.
Ensure that your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms to prevent strain.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱三头肌/仰卧ez杠三头肌伸展

exercises.description: Lie on a flat bench and lower an EZ bar from over your forehead to just behind your head, then straighten your elbows to build bigger triceps. All three heads of the triceps share the work, and the bottom position behind your head puts the long head on a deep stretch. The angled handles let your hands turn in a little, which most wrists and elbows like better than a straight bar. It usually comes after bench or overhead presses. If that deep stretch bothers your elbows, the cable or dumbbell version is the better pick.
instructions: Sit at the end of a flat bench with the loaded EZ bar on your thighs, then lie back so your head rests at the very end of the pad.
Bend your knees to about 90 degrees and plant your feet flat. Glutes, upper back and head stay on the bench for the whole set.
Hold the outer angled handles, right next to the plates, overhand and about shoulder width apart. Thumbs around the bar, knuckles up, wrists straight.
Press the bar to straight arms and let it settle over your forehead, upper arms tilted slightly back toward your head rather than straight up over your chest.
Bend only at the elbows and lower the bar in an arc past your forehead to just behind the top of your head, taking 2 to 3 seconds.
When your forearms nearly touch your biceps, reverse without a bounce and straighten along the same arc until your elbows lock out over your forehead.
To end the set, bring the bar down to your chest and sit up with it, or hand it to your spotter.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out as the bar comes down. Point them at the ceiling, about as wide as your hands, and take some weight off until you can.
Upper arms drifting forward until the bar finishes over your chest and the rep turns into a press. Keep that slight backward tilt; only your forearms move.

Stopping with the bar above your forehead even though your elbows feel fine. Lower it until it's just behind the top of your head and your forearms almost touch your biceps, and go lighter until you own that range.
Lying too far down the bench, so the bar hits the pad or your head at the bottom. Slide up until your head is at the end of the bench before the first rep.
Dropping the bar fast and bouncing out of the bottom, or lifting your hips to finish a hard rep. Lower in 2 to 3 seconds, keep your glutes down, and end the set once you need your hips.
exercises.name: Lying EZ-Bar Triceps Extension
tips: Two to four sets of 8 to 15 reps work well, often 10 to 12. For heavier work, 6 to 10 is plenty; fewer reps are rarely worth the stress on your elbows. Stay at one weight until all your sets reach the top of the range with the bar behind your head and a full lockout, then add 2.5 kg in total (1.25 kg per side) and build back up from the low end. If your smallest plates are 2.5 kg, that 5 kg jump is big, so add a set first.

At the bottom you should feel a long stretch up the back of your upper arm toward the armpit, and a hard squeeze at lockout. Pain in the elbow joint means less weight, stopping at your forehead for a while, or the cable version. To make it harder without more weight, pause for a second behind your head and take 3 seconds to lower.

The bar passes over your face. Do 1 or 2 light warm-up sets and keep a rep or two in reserve. If a rep stalls, don't force it with your shoulders: bend your elbows, bring the bar down to your chest by moving your upper arms toward your hips, and sit up with it.

Substitutes: Lying Barbell Triceps Extension when there's no EZ bar, Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension for a neutral grip, Lying Cable Skull Crusher for steady tension with no bar over your face, and Incline Barbell Triceps Extension for an even bigger stretch.

exercises.description: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, just above the knee. Hold behind the supporting thigh with both hands and draw it toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the crossed leg's glute. Keep your head down, breathe calmly and release before changing sides.
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left thigh, just above the left knee, forming a figure 4 shape.
Lift the supporting foot and hold behind that thigh with both hands.
Gently pull your left leg toward your chest until you feel a stretch in your right glute and outer hip.
Keep your head, shoulders and lower back relaxed on the floor. Do not force your right knee down.
Hold the stretch while breathing slowly and steadily.
Release with control, return both feet to the floor, then repeat on the other side.
mistakes: Letting the crossed knee collapse inward instead of opening it out to the side.
Pulling the thigh toward the chest with the shoulders and neck tense.
Forcing the stretch by yanking the supporting leg too hard.
Allowing the pelvis to twist or one hip to lift off the floor.
Placing the ankle directly on the knee joint instead of across the opposite thigh.
Pushing the crossed knee downward with your hand.
exercises.name: Lying Figure 4 Stretch
tips: Keep the crossed foot gently flexed with the toes pointing toward the shin.
Pass one arm through the space between your legs so both hands can reach the thigh comfortably.
Aim to feel the stretch in the glute and outer hip of the crossed-leg side, not sharp pain in the knee or hip.
Breathe slowly and hold the position without bouncing. Relax further into the stretch with each exhale.
Hold for 20 to 60 seconds, then switch sides.

exercises.description: The Lying Knee To Chest Stretch is a flexibility exercise targeting the lower back and glutes. It helps to relieve tension in the lumbar spine and improve overall mobility in the hip area.
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and arms at your sides.
Bend your right knee and slowly bring it towards your chest, using both hands to gently pull it closer.
Keep your left leg extended on the floor, ensuring your lower back remains in contact with the mat.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply and relaxing into the position.
Release your right knee and return to the starting position.
Repeat the stretch with your left knee.
mistakes: Pulling the knee too forcefully towards the chest, causing strain on the lower back.
Allowing the opposite leg to lift off the ground, reducing the stretch effectiveness.
Arching the back instead of keeping it flat on the ground, leading to improper stretching of the lower back.
Holding the breath instead of breathing deeply and evenly, which can increase tension in the body.
Grabbing the knee joint directly, which can put unnecessary pressure on the knee.
Failing to engage the core muscles, resulting in less stability and control during the stretch.
Rushing the movement instead of holding the stretch for sufficient time to allow muscles to relax.
exercises.name: Lying Knee To Chest Stretch
tips: Ensure your head and shoulders remain relaxed on the mat throughout the stretch.
Avoid pulling too hard on your knee; the stretch should be gentle and comfortable.
Focus on keeping your extended leg straight and in contact with the floor to maximize the stretch in your lower back.
Perform this stretch slowly and with control to prevent any sudden movements that could cause strain.
Inhale deeply as you bring your knee towards your chest, and exhale as you hold the stretch.

exercises.description: Sit in an ab crunch machine and curl your ribs down toward your pelvis to train your abs against a weight stack you can add to like any other lift. The rectus abdominis, your six-pack muscle, does the curling, and the obliques at the sides of your waist help. Your ankles are hooked under foot rollers and your chest pushes the pads of the machine arm, so your arms only hold on while your back rounds and your hips stay on the seat. The fixed path and small weight steps suit beginners and anyone who finds floor crunches awkward.
instructions: Set the pin in the stack. Go light the first time on a new machine, because crunch machines differ a lot in leverage.
Adjust the seat so that, sitting tall, the handles are about ear height and the padded bars rest on your lower chest.
Sit all the way back and slide your feet under the rollers so they rest on the front of your ankles, knees at about 90°.
Grab the handles beside your head with a full grip, elbows bent and pointing forward and down. Head neutral, eyes forward.
Breathe out and curl your ribs toward your pelvis, rounding from the upper back down. Your chest drives the pads; your arms just ride along.
Stop once your back is fully rounded and your elbows sit in front of your lower ribs. Squeeze a second, hips heavy on the seat.
Uncurl over 2–3 seconds to sitting tall, and start the next rep just before the plates touch down.
When you finish, let the stack settle completely before you take your hands off the handles.
mistakes: Folding at the hips with a flat back. The trunk tips forward in one piece and you feel it at the front of the hips. Think ribs to pelvis, round your upper back first, and lower the weight until your spine actually curls.
Pulling the handles down with your arms and shoulders before your trunk moves. Lock the elbow angle and push the pads with your chest; your hands only hold on.
Driving your shins up into the rollers until your hips leave the seat. The rollers just keep you in place, so let them rest lightly on your ankles. If your hips still lift, the weight is too heavy.
Yanking your head down and jamming your chin into your chest. Keep about a fist of space under your chin and let your head follow your trunk, eyes on your knees at the bottom.
Dropping back fast and banging the plates on the stack between reps. Take 2–3 seconds to uncurl and start every rep from a standstill.
exercises.name: Machine Abdominal Crunches
tips: Take 2–4 sets of 10–20 reps close to failure; the seat and fixed path make hard sets safe. Pick a range such as 12–15 and add reps at the same pin until you get 15 on all sets with a full curl and a slow return. Then move the pin down one plate (usually 2.5–5 kg) and go back to 12. Compare weights only on the same machine.

Feel it down the front of your stomach, from just below the breastbone to below the navel, hardest at the bottom of the curl. Burning at the front of the hips or in the groin means you're folding at the hips; tired arms mean you're pulling the handles. Sharp pain in the lower back, or pain running into a leg, means stop.

New to crunches? Learn the curl on the floor with Abdominal Crunches first. When the machine gets easy, slow down to a 3-second return and a 2-second squeeze before you add weight or switch exercises.
Looking for oblique work? Here the obliques only assist; Seated Machine Trunk Rotation trains them directly.

Substitutes: Kneeling Cable Abs Crunches (longer range, heavier loads), Seated Ab Cable Crunch (the closest seated position), Weighted Ab Crunches (just a plate and a mat) and Weighted Decline Crunch (feet hooked under pads, as here).

exercises.description: Sit at a plate-loaded grip machine and squeeze its handles shut with both hands to build grip strength and the muscles of your forearms. The work lands on the palm side of your forearms, from the inner elbow to the wrist: the flexors that curl your fingers and close your hand. Only your fingers move; your arms just hold position. Unlike a handheld gripper, the machine trains both hands together and lets you add load in small plate steps. Use it if your grip quits before your back on deadlifts, rows and pull-ups, or if you climb, grapple or play a racket sport.
instructions: Load a light plate on the lever horn to start. The lever changes how heavy a plate feels, so the number on it isn't the force in your hands.
Sit upright facing the handles, feet flat and hip-width apart, knees bent about 90°. The handles should sit just in front of your knees and slightly above them.
Take the handles overhand, one hand near each end. One handle lies across your palms at the base of the fingers with your thumbs around it; your fingers wrap the moving handle.
Straighten your wrists so your knuckles line up with your forearms. Let your upper arms hang close to your sides, shoulders down and away from your ears.
Squeeze with both hands at once until the handles meet or stop. The plate rises only a few centimeters, and your elbows and torso stay where they are.
Hold your fists tight for about a second, then open over about 2 seconds until your fingers are almost straight. Stop just before the plate settles and squeeze again.
At the end of the set, let the plate down slowly before you let go, and keep your feet and shins clear of the lever.
mistakes: Letting the handle sit out on your fingertips, so the hand can't close and the fingers slip off. Seat one handle across your palms near the base of the fingers and wrap your fingers all the way around the other.
Bending the wrists up or down to help the handles shut. Keep your knuckles in line with your forearms, and go lighter if your wrists still move.
Leaning back or pulling with your arms to lift the lever. Relax your elbows, sit tall and let your fingers do the work.
Half reps: the handles never meet, or your hands bounce straight back open. Close until the handles stop, hold for a second, then open; if you can't close fully, the plate is too heavy.
One hand squeezing harder than the other, so the handles tilt. Squeeze evenly and check that the handles stay level as they close.
exercises.name: Machine Hand Grip
tips: For strength, do 3–5 sets of 5–8 reps with a 1–2 second squeeze; for size, 2–4 sets of 10–20. End a set when the handles no longer close all the way.

Add reps before weight. Pick a range such as 3 × 8–12, and once you get 12 on every set with the handles fully shut and a one-second hold, add the smallest plate you have (usually 1.25–2.5 kg) and restart at 8. Expect several sessions at each load, and compare numbers only on the same machine.

The palm side of both forearms should burn, with tired fingers and palms. If your biceps or shoulders burn, you're pulling with your arms; if the backs of your forearms burn most, your wrists are bending back.

Too heavy to close? Use a lighter plate and close only halfway with a 2-second hold. To make it harder, hold the squeeze for 3–5 seconds and open over 3 before you add a plate. If the inside of your elbow starts to ache, cut sets and load and build back slowly.
Substitutes: Dead Hang (start with 20–30-second holds if your grip is weak), Farmer Walk, Barbell Wrist Curl. A pin-loaded grip machine works the same way as this plate-loaded one.

tips: Focus on maintaining a neutral spine throughout the exercise to avoid lower back strain.
Ensure that your knees remain aligned with your toes during the thrust to prevent knee injuries.
Control the movement both on the way up and down to maximize muscle engagement.
Experiment with foot placement to target different areas of the glutes; wider stances can engage more of the glute medius.
Keep your chin slightly tucked and gaze forward to maintain proper neck alignment.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/器械侧平举

exercises.description: Sit with your elbows bent to about 90 degrees and push the pads out and up until your upper arms reach shoulder height, to build wider shoulders. The side (middle) delts do nearly all the work; the front and rear delts help a little. Because the load goes through pads on your forearms instead of your hands, there is nothing to swing and nothing to squeeze hard. That makes it a good pick for beginners, for high-rep sets and drop sets, and for anyone whose wrists or elbows complain on dumbbell raises. Set the seat height first: it decides whether your shoulder works without a pinch.
instructions: Use the pop-pin under the seat to set your shoulder joints level with the round pivots the lever arms turn on, just behind your shoulders.
Sit tall with your feet flat, a little wider than your hips. If your machine has a chest or back pad, stay in contact with it.
Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees, upper arms by your sides and forearms pointing forward, with the outside of each forearm against its pad.
Hold the handles lightly with your thumbs up. They only keep your arms in place; your forearms do the pushing.
Drive your elbows out and up in a wide arc. The 90-degree bend stays, and your forearms keep pointing forward.
Stop when your elbows are level with your shoulders and your upper arms about parallel to the floor. Hold for a second, shoulders down.
Lower over 2–3 seconds until your upper arms are back at your sides, and stop just before the plates touch down.
mistakes: Seat set too high or too low. The pads slide along your forearms and the top of the shoulder pinches; move the seat until your shoulders sit level with the pivots and the pads stay on one spot from bottom to top.

Pulling with your hands: a white-knuckle grip, bent wrists and hands racing ahead of the elbows. Hold the handles loosely, think "elbows out and up" and push the pads with the outside of your forearms.

Shrugging, or driving the elbows well above shoulder height. Pull your shoulders down before each rep, stop when your upper arms are parallel to the floor and drop a plate if the shrug keeps coming back.
exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
tips: Sets of 12–15 reps taken close to failure suit this machine, though anything from 10 to 20 works. Add reps at the same weight until all sets reach 15 with a short pause at the top and no shrug, then move the pin one plate heavier and go back to 12.

One plate on the stack is often 5 kg, a big jump at lateral-raise weights. If the machine has a small add-on weight (1–2.5 kg), use it; if not, stay at the top of your range with a 1–2 second hold before you move the pin. On plate-loaded machines, add 1.25 kg per side.

The burn belongs on the outside of your shoulders. If your neck and the tops of your shoulders do most of the work, you're shrugging or going too high. A pinch at the top of the shoulder usually means the seat is off; if it still pinches with the seat set right, stop a little below shoulder height.

First time on the machine? Use the lightest pin, raise your elbows only about halfway (around 45 degrees) with a one-second hold, and widen the arc as it starts to feel smooth. To make it harder without adding weight, lower over 3 seconds or finish with a drop set.

Substitutes: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise when the machine is taken or doesn't fit your shoulders, Dumbbell Lateral Raise if all you have is a light pair, Cable Lateral Raise for tension right from the bottom, Band Lateral Raise at home.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/器械仰卧卷腹

exercises.description: The Machine Lying Crunch is an abdominal exercise performed on a specialized machine designed to target the rectus abdominis. This exercise provides resistance to enhance muscle engagement and improve core strength.
instructions: Adjust the machine settings to fit your body size, ensuring the back pad and foot placement are comfortable.
Lie down on the machine with your back firmly against the pad and your feet secured under the foot pads.
Grip the handles or place your hands across your chest, depending on the machine design.
Engage your core by pulling your navel towards your spine.
Exhale as you contract your abdominal muscles to lift your upper body towards your knees.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction of the abs.
Inhale as you slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the descent.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using momentum to initiate the movement instead of engaging the core muscles.
Setting the machine's resistance too high, leading to improper form and reduced range of motion.
Allowing the lower back to arch excessively, which reduces core engagement.
Failing to fully contract the abdominal muscles at the top of the movement.
Not maintaining a neutral head and neck position, leading to strain.
Rushing through repetitions without controlled movement, reducing effectiveness.
Improper alignment of the machine's pads, causing uneven muscle activation.
Neglecting to exhale during the crunch, which can reduce core activation.
Starting the movement from the shoulders rather than the core, leading to poor form.
exercises.name: Machine Lying Crunch
tips: Ensure that the machine is adjusted properly to prevent strain on your back and neck.
Focus on using your abdominal muscles rather than pulling with your arms or legs.
Maintain a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement and reduce injury risk.
Keep your lower back in contact with the pad throughout the exercise for proper form.
Avoid using momentum; instead, rely on muscle contraction to perform each repetition.
Breathe out during the crunch phase and inhale as you return to the starting position.

exercises.description: The Machine Preacher Curl is an isolation exercise targeting the biceps brachii. It involves using a preacher curl machine to perform controlled bicep curls, emphasizing the peak contraction of the biceps. This exercise helps in developing the size and strength of the biceps by providing constant tension throughout the movement.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your upper arms rest comfortably on the preacher pad.
Sit down and grasp the handles or bar with an underhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
Ensure your upper arms are flat against the pad and your chest is pressed firmly against it.
Start with your arms fully extended, but avoid locking out your elbows.
Curl the weight upwards by contracting your biceps, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or slightly past vertical for maximum contraction.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
exercises.name: Machine Preacher Curl
tips: Focus on keeping your upper arms stationary to maximize bicep engagement.
Avoid using momentum; perform each rep with controlled movements.
Adjust the machine settings to ensure a full range of motion without overextending.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows at the bottom to maintain tension on the biceps.
Exhale as you curl the weight up and inhale as you lower it back down.
Ensure your wrists remain straight throughout to prevent strain.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/器械下拉

exercises.description: Sit in a pullover machine and drive your elbows from overhead down to your sides against the arm pads to train your lats without your grip giving out. The lats along the sides of your back do most of the work, followed by the teres major at the back of your armpit, while the triceps' long head, rear delts, lower traps and lower chest chip in. The pads sit behind your elbows, so your hands only steer the bar and a weak grip or sore elbows won't end the set. Next to a cable straight-arm pulldown, the arc is longer, the path is fixed and the overhead stretch stays loaded.
instructions: Set the seat so the middle of your shoulder is level with the pivot, the axis the arm levers turn around.
Sit with your hips all the way back, your back and head on the reclined pad and your feet flat. Buckle the belt if there is one.
Bring the bar into the start position, with the foot lever if your machine has one, and rest the backs of your upper arms, just above the elbows, on the pads.
Lay your hands on the crossbar overhand, about shoulder-width apart, with a light grip. Your elbows stay bent at about 90° until the set is over.
Start in the stretch: upper arms beside your head, elbows pointing up and back, ribs down and lower back flat on the pad.
Breathe out and drive your elbows forward and down into the pads in a wide arc until they reach your sides and the bar is in front of your upper stomach.
Hold a second with your shoulders down, then let the levers carry your arms back overhead over 2–3 seconds until the sides of your back stretch.
At the end of the set, take the load on the foot lever, or let the weight settle slowly, before you slide your arms off the pads.
mistakes: Seat at the wrong height. The pads roll along your arms and the shoulder feels jammed at the top. Line the shoulder joint up with the pivot before the first set; the pads should stay on the same spot of your arms.
Pulling with your hands and squeezing the bar until your arms take over and the elbows open and close. Keep the hands loose, even open, hold the 90° elbow and push with the backs of your arms.
Arching your lower back and flaring the ribs to reach further overhead. Ribs down, lower back on the pad, and end the stretch where you can still hold that position.
Stopping with the bar at your chest. Every rep ends with the elbows at your sides and the bar at your upper stomach, held for a second; don't round forward or shrug to push it further.
Letting the weight snap your arms back into the stretch and bouncing out of it. Take 2–3 seconds on the way back and stop just before the weight touches down.
exercises.name: Machine Pullover
tips: Do 2–4 sets of 8–15 reps, often after the day's main pulldown or row; heavy sets of 6–8 add little here and load the shoulder in the stretch.

Progress by reps. When you get 15 on all sets with the whole arc and a slow return, add the smallest step (one plate on a stack, usually 2.5–5 kg, or 2.5 kg per side on a plate-loaded machine) and build the reps back up.

The work runs from the armpit down to the lower ribs, most in the stretch and at the bottom, plus a little in the lower chest and the back of the upper arm. A pinch at the front or top of the shoulder in the stretch means the seat is off or the arc is too long at the top.

Shoulder not happy overhead? Go lighter and stop the levers short of the full stretch, at the point where your lower back still stays on the pad. To progress, slow the return to 3 seconds and pause 1–2 seconds in the stretch before you add weight.
Substitutes: Straight-Arm Lat Pulldown (cable stack, standing, found in almost every gym), Dumbbell Pullover (just a dumbbell and a bench), Rope Straight-Arm Lat Pulldown, Barbell Pullover.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/器械反向飞鸟

exercises.description: Sit facing the pad of a rear delt machine and sweep both arms out to your sides at shoulder height to build the backs of your shoulders and upper back. The rear delts do most of the work, helped by the middle and lower traps between your shoulder blades and a little by the side delts. The pad holds your torso still, so your lower back stays out of it and there's nothing to balance. It's usually the pec deck machine: you sit the other way round and open your arms instead of closing them.
instructions: Set the seat so your hands are level with your shoulders when you sit tall. The arms should travel at shoulder height, not above it.
If there's a start-position adjuster at the top of the machine, set the handles in front of your chest about a hand's width apart.
Sit facing the machine with your chest against the pad, feet flat on the floor and knees bent to about 90°.
Take the short horizontal handles with an overhand grip, palms down. Your arms point straight ahead with a slight bend in the elbows.
Keep that elbow angle fixed and sweep both arms out and back in a wide arc, as if pushing the handles apart rather than pulling.
Stop when your arms line up with your shoulders and your body makes a T. Squeeze your shoulder blades, shoulders down, and hold a second.
Let the handles travel back along the same arc over 2–3 seconds until they almost meet. The plates only touch down after your last rep.
mistakes: Bending the elbows and rowing the handles toward you, so your arms take over. Set a slight bend at the start, keep it until the set is done and push the handles apart.
Peeling your chest off the pad or rocking back to get the weight moving. Chest and belly stay on the pad; if you need the rock, the weight is too heavy.
Pulling the arms behind the line of your shoulders and pushing the chest out. Stop at the T and hold it there, because going further just pinches the front of the shoulder.
Fast, short reps where the plates slam down and the hands never come back in front. Take 2–3 seconds on the way back, until the hands nearly meet, without letting the plates touch.
exercises.name: Machine Reverse Flyes
tips: Work in 2–4 sets of 10–20 reps, taken close to failure. Add reps at the same weight until you reach 20 in each set with the one-second hold, then go up one plate and drop back to 10. A full plate is a big jump for the rear delts, so use the small add-on weight if the machine has one.
You should feel it at the back of your shoulders and between your shoulder blades. Burning on top of the shoulders means you're shrugging; tired biceps mean your elbows are bending into a row.
New to it? Use the lightest weight and stop when your hands are about 45° out. Once that feels easy, make the same weight harder with a 2-second hold at the T and a 3-second return.

Substitutes: Cable Rear Delt Fly for constant tension over a longer arc, Dumbbell Incline Rear Lateral T Raise as the closest free-weight version with chest support, and Bent Over Dumbbell Lateral Raise when all you have is dumbbells.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/器械反向哈克深蹲

exercises.description: Face the hack squat machine with your chest on the pad and squat by sitting your hips back: a supported machine squat for your quads and glutes. Your quads still do most of the work, but your torso leans forward and your hips travel further back than in the standard Machine Hack Squat (back on the pad), so your glutes get more of the load. The pad holds your torso in place; the weight still sits on your shoulders. It's the one to choose when you want to squat heavy with no bar to balance.
instructions: Load the plates evenly on the carriage while it rests on the stops.
Step onto the footplate facing the machine and press your chest and stomach into the pad, with the shoulder pads resting on top of your shoulders.
Set your feet flat, hip- to shoulder-width apart with the toes turned slightly out, a little behind your hips so your body leans into the pad.
Hold the handles at the front of the shoulder pads, elbows pointing down. Your hands only pin you under the pads; they don't pull.
Stand up to lift the carriage off the stops, then release the safety lever. Take a breath and brace your stomach.
Over about 2 seconds, sit your hips back and down along the rails while your knees travel forward over your toes. Your chest stays on the pad.
Go down until your thighs are about parallel to the footplate, or a little lower if your lower back stays flat and your heels stay down.
Without bouncing, push the footplate away through your whole foot so your hips and shoulders rise together. Squeeze your glutes and stop just short of locking your knees.
At the top of the final rep, re-engage the safety lever before you let the carriage down onto it.
mistakes: Hips shooting up first out of the bottom while your chest peels off the pad. The rep turns into a good morning; keep your chest pressed in, push the footplate away so hips and shoulders rise together, and take weight off until they do.
Lower back rounding at the bottom as your pelvis tucks under. Stop the descent just before that point and brace before each rep. A slightly wider stance with the toes out can buy you some depth.

Heels lifting as your knees travel forward. Set your feet a little further back from the machine and keep pressure through the whole foot; the depth should come from your hips moving back, not only from your knees.
Knees caving in on the way up. Push them out in line with your second and third toes, and drop the load if they still drift.
Depth shrinking as the plates go up. Pick one depth, such as thighs parallel to the footplate, and hit it on every rep so the progress you log is real.
exercises.name: Machine Reverse Hack Squat
tips: Use 6–10 reps for strength and 8–15 for muscle; a last set can go to 20 because the carriage is easy to rack. Hit the top of your range on every set at the same depth first, then add 10 kg (5 kg per side) and drop back to the bottom of the range. Switch to 5 kg jumps when progress slows, and log the plates the same way every time, since the empty carriage weighs something different on every machine.

Glutes and the front of your thighs do the work, with a strong glute stretch at the bottom. Your lower back only holds position. If it tires first, your chest is leaving the pad or you're going deeper than your hips allow. Pain at the front of the knee? Check that your knees follow your toes and your heels stay down.

Easier: the Leg Press, or this machine with the empty carriage and a shorter range, down to about 90 degrees at the knee. Harder without more plates: a 2-second pause at the bottom or a 3-second lowering.
Substitutes: Machine Hack Squat (back on the pad, more upright, more quads), Machine Belt Squat (no load on your shoulders), Leg Press, Dumbbell Goblet Squat (no machine needed).

exercises.description: A plate-loaded hip extension done face down on a reverse hyper machine, with your torso on the pad, hips at its edge and ankles between the roller pads of the lever. Starting with your legs hanging down, you raise them nearly straight until they line up with your torso. It works the glutes, hamstrings and lower back.
instructions: Load a light plate on the lever, then lie face down on the pad with your hips at its edge and hold the handles.
Place your ankles between the two roller pads, with the rear roller against the back of your lower legs just above your heels.
Let your legs hang straight down with your knees slightly soft and brace your abs.
Exhale, squeeze your glutes and raise your legs back and up, keeping them nearly straight.
Stop when your legs are in line with your torso, with your pelvis still pressed into the pad.
Inhale and lower your legs slowly until they hang straight down again.
After the last rep, let the lever come to rest at the bottom before you take your feet out of the rollers.
mistakes: Swinging the legs up with momentum instead of lifting them with the hips
Raising the legs above the line of the torso and overarching the lower back
Bending the knees on the way up, which turns the lift into a leg curl
Dropping the legs quickly instead of lowering them under control
Cutting the range short instead of letting the legs hang straight down at the bottom
Lifting one leg higher than the other or twisting the hips
exercises.name: Machine Reverse Hyperextension
tips: Set the crease of your hips right at the edge of the pad, so your legs move freely while your pelvis stays supported.
Pull yourself into the pad with the handles to keep your upper body still.
Start each rep by squeezing your glutes, then drive your lower legs back into the rear roller.
Hold the top for a second with your glutes squeezed.
Use a moderate load for sets of 10 to 15 reps. This is an accessory for the glutes and hamstrings, not a max-effort lift.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/器械肩推举

exercises.description: The Machine Shoulder Press is a compound exercise that targets the deltoid muscles, particularly the anterior and medial heads, as well as the triceps and upper pectoral muscles. It is performed using a shoulder press machine, which provides stability and allows for controlled movement, making it suitable for both beginners and advanced lifters.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that the handles are at shoulder level or slightly below when seated.
Sit down with your back firmly against the backrest and feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing forward.
Engage your core and keep your chest up throughout the exercise.
Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended but not locked out.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Setting the seat too high or too low, misaligning the handles with shoulder height.
Allowing the back to arch excessively, reducing core engagement.
Using a grip that is too wide or too narrow, affecting shoulder joint alignment.
Failing to maintain a neutral wrist position, leading to unnecessary strain.
Pressing the weight too quickly, sacrificing control and muscle engagement.
Not fully extending the arms, limiting the range of motion.
Lowering the weight too far, causing shoulder joint stress.
Engaging the traps instead of focusing on the deltoids.
Shrugging the shoulders upward during the press, reducing shoulder isolation.
Using momentum to lift the weight, rather than controlled muscle contraction.
exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
tips: Ensure that your elbows are slightly in front of your body to reduce shoulder joint strain.
Keep a neutral spine and avoid arching your back during the press.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout all repetitions.
Focus on a slow and controlled movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Exhale as you press the weight up and inhale as you lower it back down.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders; keep them relaxed to prevent neck strain.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/器械耸肩

exercises.description: Machine Shrugs target the trapezius muscles, primarily focusing on the upper traps. This exercise is performed using a shrug machine, which provides stability and allows for controlled movement. It is effective for building strength and size in the upper back and improving posture.
instructions: Adjust the seat height of the shrug machine so that the shoulder pads rest comfortably on your shoulders.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the handles firmly.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears in a shrugging motion, squeezing your traps at the top of the movement.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using too much weight, causing reliance on momentum rather than muscle engagement.
Failing to fully elevate the shoulders, limiting the range of motion.
Allowing the shoulders to roll forward, which disengages the upper trapezius.
Tilting the head forward or downward, leading to neck strain.
Shrugging unevenly, causing muscle imbalance and poor form.
Gripping the handles too tightly, which can cause unnecessary tension in the forearms.
Leaning back or forward, compromising posture and reducing effectiveness.
Not maintaining a controlled pace, leading to jerky movements.
exercises.name: Machine Shrugs
tips: Focus on using your trapezius muscles to lift the weight, not your arms.
Avoid rolling your shoulders; lift them straight up and down.
Keep your movements controlled to maximize muscle engagement and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you lift your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
Start with a lighter weight to ensure proper form before increasing resistance.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱三头肌/器械三头肌伸展

exercises.description: The Machine Triceps Extension is an isolation exercise targeting the triceps brachii muscle. It involves extending the elbows against resistance provided by a machine, allowing for controlled and focused engagement of the triceps. This exercise is ideal for building strength and mass in the triceps while minimizing involvement of other muscle groups.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your upper arms are parallel to the floor when gripping the handles.
Sit down and firmly plant your feet on the floor, ensuring your back is supported by the seat.
Grip the handles with a neutral or overhand grip, depending on machine design.
Start with your elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Extend your arms by pushing the handles forward until your elbows are fully extended but not locked.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to maximize contraction.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Failing to adjust the seat height, leading to improper alignment of elbows and shoulders.
Allowing the elbows to flare out, reducing triceps engagement.
Using momentum to lift the weight instead of controlled movements.
Not fully extending the arms, limiting the range of motion.
Locking the elbows at the bottom of the movement, increasing joint stress.
Letting the wrists bend excessively, causing strain and reducing effectiveness.
Leaning forward or backward, disrupting posture and muscle engagement.
Selecting too much weight, compromising form and control.
exercises.name: Machine Triceps Extension
tips: Ensure that your elbows remain stationary throughout the movement to isolate the triceps effectively.
Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Keep your core engaged and maintain a neutral spine to prevent unnecessary strain on your lower back.
Adjust the weight appropriately; start with a lighter weight to perfect your form before increasing resistance.
Breathe out as you extend your arms and inhale as you return to the starting position.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/药球旋转投掷

exercises.description: Stand side-on to a wall with a medicine ball held near the hip in both hands. Rotate the hips and torso toward the wall to throw the ball, allowing the rear foot to pivot. The throw develops rotational power by transferring force from the legs through the trunk to the arms.
instructions: Stand side-on to a solid wall with feet about shoulder width apart.
Hold the ball in both hands near the hip away from the wall.
Bend your knees slightly and turn the hips and torso away from the target.
Drive through your feet and rotate toward the wall, letting the rear foot pivot.
Throw the ball into the wall with both hands and follow through with the rotation.
Catch or retrieve the ball and reset your stance before the next throw.
Complete the repetitions, then turn around and repeat in the opposite direction.
mistakes: Using the arms only instead of initiating the throw with hip and trunk rotation
Letting the knees collapse inward during the rotation and throw
Over-rotating the lower back instead of turning through the hips and upper back
Rounding the back or leaning excessively forward during the loading phase
Failing to brace the core, causing the torso to wobble or arch during the throw
Stopping the follow-through abruptly instead of allowing the body to rotate naturally after release
exercises.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
tips: Choose a ball you can accelerate quickly.
Aim at a consistent point on the wall.
Keep enough distance from the wall to follow through freely.
Match the number of throws in each direction.
Use a ball designed for wall throws and a wall that can take the impact.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/药球俄罗斯转体

exercises.description: Sit leaning back with your heels on the floor and twist side to side, lowering a medicine ball to the floor by each hip to strengthen your obliques. You feel it along the sides of your waist, just under the lower ribs, while the front of your abs holds the lean. Keeping the feet down makes this version easier to learn than the feet-up twist, and medicine balls come in small weight steps, so it suits beginners and home workouts. It beats the dumbbell version when you want an easier grip and smaller jumps in load.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent about 90°, knees and feet together, heels down and toes pointing up.
Hold the ball at your chest with a hand on each side, palms facing and fingers spread. Keep your fingers off the bottom of the ball so the floor can't pinch them.
Lean back to about 45°, halfway between sitting upright and lying down. Chest up, spine long, and brace your abs as if someone were about to poke your stomach.
Turn your chest and shoulders to one side and lower the ball beside that hip until it touches, or nearly touches, the floor. Your knees stay put.
Rotate back through the middle, where the ball passes in front of your chest, and lower it beside the other hip. Breathe out each time you reach a side.
Take 1–2 seconds from side to side without changing the lean. Right plus left counts as one rep; finish the set with the ball back at your chest and sit up.
mistakes: Swinging the ball with your arms while your chest keeps facing your knees. Keep the elbows bent and the ball close, and turn until your chest faces the side.
Slumping into a rounded lower back, or leaning back so far that the front of your hips cramps. Sit tall on your sit bones with your chest up at about 45°, and lean back less if you can't hold it.
Knees drifting side to side with every turn. Squeeze them together and press your heels lightly into the floor so only your upper body rotates.
Stopping the ball at your ribs, or rushing and bouncing it off the floor. Bring it all the way down beside each hip and just tap the floor; switch to a lighter ball if you can't.
exercises.name: Medicine Ball Russian Twist
tips: Go for 2–4 sets of 10–20 turns per side.
Add turns with the same ball until you reach 20 a side in every set with full turns to the floor, then move to the next ball, usually 1–2 kg heavier, and work back up from 10.
The burn belongs on the sides of your waist, switching as you turn. Some effort at the front of the hips is normal, but if your hips or lower back give out before your abs, sit more upright.
Too hard? Do the same twist with no ball and your hands together, or lean back less. Too easy? Lift your heels just off the floor and keep them still, or pause for a second at each side.
Substitutes: Weighted Russian Twist with a plate, Dumbbell Russian Twist, Sitting Twist with no weight, or Cable Twist (horizontal) if sitting reclined bothers your lower back.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/药球砸地

exercises.description: The slam ball exercise is a dynamic, full-body workout that primarily targets the core, shoulders, and legs. It involves lifting a weighted ball overhead and forcefully slamming it to the ground, engaging multiple muscle groups and enhancing power, coordination, and cardiovascular endurance.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Hold a slam ball with both hands in front of you.
Engage your core and lift the ball overhead by extending your arms fully.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as you lift the ball for added power.
Forcefully slam the ball down to the ground in front of you by using your core and arms.
Catch the ball on the rebound or pick it up if it doesn't bounce.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Failing to engage the core, leading to reduced power and effectiveness.
Not using the full range of motion, limiting the exercise's benefits.
Bending at the waist instead of hinging at the hips, increasing lower back strain.
Slamming the ball without control, risking injury from the ball rebounding unexpectedly.
Not maintaining a stable stance, which can affect balance and power.
Using too light a ball, reducing the exercise's intensity and effectiveness.
Allowing the knees to collapse inward, which can strain the joints.
Neglecting to follow through with the arms, decreasing the force of the slam.

exercises.description: The Mini Band Glute Bridge is an effective lower body exercise targeting the gluteal muscles, hamstrings, and core. By using a mini resistance band placed above the knees, this variation increases muscle activation and stability demands.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a mini resistance band just above your knees.

Push through your heels to lift your hips towards the ceiling, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.

Hold for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without letting them touch the ground.

Feet positioned too close or too far from the glutes, affecting the range of motion and muscle activation.

Lifting the hips too high, causing hyperextension of the lower back and reducing glute activation.
Failing to engage the core, leading to a lack of stability and potential lower back discomfort.
Moving too quickly, sacrificing control and reducing time under tension for the glutes.
Not squeezing the glutes at the top of the movement, limiting muscle activation and growth.
Allowing the heels to lift off the ground, shifting focus away from the glutes to the calves.
Dropping the hips too quickly on the descent, reducing control and increasing the risk of injury.
exercises.name: Mini Band Glute Bridge
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to protect your lower back.
Focus on squeezing your glutes as you lift and lower your hips.
Avoid arching your back; maintain a neutral spine position.
Ensure that your knees remain aligned with your toes and do not cave inward.
Control the movement both on the way up and down for maximum effectiveness.

Bend your knees and place both feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart.
Brace your abdomen and keep your chin lightly tucked.
Press through both feet and keep pushing your knees out against the band as you lift your hips, with your upper back supported.
Finish when your shoulders, hips and knees form a line, then squeeze your glutes.
Lower your hips under control and repeat without bouncing.

Overarching the lower back at the top instead of finishing with glute squeeze and a neutral pelvis.
Flaring the ribs and losing core tension during the thrust.
Placing the feet too far forward, which shifts the work toward the hamstrings.
Placing the feet too close to the hips, which shifts the work toward the quads.
Pushing through the toes or lifting the heels instead of driving through the whole foot.
exercises.name: Mini Band Hip Thrust
tips: Exhale through the hardest part of the upward movement.
Rest the upper back on the bench edge below the shoulder blades.
Place the bench against a wall if it tends to slide.
Choose a band light enough that your knees stay apart for the whole set.
Rest your arms along the bench to help balance the movement.

instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands placed shoulder-width apart directly under your shoulders.

Drive your right knee towards your chest while keeping your left leg extended.

Hips raised too high, reducing core engagement.
Allowing the back to sag, leading to lower back strain.

Rushing the movement, sacrificing form for speed.

Engage your core throughout the exercise to prevent your hips from sagging or lifting too high.

exercises.description: Lift the barbell from the floor with an overhand grip, keeping it close to your legs. Extend your hips and knees, pull the elbows high and turn them forward to receive the bar on your shoulders while standing tall. Do not dip under the bar, and lower it under control to reset.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, with the barbell over the middle of your feet. Grip the bar just outside your legs, with your arms straight and your back neutral.
Bend your knees and hips to reach the bar, keeping your chest up, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, and weight balanced through your whole feet.
Push the floor away and lift the bar close to your legs. Extend your knees and hips together, keeping your arms straight as the bar passes your knees.
As the bar reaches mid-thigh, drive forcefully through the floor and extend your hips, knees, and ankles. Shrug your shoulders upward while keeping the bar close to your body.
Continue pulling the bar upward with your elbows high and to the sides. Do not bend your knees again to move under the bar.
When the bar reaches chest height, rotate your elbows quickly forward and bring the bar onto the front of your shoulders. Catch it standing tall, with your knees and hips extended.
Keep your elbows in front of the bar, brace your core, and stabilize the bar on your shoulders for a moment.
Lower the bar under control to your thighs and then to the floor, and reset for the next repetition.
mistakes: Starting with the bar too far from the body.
Pulling with the arms before fully extending the hips, knees, and ankles.
Letting the bar loop away from the torso instead of keeping it close.
Dropping the elbows during the pull instead of keeping them high and outside.
Dipping under the bar or bending the knees to receive it, turning it into a power clean.
Leaning backward to finish the lift instead of standing tall with the ribs controlled.
exercises.name: Muscle Clean
tips: Use a light bar or training bar first. A muscle clean is a technical lift and should not be loaded like a power clean.
Set your grip just outside your legs so the elbows have room to turn around the bar.
Connect the pull and turnover smoothly rather than pausing with the bar at your waist.
Receive the bar on the front of your shoulders with your elbows pointing forward. Keep your hands relaxed enough to allow a secure front rack.
Return the bar to the floor under control and reset before each repetition.

Engage your core throughout to maintain stability and control.

exercises.description: The Narrow Grip Australian Pull-Up With Rings is a bodyweight exercise that targets the upper back, biceps, and forearms. Walk your feet forward until your body is in a straight line from head to heels, leaning back with your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight body position.
Pull your chest towards the rings by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement when your chest is near the rings.
Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.

Pulling with shoulders instead of back, limiting effectiveness.
Inadequate range of motion, not fully extending arms.

Gripping the rings too tightly, causing forearm fatigue.
Allowing rings to rotate excessively, reducing stability.
exercises.name: Narrow Grip Australian Pull-Up With Rings
tips: Keep your body straight by engaging your core throughout the movement.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together as you pull up to maximize upper back engagement.
Maintain a controlled motion both when pulling up and lowering down to enhance muscle activation.
Ensure that your grip on the rings is firm but not overly tight to avoid unnecessary tension in the forearms.
Adjust the height of the rings or your foot position to modify the difficulty level of the exercise.

exercises.description: Press the sled of a 45-degree leg press with your feet only a few centimeters apart to shift more of the work onto your quads. Feet inside hip width keep your knees close together, so the press becomes more knee-driven: the front of your thighs works harder than in a hip-width stance, and your glutes chip in mostly at the bottom. Your back rests on the pad the whole time, which makes this a simple way to add quad sets without loading your spine. Expect to handle less weight than on your regular leg press.
instructions: Load the plates evenly on both sides of the sled, a little lighter than for your usual leg press.
Sit all the way back: hips down in the seat, back and head on the pad.
Set your feet flat and parallel mid-platform, a fist's width apart or less, toes pointing up or turned out just a touch.
Press the sled off the stops, turn the safety handles out to free it, then hold the seat handles beside your hips.
Bend your knees and lower the sled for about 2 seconds, knees side by side and traveling straight toward your chest.
Lower to about 90 degrees at the knee. Your thighs reach your ribs early, so stop before your hips lift off the seat.
Drive the sled back up through your whole foot, heels down, and stop just short of locking your knees.
At the top of the last rep, turn the safety handles back in and let the sled settle onto them.
mistakes: Feet jammed together so the knees knock or cave in as you push. Leave a small gap, about a fist's width or less, turn your toes out slightly and drive each knee over your second toe.
Tailbone curling off the seat at the bottom, because narrow feet bring your thighs to your belly sooner. End the descent just before it lifts, or move your feet a bit higher.
Heels peeling up and the push coming from your toes because the feet sit too low. Move them up until the whole foot stays flat at the bottom.
Feet sliding wider rep by rep until it turns into a regular leg press. Note where they sit against the platform edges and reset them before every set.

Loading the plates you use with a hip-width stance and cutting the depth to make it work. Strip weight until every rep reaches about 90 degrees at the knee, and keep that depth from set to set or your logged numbers won't mean much.
exercises.name: Narrow Stance 45 Degree Leg Press
tips: Use 8–15 reps here, often as the quad-focused second leg exercise after squats or a regular leg press. For strength, 6–8 works, though most lifters save their heaviest pressing for the standard stance. When all your sets reach 15 at the same depth, add 10 kg (a 5 kg plate per side) and drop back to 8; switch to 5 kg jumps when progress slows.

Foot height is a separate lever. A low and narrow stance bends the knees more and loads the quads even further, as long as your heels stay flat; moving the feet higher brings in more hip bend and more glutes.

A burn in the front of your thighs is what you're after. Pressure in your lower back means you went too deep, and a sharp pain at the front or inside of the knee usually means your knees are caving or your heels are lifting. If the narrow stance pinches your hips, widen your feet a little or go back to the standard Leg Press.

Substitutes: Leg Press (hip-width stance, easier on hips and knees), Machine Hack Squat (more upright and even more knee-driven), Lever Horizontal Leg Press, Smith Squat. To make this one harder without more plates, pause for 2 seconds at the bottom of every rep.

Place a small weight plate or resistance band across your forehead.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and your body stable throughout the exercise.
Slowly curl your chin towards your chest by flexing your neck.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the neck muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, avoiding any sudden movements.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Not keeping the chin tucked, resulting in improper neck alignment.
Lifting the head too high, causing excessive cervical spine extension.
Failing to engage neck flexor muscles, reducing exercise effectiveness.

Holding breath, increasing tension and reducing control.
exercises.name: Neck Curl

Focus on slow, controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and minimize injury risk.
Maintain a neutral spine and avoid lifting your shoulders during the exercise.
Ensure that your breathing is steady; exhale as you curl up and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Perform this exercise at the end of your workout to prevent fatigue from affecting other exercises.

Gently tilt your head to one side, bringing your ear towards your shoulder without lifting the shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull along the side of your neck.
Return your head to the neutral position and repeat on the opposite side.

Lifting the shoulder towards the ear, reducing the effectiveness of the stretch.
Twisting the neck instead of maintaining a straight side tilt.
Failing to keep the spine aligned, leading to improper posture.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement, risking muscle strain.

Not engaging the core, resulting in instability and poor form.
Stretching only one side, leading to muscle imbalance.

Neglecting to engage the back muscles, relying too much on the arms.
