exercises.description: Perform a push-up with an explosive press that briefly lifts both hands off the floor. Keep the body aligned from head to heels and bend the elbows as the hands land back in place. This bodyweight pressing movement develops upper-body power and controlled absorption of the landing, without a clap.
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width, arms straight, legs extended, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your stomach, squeeze your glutes, and keep your neck neutral by looking slightly ahead of your hands.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them angled about 30 to 45 degrees from your body.
Push through your palms as forcefully as possible to drive your upper body away from the floor.
Allow your hands to leave the floor briefly, then prepare to absorb the landing with soft elbows.
Land with your hands in the same position, bend your elbows to cushion the impact, and immediately move into the next repetition.
mistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides instead of keeping them slightly angled back
Lowering only a few centimeters and skipping a controlled full range of motion
Dropping the chest too quickly and losing tension at the bottom
Pushing off unevenly, causing one shoulder or hand to take more load
Landing with locked elbows instead of absorbing the landing with soft elbows
Landing with the hands too far forward or too wide, which can stress the shoulders
Allowing the head to jut forward instead of keeping the neck neutral
exercises.name: Plyometric Push-Up
tips: Start in a strong high-plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width, your body in one line from head to heels, and your core and glutes braced.
Drive forcefully through the floor to lift your hands off the ground. Think about pushing the floor away fast, not just trying to jump high.
Use a small hand lift at first. Quality and controlled landings matter more than height or clapping.
Stop the set when you can no longer land quietly and maintain a stable plank. Fatigue can increase stress on the wrists, elbows, and shoulders.
Perform these early in your workout while you are fresh, using low to moderate repetitions with full rest between sets to maintain power.

exercises.description: Pogo Jumps are a plyometric exercise designed to improve lower body explosiveness, agility, and coordination. This exercise primarily targets the calves, but also engages the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. It is performed by bouncing off the ground with minimal knee bend, focusing on quick and repetitive movements.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Begin by bouncing off the balls of your feet, keeping your knees slightly bent.
Use minimal knee flexion to propel yourself upward quickly.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and immediately rebound into the next jump.
Maintain a steady rhythm and focus on quick, controlled movements.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions or time duration.
mistakes: Landing with flat feet instead of on the balls of the feet, reducing spring effect and increasing impact on joints.
Allowing knees to cave inward during jumps, leading to poor alignment and potential knee strain.
Failing to engage the core muscles, resulting in a lack of stability and control during the exercise.
Using excessive arm movement, which can throw off balance and reduce efficiency of the jump.
Not maintaining a consistent rhythm, causing uneven jumps and increased risk of losing balance.
Jumping too high, which can lead to loss of control and improper landing mechanics.
Neglecting to keep the chest up and shoulders back, which can lead to a hunched posture and reduced power output.
Landing with locked knees, increasing the risk of joint strain and reducing shock absorption.
exercises.name: Pogo Jumps
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain balance.
Focus on landing softly to reduce impact on your joints.
Use your arms to help maintain rhythm and balance.
Start with a small range of motion and gradually increase as you become more comfortable.
Ensure that your knees remain slightly bent to absorb shock effectively.
Perform this exercise on a flat, stable surface to prevent injury.
Incorporate Pogo Jumps into your warm-up routine to activate lower body muscles.

exercises.description: Poliquin flys, also known as Poliquin dumbbell flys, are a variation of the traditional dumbbell fly exercise. This movement targets the pectoral muscles with a unique angle and range of motion, emphasizing the stretch and contraction phases. It is performed on an incline bench to increase the activation of the upper chest fibers.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 30-45 degree angle.
Sit on the bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Lie back on the bench, keeping your feet flat on the floor and your back pressed against the bench.
Extend your arms above your chest with a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells slowly in an arc motion to the sides until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring tension remains in your chest.
Bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles together.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing the elbows to drop below shoulder level, reducing tension on the chest.
Arching the lower back excessively, leading to poor core engagement.
Using momentum to swing the weights, compromising muscle control.
Failing to maintain a slight bend in the elbows, increasing shoulder strain.
Not keeping the wrists neutral, risking unnecessary joint stress.
Bringing the weights too close together at the top, reducing chest activation.
Descending too quickly, losing control and risking shoulder injury.
Neglecting to engage the scapula, limiting chest muscle recruitment.
exercises.name: Poliquin Flyes
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to protect your joints.
Focus on controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and minimize injury risk.
Keep your shoulder blades retracted and pressed against the bench to stabilize your upper body.
Avoid using too much weight; prioritize form and muscle contraction over heavy loads.
Breathe out as you lift the weights and breathe in as you lower them.
Ensure that your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms during the exercise.

exercises.description: The Poliquin Step-Up is a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. It is performed with a focus on controlled movement and balance, enhancing knee stability and strength. This exercise is named after Charles Poliquin, a renowned strength coach, and is particularly effective for athletes looking to improve their leg power and knee health.
instructions: Stand facing a bench or step with your feet hip-width apart.
Place one foot on the bench, ensuring your entire foot is flat and stable.
Push through the heel of the foot on the bench to lift your body upward.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward excessively.
Bring the trailing leg up to tap the bench lightly without placing weight on it.
Lower the trailing leg back to the ground in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
mistakes: Allowing the knee to collapse inward, leading to poor alignment and reduced effectiveness.
Pushing off with the back leg instead of using the lead leg to drive the movement.
Failing to maintain a neutral spine, resulting in unnecessary strain on the lower back.
Using momentum to swing the body up rather than controlled muscle engagement.
Not keeping the heel of the lead foot flat on the step, which can reduce stability and effectiveness.
Leaning too far forward, which shifts the focus away from the target muscles.
Not fully extending the lead leg at the top of the movement, limiting range of motion.
Allowing the toes of the lead foot to point outward, affecting knee alignment and muscle activation.
exercises.name: Poliquin Step-Up
tips: Ensure the bench or step is at a height where your knee is at or slightly below hip level when stepping up.
Focus on pushing through the heel of the working leg to engage the glutes effectively.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement to prevent lower back strain.
Control the descent to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Start with body weight and progress to holding dumbbells as you become more comfortable with the exercise.
Keep your core engaged to aid in balance and stability during the movement.

exercises.description: The Dumbbell Powell Raise is an isolation exercise targeting the rear deltoids, part of the shoulder muscle group. It is performed with a single dumbbell, focusing on shoulder stabilization and control. This exercise helps improve shoulder symmetry and posture by strengthening the often underdeveloped rear deltoids.
instructions: Begin by lying on your side on a bench, with your upper body supported and your lower body hanging off the edge.
Hold a dumbbell in your top hand with a neutral grip (palm facing down) and let it hang straight down from your shoulder.
Keep your core engaged and your body stable throughout the movement.
Slowly raise the dumbbell upward in an arc until your arm is parallel to the ground, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring you feel the contraction in your rear deltoid.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
mistakes: Lifting the arm too high, causing shoulder impingement.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement.
Allowing the torso to rotate, losing isolation of the rear deltoid.
Failing to keep the arm slightly bent, putting strain on the elbow.
Engaging the trapezius instead of focusing on the rear deltoid.
Not maintaining a stable position with the supporting hand and knee.
Performing the exercise too quickly, reducing muscle engagement.
Neglecting to keep the head and neck in a neutral position.
exercises.name: Powell Raise
tips: Focus on maintaining a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid using momentum or swinging the weight; this ensures that the rear deltoids are doing most of the work.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them during the lift to prevent tension in the neck.
Ensure that your core is tight to stabilize your body and prevent unnecessary movement.
Start with a lighter weight to master form before progressing to heavier loads.
Breathe out as you lift the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it back down.

exercises.description: The power clean is a dynamic, full-body exercise that primarily targets the muscles of the posterior chain, including the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back, while also engaging the shoulders, traps, and core. It is a compound movement that involves lifting a barbell from the floor to the shoulders in one explosive motion. The power clean is commonly used to develop strength, power, and coordination.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and position the barbell over the mid-foot. Bend at the hips and knees to grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set your back by pulling your shoulder blades together and maintaining a neutral spine. Your chest should be up and your gaze forward.
Initiate the lift by extending your hips and knees simultaneously, keeping the bar close to your body as you pull it upwards.
As the bar passes your knees, explosively extend your hips and shrug your shoulders to accelerate the bar upward.
Quickly drop under the bar by bending your knees and catching it on your shoulders in a front rack position with elbows high.
Stand up fully to complete the lift, ensuring the bar is stable on your shoulders before lowering it back to the starting position.
mistakes: Starting with hips too low, resembling a squat rather than a hinge.
Pulling with the arms instead of driving with the legs and hips.
Not fully extending the hips, knees, and ankles in the triple extension phase.
Catching the bar with elbows pointing down instead of forward.
Failing to keep the barbell close to the body during the lift.
Using an incorrect grip width, either too wide or too narrow.
Landing with feet too wide or unevenly during the catch phase.
Not maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Rushing the transition from the pull to the catch, leading to poor control.
Neglecting to engage the core, resulting in instability.
exercises.name: Power Clean
tips: Keep the bar close to your body throughout the lift to maintain control and efficiency.
Focus on a powerful hip extension to generate maximum force during the pull phase.
Practice proper breathing: inhale before lifting and exhale as you catch the bar on your shoulders.
Ensure your elbows are high in the front rack position to support the weight effectively.
Start with lighter weights to master technique before progressing to heavier loads.
Engage your core throughout the movement to protect your lower back.

exercises.description: Start with the barbell resting on the front of your shoulders. Dip briefly with an upright torso, drive through your legs and receive the bar overhead with straight arms in a shallow squat, keeping the feet parallel. Stabilize the bar, stand fully upright and lower it back to the shoulders with control.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip width apart. Grip the bar just outside your shoulders, with elbows slightly in front of the bar and your chest lifted.
Take the bar out of the rack and step back. Keep the bar resting on the front of your shoulders, brace your core, and keep your eyes forward.
Dip straight down by bending your knees and hips slightly. Keep your torso upright, your heels on the floor, and let your knees track over your toes.
Immediately drive hard through the floor with your legs. Extend your hips, knees, and ankles to accelerate the bar upward.
Move quickly under the rising bar and receive it in a shallow squat with both feet parallel.
Lock your arms fully overhead. Keep the bar directly over the middle of your feet, with your head slightly forward between your arms and your shoulders active.
Stabilize the catch position, then stand fully upright with the bar locked overhead. Your knees and hips should be fully extended before lowering the bar.
Lower the bar under control back to your shoulders, bending your knees slightly to absorb the weight. Reset your position before the next repetition.
mistakes: Dipping with the knees collapsing inward instead of tracking over the toes.
Leaning forward or letting the heels lift during the dip.
Pressing the bar out with the arms before fully extending the hips and knees.
Driving the bar forward instead of straight up over the midfoot.
Receiving the bar with bent elbows instead of locking out overhead.
Failing to re-bend the knees to receive the bar, forcing the arms to press out a heavy load.
Relaxing the core and letting the ribs flare as the bar reaches overhead.
exercises.name: Power Jerk
tips: Start with the bar in the front rack, resting on the shoulders with elbows slightly in front of the bar and hands relaxed enough to let the bar sit on the shoulders.
Set your feet about hip width apart, brace your trunk, and keep your weight balanced through the whole foot before the dip.
Practice the timing with an empty bar before adding load.
Use a wider receiving stance if needed, but land with both feet at the same time and maintain even pressure through both feet.
Stabilize overhead before standing fully upright; lower the bar to your shoulders with soft knees.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/力量抓举-2

exercises.description: Stand with the barbell over mid-foot, grip wide, and keep your back neutral. Drive through the floor with the legs, extending the hips and knees powerfully while keeping the bar close to the body. Shrug and pull under the bar, then catch it overhead in a partial squat with locked elbows and an active shoulder position. Stand tall under control, then lower the bar safely and reset.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, with the barbell over the middle of your feet. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width using a hook grip if comfortable.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees until your shoulders are slightly in front of the bar. Keep your chest up, back neutral, arms straight, and eyes forward.
Push through the floor to lift the bar smoothly, keeping it close to your shins and thighs. Extend your knees first while maintaining your back angle.
As the bar passes your knees, forcefully extend your hips, knees, and ankles, driving upward explosively and shrugging your shoulders while keeping the bar close to your body.
Pull yourself under the bar by quickly rotating your elbows underneath it, then catch the bar overhead with locked arms in a partial squat. Keep your torso upright and knees tracking over your toes.
Stabilize the bar directly over your shoulders and mid-foot, then stand fully upright with your hips and knees locked out.
Lower the bar under control to the hips and then to the floor, or drop it safely if using appropriate bumper plates and a designated lifting area.
mistakes: Starting with the hips too low or too high, causing poor bar path and loss of leg drive.
Letting the bar drift away from the body instead of keeping it close through the pull.
Pulling with the arms too early before fully extending the hips, knees, and ankles.
Failing to reach full extension through the hips and ankles before pulling under the bar.
Swinging or looping the bar forward instead of pulling it vertically close to the torso.
Jumping forward or backward during the pull instead of moving the feet into a stable receiving position.
Catching the bar with bent elbows rather than locking the arms overhead quickly.
Receiving the bar with the shoulders relaxed instead of actively pushing up into the bar.
Catching with the bar in front of the head rather than stacked over the mid-foot.
Overarching the lower back overhead instead of keeping the ribs down and torso braced.
Dropping into an excessively deep squat rather than receiving in a controlled partial squat.
Pressing the bar overhead after the catch instead of securing it in one smooth movement.
exercises.name: Power Snatch
tips: Start with the bar over the mid-foot, feet about hip-width apart, and use a hook grip if it is comfortable and appropriate for your hands.
Set your back tight with a neutral spine, chest proud, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, and arms fully straight before initiating the pull.
Push through the floor with your legs during the first pull, keeping the bar close to your shins and avoiding an early arm bend.
As the bar passes the knees, sweep it back toward your body and keep your balance over the whole foot rather than shifting excessively onto the toes.
Accelerate violently through the hips, knees, and ankles in the second pull, finishing tall before pulling yourself under the bar.
Keep the barbell close to the body throughout the lift; a looping bar path makes the catch less stable and places unnecessary stress on the shoulders.
After full extension, actively pull under the bar and rotate the elbows quickly to receive it overhead with locked arms.
Catch the bar in a partial squat with the feet flat, knees tracking over the toes, torso braced, and the bar directly above or slightly behind the crown of the head.
Use an overhead position with active shoulders: press up into the bar, keep the upper back engaged, and avoid allowing the bar to drift forward.
Stand up under control after the catch, maintaining a rigid trunk and balanced overhead position before lowering or dropping the bar safely.
Practice first with a PVC pipe, empty bar, or light load to develop timing and positions; increase weight only when the bar path and overhead catch remain consistent.
Perform power snatches in an open area with suitable bumper plates and a platform when possible, and do not attempt to save a missed lift by chasing a falling bar.

exercises.description: The Preacher Hammer Curl is an isolation exercise targeting the brachialis and brachioradialis muscles of the upper arm. It is performed using a preacher bench, which stabilizes the arms and minimizes momentum, allowing for focused contraction of the target muscles. This exercise is typically performed with dumbbells or a specialized hammer curl bar.
instructions: Adjust the seat height of the preacher bench so that your upper arms rest comfortably on the padding.
Sit on the bench and grip a pair of dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Position your upper arms on the preacher bench pad, ensuring your elbows are slightly bent to maintain tension.
Begin with your arms fully extended downward, holding the dumbbells.
Curl the weights upward by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary on the pad.
Raise the dumbbells until your forearms are vertical or just before they reach full contraction.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Elbows flaring out, reducing bicep engagement.
Using momentum by swinging the weights, leading to poor muscle activation.
Not fully extending the arms, limiting the range of motion.
Lifting the shoulders, which can cause strain and reduce bicep isolation.
Bending the wrists, which shifts the focus away from the biceps.
Leaning back, which can lead to improper form and decreased effectiveness.
Allowing the weights to drop quickly, reducing time under tension.
Not maintaining a neutral grip, which can affect muscle engagement.
exercises.name: Preacher Hammer Curl
tips: Focus on keeping your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms to prevent strain.
Avoid using momentum; perform each repetition in a slow and controlled manner.
Ensure that your shoulders remain relaxed and do not lift off the bench during the exercise.
Breathe out as you curl the weights up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Start with a lighter weight to master form before progressing to heavier loads.
Keep your core engaged to maintain stability throughout the movement.

exercises.description: A bodyweight back exercise done face down on the floor. With your chest lifted, you reach your arms forward past your head, then pull your elbows down and back to your ribs as in a lat pulldown, squeeze your upper back and reach out again. Your legs stay on the floor with the toes tucked.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your legs straight and your toes tucked under.
Lift your chest slightly off the floor and reach both arms forward past your head, hands off the floor.
Pull your elbows down and back toward your ribs, as if pulling a bar to your upper chest.
Finish with your elbows by your sides and your hands near your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades down and together.
Hold for a moment while keeping your chest lifted.
Reach your arms forward again until they are straight.
Keep your chest and arms off the floor for the whole set, then lower down.
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift the chest higher.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
Letting the arms rest on the floor between repetitions.
Stopping the elbows short of the ribs.
Not straightening the arms fully at the front.
Lifting the head to look forward, which strains the neck.
Swinging the arms instead of pulling with the back.
exercises.name: Prone Lat Pulldown
tips: Lead with your elbows; your hands simply follow.
Imagine squeezing a pencil between your shoulder blades at the end of the pull.
Hold the end position for one to two seconds to feel your back working.
Squeeze your glutes and keep your legs on the floor for a stable base.
Breathe out as you pull and breathe in as you reach forward.

exercises.description: The Prone Lying Leg Curl is an isolation exercise targeting the hamstrings. It involves flexing the knees against resistance while lying face down on a leg curl machine. This exercise helps in strengthening the hamstrings, improving knee joint stability, and enhancing overall lower body performance.
instructions: Adjust the leg curl machine so that the roller pad sits comfortably just above your heels when you are lying face down.
Lie prone on the machine, ensuring your knees are aligned with the pivot point of the machine.
Grip the handles or sides of the bench for stability.
Engage your core and keep your hips pressed against the bench.
Exhale and curl your legs by bending your knees, bringing your heels towards your glutes.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring maximum contraction in the hamstrings.
Inhale and slowly lower your legs back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
exercises.name: Prone Lying Leg Curl
tips: Ensure the roller pad is positioned correctly to avoid unnecessary strain on your knees.
Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle engagement and reduce injury risk.
Avoid lifting your hips off the bench during the exercise to maintain proper form.
Focus on squeezing your hamstrings at the top of each repetition for optimal contraction.
Start with a lighter weight to perfect your form before progressing to heavier loads.
Maintain a neutral spine by keeping your head aligned with your spine throughout the exercise.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/俯卧肩关节控制性旋转

exercises.description: A shoulder mobility drill done lying face down. Both arms move together from the hands behind your head, out wide to the sides and around to your lower back, then back along the same path. Keep the torso still so the motion comes only from the shoulders.
instructions: Lie face down with your legs straight and both hands on the back of your head, elbows out to the sides.
Keep your hips and legs on the floor and your neck long, with your eyes on the floor.
Slowly move both arms out to the sides, straightening your elbows until your arms form a T with your hands just above the floor.
Keep sweeping your arms toward your hips, then bend your elbows and turn your arms inward to rest your hands on your lower back.
Reverse the path: straighten your arms out to the sides, then bend your elbows and bring your hands back behind your head.
Repeat at a slow, even pace, keeping your torso still throughout.
mistakes: Swinging the arms quickly through the arc.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
Arching the lower back or lifting the chest high to gain range.
Letting the hands drop and drag on the floor as the arms pass the sides.
Cranking the neck up or pushing the head forward.
Rolling the torso to one side when the hands reach the lower back.
exercises.name: Prone Shoulder CARs
tips: Reach long through your fingertips when your arms are out to the sides.
Squeeze your glutes lightly to keep your lower back neutral.
Work in the largest range you can control. Shorten it if you feel a pinch at the front of the shoulder.
Let your shoulder blades glide with your arms instead of locking them in place.
Breathe steadily throughout the set.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/俯卧游泳者

exercises.description: The Prone Swimmer is a bodyweight exercise that targets the muscles of the upper back, shoulders, and core. It mimics the swimming motion while lying face down, enhancing shoulder mobility and stability. This exercise is beneficial for improving posture and strengthening the posterior chain.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended straight overhead and legs fully extended.
Keep your forehead gently resting on the ground to maintain a neutral neck position.
Engage your core muscles to stabilize your torso throughout the movement.
Simultaneously lift your right arm and left leg off the ground, keeping them straight.
Lower them back to the starting position and immediately lift your left arm and right leg.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled manner, simulating a swimming motion.
Perform the exercise for a set number of repetitions or time duration.
mistakes: Lifting the head too high, causing neck strain.
Arching the lower back excessively, leading to discomfort.
Failing to engage the core, resulting in poor stability.
Moving arms and legs too quickly, reducing control.
Allowing the hips to sway, disrupting alignment.
Not fully extending the arms and legs, limiting range of motion.
Holding the breath, causing unnecessary tension.
Dropping the chest to the floor, compromising posture.
Neglecting to engage the glutes, weakening lower body involvement.
Failing to synchronize arm and leg movements, leading to imbalance.
exercises.name: Prone Swimmer
tips: Focus on keeping your movements smooth and controlled to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid lifting your head or arching your back excessively; maintain a neutral spine throughout.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your limbs and inhaling as you lower them.
If you experience discomfort in your lower back, reduce the range of motion or perform the exercise on a softer surface.
To increase difficulty, hold each lift for a moment before switching sides.
Ensure that your movements are symmetrical to prevent imbalances in muscle development.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/俯卧t字抬臂

exercises.description: A bodyweight exercise for the middle trapezius, rhomboids and rear shoulders, done lying face down on the floor. With straight arms out to the sides at shoulder height and thumbs up, your body forms a T. You squeeze your shoulder blades together, lift the arms off the floor and lower them slowly.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or a mat with your legs straight and your forehead just above the floor.
Extend your arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height so your body forms a T, with thumbs pointing up.
Brace your abs lightly and set your shoulder blades down.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and lift both straight arms off the floor.
Raise them as high as you can without shrugging or arching your lower back.
Hold the top for a second, then lower your arms slowly to the floor and repeat.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears instead of squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Arching the lower back or lifting the chest to raise the arms higher.
Bending the elbows, which shortens the lever and makes the lift easier.
Letting the arms drift toward the head or the hips, losing the T.
Turning the thumbs down, which rolls the shoulders forward.
Lifting the head to look forward instead of keeping the neck neutral.
Swinging the arms up quickly instead of lifting and lowering under control.
exercises.name: Prone T Raise
tips: Lift both arms to the same height so one side does not do more of the work.
Reach your fingertips out to the sides as you lift to keep the arms long.
Keep your legs and hips on the floor so the work stays in your upper back.
Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
A small range done slowly works better than a high lift with your neck tense.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/俯卧w字抬臂

exercises.description: A bodyweight exercise for the middle trapezius, rhomboids and rear shoulders, done lying face down on the floor. With elbows bent and hands beside your head so your arms form a W, you squeeze your shoulder blades together and lift your elbows and hands off the floor, then lower them slowly.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or a mat with your legs straight and your forehead just above the floor.
Bend your elbows and place your hands on the floor beside your head, palms down, so your arms form a W.
Keep your elbows out to the sides, a little below shoulder height.
Brace your abs lightly and set your shoulder blades down.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and lift your elbows, forearms and hands off the floor at the same time.
Hold the top for a second, then lower your arms slowly to the floor and repeat.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears instead of squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Arching the lower back or lifting the chest off the floor.
Straightening the arms or sliding the hands away from the head, losing the W.
Lifting only the hands while the elbows stay on the floor.
Lifting the head to look forward instead of keeping the neck neutral.
Dropping the arms quickly instead of lowering them under control.
exercises.name: Prone W Raise
tips: Squeeze your shoulder blades as if trapping a pencil between them.
As you lift, think of drawing your elbows down and back toward your hips.
Keep your legs and hips on the floor so the work stays in your upper back.
Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
A lift of a few centimetres is enough when your shoulder blades are fully squeezed.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/俯卧y字抬臂

exercises.description: A bodyweight exercise for the lower trapezius and rear shoulders, done lying face down on the floor. With straight arms overhead in a Y and thumbs pointing up, you lift the arms off the floor using the muscles around your shoulder blades, then lower them slowly.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or a mat with your legs straight and your forehead just above the floor.
Extend your arms overhead in a Y, about 30 degrees out from your head, with thumbs pointing up.
Brace your abs lightly and set your shoulder blades down and back.
Lift both straight arms off the floor as high as you can without shrugging or arching your lower back.
Hold the top for a second and squeeze the muscles below your shoulder blades.
Lower your arms slowly to the floor and repeat.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears, which shifts the work to the upper traps.
Arching the lower back or lifting the chest to raise the arms higher.
Bending the elbows and turning the lift into a row.
Letting the arms drift wide into a T or close to the head, losing the Y.
Lifting the head to look forward instead of keeping the neck neutral.
Turning the thumbs down, which rolls the shoulders forward.
Swinging the arms up quickly instead of lifting and lowering under control.
exercises.name: Prone Y Raise
tips: Think of pulling your shoulder blades toward your back pockets as you lift.
Reach long through your thumbs, as if your hands were being pulled away from your shoulders.
Keep your legs and hips on the floor so the work stays in your upper back.
Exhale as you lift and inhale as you lower.
A small range done slowly works better than a high lift with your neck tense.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/雪橇推车

exercises.description: The Prowler Sled is a versatile piece of equipment used for strength and conditioning. It involves pushing or pulling a weighted sled across a surface, engaging multiple muscle groups including the legs, core, and upper body. This exercise is excellent for building power, endurance, and cardiovascular fitness.
instructions: Begin by loading the sled with an appropriate amount of weight. Start light if you are new to this exercise.
Position yourself behind the sled. Place your hands on the handles or the horizontal bar, depending on the sled design.
Adopt a forward-leaning stance with your back straight and core engaged. Keep your feet shoulder-width apart.
Drive through your legs and push the sled forward using powerful strides. Maintain a steady pace and control throughout.
To pull the sled, attach straps to the sled and hold them securely. Walk backward or forward while pulling, keeping your core tight and movements controlled.
mistakes: Leaning too far forward, causing loss of balance and control.
Using arms to push instead of engaging the core and legs.
Hips rising too high, reducing power output and efficiency.
Feet too close together, leading to instability.
Taking overly long strides, causing loss of momentum.
Allowing the back to round, increasing risk of lower back strain.
Pushing with locked elbows, reducing force generation.
Neglecting to maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Failing to engage glutes, limiting power and speed.
Starting with too much weight, compromising form and control.
exercises.name: Prowler Sled
tips: Focus on maintaining a strong core throughout the movement to prevent lower back strain.
Keep your strides consistent and avoid overextending your legs; this helps maintain balance and control.
Start with lighter weights to perfect your form before increasing the load.
Ensure you have enough space to perform the exercise safely, free from obstacles.
Use this exercise as part of a circuit for conditioning or as a standalone for strength building.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/环绕拉动

exercises.description: The Pull Around is an isolation exercise primarily targeting the latissimus dorsi, with secondary engagement of the rear deltoids and rhomboids. It involves a cable machine and is performed with a single handle attachment, emphasizing a wide range of motion to effectively stretch and contract the lats.
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley on a cable machine.
Stand sideways to the machine, holding the handle with the hand furthest from the machine.
Step away from the machine to create tension in the cable, keeping your feet shoulder-width apart.
Start with your arm extended across your body, palm facing down.
Pull the handle in an arc across your body and upwards, keeping your arm slightly bent.
Focus on squeezing your lats as you pull, stopping when your hand reaches shoulder height.
Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
mistakes: Using too much weight, leading to momentum-driven movement instead of controlled execution.
Allowing the elbows to flare out excessively, reducing target muscle engagement.
Failing to maintain a stable core, resulting in unnecessary torso movement.
Not keeping the shoulders down and back, causing strain on the neck and upper traps.
Performing the exercise too quickly, compromising form and muscle activation.
Neglecting to engage the lats, shifting the focus away from the intended muscles.
Starting the movement from the wrong position, which can lead to improper range of motion.
Overextending the arms during the pull, risking shoulder joint strain.
exercises.name: Pull Around
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the exercise to reduce strain on the joint.
Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body and prevent unwanted movement.
Focus on a slow and controlled motion, especially during the eccentric phase as you return to the starting position.
Visualize pulling with your back muscles rather than your arm to maximize lat engagement.
Ensure that your shoulder remains down and back during the movement to avoid unnecessary strain.
Adjust the weight so that you can perform the exercise with proper form for all repetitions.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/引体向上

exercises.description: The pull-up is a compound upper-body exercise that primarily targets the latissimus dorsi muscles in the back, along with the biceps, forearms, shoulders, and core. It involves pulling your body up towards a bar until your chin is above it, using an overhand grip.
instructions: Stand under a pull-up bar and reach up to grasp it with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body straight as you hang from the bar with your arms fully extended.
Initiate the movement by pulling your shoulder blades down and back, then pull your body upwards by bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, keeping your chest open and shoulders away from your ears.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using momentum by swinging or kipping instead of controlled movement.
Not engaging the core, leading to an arched back.
Failing to achieve full range of motion by not lowering completely or not bringing chin above the bar.
Gripping the bar too tightly, causing forearm fatigue and reducing pull efficiency.
Letting shoulders shrug up towards ears instead of keeping them down and back.
Pulling with the arms instead of engaging the back muscles.
Crossing legs or bending knees excessively, which can destabilize the body.
Not maintaining a neutral head position, leading to neck strain.
Allowing elbows to flare out too much, reducing lat engagement.
Rushing the eccentric phase, missing out on muscle engagement and control.
exercises.name: Pull-Up
tips: Focus on engaging your back muscles rather than relying solely on your arms to pull yourself up.
Maintain a tight core throughout the exercise to prevent swinging or arching of the back.
If you're unable to perform a full pull-up, start with assisted variations using resistance bands or an assisted pull-up machine.
Avoid using momentum; perform each repetition in a controlled manner for maximum muscle engagement.
Ensure that you breathe out as you pull yourself up and inhale as you lower yourself down.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/宽握引体向上

exercises.description: The Pull-Up Wide Grip is a compound upper body exercise that primarily targets the latissimus dorsi muscles in the back, while also engaging the biceps, shoulders, and core. This variation uses a wider grip than the standard pull-up, which increases the emphasis on the outer portions of the lats and can help in building a broader back.
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and reach up to grasp it with an overhand grip, hands positioned wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back to stabilize your upper body.
Initiate the pull by driving your elbows down towards your sides, lifting your body until your chin is above the bar.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the back muscles.
Lower yourself in a controlled manner back to the starting position with arms fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Gripping the bar too wide, which can reduce range of motion and strain the shoulders.
Failing to engage the core, leading to swinging or kipping during the movement.
Not pulling the chest up to the bar, resulting in incomplete range of motion.
Allowing the shoulders to shrug, which decreases lat engagement and increases neck tension.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement, reducing muscle activation.
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom, limiting the exercise's effectiveness.
Pulling with the arms instead of initiating the movement with the back muscles.
Tilting the head up, which can strain the neck and disrupt alignment.
Allowing the elbows to flare excessively, reducing lat activation and increasing shoulder stress.
exercises.name: Pull-Up Wide Grip
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together as you pull up to maximize lat engagement.
Avoid swinging or using momentum; maintain a controlled movement throughout the exercise.
If you struggle with full pull-ups, consider using an assisted pull-up machine or resistance bands for support.
Ensure your grip is secure but not overly tight to prevent unnecessary forearm fatigue.
Keep your body straight and avoid arching your back during the movement to maintain proper form.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/沙袋拳击

exercises.description: Punching Bag Boxing is a cardiovascular and strength training exercise that involves striking a heavy bag with various punches. This exercise improves hand-eye coordination, builds upper body strength, enhances cardiovascular endurance, and helps in stress relief. It engages muscles in the shoulders, arms, chest, and core.
instructions: Stand in a boxing stance with your feet shoulder-width apart, dominant foot slightly back.
Keep your knees slightly bent and weight balanced on the balls of your feet.
Raise your hands to chin level, elbows close to your body, and fists clenched.
Start with basic punches: jab with your lead hand, cross with your rear hand.
Rotate your hips and shoulders for power while keeping your core engaged.
Maintain a steady rhythm and breathe consistently throughout the exercise.
Incorporate combinations of punches such as jab-cross, hook, and uppercut.
Focus on accuracy and speed rather than just power.
mistakes: Standing too close to the bag, limiting punch extension and power.
Leaning forward excessively, causing imbalance and reduced mobility.
Failing to keep hands up, leaving the face unprotected.
Punching with locked elbows, increasing joint strain.
Neglecting to rotate hips and shoulders, reducing punch effectiveness.
Overextending punches, risking shoulder strain.
Not engaging core muscles, leading to poor stability.
Dropping hands after punching, creating openings for counterattacks.
Standing flat-footed, hindering quick movement and agility.
Punching without proper wrist alignment, increasing risk of wrist injury.
Ignoring breathing rhythm, leading to early fatigue.
exercises.name: Punching Bag Boxing
tips: Ensure your wrists are straight when making contact with the bag to avoid injury.
Keep your movements fluid and controlled for better technique and efficiency.
Warm up thoroughly before starting to prevent muscle strain or injury.
Use wraps or gloves to protect your hands and wrists during the workout.
Practice footwork alongside punching to improve agility and balance.
Start slowly to focus on form before increasing speed or intensity.
Stay relaxed; tension can reduce speed and increase fatigue.
Regularly switch up combinations to keep the workout challenging and engaging.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/俯卧撑

exercises.description: The push-up is a bodyweight exercise that primarily targets the chest, triceps, and shoulders. It also engages the core and stabilizing muscles, making it a comprehensive upper body workout. Push-ups can be performed anywhere and are fundamental for building strength and endurance.
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core by pulling your belly button towards your spine to maintain a neutral spine position.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your torso. Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then push through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the starting position.
Ensure that your body remains in a straight line throughout the movement without sagging or arching your back.
mistakes: Allowing hips to sag, leading to lower back strain.
Flaring elbows out too wide, increasing shoulder stress.
Not maintaining a straight line from head to heels.
Failing to engage core muscles, compromising stability.
Inadequate range of motion, not lowering chest fully to the ground.
Hands positioned too far forward, reducing chest engagement.
Neck craning or looking up, causing neck strain.
Rushing through reps, sacrificing form for speed.
Locking elbows at the top, losing muscle tension.
Uneven weight distribution, favoring one side.
exercises.name: Push-Up
tips: Keep your elbows at a 45-degree angle to protect your shoulders and maximize chest engagement.
Maintain a tight core throughout the exercise to prevent your hips from sagging.
Focus on controlled movements; avoid bouncing off the floor at the bottom of the push-up.
If you struggle with full push-ups, start with knee push-ups or incline push-ups to build strength.
Breathe in as you lower yourself and exhale as you push back up.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/双杠俯卧撑

exercises.description: The push-up on parallel bars is a compound upper body exercise that primarily targets the chest, triceps, and shoulders. It involves supporting your body weight on parallel bars and lowering your chest towards the bars before pushing back up to the starting position. This exercise enhances upper body strength, stability, and muscle endurance.
instructions: Position yourself between the parallel bars, gripping each bar firmly with your palms facing inward.
Extend your arms fully to lift your body off the ground, keeping your legs straight and feet together.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement.
Slowly bend your elbows to lower your chest towards the bars until your elbows reach approximately a 90-degree angle.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring control and stability.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing hips to sag or rise, compromising core engagement and alignment.
Flared elbows, increasing shoulder strain and reducing tricep activation.
Incomplete range of motion, preventing full muscle engagement.
Rushing the movement, leading to loss of control and form.
Neglecting to keep shoulders down and back, causing neck tension.
Failing to maintain a straight line from head to heels, affecting posture.
Hands positioned too wide or too narrow, altering muscle focus.
Not engaging the chest and triceps fully, reducing exercise effectiveness.
exercises.name: Push-Up on Parallel Bars
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body to maximize tricep engagement and reduce shoulder strain.
Maintain a neutral spine by engaging your core muscles throughout the exercise.
Control the descent to avoid dropping too quickly, which can lead to injury.
Focus on a full range of motion for maximum muscle activation.
If you're new to this exercise, consider using resistance bands for assistance or performing negative repetitions to build strength gradually.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/俯卧撑加肩胛前伸

exercises.description: The push-up plus combines a full push-up with an extra shoulder blade movement that works the serratus anterior. Lower your chest toward the floor, press back to straight arms, then push the floor farther away to spread your shoulder blades while keeping your trunk aligned.
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, arms straight, legs extended and feet about hip-width apart.
Brace your abdomen, squeeze your glutes and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor as in a standard push-up. Keep your elbows angled slightly back rather than flared wide.
Press through your palms to return to the top position with your elbows fully straight.
Without bending your elbows, push the floor away further by spreading your shoulder blades apart and lifting your upper back slightly toward the ceiling.
Keep your neck neutral and avoid letting your hips sag, rise or rotate during the extra shoulder blade movement.
Pause briefly at the top of the shoulder blade protraction, then let your shoulder blades return to neutral and repeat.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike instead of keeping a straight line from head to heels.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears instead of keeping the neck long and shoulders controlled.
Flaring the elbows wide during the push-up portion instead of keeping them angled slightly back.
Skipping the final shoulder blade protraction at the top of each rep.
Bending the elbows during the plus phase instead of pushing the floor away with straight arms.
Letting the head jut forward instead of keeping it aligned with the spine.
exercises.name: Push-Up Plus
tips: Exhale through the hardest part of the upward movement.
Spread your fingers and distribute pressure across both palms.
Use knee support to practise the movement with a lighter load.
Notice the effort along the sides of your ribs during the final push.
Use a firm surface with enough grip for both palms.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/俯卧撑接侧平板支撑

exercises.description: This exercise combines a floor push-up with a side plank, working the chest, arms and trunk. After pressing up, rotate onto one hand and the sides of the feet, reaching the free arm upward; return to the push-up position and alternate the direction of rotation on successive repetitions.
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, legs straight, feet about hip-width apart, and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your neck neutral by looking slightly ahead of your hands.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor in a controlled push-up. Keep your elbows angled back rather than flared wide.
Press through both palms to return to the high plank position without letting your hips sag or rise.
Shift your weight onto your right hand and turn your chest to the left, pivoting onto the sides of your feet.
Reach your left arm straight toward the ceiling and hold briefly, keeping your hips lifted and your body long and straight.
Return your left hand to the floor, perform the next push-up, then rotate into a side plank on the opposite side. Continue alternating sides.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike during the push-up instead of keeping a straight line from head to heels.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides instead of keeping them angled slightly back.
Lowering only the chest or only the hips, rather than moving the body as one unit.
Cutting the push-up short and not lowering the chest close to the floor with control.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears during the push-up or side plank.
Letting the hips drop in the side plank instead of lifting them into a straight body line.
exercises.name: Push-Up to Side Plank
tips: Press the floor away to return to the top of the push-up. Finish the press-up before rotating into the side plank.
Shift your weight into one hand, rotate your chest to the side, and stack your shoulders vertically. Reach the free arm toward the ceiling.
Return your free hand to the floor with control, reset a stable high plank, then perform the next repetition and rotate to the other side.
Keep your neck neutral throughout. Look slightly ahead during the push-up and toward your raised hand only if this does not strain your neck.
If full push-ups or side planks are too difficult, perform the movement from your knees or shorten the side plank hold while maintaining good alignment.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/后束三角肌拉伸

exercises.description: The Rear Deltoid Stretch targets the posterior deltoid muscles, helping to improve shoulder flexibility and reduce tension. This stretch is essential for maintaining shoulder health, especially after upper body workouts.
instructions: Stand or sit with your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
Extend one arm across your body at shoulder height.
Use your opposite hand to gently pull the extended arm towards your chest.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling a gentle stretch in the back of your shoulder.
Release and repeat on the other side.
mistakes: Pulling the arm too aggressively across the body, causing strain on the shoulder joint.
Allowing the shoulder to rise towards the ear, disengaging the rear deltoid.
Twisting the torso instead of keeping it stable, reducing the effectiveness of the stretch.
Failing to keep the arm straight, which decreases the stretch intensity on the rear deltoid.
Not engaging the core to maintain posture, leading to an imbalanced stretch.
Holding the stretch for too short a duration, preventing adequate muscle lengthening.
Using momentum to pull the arm across the body, which reduces control and precision.
exercises.name: Rear Deltoid Stretch
tips: Keep your shoulders down and relaxed to avoid unnecessary tension.
Do not force the stretch; it should feel comfortable and not painful.
Breathe deeply and evenly throughout the stretch to enhance relaxation.
Perform this stretch after workouts to aid in muscle recovery and flexibility.
Ensure your back remains straight to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/后弓步

exercises.description: The rear lunge is a lower body exercise targeting the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and calves. It involves stepping backward into a lunge position, which helps improve balance, coordination, and lower body strength. This exercise can be performed with body weight or additional resistance such as dumbbells or a barbell.
instructions: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or holding weights at your sides.
Step back with your right foot, landing on the ball of your foot and keeping your heel off the ground.
Lower your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees. Your front knee should be directly above your ankle, and your back knee should hover just above the floor.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with the left leg stepping back. Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing the front knee to move past the toes, increasing knee joint stress.
Failing to maintain a straight torso, leading to excessive forward lean.
Not engaging the core, resulting in poor balance and stability.

Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your core engaged and back straight.

Control the movement both on the way down and up to maximize muscle engagement and effectiveness.

Engage your core by drawing your belly button towards your spine.
Exhale as you curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees towards your chest. Keep the movement controlled.
Inhale as you slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without letting your feet touch the ground.

Exhale during the exertion phase as you lift your hips and inhale as you return to the starting position.

exercises.description: The Reverse Grip Cable Curl is an isolation exercise targeting the brachialis and brachioradialis muscles, with secondary emphasis on the biceps brachii. It is performed using a cable machine with a straight or EZ bar attachment, utilizing a reverse (palms-down) grip to focus on the forearms and the outer portion of the upper arm.
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ bar to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your back straight.
Exhale and curl the bar upward by flexing your elbows, keeping your wrists straight.
Continue curling until your forearms are vertical or just past perpendicular to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing the forearms and biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the bar back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using too much weight, leading to swinging and momentum instead of controlled movement.
Allowing elbows to flare out, reducing bicep engagement and increasing shoulder involvement.
Leaning back excessively, which shifts focus away from the biceps and can strain the lower back.
Failing to fully extend the arms at the bottom of the movement, limiting range of motion.
Curling the wrists excessively, which can lead to wrist strain and reduces bicep activation.
Not keeping the core engaged, resulting in a lack of stability and potential for poor posture.
Rushing through reps without controlled tempo, decreasing muscle tension and effectiveness.
exercises.name: Reverse Grip Cable Curl
tips: Focus on keeping your elbows stationary throughout the movement to maximize muscle isolation.
Avoid swinging your body or using momentum to lift the weight; maintain strict form for effectiveness.
Start with a lighter weight to ensure proper form, especially if you're new to this exercise.
Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body and prevent lower back strain.
Use a controlled tempo both on the way up and down to increase muscle tension and effectiveness.
Ensure that your wrists remain in a neutral position to avoid unnecessary strain.

exercises.description: Facing a high pulley, you hold a short bar palms up and straighten your elbows to push it from your upper chest down to your thighs, working the triceps. All three heads share the load, and you'll feel it most at the back of the arm just above the elbow. Your forearms only hold the bar, but the palms-up grip tires fast, so expect to use clearly less weight than on the overhand pushdown. Most lifters use it as a second or last triceps exercise when they want a different feel from the overhand or rope version.
instructions: Set the pulley at the top of a cable column or lat-pulldown station and clip on a short straight or EZ pushdown bar.
Grab the bar underhand, palms up, hands about shoulder-width or a little closer. Wrap your thumbs around it and keep your wrists straight.
Stand about a forearm's length from the stack, feet hip-width, knees soft, torso upright. The cable hangs almost straight down in front of your chest.
Pin your upper arms to your sides, elbows fully bent and the bar near your upper chest. The plates should already be off the stack.
Straighten your elbows and push the bar down in an arc to the front of your thighs. Hold the straight-arm position for a second.
Take 2–3 seconds to let the bar rise until your elbows are fully bent, upper arms still at your sides and the plates still up.
End the set by guiding the bar all the way up before you let go. Release it at the bottom and the bar snaps up while the plates crash down.
mistakes: Elbows drifting forward and up as the bar rises, so your shoulders join in and the rep turns into a press. Keep your upper arms pinned and stop the return when the elbows are fully bent, not when the bar reaches your face.
Wrists bending back while the bar rolls toward your fingertips. Hold it deep in your hand with the thumbs wrapped around; if your wrists won't stay straight, the weight is too heavy.
Leaning over the bar and pushing it down with your body weight. Stand tall and close to the stack. If you need a lean to finish a rep, drop the weight.

Starting with the forearms parallel to the floor and stopping short of straight arms. Use the whole path: fully bent elbows with the bar at your upper chest, down to straight arms with the bar at your thighs.
Hands too wide on the bar. With your palms up, a wide grip twists the wrists and elbows; keep your hands shoulder-width or closer.
exercises.name: Reverse Grip Cable Triceps Pushdown
tips: Do 2–4 sets of 10–15 reps, up to 20 as a finisher; going heavier than 8–10 rarely pays off, because your wrists and grip give out before your triceps do. Add reps before weight, and move the pin down one plate only when you get 15 on all sets with your elbows pinned. Lat-pulldown stacks often jump 5–7 kg, so use the add-on weight if there is one, or stay at that weight longer and keep adding reps.

The burn belongs in the back of your upper arms, hardest just above the elbows near lockout. If your chest or the front of your shoulders start doing the work, your elbows are drifting forward or you're leaning onto the bar.

Palms up puts more stress on your wrists and the inside of your elbows than the overhand grip. Start light and stop if either one hurts. Once a weight feels easy, hold the lockout for 1–2 seconds and take 3–4 seconds on the way up before you add a plate.

Substitutes: One-Arm Reverse Grip Triceps Cable Pushdown to train each arm on its own; Cable Triceps Pushdown when you want to go heavier with an easier grip; Rope Triceps Pushdown if the palms-up grip bothers your wrists; Band Triceps Pushdown when there's no cable station around.

exercises.description: Push your hips back on soft knees and slide a barbell down your thighs to just below the knees: a hinge that builds bigger, stronger hamstrings and glutes. On the way down you feel a deep stretch along the back of your thighs; on the way up your glutes and hamstrings stand you back up while your lower back works to stay flat. Unlike the conventional deadlift, each rep starts from the top and the bar never touches the floor, so your hamstrings get more work with less knee bend and less whole-body fatigue.
instructions: Set the bar in a rack at mid-thigh height, grip it and step back. Without a rack, deadlift it from the floor with a flat back.
Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes forward, and unlock your knees to a soft bend of about 15–20°. Keep that bend for the whole set.
Hold the bar overhand with your hands about shoulder-width, just outside your thighs. Your arms stay straight and long; they only hold the bar.
Take a breath, brace your stomach and press the bar into your thighs with your lats. Shoulders down, no shrug.
Push your hips straight back, as if closing a car door with your backside. Your torso tips forward on its own, back flat and neck in line.
Slide the bar down your thighs over 2–3 seconds, keeping it against your legs. Stop when your hips stop moving back, usually just below the knees.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall, hips under your shoulders. Breathe out near the top, then breathe in for the next rep.
When you finish, walk the bar back into the rack, or bend your knees and lower it to the floor with a flat back.
mistakes: Squatting the bar down: your knees bend more and slide forward as the bar lowers, and the lift turns into a conventional deadlift. Set the soft bend at the top, keep your shins vertical and reach your hips toward the wall behind you.
Rounding your lower back to get the bar lower. The rep ends where your hips stop moving back with a flat back, not at the floor; take weight off if you need to.
Letting the bar drift forward, away from your legs. Keep your lats tight and press the bar into your thighs so it brushes them on the way down and up.
Leaning back and over-arching at the top. Finish by squeezing your glutes with your ribs down, and stop as soon as your hips are straight under your shoulders.
Cranking your neck back to watch yourself in the mirror. Keep your head in line with your spine; at the bottom your eyes are on the floor 1–2 m ahead.
Dropping fast and bouncing out of the bottom. Take 2–3 seconds to lower, pause for a moment, then drive up.
exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
tips: For muscle, use 2–4 sets of 8–12 reps; for strength, 5–8. Add reps first; once you get 12 on all sets with the same depth and a flat back, add 2.5–5 kg and start again at 8.

Expect a strong stretch from just under your glutes toward the backs of your knees. If your lower back burns more than your hamstrings, you're going too deep or rounding; if your quads do most of the work, your knees are bending too much.
When your grip gives out before your hamstrings do, use lifting straps, but keep the weight at a level where your back stays flat on every rep.
New to hinging? Practice the Hip Hinge with a dowel along your spine, or stop the bar just above your knees. Once that feels easy, add a 2-second pause just below the knees at the same weight.
Substitutes: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift, Barbell Straight Leg Deadlift, Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift, Cable Romanian Deadlift.

exercises.description: Climb a hanging rope by moving your hands upward in turn and clamping the rope between your feet. Bend your knees to bring the feet higher, then extend your legs to help raise the body, repeating the sequence before descending with controlled hand and foot support.
instructions: Inspect the rope, anchor point, landing area, and any crash mats before starting.
Stand under the rope and grip it with both hands, one above the other.
Pull yourself slightly off the floor and bend your knees to bring your feet higher on the rope.
Clamp the rope securely between your feet before extending your legs.
Stand up through your legs while pressing the rope between your feet.
Once your legs are extended, slide both hands higher on the rope, one hand at a time.
Bring your knees up again, reset the foot lock, and repeat the stand and pull sequence until you reach the desired height.
Descend under control by lowering your hands and releasing the foot lock gradually.
mistakes: Pulling mostly with the arms instead of using a secure foot lock to drive upward.
Failing to pinch or wrap the rope properly with the feet, causing the body to slide down.
Letting the shoulders hang passively while moving the hands, rather than maintaining active shoulder support.
Reaching too far with one hand, which causes excessive swinging and loss of control.

exercises.name: Rope Climb

Plan the climb height before starting and include the return in the effort you reserve.
Establish the next hand grip before moving the supporting hand.
Look up occasionally to plan your next hand placement, but keep your body position controlled and avoid rushing near the top.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/绳索直臂背阔肌下拉

exercises.description: Hinge forward at a high pulley and sweep a rope from head height to your thighs on straight arms, so your lats move the weight instead of your biceps. Most of the work lands along the sides of your back and in the teres major, the small muscle at the back of the armpit that helps the lats. Rear delts and the small shoulder-blade muscles hold the joint in place; your triceps only stop the elbows from bending. The rope's neutral grip, hands close together, sits better with many wrists and shoulders than a bar. Use it as a lat warm-up before pull-ups or rows, or as a finisher.
instructions: Set the pulley at the very top of the column and clip on a triceps rope.
Hold one rope end in each hand just above the knobs, palms facing each other and hands about a fist apart.
Walk back about two steps, until the plates lift with your arms reaching up toward the pulley. Feet hip-width, knees softly bent.
Push your hips back and lean your torso to roughly 30–40° above horizontal. Back flat, head neutral, arms in line with your torso.
Pull your shoulders down, away from your ears, and set a slight elbow bend that stays fixed for the whole set.
Moving only at the shoulders, sweep the rope down in a wide arc to the front of your thighs, just above the knees. Pause a beat.
Take 2–3 seconds to let the rope rise along the same arc, until you feel a stretch under your armpits. Keep the plates off the stack.
When you finish, step toward the column and let the rope ride up before you let go, so the stack doesn't slam.
mistakes: Bending your elbows on the way down so the rope gets pushed like in a triceps pushdown. Set a slight bend at the top and keep it; if the elbows still move, go lighter.
Standing up as the rope comes down, with the hips driving forward to help. Set the hinge before the first rep and keep your chest at the same angle, braced as if someone were about to shove you.

Standing too upright or too close to the column. The cable then hangs almost straight down and goes slack before your hands reach your thighs. Step back until the cable lines up with your arms at the start.
Rounding your lower back to drive the rope further. The rep ends at the front of your thighs; hinge from the hips with a flat back and let only the shoulders move.
Cutting the top short, so your arms never get back in line with your torso. Let the rope rise until you feel the stretch under your armpits, with the plates still in the air.
exercises.name: Rope Straight-Arm Lat Pulldown
tips: Work with 10–20 reps a set; 12–15 is a good place to start. Below about 8 reps the elbows tend to start bending. Build the reps before the load. Once all sets reach 20 with the same hinge and still elbows, go up the smallest step on the stack (usually 2.5–5 kg) and drop back to about 12. If your stack only jumps in 5 kg plates, stay at each weight longer and slow the way up to 3 seconds.

Feel it along the sides of your back from the armpit toward your waist, with a clear stretch under the armpits at the top. A burning lower back means your torso is moving or your back is rounding: end the set there. If your triceps tire first, your elbows are bending.

Pick the rope over the bar when your wrists or shoulders like a neutral grip, and the bar when you want a fixed overhand grip and a bit more weight. Since the elbows never bend, it's also a good lat option when rows and pulldowns bother your elbows. Easier: stand a little taller and stop at your hips. Harder: take 3–4 seconds on the way up and hold 1–2 seconds at your thighs.

Substitutes: Straight-Arm Lat Pulldown (same arc with a bar and an overhand grip), One-Arm Straight-Arm Cable Lat Pulldown (one side at a time), Machine Pullover (seated, no hinge to hold), Dumbbell Pullover (on a bench when there's no cable).

exercises.description: The Rotary Calf Raise is an exercise targeting the calf muscles, specifically the gastrocnemius and soleus. It involves a rotary motion that engages the calves through a full range of motion, enhancing muscle development and strength. instructions: Adjust the seat height on the rotary calf raise machine so that your knees are slightly bent when seated.
