exercises.description: The Seated Single Leg Curl is an isolation exercise targeting the hamstring muscles. It involves flexing the knee joint to bring the heel towards the glutes while seated on a leg curl machine. This exercise helps in developing strength and muscle definition in the hamstrings, improving knee stability and overall leg performance.
instructions: Adjust the seat and backrest of the leg curl machine so that your knees align with the pivot point of the machine.
Sit on the machine with your back firmly against the backrest and place one leg under the padded lever, ensuring your ankle is just above the lever.
Secure your position by holding onto the side handles.
Begin by flexing your knee to bring your heel towards your glutes, keeping your movement controlled.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the hamstring.
Slowly extend your leg back to the starting position without locking your knee.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.
mistakes: Allowing the knee to lift off the pad during the curl, reducing hamstring engagement.
Failing to adjust the machine to fit leg length, leading to improper alignment.
Using momentum to swing the weight instead of controlled muscle contraction.
Not fully extending the leg at the start, limiting range of motion.
Curling too quickly, which can lead to poor muscle control and engagement.
Leaning back or shifting body weight to compensate for lack of strength.
Neglecting to keep the ankle dorsiflexed, reducing the effectiveness of the exercise.
Setting the weight too heavy, causing form breakdown and potential strain.
exercises.name: Seated Single Leg Curl
tips: Ensure your knee aligns with the machine's pivot point to prevent strain.
Maintain a slow and controlled motion throughout to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid locking your knee at the end of each repetition to maintain tension on the hamstrings.
Focus on squeezing your hamstring at the bottom of each curl for optimal contraction.
Keep your core engaged and back pressed against the seat to stabilize your body.
Start with a lighter weight to perfect your form before progressing to heavier loads.

exercises.description: The Seated Single Leg Hamstring Stretch is a flexibility exercise targeting the hamstring muscles located at the back of the thigh. This stretch helps improve flexibility, reduce muscle tension, and enhance overall lower body mobility. It is particularly beneficial for athletes and individuals who engage in activities that require strong and flexible legs.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your right knee and place the sole of your right foot against the inner thigh of your left leg.
Keep your left leg straight and toes pointing towards the ceiling.
Inhale deeply, then slowly exhale as you lean forward from your hips, reaching towards your left foot with both hands.
Maintain a straight back and avoid rounding your shoulders as you stretch.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull along the back of your left thigh.
Slowly return to the starting position and switch legs to repeat on the other side.
mistakes: Rounding the back instead of hinging at the hips, reducing hamstring engagement.
Locking the knee of the stretched leg, increasing tension on the joint rather than the muscle.
Allowing the foot of the stretched leg to rotate outward, decreasing stretch effectiveness.
Bending the supporting leg excessively, leading to an unstable base.
Pulling on the toes instead of reaching towards them, risking strain on the calf and ankle.
Failing to engage the core, resulting in poor posture and reduced stretch efficiency.
Leaning too far forward, causing overstretching and potential muscle strain.
Holding the breath, which can increase tension and reduce relaxation in the muscles.
exercises.name: Seated Single Leg Hamstring Stretch
tips: Ensure your movements are slow and controlled to prevent injury.
Focus on keeping your back straight to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch.
If you cannot reach your foot, aim to reach as far as comfortable without straining.
Breathe deeply throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
Perform this stretch after a workout or as part of a cool-down routine for best results.

exercises.description: Sit on the floor with one leg folded underneath and the opposite foot planted outside that thigh. Place one hand behind you and hook the other arm around the raised knee, then turn your torso toward that knee. Hold the stretch with your spine tall and release the twist slowly.

Bend your right knee and place your right foot on the floor outside your left thigh.
Fold the lower leg underneath you so its foot rests beside the opposite hip.
Place your right hand on the floor behind your hips for support.

Relax the shoulders and keep your elbows soft as you hold the position.
Exhale as you rotate and inhale to create more length through the spine. Use each exhale to move only slightly deeper if it feels comfortable.

exercises.description: The Seated Triceps Bench Dip is an effective bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps brachii. Ensure that your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to prevent unnecessary strain.

exercises.description: The Shoulder Tap is a bodyweight exercise that targets the core, shoulders, and stabilizing muscles. It involves alternating taps on the opposite shoulder while maintaining a plank position, promoting balance and coordination.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent your hips from swaying.
Lift your right hand off the ground and tap your left shoulder, keeping your body as still as possible.
Return your right hand to the starting position and immediately lift your left hand to tap your right shoulder.
Continue alternating taps for the desired number of repetitions or time.

Feet positioned too wide, reducing core engagement.
Rotating the torso excessively, losing stability.
Tapping shoulders too quickly, sacrificing control.

Arms not fully extended, limiting range of motion.
Hands placed too far forward, altering body alignment.
Not engaging the core, leading to improper form.
Allowing elbows to bend, reducing shoulder stability.
Holding breath, decreasing overall control and endurance.
exercises.name: Shoulder Tap

Focus on minimizing movement in your hips and torso to engage the core effectively.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you tap each shoulder.
If you find it difficult to maintain balance, try performing the exercise on your knees as a modification.
Ensure that your hands are aligned under your shoulders to maintain proper form.

exercises.description: The Shoulderstand, also known as Sarvangasana in yoga, is an inversion exercise that strengthens the shoulders, neck, and core muscles. It improves balance, flexibility, and circulation by elevating the legs above the heart.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your arms at your sides and legs extended.
Engage your core and lift your legs towards the ceiling, keeping them straight.
Place your hands on your lower back for support as you lift your hips off the ground.
Continue to raise your legs and torso until they form a straight line perpendicular to the floor.
Keep your chin tucked slightly to protect your neck and hold the position for several breaths.
To release, slowly lower your back and legs to the floor in a controlled manner.
mistakes: Failing to align the shoulders and neck properly, leading to unnecessary strain on the cervical spine.
Allowing the legs to drift backward, causing imbalance and pressure on the neck.
Engaging the core inadequately, resulting in a lack of stability and control.
Placing the weight on the head instead of distributing it evenly across the shoulders.
Not using the arms to support the back, leading to poor posture and potential discomfort.
Bending the knees instead of keeping the legs straight, reducing the effectiveness of the pose.
Neglecting to engage the glutes and thighs, which can destabilize the pose.
Holding the breath, which can increase tension and reduce balance.
exercises.name: Shoulderstand Pose
tips: Ensure that your weight is supported by your shoulders and upper arms, not your neck.
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability.
Focus on maintaining a straight line from shoulders to feet for proper alignment.
Use a folded blanket under your shoulders if you need extra support or comfort.
Avoid turning your head while in the Shoulderstand to prevent neck strain.

exercises.description: Squat on one leg while holding the other foot behind you with the same-side hand. Reach the free arm forward and lower the rear knee close to the floor, then stand on the supporting leg. The held-leg position increases the balance and mobility demands while the quadriceps and glutes lift the body.
instructions: Stand tall on one leg with your weight centered over the middle of the foot. Bend the other knee behind you and hold that foot with the hand on the same side.
Extend your free arm forward for balance. Keep your chest lifted, hips level, and the standing foot flat on the floor.
Bend the standing knee and sit down slowly. Let the knee travel in line with your toes while keeping the held foot close behind you.
Lower until the rear knee is close to the floor without resting on it.
Press through the whole standing foot to return to standing. Keep your torso controlled and avoid pushing off the floor with the lowered knee.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then switch legs. Use a light hand support or reduce the depth if you cannot keep balance or control.
mistakes: Letting the front knee cave inward instead of tracking over the toes.
Lifting the heel of the working foot off the floor.
Pushing off the floor with the trailing knee or toes instead of using the front leg.
Twisting the hips to one side rather than keeping the pelvis square.
Dropping too quickly and losing control through the descent.
Pulling aggressively on the rear foot and losing balance or hip position.
exercises.name: Shrimp Squat
tips: Hold the rear foot close to the body with the knee pointing down.
Allow a slight forward torso lean to help balance.
Spread foot pressure across the heel and the bases of the big and little toes.
Use the same depth on both sides.
Look at a fixed point in front of you to steady your balance.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/侧向卷腹

exercises.description: The Side Crunch is an abdominal exercise targeting the oblique muscles. It involves a lateral flexion of the spine, engaging the side muscles of the abdomen to enhance core stability and definition.
instructions: Lie on your side on a mat with your knees bent and stacked on top of each other.
Place your bottom arm extended on the floor for support and your top hand behind your head.
Engage your core by pulling your belly button towards your spine.
Lift your upper body towards your hip, contracting your obliques.
Hold the contraction for a moment at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
mistakes: Lifting the head with the neck instead of engaging the oblique muscles.
Using momentum to swing the upper body rather than controlled muscle contraction.
Allowing the lower back to lift off the floor, reducing core engagement.
Failing to keep the elbow wide, leading to shoulder strain.
Not fully engaging the obliques by twisting insufficiently towards the knee.
Pulling on the head with the hands, causing neck strain.
Neglecting to keep the core tight throughout the movement.
Performing the movement too quickly, sacrificing form for speed.
exercises.name: Side Crunch
tips: Focus on using your obliques to lift your torso rather than pulling with your neck or shoulders.
Keep movements controlled and avoid using momentum to ensure maximum muscle engagement.
Exhale as you crunch up and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Ensure that your neck remains in a neutral position throughout the exercise to avoid strain.
Perform the exercise slowly to maintain tension on the muscles and improve effectiveness.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/侧腿摆动

exercises.description: Side Leg Swings are a dynamic stretching exercise that targets the hip flexors, abductors, and adductors. This movement helps improve flexibility, balance, and prepares the lower body for more intense physical activity.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold onto a stable object like a wall or a pole for support.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and lift your right leg slightly off the ground.
Swing your right leg gently across your body to the left, then out to the right side in a controlled manner.
Keep your torso upright and engage your core to maintain balance.
Perform 10-15 swings on one leg before switching to the other leg.
mistakes: Swinging the leg too high, compromising control and balance.
Allowing the torso to lean excessively, reducing core engagement.
Failing to keep the standing leg stable, leading to wobbling.
Not maintaining a neutral spine, causing unnecessary lower back strain.
Using momentum instead of controlled muscle activation.
Neglecting to engage the glutes and hip abductors, reducing effectiveness.
Letting the foot of the swinging leg point downwards, misaligning the hips.
Performing the movement too quickly, limiting range of motion control.
exercises.name: Side Leg Swings
tips: Ensure that the movement is controlled and avoid using momentum to swing your leg.
Focus on keeping your upper body stable and avoid leaning too much to either side.
Start with small swings and gradually increase the range of motion as you become more comfortable.
Maintain a slight bend in the standing knee to help with balance.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise to maintain rhythm and control.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/侧弓步蹲

exercises.description: Side lunges, also known as lateral lunges, are a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and adductors. This movement enhances balance, flexibility, and strength by engaging multiple muscle groups and stabilizing muscles.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips or clasped in front of your chest.
Take a large step to the right, bending your right knee while keeping your left leg straight.
Lower your hips down and back as if sitting into a chair, ensuring your right knee does not extend past your toes.
Keep your chest up and core engaged throughout the movement.
Push off with your right foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat on the left side.
mistakes: Knee collapsing inward during the lunge, increasing strain on the knee joint.
Not keeping the chest up and shoulders back, leading to a rounded back.
Stepping too far to the side, causing loss of balance and control.
Allowing the heel of the lunging leg to lift off the ground, reducing stability.
Failing to push the hips back, which limits glute and hamstring engagement.
Not bending the knee enough, resulting in insufficient range of motion.
Leaning too far forward, shifting weight onto the toes instead of the heel.
Rushing through the movement, compromising form and muscle engagement.
Not keeping the non-lunging leg straight, reducing the stretch and effectiveness.
exercises.name: Side Lunges
tips: Maintain a neutral spine by keeping your back straight and chest lifted.
Focus on pushing through the heel of the bent leg to engage the glutes effectively.
Ensure that your knee is aligned with your toes to prevent strain on the joint.
Start with a smaller step if you're new to this exercise to maintain balance and control.
Inhale as you step out and exhale as you push back to the starting position.

exercises.description: Lie on your side with your upper arm resting against your torso and your elbow bent at 90 degrees. Keep your elbow fixed and rotate your forearm upward, lifting the dumbbell or resistance band away from your body while maintaining control. This exercise targets the rotator cuff muscles, particularly the infraspinatus and teres minor, helping to improve shoulder stability and external rotation strength. Perform slowly and with proper form to avoid shoulder strain.
instructions: Lie on your side with the arm you want to exercise on top and bent at a 90-degree angle at the elbow, resting against your side.
Keep your elbow tucked close to your body throughout the movement to isolate the shoulder muscles.
Hold a lightweight dumbbell or resistance band in your top hand, allowing your forearm to rest across your abdomen.
Slowly rotate your forearm upward, lifting the dumbbell or band away from your body while keeping your elbow fixed in place.
Raise your forearm until it is approximately perpendicular to your torso or as far as comfortable without pain.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Slowly lower your forearm back to the starting position with control, avoiding any sudden movements.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout.
Switch sides and repeat the exercise with the other arm to ensure balanced shoulder strength.
mistakes: Allowing the elbow to drift away from the body, reducing shoulder stabilization.
Using momentum or swinging the arm instead of controlled rotation.
Raising the shoulder off the floor, compromising proper alignment.
Rotating the arm beyond a comfortable range, causing shoulder strain.
Not maintaining a 90-degree bend at the elbow throughout the movement.
Engaging the trapezius muscles excessively instead of the rotator cuff.
Performing the movement too quickly, leading to poor muscle activation.
Neglecting to keep the wrist in a neutral position, causing undue stress.
exercises.name: Side Lying External Rotation
tips: Keep your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle and tucked close to your side throughout the movement.
Use a light dumbbell or resistance band to avoid straining your shoulder muscles.
Slowly rotate your forearm upward while keeping your upper arm stationary and pressed against your side.
Focus on controlled, smooth movements rather than speed to maximize muscle engagement and reduce injury risk.
Maintain a neutral spine and avoid twisting your torso during the exercise.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation before lowering your arm back down.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift the weight and inhaling as you lower it.
Perform the exercise on both sides to maintain balanced shoulder strength and stability.

exercises.description: Lie on your side, propped up on your bottom arm, and raise your straight top leg to about 45 degrees to strengthen the side of your hip. The work lands on the gluteus medius, the muscle on the upper outer buttock that holds your pelvis level when you stand on one leg. You need no equipment, so it suits beginners, home sessions and warm-ups before leg day. Compared with a clamshell, the straight leg is a longer lever and loads the hip harder; when you want heavy, measurable load, a cable or the abduction machine does that better.
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor or a mat. Bend your bottom knee to about 90 degrees, shin pointing back, as your base.
Prop your upper body up on your straight bottom arm, hand flat a little ahead of the shoulder. Head up, eyes forward.
Put your top hand flat on the floor in front of your stomach. Pressing it down helps keep your pelvis from rolling back.
Straighten your top leg in line with your torso and stack your top hip over the bottom one, toes pointing forward, not up.
Lead with your heel and lift for about 2 seconds, to roughly 40-45 degrees or until your pelvis starts to roll back.
Pause briefly with the knee straight, then take about 2 seconds to lower along the same arc until the leg touches the bottom one.
Go into the next rep without bouncing. After the last one, turn over and do the same number on the other side.
mistakes: Letting the leg drift forward in front of your body, so the front of the hip does the lifting. Keep it in line with your torso or a touch behind, as if sliding your heel along a wall behind you.
Turning the toes and kneecap up toward the ceiling. Keep them facing forward and let the heel lead.
Rolling the pelvis back to get the leg higher. Keep the top hip stacked over the bottom one, press your top hand into the floor and stop at about 45 degrees.
Hitching the hip up toward your ribs. Keep the top side of your waist long and accept a smaller lift.
Swinging the leg up and letting it drop. Count about 2 seconds up and 2 down, and set the leg on the bottom one quietly.
exercises.name: Side Lying Hip Abduction
tips: Do 2-4 sets of 12-20 reps per side, stopping 1-3 reps short of failure. Add reps first: once both sides get 20 clean reps in all sets, put on a mini band or a 0.5-1 kg ankle weight and drop back to 12. A 2-3 second hold at the top is a step in between.

A burn should build just below the hip bone on the side of the top leg. If it's mostly the front of the hip, your leg has drifted forward or your foot has turned up; if it's your waist or lower back, you're hitching the hip or rolling back.

Wrist or shoulder of the support arm complaining? Prop on your forearm with the elbow under the shoulder, or lie all the way down with your head on the bottom arm. Bending the top knee shortens the lever if the straight leg is still too hard.

Substitutes: Cable Hip Abduction and Standing Hip Abduction train the same muscle standing up, Seated Hip Abduction is the machine to load it heavily, and Side Plank Hip Abduction is the harder no-equipment step once banded sets feel easy.

exercises.description: Side-lying hip adduction raises the straight bottom leg toward the top leg, working the inner thigh. Bend the top leg and place its foot on the floor in front of the bottom thigh, supporting the head with the lower arm and keeping the pelvis stacked as the bottom leg rises and lowers.
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs straight and your body in one line. Rest your head on your lower arm or support it with your hand.
Bend your top leg and place its foot on the floor in front of your lower thigh or knee. Keep the bottom leg straight.
Brace your abdominal muscles and keep your hips stacked, without rolling your pelvis backward or forward.
Exhale and lift the bottom leg upward toward the ceiling using the inner thigh muscles.
Raise the leg only as far as you can without rotating your hips or bending the knee.
Inhale and lower the leg slowly until it is just above the floor. Do not let it drop.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then turn over and repeat with the other leg.
mistakes: Rolling the pelvis forward or backward.
Bending the working knee.
Swinging the leg up with momentum.
Moving the leg forward or backward instead of toward the top leg.
Turning the toes toward the ceiling to change the hip position.
Dropping the leg without control.
exercises.name: Side Lying Hip Adduction
tips: Use a mat for comfortable contact at the hip.
Support the head with the lower arm so the neck can relax.
Position the top foot far enough forward to leave room for the bottom leg.
Exhale during the lift and inhale during the return.
Perform the same number of repetitions on both sides.

exercises.description: The Side Lying Quadriceps Stretch is a flexibility exercise targeting the quadriceps muscles located at the front of the thigh. This stretch is performed while lying on your side, allowing for a deep and controlled extension of the quadriceps, improving flexibility and reducing muscle tightness.
instructions: Lie down on your side on a flat surface, ensuring your body is in a straight line.
Support your head with your lower arm or rest it on the floor.
Bend your top knee and bring your heel towards your glutes.
Reach back with your top hand and grasp your ankle or foot.
Gently pull your ankle towards your glutes until you feel a stretch in the front of your thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, maintaining steady breathing.
Release slowly and switch sides to repeat the stretch on the other leg.

Allowing the hips to rotate backward instead of keeping them stacked.
Failing to keep the bottom leg straight and aligned with the body.
Gripping the ankle too tightly, leading to tension in the foot and ankle.
Arching the lower back instead of maintaining a neutral spine.
Not engaging the core, resulting in loss of balance and stability.
Letting the head drop forward instead of keeping it aligned with the spine.
Forgetting to breathe steadily, causing unnecessary tension in the body.
Using the hand to push the knee down instead of gently guiding it.
exercises.name: Side Lying Quadriceps Stretch
tips: Keep your hips stacked and aligned to avoid twisting your torso.
Engage your core to maintain stability throughout the stretch.
If you can't reach your ankle, use a strap or towel around your foot to assist.
Focus on keeping your knees close together to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch.
Avoid pulling too hard; aim for a gentle stretch to prevent injury.
Perform this stretch after workouts to aid in muscle recovery and flexibility.

instructions: Lie on your side with your legs extended and stacked from hip to feet.
Place your elbow directly under your shoulder, ensuring your forearm is perpendicular to your body.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from head to feet.
Keep your head in line with your spine and hold the position while breathing steadily.
Maintain the position for the desired duration, then switch sides.

Shoulder not aligned directly above the elbow, increasing strain on the joint.
Feet not stacked, leading to instability and reduced effectiveness.
Neck misaligned, causing unnecessary tension.
Top hip rotating forward or backward, compromising form.
Core muscles not engaged, reducing stability and effectiveness.
Top arm not extended or positioned correctly, affecting balance.
Breathing inconsistently, leading to loss of control and stability.
exercises.name: Side Plank
tips: Ensure your elbow is directly under your shoulder to avoid strain.
Engage your core muscles to maintain balance and stability.
Keep your body in a straight line to maximize effectiveness.
Avoid letting your hips sag or rise too high; aim for a neutral position.
Focus on steady breathing to help maintain the position longer.

Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground into a side plank position, maintaining a straight line from head to knees.

Lower the knee back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

Not engaging the glutes, limiting the effectiveness of the exercise.
Allowing the shoulder to collapse, increasing shoulder strain.
Rushing the movement, sacrificing control and precision.

Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability.
Avoid letting your hips drop; maintain a straight line from head to knees.

Breathe steadily and do not hold your breath during the exercise.

Engage your core muscles to maintain stability during the exercise.

Raise your hips back to the straight side plank position by squeezing the muscles along the side of your waist and your glutes.

exercises.description: Hold one dumbbell upright in both hands, palms up under its top end, and curl it from your thighs to your upper chest to build your biceps. Both arms bend together; the two heads of the biceps do the lifting while your hands and forearms simply hold the weight. Since the arms share one dumbbell, each moves about half of it, and the next dumbbell up is a small step. It suits beginners, home workouts with a single dumbbell and light finishers after heavier curls. Your hold usually gives out before your biceps do, so switch to a barbell or EZ bar for heavy sets.
instructions: Pick one dumbbell, ideally a fixed one, and hold it on end: both palms face up under the top plates, hands side by side, fingers curled around the rim.
Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your knees straight but not locked. Chest up, shoulders down, abs braced.
Let your arms hang straight so the dumbbell sits vertically in front of your thighs, handle pointing at the floor, elbows at your sides.
Bend both elbows together and curl the weight up. The bottom end tips forward as your forearms rise; let it tip, but don't let it swing.
Stop when your hands reach your upper chest and your forearms are almost vertical, then squeeze for about a second.
Take about 2 seconds to lower until your elbows are fully straight and the dumbbell hangs vertically again.
Bend your knees at the end of the set and set the dumbbell down on the floor or back on the rack.
mistakes: Leaning back or pushing your hips forward to get the dumbbell moving. Brace your abs and keep your chest still; if you still sway, take a lighter dumbbell.
Elbows drifting forward and up at the top, so your front delts start doing the lifting. Keep your elbows against your ribs and stop when your hands reach your upper chest.
Wrists bending back under the plates. Keep your wrists straight and your palms flat under the top end; if you can't, the dumbbell is too heavy.
Letting the stronger arm do most of the work, so the dumbbell drifts to one side. Keep your hands centered in front of your body and both elbows level.
exercises.name: Single Dumbbell Curl
tips: Curl 8–15 reps, or 6–10 if the hold still feels secure at that weight. Stay with one dumbbell and add reps until you get the top number cleanly in all sets, then take the next dumbbell and start again from the bottom. That step is usually 2–2.5 kg, only about 1–1.25 kg per arm. Log the weight of the one dumbbell.
Both upper arms work at the front, hardest at the top. A tired lower back means you're leaning back; if the front of your shoulders takes over, your elbows are drifting forward.
Can't keep your elbows still? Go lighter and stop at mid-chest for a few sessions, or use the Machine Biceps Curl. To make it harder, take 3–4 seconds on the way down.
With an adjustable dumbbell, check both collars before every set: the bottom plates hang right over your feet.

Substitutes: Dumbbell Biceps Curl (a dumbbell in each hand, the better pick when one arm lags), Barbell Biceps Curl (for heavier sets), EZ-Bar Biceps Curl (easier on the wrists), Bar Cable Biceps Curl.

Not controlling the descent, leading to a loss of balance.

Neglecting to keep the shoulder blades retracted and stable.
Allowing the non-working leg to drift too far from the midline.
exercises.name: Single Leg Dumbbell Deadlift
tips: Focus on maintaining a neutral spine throughout the exercise to avoid lower back strain.
Engage your core muscles to help stabilize your body during the movement.
Control the descent and ascent of the dumbbell to maximize muscle engagement.
Keep your gaze fixed on a point on the floor to help maintain balance.

Lower your hips back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.

Neglecting to fully extend the hip at the top of the movement, limiting range of motion.
Allowing the non-working leg to move excessively, disrupting balance.
Not keeping the bench at the correct height, affecting hip thrust mechanics.
exercises.name: Single Leg Hip Thrust
tips: Ensure your upper back remains in contact with the bench throughout the movement for stability.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of each rep to maximize muscle activation.
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and prevent lower back strain.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to enhance muscle engagement and reduce injury risk.

exercises.description: Press the sled of a 45-degree leg press with one leg while the other foot rests on the frame, so each thigh works on its own. The quads on the front of the working thigh do almost all the work; the inner and back of the thigh help a little. Your back stays on the pad, which makes it a good pick when one leg lags or when you want more quad work without loading your spine. Choose it over the Bulgarian split squat when balance, not leg strength, ends your sets. A seated stack-loaded leg press works the same way.
instructions: Load the plates evenly on both sides of the sled. For your first sets, start well under half of what you press with two legs.
Slide all the way back so your hips sit deep in the seat and your back and head rest on the pad.
Put both feet on the platform, press the sled off the stops and turn the safety handles out to free it.
Take one foot down and rest it flat on the frame near the floor, well clear of the sled and the stops.
The working foot stays flat on its own side of the platform, in line with that hip, toes up or turned out a touch.
Hold the seat handles and pull down lightly so both hips stay pinned to the seat.
Bend the knee and lower the sled over about 2 seconds, the knee heading straight for the shoulder on the same side.
At about 90 degrees at the knee, before that hip rolls up, press back through the whole foot and stop short of lockout.
At the end of the set, put the free foot back on the platform, turn the safety handles in and switch legs.
mistakes: Unracking or racking the sled with one leg. Use both feet to press it off the stops and to set it back on the safety catches; go single-leg only in between.
Working foot in the middle of the platform, so the knee angles inward and the pelvis twists. Set it on its own side, in line with the hip, and keep the knee over your second and third toes.
The working-side hip rolls up off the seat at the bottom. Cut the depth to where both hips stay flat, pull down on the handles and move the foot a little higher.
Knee caving in on the way up. Turn the toes out slightly, push the knee out over the foot and take weight off until it stays in line.
Heel lifting at the bottom so you push from the toes. Move the foot up until the whole sole stays flat, then press through the mid-foot and heel.
exercises.name: Single Leg Press
tips: Use 6–10 reps per leg for strength and 10–15 for size, up to about 20 on a lighter last set. Start with your weaker leg and stop the stronger one at the same count and depth. Once both legs reach the top of your range, add 5 kg (2.5 kg per side) and drop back to the bottom of the range; go to 2.5 kg jumps when progress slows.
Foot height is the lever that matters. Higher on the platform gives you more hip bend, lower gives more knee bend and more quad work, as long as your heel stays flat at the bottom.

The front of the working thigh should do most of the work. Pinching at the front of the hip or your tailbone lifting means you went too deep; pain at the front or inside of the knee usually comes from the knee caving or the heel lifting.

Substitutes: Leg Press (both feet, the easier version), Lever Horizontal Leg Press (also works one leg at a time), Dumbbell Bulgarian Squat (harder, adds balance), Dumbbell Split Squat. Stuck on the last reps? Let the free foot rest lightly on the platform to help. To make it harder, pause 2 seconds at the bottom or take 3–4 seconds to lower.

exercises.description: The Sitting Twist is an effective core exercise targeting the oblique muscles. It involves rotating the torso while seated, engaging the abdominal muscles for stability and control. This exercise can be performed with or without added resistance, such as a medicine ball or dumbbell, to increase intensity.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground. Lean back slightly to engage your core.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest or grasp a weight if using resistance.
Keep your back straight and rotate your torso to the right, bringing your hands or weight beside your hip.
Return to the center and then rotate to the left, repeating the movement.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Leaning too far back, causing strain on the lower back.
Rounding the shoulders, leading to poor posture and reduced core engagement.
Failing to keep the spine straight, resulting in ineffective twisting motion.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement, diminishing muscle activation.
Not engaging the core, leading to over-reliance on the arms for movement.
Allowing the knees to wobble or move excessively, reducing stability.
Twisting only the arms without rotating the torso, limiting range of motion.
Holding the breath, which can increase tension and reduce performance.
exercises.name: Sitting Twist
tips: Maintain a straight back throughout the exercise to avoid strain on the lower back.
Engage your core muscles by pulling your navel towards your spine for better stability.
Control the movement speed; avoid using momentum to twist.
If using a weight, start with a lighter one to ensure proper form before increasing resistance.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you twist and inhaling as you return to center.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/平凳直腿悬停

exercises.description: Lie on a flat bench and grip its edges beside your hips. Raise your straight legs slightly above the bench while lifting your head and shoulders, keeping your lower back supported. Hold this position with your abdomen braced and breathe steadily, then lower your legs and upper body under control.
instructions: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your legs straight.
Grip the bench edges beside your hips.
Brace your abdomen and keep your lower back supported.
Lift both legs slightly above the bench and raise your head and shoulders.
Hold your legs and upper body still while breathing steadily.
Lower your legs, head and shoulders under control to finish.
mistakes: Arching the lower back away from the bench.
Letting the knees bend during the hold.
Swinging the legs instead of holding them still.
Pulling the chin tightly against the chest.
Lifting the legs too high and shortening the lever of the hold.
Letting the pelvis twist to one side.
exercises.name: Six-Inch Hold
tips: Begin with short holds and increase the time gradually.
Use an audible timer to mark the planned holding time.
Exhale as you lift into the hold.
Keep your jaw relaxed and look toward your feet.
End the hold as soon as fatigue makes the position unstable.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/臀部/滑冰跳

exercises.description: A bodyweight plyometric exercise in which you bound sideways from one leg to the other, copying a speed skater's stride. You land on the outside leg with the hips back while the free leg swings behind it. It works the glutes, quads and calves and builds balance and control on one leg.
instructions: Stand on your right leg with the knee bent and the hips back, the left leg bent behind it with the foot off the floor. Keep your chest up and core braced.
Push off hard through your right leg and jump sideways to the left.
Land softly on the ball of your left foot and let the heel settle, with the knee bent over the toes and the hips pushed back.
Let your right leg swing behind your left leg without touching the floor, and swing your right arm across your body toward the left knee.
Absorb the landing, then push off your left foot right away and jump to the right, landing on your right leg in the same position.
Keep alternating sides in a steady rhythm for the planned number of reps.
mistakes: Letting the landing knee cave inward instead of tracking over the toes
Jumping upward instead of sideways, so each jump covers little distance
Landing stiff-legged or on the heel, which sends the impact into the knee
Putting the free foot down on every landing instead of keeping your weight on the landing leg
Letting the hip on the free-leg side drop instead of keeping the pelvis level
Twisting the torso too far while swinging the arms
exercises.name: Skater Jumps
tips: Keep a slight forward lean from the hips with a flat back, like a speed skater.
Push off through the whole foot and let your hips lead the jump sideways.
Keep your eyes forward and your shoulders level to stay balanced on one leg.
While learning, hold each landing for a second or two before jumping back.
Increase the jump distance first and the speed later, as long as every landing stays stable.
Use a flat, non-slip surface so your push-off foot does not slide out.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/滑冰者深蹲

exercises.description: Squat on one leg while keeping the other knee bent behind you and the hands together at the chest. Lower the rear knee close to the floor, then stand using the supporting leg. This bodyweight movement works the quadriceps and glutes while challenging balance and control on one side.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart. Shift your weight onto one foot and lift the other foot slightly behind you, keeping the knee bent.
Clasp your hands at your chest and brace your abdomen. Keep the supporting foot flat.
Bend your standing knee and sit your hips back as you lower into a single-leg squat. Let the knee of your lifted leg travel behind and toward the floor.
Lower until the rear knee is close to the floor, keeping it off the ground.
Drive through the middle of your standing foot to return to standing. Keep your knee tracking in line with your toes and avoid letting it collapse inward.
Complete all repetitions on one side, then repeat on the other leg.
mistakes: Letting the working knee cave inward instead of tracking in line with the toes.
Losing balance by shifting weight to the outside edge of the foot.
Allowing the heel of the working foot to lift off the floor.
Dropping or rotating the pelvis toward the non-working side.
Using momentum and bouncing out of the bottom position.
Letting the free leg swing or touch down to assist the repetition.
exercises.name: Skater Squat
tips: Keep your hands together at the chest.
Look at a fixed point in front of you.
Allow a slight forward torso lean as the hips move back.
Use the same depth on both legs.
Exhale as you stand and inhale as you lower.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/滑雪测功仪

exercises.description: The Ski Ergometer, often referred to as the SkiErg, is a cardiovascular exercise machine that simulates the motion of Nordic skiing. It primarily targets the upper body, including the shoulders, arms, and core, while also engaging the legs. This machine is ideal for improving aerobic capacity, endurance, and overall strength.
instructions: Adjust the resistance level on the SkiErg to match your fitness level.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the machine.
Grip the handles firmly with both hands, keeping your arms extended overhead.
Engage your core and slightly bend your knees.
Pull the handles down in a smooth motion, bending at the hips and knees while keeping your back straight.
Drive through your hips and legs as you pull the handles down past your thighs.
Return to the starting position by extending your arms overhead while maintaining control.
Repeat the motion for the desired number of repetitions or time duration.
mistakes: Leaning too far forward, causing excessive strain on the lower back.
Bending the knees too much, reducing efficiency and power output.
Pulling with the arms only, neglecting engagement of the core and legs.
Failing to fully extend the arms overhead, limiting range of motion.
Rounding the shoulders, leading to poor posture and reduced performance.
Using a jerky motion instead of a smooth, controlled pull.
Not maintaining a consistent breathing pattern, affecting endurance.
Allowing the hips to drop, decreasing core stability and power.
Gripping the handles too tightly, causing unnecessary tension in the forearms.
Neglecting to engage the lats, reducing power and efficiency.
exercises.name: Ski Ergometer
tips: Focus on maintaining a strong core throughout the exercise to prevent lower back strain.
Ensure that your movements are smooth and controlled to maximize efficiency and reduce injury risk.
Keep your elbows slightly bent at the bottom of the pull to avoid locking out your joints.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise; inhale as you return to the starting position and exhale during the pull.
Start with a lower resistance setting if you're new to using the SkiErg to build endurance and technique before increasing intensity.
Incorporate intervals by alternating between high-intensity bursts and moderate recovery periods to enhance cardiovascular benefits.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/雪橇拖行

exercises.description: Fasten the sled straps to a shoulder harness and face away from the sled. Lean forward with your trunk braced, then walk ahead in short, steady steps to drag the load behind you. Keep tension on the straps and let your legs drive the sled without pulling with your arms.
instructions: Load the sled and fasten its towing straps securely to a shoulder harness.
Put on the harness and face away from the sled with the straps taut.
Set your feet about hip-width apart and brace your trunk before taking the first step.
Lean your body forward into the harness while keeping your spine neutral.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps, driving through the whole foot and keeping steady tension on the straps.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes and avoid twisting your torso as you move.
Continue for the planned distance or time, then slow down gradually before stopping and turning around.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag or the low back round instead of keeping the torso braced
Taking long, uncontrolled strides that cause the sled to jerk
Leaning too far forward or backward and losing a stable body angle
Allowing the knees to collapse inward during each step
Starting with slack in the straps, which creates a sudden jerk when the load moves
Taking steps that are too narrow and crossing the feet
exercises.name: Sled Drag
tips: Adjust the shoulder harness so it stays secure and distributes the pull evenly.
Choose a load that lets the sled move continuously at your walking pace.
Keep your elbows bent near your chest as the harness takes the pull.
Push through the whole foot and let each step roll smoothly into the next.
Keep your head neutral and look ahead in the direction you are traveling. Do not twist your torso to watch the sled.

exercises.description: Attach a rope securely to a loaded sled and stand facing it with feet shoulder-width apart. Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and pull the rope hand-over-hand in a controlled motion, drawing the sled toward you. Keep your feet planted and your knees bent throughout.
instructions: Load the sled with an appropriate amount of weight and attach a secure training rope to the sled’s front attachment point.
Stand facing the sled with your feet about shoulder-width apart, holding the rope firmly with both hands and keeping enough distance to maintain tension in the rope.
Brace your core, keep your chest lifted, and bend your knees slightly into an athletic stance with a neutral spine.
Pull the rope toward you with one hand, then reach forward with the other and continue alternating.
After each pull, reach forward under control to take another grip on the rope while maintaining a stable torso and avoiding excessive rounding of the lower back.
Continue pulling hand over hand until the sled reaches you, keeping the rope taut and using smooth, powerful pulls rather than jerking the load.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back while reaching forward for the rope.
Leaning excessively backward instead of keeping the torso tall and stable.
Pulling with jerky, uncontrolled tugs rather than smooth hand-over-hand motions.
Allowing the rope to go slack between pulls.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears instead of keeping them down and engaged.
Rotating or twisting the torso excessively during each pull.
exercises.name: Sled Rope Pull
tips: Set the sled on a clear lane and make sure the rope is fully extended, untangled, and securely attached before starting.
Keep the rope close to your body as you pull to maintain leverage and reduce unnecessary strain on the shoulders.
Brace your core and exhale gradually during the pull, especially when moving a heavier sled.
Choose gloves only if needed for rope friction, but make sure they do not reduce your grip or control of the rope.
To progress, increase the sled load, distance, rope thickness, or pulling speed gradually while preserving clean technique.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/侧卧肩关节内旋拉伸

exercises.description: Lie on your side with your head supported and the lower arm in front at shoulder height. Bend the elbow to 90 degrees and use the upper hand to guide the lower forearm toward the floor. Hold a mild stretch at the back of the shoulder without rolling your torso or forcing the range.
instructions: Lie on your side with the shoulder you want to stretch on the bottom. Keep your head supported and your torso stable.
Bring the bottom arm straight out in front of you at shoulder height, with the elbow bent to 90 degrees and the forearm pointing upward.
Keep the bottom shoulder blade gently pulled back and down. Do not let the shoulder roll forward toward your ear.
Use your top hand to hold the wrist or forearm of the bottom arm.
Slowly guide the bottom forearm down toward the floor, creating a gentle stretch at the back of the shoulder.
Hold the stretch without forcing the arm down. Breathe normally, then slowly release and repeat on the other side if needed. Stop if you feel pinching or pain in the front or top of the shoulder.
mistakes: Rolling the torso backward instead of keeping the shoulder stacked over the supporting side.
Letting the bottom shoulder shrug toward the ear.
Moving the elbow away from shoulder height or letting it drift behind the body.
Letting the wrist bend instead of rotating through the shoulder.
Lifting the lower upper arm off the floor to gain extra range.
Bouncing or repeatedly pushing deeper instead of using a slow, steady hold.
exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
tips: Support your head so your neck stays aligned with your trunk.
Keep the lower elbow bent to about 90 degrees while the forearm rotates.
Keep the shoulder blade gently set against your rib cage. Do not let the shoulder roll forward toward your chest.
Apply only light pressure and stop when you feel a mild stretch at the back of the shoulder. Do not force the hand all the way to the floor.
Breathe slowly throughout the hold and release the pressure gradually before changing sides.

exercises.description: The Sliding Leg Curl is a bodyweight exercise targeting the hamstrings, glutes, and core. It involves sliding your feet on a smooth surface while maintaining a bridge position, which increases the engagement of the posterior chain muscles.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on a smooth surface.
Place your arms at your sides with palms facing down for stability.
Lift your hips off the ground to form a straight line from shoulders to knees, engaging your core and glutes.
Slowly slide your feet away from your body, extending your legs while keeping hips elevated.
Pause briefly when legs are fully extended, then slide feet back towards your body to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions while maintaining control and form.
mistakes: Hips sagging towards the floor, reducing hamstring engagement.
Allowing the knees to flare outwards, losing alignment and stability.
Not extending the legs fully, limiting the range of motion.
Using momentum to pull the legs back instead of controlled muscle contraction.
Failing to keep the core engaged, leading to lower back strain.
Rushing through reps, compromising form and muscle activation.
Lifting the hips too high, shifting focus away from the hamstrings.
Feet slipping due to lack of proper grip or surface friction.
exercises.name: Sliding Leg Curl
tips: Ensure your core remains engaged throughout the movement to prevent lower back strain.
Keep your hips elevated and avoid letting them drop as you slide your feet.
Perform the movement slowly to maximize muscle engagement and control.
Use a towel or sliders under your feet if performing on a non-slippery surface.
Focus on squeezing the glutes and hamstrings as you bring your feet back towards you.

exercises.description: The Smith Bench Press is a variation of the traditional bench press performed using a Smith machine. This exercise targets the pectoral muscles, triceps, and anterior deltoids. The Smith machine provides a guided bar path, which can help stabilize the movement and focus on muscle engagement.
instructions: Set the bench to a flat position under the Smith machine bar.
Lie back on the bench with your eyes directly under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar by rotating your wrists to release it from the safety hooks.
Lower the bar slowly to your mid-chest, keeping your elbows at about a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the bar back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
After completing your set, rotate your wrists to re-engage the safety hooks and rack the bar.
mistakes: Placing the bench too far forward or backward, leading to an unnatural bar path.
Using a grip that is too wide or too narrow, causing shoulder strain.
Failing to maintain a stable shoulder position, leading to shoulder impingement.
Arching the lower back excessively, reducing core engagement.
Allowing the elbows to flare out excessively, increasing stress on the shoulders.
Bouncing the bar off the chest, reducing muscle tension and control.
Not fully engaging the chest muscles, relying too much on the triceps.
Descending the bar too quickly, compromising control and form.
Locking the elbows too forcefully at the top, causing joint stress.
Neglecting to keep feet firmly planted, reducing overall stability.
exercises.name: Smith Bench Press
tips: Ensure your feet are flat on the floor for stability throughout the exercise.
Keep your core engaged to maintain proper form and support your lower back.
Focus on controlled movements; avoid bouncing the bar off your chest.
Adjust the bench position so that when you lower the bar, it touches just above your sternum.
Use a spotter if lifting heavy weights or when attempting new personal records.
Warm up properly before starting with lighter weights to prepare your muscles and joints.

exercises.description: Smith Calf Raises are a strength training exercise targeting the calf muscles, primarily the gastrocnemius and soleus. Utilizing the Smith machine provides stability, allowing for controlled movement and focus on muscle contraction. This exercise is effective for building calf strength and size.
instructions: Position yourself under the Smith machine bar with the balls of your feet on a raised platform or block, heels hanging off.
Adjust the bar to rest comfortably across your upper back and shoulders.
Unlock the bar by rotating it forward and ensure your feet are shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your knees slightly bent throughout the exercise.
Raise your heels by extending your ankles, lifting as high as possible onto your toes.
Pause at the top of the movement for a moment to maximize contraction.
Slowly lower your heels back to the starting position, feeling a stretch in your calves.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using too much weight, compromising form and range of motion.
Placing feet too far forward or backward, misaligning the body.
Allowing heels to drop too low, risking Achilles strain.
Failing to fully extend the ankles, limiting calf engagement.
Bouncing at the bottom instead of controlled movement.
Locking knees, reducing calf activation and increasing joint stress.
Leaning forward or backward, causing imbalance.
Not maintaining a stable core, leading to poor posture.
Neglecting to keep toes pointing straight ahead, altering muscle focus.
Rushing through reps, sacrificing muscle tension and control.
exercises.name: Smith Calf Raises
tips: Maintain a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.
Focus on squeezing the calf muscles at the top of each rep.
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability.
Avoid locking your knees; keep them slightly bent to reduce strain.
Ensure full range of motion by lowering your heels below parallel if possible.
Use a weight that allows you to perform all reps with proper form.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/史密斯椅式深蹲

exercises.description: The Smith Chair Squat is a lower body exercise performed using a Smith machine. It targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and calves. The exercise involves squatting down as if sitting on an imaginary chair, providing stability and control through the guided bar path of the Smith machine.
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar to shoulder height and lock it in place.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, positioning yourself under the bar so it rests comfortably across your upper back.
Grip the bar with both hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unlatch the bar by rotating it forward and step back slightly to clear the safety stops.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to lower your body by bending at the hips and knees.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below, ensuring your knees do not extend past your toes.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, maintaining tension in your legs.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, fully extending your hips and knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Placing feet too far forward, causing excessive forward lean.
Allowing knees to cave inward during the squat.
Not lowering to at least parallel, limiting range of motion.
Rising onto toes instead of keeping heels grounded.
Failing to engage core, leading to poor stability.
Using momentum rather than controlled movement.
Setting the bar too high or too low on the back.
Neglecting to maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Pushing through the balls of the feet instead of the heels.
Rushing the descent, resulting in loss of control.
exercises.name: Smith Chair Squat
tips: Keep your back straight and chest lifted throughout the movement to avoid unnecessary strain on your lower back.
Ensure that your knees track over your toes during the squat to maintain proper alignment and prevent injury.
Focus on engaging your core muscles to stabilize your torso during the exercise.
Adjust the foot placement if necessary to find a comfortable position that allows for a full range of motion without compromising form.
Control the descent and ascent speed to maximize muscle engagement and reduce risk of injury.
Use a spotter or safety stops if you're lifting heavy weights for added security.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/史密斯机前蹲

exercises.description: The Smith Front Squat is a compound exercise targeting the quadriceps, glutes, and core muscles. It utilizes the Smith machine to provide stability and control, making it suitable for lifters who want to focus on form and muscle activation without the need for a spotter.
instructions: Set the bar on the Smith machine at shoulder height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and position yourself under the bar.
Cross your arms over your chest and rest the bar across your front deltoids.
Unrack the bar by rotating it forward and step back slightly.
Keep your chest up, core engaged, and back straight.
Lower your body by bending at the knees and hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Placing feet too far forward, causing imbalance and excessive knee stress.
Allowing knees to cave inward, leading to improper alignment and potential knee injury.
Failing to maintain an upright torso, resulting in excessive forward lean and lower back strain.
Not keeping the barbell close to the body, increasing stress on shoulders and wrists.
Descending too quickly, reducing control and increasing risk of losing balance.
Not reaching sufficient depth, limiting muscle engagement and effectiveness.
Rounding the upper back, compromising spinal alignment and reducing core stability.
Neglecting to engage the core, leading to poor posture and increased risk of injury.
Using too much weight, sacrificing form for load and risking injury.
exercises.name: Smith Front Squat
tips: Ensure that your elbows remain high throughout the movement to keep the bar stable.
Focus on maintaining a neutral spine to prevent lower back strain.
Engage your core muscles to enhance stability and control during the squat.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes to avoid unnecessary stress on the joints.
Breathe in as you lower into the squat and exhale as you push back up.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/史密斯机哈克深蹲

exercises.description: The Smith Hack Squat is a compound lower body exercise performed using a Smith machine. It primarily targets the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the glutes, hamstrings, and calves. This exercise provides stability and control, making it suitable for lifters of varying experience levels.
instructions: Position yourself under the Smith machine bar with your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly in front of you.
Unrack the bar by rotating it forward and position it across your upper back, ensuring it's comfortable and secure.
Keep your chest up, core engaged, and back straight throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending at the knees and hips, keeping your knees aligned with your toes.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below, ensuring your heels remain flat on the ground.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, fully extending your legs without locking your knees.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Feet positioned too far forward or backward, leading to improper knee alignment.
Allowing knees to cave inward during the squat, increasing strain on the joints.
Not maintaining a neutral spine, resulting in excessive lower back stress.
Descending too quickly, causing loss of control and potential for improper form.
Failing to engage the core, leading to instability and increased risk of injury.
Not reaching a full range of motion, limiting muscle activation and effectiveness.
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels, reducing glute and hamstring engagement.
Locking out the knees at the top of the movement, causing unnecessary joint stress.
exercises.name: Smith Hack Squat
tips: Ensure proper alignment by keeping your knees in line with your toes to prevent injury.
Maintain a controlled tempo throughout the exercise to maximize muscle engagement.
Focus on pushing through your heels to effectively target the quadriceps and glutes.
Keep your core tight to support your lower back and maintain balance.
Adjust the foot positioning as needed to find a comfortable stance that allows full range of motion.
Avoid locking out your knees at the top of the movement to maintain tension on the muscles.

exercises.description: The Smith Incline Chest Press is a compound exercise targeting the upper portion of the pectoral muscles, utilizing the Smith machine for guided movement. This exercise allows for controlled lifting with added stability, making it suitable for both beginners and advanced lifters aiming to enhance upper chest development.
instructions: Set the bench to an incline angle of about 30-45 degrees under the Smith machine bar.
Position yourself on the bench with your back firmly against it and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, ensuring wrists are straight and aligned with forearms.
Unrack the bar by rotating it forward and position it directly above your upper chest.
Inhale and lower the bar slowly to your chest, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Pause briefly when the bar is just above your chest without bouncing.
Exhale and press the bar back up to the starting position, ensuring arms are fully extended but not locked.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Setting the bench at too steep an angle, which shifts focus from the chest to the shoulders.
Placing hands too wide or too narrow on the bar, leading to improper chest muscle engagement.
Failing to maintain a slight arch in the lower back, which can reduce chest activation.
Allowing the bar to bounce off the chest, reducing muscle tension and control.
Lowering the bar too far down, causing excessive shoulder strain.
Pushing the bar unevenly, leading to muscle imbalance and reduced effectiveness.
Using momentum to lift the bar instead of controlled muscle contraction.
Not aligning the bar path with the upper chest, which can shift tension away from target muscles.
Locking out elbows at the top, reducing time under tension for the chest muscles.
Neglecting to engage the core, which can lead to instability during the lift.
exercises.name: Smith Incline Chest Press
tips: Ensure the bench is securely positioned before starting to prevent any movement during the exercise.
Maintain a controlled tempo throughout, focusing on both the eccentric (lowering) and concentric (pressing) phases.
Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body and prevent arching of the back.
Adjust the incline angle if needed to target different areas of the chest more effectively.
Warm up properly before attempting heavier weights to reduce risk of injury.
Use a spotter if lifting heavy to ensure safety, especially when nearing muscle fatigue.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/史密斯机跪姿臀桥

exercises.description: The Smith Kneeling Hip Thrust is a lower body exercise that primarily targets the gluteus maximus, with secondary emphasis on the hamstrings and core. It is performed using a Smith machine, which provides stability and control, allowing for focused muscle engagement. This exercise is ideal for building strength and size in the glutes while minimizing lower back strain.
instructions: Position a bench or padded surface behind the Smith machine bar at knee height.
Kneel on the floor with your back facing the bench, and position your shoulders against it.
Place the Smith machine bar across your hips, ensuring it is securely locked in place.
Grip the bar with both hands for stability.
Engage your core and glutes, then thrust your hips upward until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your glutes tightly.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position without resting them on the ground.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Placing feet too far forward or backward, leading to improper hip alignment.
Allowing the bar to rest on the lower back instead of the hips, causing discomfort and reducing effectiveness.
Failing to engage the glutes fully, relying too much on the lower back.
Using excessive weight that compromises form and control.
Rushing through the movement without pausing at the top to maximize muscle engagement.
Not maintaining a neutral spine, leading to potential lower back strain.
Allowing knees to collapse inward, reducing glute activation.
Performing partial reps without reaching full hip extension.
exercises.name: Smith Kneeling Hip Thrust
tips: Ensure that your knees are directly below your hips at the starting position to maximize glute engagement.
Keep your chin tucked and gaze forward throughout the movement to maintain a neutral spine.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of each repetition to enhance muscle activation.
Avoid hyperextending your lower back by controlling the movement and maintaining core engagement.
Start with lighter weights to perfect your form before progressing to heavier loads.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/史密斯器械俯身划船

exercises.description: Bend over inside a Smith machine and row the guided bar from knee height to your upper abdomen to build your lats and mid-back. Your lats do most of the pulling, while your middle and lower traps, rhomboids and the small shoulder-blade muscles draw your shoulder blades together; your rear delts and arms help. The bar rides in fixed tracks, so there's nothing to balance, and your foot position decides where it meets your body. It's a good way to learn the bent-over row, or to push hard sets late in a back session with the safety stops set; for the heaviest rows, use a free barbell.
instructions: Set the safety stops a few centimeters below the bottom of your rep, around knee height, and the hooks at mid-thigh.
Stand behind the bar with your feet hip-width, placed so the bar will hang straight under your shoulders once you lean over.
Grip the bar overhand with your thumbs wrapped, hands just outside your thighs at shoulder width or a little wider.
Unhook the bar, soften your knees and push your hips back until your torso leans about 45° (lower only if your back stays flat).
Let the bar hang at arm's length and brace your stomach, neck in line and eyes on the floor just ahead of your feet.
Pull your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows up and back, about 30–45° from your sides, until the bar touches just under your ribs.
Squeeze for a second at the top, then lower over about 2 seconds to straight arms, your head at the same height every rep.
Re-hook the bar only after the last rep, with your back still flat.
mistakes: Feet in the wrong spot for the track: the bar scrapes your thighs and knees, or hangs out in front of your shoulders and drags you forward. Move your feet until it hangs straight under your shoulders, and test that with an empty bar before loading.
Standing up a little on every pull so your hips lift the bar. Lock in your torso angle in the hang and keep your head at one height; if you can't, the weight is too heavy.
Rowing to your chest or neck with your elbows flared out to 90°. Aim the bar at your upper abdomen and keep your elbows about 30–45° from your sides.
Cutting reps short, with your elbows stopping level with your torso. Finish each rep with your shoulder blades pinched together and hold it for a second.
Resting the bar on the safety stops, or bouncing it off them, between reps. Set the stops below your hang so every rep starts from straight arms with the bar in the air.
Rounding your upper back and letting your shoulders roll forward at the bottom. Keep your chest open; your shoulder blades should spread only a little.
exercises.name: Smith Machine Bent Over Row
tips: Row 3–4 sets of 8–12 reps, up to 15, or 6–8 for strength. Keep the same weight until you get the top number in all sets with the same torso angle and a full squeeze, then add 2.5–5 kg in total and drop back to the low end.
Bar weight varies from one Smith machine to the next, and some are counterbalanced, so log your plates and compare sessions on the same machine.

Expect to feel it along the sides of your back and between your shoulder blades. Your lower back and hamstrings only hold the bent-over position: steady effort, never pain. If your biceps and forearms do most of the work, you're pulling with your hands; think “elbows back.”

Lower back giving out before your upper back? Take weight off and stand a little taller, or switch to the Chest Supported Machine Row. To make it harder, pause 2 seconds at the top or lower over 3–4 seconds.

Substitutes: Barbell Bent Over Row (free bar, heavier loads, lower torso), Double Dumbbell Bent Over Row (easiest swap when the Smith is taken), T-Bar Bent Over Row, Barbell Bent Over Row From Pin (every rep from a dead stop).

Engage your core and slowly extend your leg backward, pushing the bar with your foot.

Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the movement.

Focus on squeezing your glutes throughout the movement for maximum activation.
Keep your core engaged to prevent lower back strain.

exercises.description: The Smith Machine Good Morning is a compound exercise targeting the posterior chain, primarily focusing on the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings. It involves bending at the hips while maintaining a neutral spine, using the Smith Machine to guide the movement safely.
instructions: Set the bar of the Smith Machine at shoulder height and position yourself under it, resting the bar across your upper traps.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Unlock the bar by rotating it forward and take a step back to clear the safety stops.
Keep your chest up and core engaged as you hinge at the hips, pushing them backward.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, maintaining a slight bend in your knees.
Reverse the movement by driving through your heels and extending your hips to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Placing the bar too high on the neck, causing discomfort and potential strain.
Bending the knees excessively, turning the movement into a squat.
Not hinging at the hips, leading to poor engagement of the posterior chain.
Allowing the bar to drift forward, increasing strain on the lower back.

Failing to engage the core, leading to instability.
Moving too quickly, reducing control and muscle engagement.
Not maintaining a straight line from head to tailbone.
exercises.name: Smith Machine Good Morning
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement to avoid lower back strain.
Engage your core muscles to stabilize your torso and protect your spine.
Focus on hinging at the hips rather than bending at the waist.
Keep a slight bend in your knees to reduce stress on the joints.
Control the descent and ascent to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Start with a lighter weight to master form before progressing to heavier loads.
Ensure that your feet remain flat on the ground throughout the exercise.

exercises.description: Stand in a Smith machine, push your hips back and lower the guided bar along your thighs to just below the knees to build your glutes and hamstrings. The stretch grows along the back of your thighs on the way down, then your glutes and hamstrings stand you up while your lower back stays flat. The bar runs in fixed tracks, so you never balance it: your feet set its path, and the safety stops let you push sets close to failure without a spotter. Reach for it when learning to hinge or for hard hamstring work late in a session; for the heaviest loads, the barbell version wins.
instructions: Set the bar hooks at about mid-thigh height and the safety stops just below your lowest point, roughly mid-shin.
Stand behind the bar, feet hip-width and parallel, so it touches your thighs and sits over mid-foot. The track won't move; your feet set the path.
Take an overhand grip about shoulder-width, hands just outside your thighs, and rotate the bar off the hooks. No step back: you're already in position.
Breathe in, brace your stomach and unlock your knees to a soft bend of about 15–20°. That knee angle doesn't change until the last rep.
Push your hips straight back. Your torso tips forward as the bar slides down your thighs, back flat, eyes on the floor 1–2 m ahead.
Lower over 2–3 seconds and stop when your hips stop traveling back, usually with the bar just below the knees, well above the stops.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes until you stand tall, hips under shoulders. Re-hook the bar only from this upright position, never from the bottom.
mistakes: Feet in the wrong spot for the track: the bar drags off your thighs or jams into your knees and shins on the way down. Place your feet so the bar touches your thighs at the top and sits over mid-foot, and test it with one empty-bar rep before loading.
Bending the knees more as you descend until the shins tip forward and the rep becomes a regular Smith deadlift. Lock in the soft bend at the top and think "hips back, shins vertical."
Rounding your lower back to reach the stops or the floor. Depth ends where your hips stop moving back with a flat back; if the back rounds before that, take plates off.
Parking or bouncing the bar on the safety stops between reps. Set them below your working range and lower over 2–3 seconds so a normal rep never touches them.
exercises.name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
tips: Do 2–4 sets of 8–12 reps here, up to 15, or 6–8 when strength is the goal.
Add reps first. Once you get 12 on all sets with the same depth and a flat back, add 2.5–5 kg in total and go back to 8.
Smith bars weigh different amounts, and some are counterbalanced, so log the plates you load and compare sessions on the same machine.

Expect a strong pull behind your thighs on the way down. A lower back that burns more than your hamstrings means you're going too deep or rounding; feeling it mostly in the front of your thighs means your knees are bending too much. If your grip quits first, use lifting straps.

Still learning the hinge? Groove it with the Cable Pull Through, or stop the bar just above your knees with a light load. When that feels easy, add a 2-second pause just below the knees, slow the lowering to 4 seconds, or move to the free barbell.

Substitutes: Romanian Deadlift (free barbell, you balance it and can go heavier), Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (easiest swap when the Smith is taken), Cable Romanian Deadlift, Smith Machine Good Morning (bar on your upper back, so grip drops out).

Lifting the bar too high, placing undue stress on the shoulder joints.
Shrugging the shoulders instead of focusing on the deltoids and traps.
Leaning forward, which can strain the lower back.
Pulling with the wrists instead of leading with the elbows.
Failing to engage the core, resulting in instability.
Rushing through reps without controlled movement.
Allowing the elbows to drop below the wrists at the top of the movement, reducing muscle engagement.
exercises.name: Smith Machine Upright Row
tips: Maintain a neutral spine and avoid leaning forward or backward during the lift.
Focus on leading with your elbows rather than pulling with your hands.
Keep your wrists straight to minimize strain and reduce injury risk.
Control the movement speed to maximize muscle engagement and avoid momentum.
Exhale as you lift the bar and inhale as you lower it back down.
Start with a lighter weight to master form before progressing to heavier loads.

Step back with one leg into a lunge position, ensuring your front knee is aligned with your ankle.
Lower your back knee towards the ground without letting it touch, keeping your torso upright.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
