Dropping the back knee too quickly, leading to a lack of control and potential strain.
Failing to keep the torso upright, resulting in excessive forward lean and reduced effectiveness.
Not engaging the core, which compromises stability and control.
Using too much weight, leading to compromised form and increased risk of injury.
Allowing the front foot to rotate outward, reducing alignment and muscle engagement.
Neglecting to push through the heel of the front foot, minimizing glute activation.
Rushing through the movement, which reduces muscle tension and control.
Not maintaining a consistent tempo, causing uneven muscle engagement.
exercises.name: Smith Rear Lunge
tips: Ensure your front knee does not extend beyond your toes to prevent strain on the knee joint.
Maintain a straight back and engage your core throughout the movement for stability.
Focus on a controlled descent and ascent to maximize muscle engagement.
Adjust the position of your feet to find a comfortable stance that allows for full range of motion.

Lower the bar slowly behind your head until it is just above your shoulders.
Press the bar back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms but avoiding locking your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Not engaging the core, resulting in poor posture and support.

Not maintaining a controlled descent, increasing risk of injury.
Locking out the elbows at the top, which can stress the joints.
Neglecting to adjust the seat height, affecting shoulder alignment.
exercises.name: Smith Seated Behind Neck Press
tips: Ensure your back remains straight and pressed against the bench throughout the movement to prevent injury.
Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Avoid lowering the bar too far down to prevent shoulder strain; stop when your elbows are at about a 90-degree angle.
Use a controlled tempo both when lowering and pressing the bar to maximize muscle engagement.

Not keeping the back straight, which can lead to poor posture and reduced effectiveness.

tips: Ensure the bar is securely locked in place before beginning the exercise.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement to avoid unnecessary strain on your back.
Focus on keeping your elbows close to your body to maintain control of the barbell.
Use a moderate weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form.
Breathe in as you lower into the squat and exhale as you push back up to standing.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes to prevent inward or outward collapse during the squat.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/抓举

exercises.description: The snatch is a dynamic Olympic weightlifting exercise that involves lifting a barbell from the ground to overhead in one continuous motion. It requires a combination of strength, speed, flexibility, and technique. The movement is divided into several phases: the first pull, transition, second pull, and catch.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes slightly turned out. Position the barbell over the middle of your feet.
Grip the barbell with a wide grip, arms straight and outside of your knees.
Lower your hips with your chest up and back straight, keeping your gaze forward.
Initiate the lift by pushing through your heels, extending your knees and hips in a smooth motion.
As the bar passes your knees, transition by pulling the bar close to your body and shrugging your shoulders.
Explosively extend your hips and knees while pulling yourself under the bar.
Catch the bar overhead in a deep squat position with arms fully extended and locked out.
Stand up from the squat position to complete the lift, keeping the bar stable overhead.
mistakes: Starting with hips too high or too low, disrupting the pull mechanics.
Pulling with the arms too early, reducing power from the legs and hips.
Not keeping the barbell close to the body, leading to inefficient movement.
Failing to fully extend the hips, resulting in a lack of upward momentum.
Inadequate shoulder mobility, causing poor overhead positioning.
Catching the barbell with bent elbows, compromising stability overhead.
Landing with feet too wide, affecting balance and control.
Neglecting to engage the core, leading to instability during the lift.
Rushing the lift, which can lead to a loss of control and precision.
Improper grip width, affecting the bar path and balance.
exercises.name: Snatch
tips: Ensure your grip is wide enough to allow for a comfortable overhead position.
Keep the barbell close to your body throughout the lift to maintain control and efficiency.
Focus on an explosive hip extension to generate maximum power during the second pull.
Practice flexibility in shoulders and ankles to achieve a stable overhead squat position.
Use lighter weights initially to perfect technique before progressing to heavier loads.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the lift to prevent injury and ensure proper form.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/抓举平衡

exercises.description: Start with the barbell across your upper back in a wide snatch grip, then use a short leg drive to move under it. Receive the bar overhead with straight arms in a squat, stabilize the position and stand up while keeping the bar above your base of support.
instructions: Grip the bar with a wide snatch grip, then place it across your upper traps behind your neck.
Step back from the rack with your feet about hip width apart.
Bend your knees and hips slightly into a short, vertical dip.
Drive forcefully through the floor to extend your legs.
Descend into a squat as you straighten the arms to receive the bar overhead.
Stabilize at the bottom with straight arms, active shoulders and a tight core.
Stand up from the squat while maintaining the locked-out overhead position.
mistakes: Starting with the bar too low on the upper back instead of resting it securely on the traps.
Using a narrow grip that prevents a stable overhead lockout.
Pressing the bar to straight arms before dropping under it, instead of coordinating the leg drive with the descent.
Jumping forward or backward instead of driving straight down into the receiving position.
Catching the bar with soft elbows instead of locking the elbows immediately overhead.
Allowing the chest to fall and the torso to lean forward in the bottom position.
exercises.name: Snatch Balance
tips: Use the bar markings to place your hands symmetrically.
Use a short, controlled dip by bending the knees while keeping your torso upright and your heels down.
Practice landing in the same squat stance on each repetition.
Pause briefly in the bottom to confirm control, then stand up without letting the bar drift forward.
Start with a light bar to coordinate the leg drive and descent.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/抓举握距硬拉

exercises.description: Set your feet about hip-width apart and take a very wide overhand grip on a barbell on the floor. Brace your trunk and push through your legs to stand, keeping the bar close as your hips and knees extend. Lower by sending your hips back, then bending your knees to return the bar to the floor.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, with the barbell over the middle of your feet.
Bend at your hips and knees to reach the bar, using a very wide grip. Your hands should be close to the outer markings on the bar, wider than your normal deadlift grip.
Keep your arms straight and place your shoulders slightly in front of the bar. Keep the bar close to your shins.
Set your back in a neutral position, lift your chest slightly, brace your abdominal muscles, and pull the slack out of the bar without lifting it from the floor.
Push the floor away with your legs and extend your hips and knees together. Keep the bar in contact with, or very close to, your legs throughout the lift.
Finish standing tall with your hips and knees fully extended. Do not lean backward or shrug the bar upward.
Lower the bar by pushing your hips back first, then bend your knees once the bar passes them. Return the bar to the floor under control and reset your position before the next repetition.
mistakes: Using a grip that is too narrow, turning the lift into a regular deadlift.
Letting the bar drift away from the legs instead of keeping it close throughout the lift.
Rounding the lower or upper back as the bar leaves the floor.
Shooting the hips up before the chest, turning the lift into a stiff-legged pull.
Bending the elbows or trying to pull the bar with the arms.
Jerking the bar off the floor instead of building tension before the pull.
exercises.name: Snatch Grip Deadlift
tips: Start with a lighter load than your conventional deadlift because the wide grip increases the travel.
Set your feet about hip width apart with the bar over your midfoot.
Use a level floor and equal plates on both ends of the bar.
Take a breath before lifting and exhale after reaching the standing position.
Use straps if grip limits your training, especially for higher reps, but keep your hands secure and do not rely on straps to compensate for poor position.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/抓举拉高

exercises.description: The Snatch Pull is a weightlifting exercise that focuses on developing explosive power, strength, and technique for the snatch lift. It targets the posterior chain, including the hamstrings, glutes, lower back, traps, and shoulders. This exercise is crucial for improving the second pull phase of the snatch by emphasizing speed and power through the hips and legs.
instructions: Start by standing with your feet hip-width apart, with the barbell over your mid-foot.
Bend at the hips and knees to grip the barbell with a wide, overhand grip.
Set your back by retracting your shoulder blades and engaging your core.
Initiate the lift by extending your knees and hips simultaneously, keeping the bar close to your body.
As the bar passes your knees, explosively extend your hips and knees while shrugging your shoulders upward.
Keep your arms straight until you reach full extension, then allow a slight bend as you pull the bar to chest height.
Control the bar back to the starting position for the next repetition.
mistakes: Starting with hips too high, leading to poor leverage and reduced power.
Rounding the back, increasing the risk of lower back strain.
Pulling with the arms too early, reducing the effectiveness of the leg and hip drive.
Not fully extending the hips, limiting the power transfer from the lower body.
Allowing the bar to drift away from the body, causing imbalance and inefficiency.
Neglecting to engage the core, leading to instability during the lift.
Failing to keep elbows high and outside, compromising the bar path.
Using an incorrect grip width, affecting the lift's mechanics and range of motion.
Rushing the lift, sacrificing control and technique for speed.
exercises.name: Snatch Pull
tips: Focus on maintaining a strong back position throughout the lift to prevent injury.
Keep the barbell close to your body to maximize power transfer.
Use a hook grip for better control of the barbell during explosive movements.
Engage your core muscles to stabilize your torso during the lift.
Practice with lighter weights to perfect technique before increasing load.
Visualize driving through your heels to generate maximum force from the ground up.
Ensure a smooth transition from knee extension to hip extension for optimal power output.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱二头肌/蜘蛛锤式弯举

exercises.description: The Spider Hammer Curl is an isolation exercise targeting the brachialis and brachioradialis muscles in the arms. It involves curling dumbbells with a neutral grip while leaning forward, typically performed on an incline bench. This exercise enhances arm thickness and forearm strength.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle.
Lie face down on the bench, ensuring your chest is supported and your arms hang straight down.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep your elbows slightly bent and stationary throughout the movement.
Curl the dumbbells upward by flexing your elbows, keeping your wrists straight.
Squeeze at the top of the movement, focusing on contracting the brachialis.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weights instead of isolating the biceps.
Allowing the elbows to drift forward or backward, reducing bicep engagement.
Using a grip that is too tight, causing unnecessary forearm tension.
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom, limiting range of motion.
Curling the wrists at the top of the movement, shifting focus away from the biceps.
Rushing through the movement, sacrificing control and muscle engagement.
Lifting weights that are too heavy, compromising form and increasing injury risk.
Failing to maintain a neutral spine, leading to poor posture and potential back strain.
exercises.name: Spider Hammer Curl
tips: Maintain a controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid swinging your arms or using momentum to lift the weights.
Focus on keeping your elbows stationary to isolate the target muscles effectively.
Exhale as you curl the weights up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Start with lighter weights to ensure proper form before progressing to heavier loads.
Ensure your chest remains in contact with the bench to prevent unnecessary strain on your back.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/分腿挺举

exercises.description: Hold the barbell on the front of your shoulders, dip vertically and drive it upward with your legs. Move one foot forward and the other back to receive the bar overhead with straight arms and bent knees. Stabilize the split, move the front foot back first and recover your stance before lowering the bar.
instructions: Set the barbell in the front rack position, resting on your shoulders with elbows slightly in front of the bar. Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and brace your core.
Take a small controlled dip by bending your knees and hips straight down. Keep your chest upright, heels on the floor, and knees tracking over your toes.
Drive forcefully through the floor to extend your hips, knees, and ankles, sending the bar upward from your shoulders.
As the bar rises, quickly split your legs, placing one foot forward and the other behind you. Land with both knees bent, your front shin close to vertical, and your back heel raised.
Punch your arms straight overhead and lock out your elbows as you receive the bar. Keep the bar directly over the middle of your body, with your head slightly forward between your arms.
Hold the split position briefly to confirm balance and control. Keep your torso upright and do not let the bar drift forward or behind you.

Recover by stepping your front foot back partway, then bringing your back foot forward to stand with your feet together. Keep the bar locked overhead until you are fully stable, then lower it safely to the shoulders or rack.
mistakes: Dipping forward instead of keeping the torso upright
Letting the knees cave inward during the dip and drive
Pressing the bar up before fully extending the hips and knees
Letting the bar travel forward instead of driving it straight overhead
Landing with soft elbows instead of locking the arms overhead
Taking an uneven split stance, with the feet too narrow, too wide, or on the same line
Keeping the back leg too straight instead of bending the knee to absorb the catch
Recovering the feet in the wrong order or stepping out of the split before control is established
exercises.name: Split Jerk
tips: Start with the bar in the front rack, elbows slightly in front of the bar, chest tall and weight balanced through the whole foot.
Set your feet about hip width apart before the dip. Keep them parallel and avoid starting too wide.
Use the same lead leg throughout a set to keep the split pattern consistent.
Keep your head neutral and look straight ahead once the bar is locked out. Do not crane your neck forward.
Practice with an empty bar or light weight until your dip, drive, split and recovery are consistent. Increase load only when you can lock out and stabilize every repetition.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/分腿蹲

exercises.description: The split squat is a lower-body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and calves. It involves a unilateral movement pattern that enhances balance and stability while improving strength in the legs. This exercise is performed by stepping one foot forward and lowering the hips until the rear knee nearly touches the ground, then returning to the starting position.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart.
Step forward with your right foot, keeping your torso upright.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your left knee nearly touches the floor.
Ensure your right knee is aligned over your right ankle and does not extend past your toes.
Push through the heel of your right foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
mistakes: Allowing the front knee to cave inward, which can lead to knee strain.
Letting the back knee touch the ground, reducing control and engagement.
Failing to keep the torso upright, resulting in poor balance and core disengagement.
Pushing off with the front foot's toes instead of the heel, limiting glute activation.
Not maintaining a stable and straight back leg, causing imbalance.
Allowing the front foot to be too far forward, leading to ineffective range of motion.
Neglecting to engage the core, which can lead to lower back strain.
Rushing through the movement, sacrificing control and proper muscle engagement.
Not keeping the weight evenly distributed between both legs, causing uneven muscle activation.
exercises.name: Split Squat
tips: Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement to engage core muscles.
Focus on keeping your front knee aligned with your ankle to prevent injury.
Control the descent to maximize muscle engagement and maintain balance.
Use a mirror or a partner to check form and ensure proper alignment.
Start with body weight before adding resistance like dumbbells or a barbell.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/前脚抬高分腿蹲

exercises.description: The Split Squat Front Foot Elevated is a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. Elevating the front foot increases the range of motion, enhancing muscle activation and flexibility. This exercise also engages the core for stability and balance.
instructions: Begin by standing in front of a platform or step, about 6-12 inches high.
Place your right foot on the platform, ensuring your heel is firmly planted.
Step back with your left foot, positioning it so that both knees can bend comfortably.
Keep your torso upright and engage your core.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.
Ensure your right knee does not extend beyond your toes.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
mistakes: Knee extends beyond toes, increasing stress on the joint.
Back leg is too straight, reducing range of motion and muscle engagement.
Torso leans forward excessively, shifting focus away from target muscles.
Front foot is not fully supported, leading to instability.
Hips are not squared, causing uneven weight distribution.
Front knee caves inward, risking knee strain.
Inadequate depth, limiting muscle activation.
Rushed movements, reducing control and effectiveness.
Uneven weight distribution between legs, leading to imbalance.
Neglecting core engagement, compromising stability.
exercises.name: Split Squat Front Foot Elevated
tips: Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement to protect your lower back.
Focus on a slow and controlled descent to maximize muscle engagement.
Keep your core tight to help maintain balance and stability.
Ensure your front knee tracks over your toes to avoid unnecessary strain.
Adjust the height of the platform according to your flexibility and comfort level.
Use a mirror to check form and alignment during the exercise.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/臀部/前脚抬高分腿蹲

exercises.description: The Split Squat Front Foot Elevated is a unilateral lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. Elevating the front foot increases the range of motion, enhancing muscle activation and flexibility. This exercise also improves balance and stability.
instructions: Stand in front of a platform or step, about 6-12 inches high.
Place your right foot on the platform, ensuring your heel is secure.
Step back with your left foot into a split stance, keeping your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core and maintain an upright torso throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.
Ensure your right knee does not extend beyond your toes and your left knee hovers just above the floor.
Push through the heel of your right foot to return to the starting position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
mistakes: Knee caves inward during descent, reducing stability and increasing joint stress.
Front knee extends past toes, leading to improper weight distribution.
Back leg is too straight, limiting range of motion and hip flexor engagement.
Torso leans too far forward, shifting focus away from the targeted muscles.
Front foot is placed too high, causing excessive strain on the knee joint.
Lack of core engagement, leading to balance and control issues.
Pushing off with the back foot instead of driving through the front heel.
Allowing the front heel to lift off the platform, reducing stability.
Inadequate depth, preventing full activation of the glutes and quads.
Rushing through the movement, compromising form and muscle activation.
exercises.name: Split Squat Front Foot Elevated
tips: Keep your chest up and shoulders back to maintain proper posture.
Focus on driving through the heel of the front foot for maximum glute activation.
Maintain a controlled tempo to enhance stability and muscle engagement.
Avoid locking out the knees at the top of the movement to keep tension on the muscles.
Use a mirror or ask for feedback to ensure proper form and alignment.
Start with body weight before adding resistance like dumbbells or a barbell.

exercises.description: The Spoto Press is a bench press variation that involves pausing the barbell just above the chest, enhancing control and tension in the muscles. This exercise targets the pectoral muscles, triceps, and anterior deltoids, and is particularly effective for improving bench press strength and stability.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the ground.
Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and position it directly above your shoulders with arms fully extended.
Lower the barbell slowly towards your chest, stopping 1-2 inches above it.
Pause for a brief moment, maintaining tension in your muscles.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position with controlled force.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest instead of pausing just above it.
Allowing the elbows to flare out excessively, reducing shoulder stability.
Arching the lower back excessively, compromising form and increasing injury risk.
Failing to maintain a tight grip on the bar, leading to poor control.
Dropping the bar too quickly, losing tension and control during the descent.
Not engaging the core, resulting in a lack of overall body stability.
Positioning the wrists incorrectly, leading to unnecessary strain.
Using too much weight, causing form breakdown and reduced effectiveness.
exercises.name: Spoto Press
tips: Focus on maintaining a tight core and stable shoulder position throughout the movement.
Keep your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body to reduce shoulder strain.
Use a spotter or safety bars if lifting heavy weights to ensure safety.
Control the descent of the barbell to maximize muscle engagement.
Practice proper breathing: inhale as you lower the bar, exhale as you press it up.
Start with lighter weights to master form before progressing to heavier loads.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/冲刺跑

exercises.description: Run at maximal or near-maximal speed for a short burst. Drive your knees forward and up, push the ground back hard with each stride and pump your arms from the shoulders with your elbows bent at about 90 degrees. Keep your torso tall and stable and land under your hips with quick, springy contacts.
instructions: Choose a flat, non-slip surface with enough room to slow down safely after the sprint.
Stand with one foot slightly ahead of the other, your weight over the front foot and your elbows bent to about 90 degrees.
Push off explosively, driving the back knee forward while the opposite arm swings forward.
For the first strides, lean slightly forward from the ankles and push the ground back behind you, then rise gradually as you gain speed.
At top speed, run tall with your hips high, drive each knee forward and up, and land on the ball of the foot under your hips.
Pump your arms forward and back from the shoulders, hands rising to about chin height and elbows driving back. Do not swing them across your body.
When the set time is up, slow down gradually over several strides, then walk back and rest before the next sprint.
mistakes: Standing upright from the first step instead of leaning forward while accelerating
Overstriding, with the foot landing far in front of the hips and braking each stride
Landing heavily on the heel instead of the ball of the foot
Weak knee drive, so the thigh barely rises in front of the body
Letting the hips sink or bending at the waist, which shortens the stride
Leaning back as you reach top speed
Swinging the arms across the body instead of straight forward and back
Short, passive arm swings without driving the elbows back
exercises.name: Sprint
tips: Do two or three build-up runs at increasing speed before your first all-out sprint.
Fold the swing leg so the heel rises close to your glutes. A folded leg swings forward faster.
Pull your toes up toward the shin before each contact so the ankle stays stiff and springy.
Keep your jaw, shoulders and hands relaxed. Upper-body tension slows your stride.
For speed work, keep each sprint short, about 6 to 15 seconds, and stop the set when your speed or form drops.
Rest 2 to 5 minutes between maximal sprints so every one is fast.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/深蹲

exercises.description: The squat is a fundamental lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and core muscles. It is performed by lowering the hips from a standing position and then returning to standing, while keeping the back straight and feet flat on the ground.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Bend your knees and push your hips back as if sitting in a chair.
Lower your body until your thighs are at least parallel to the ground.
Ensure your knees are tracking over your toes without collapsing inward.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
mistakes: Allowing knees to cave inward during the movement.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the squat.
Not keeping the chest up and shoulders back.
Letting heels lift off the ground.
Descending too quickly without control.
Not reaching full depth, stopping too high.
Leaning too far forward, shifting weight onto toes.
Failing to engage core muscles for stability.
Using momentum instead of muscle engagement to rise.
Placing feet too close or too wide apart for balance.
exercises.name: Squat
tips: Keep your weight on your heels to maintain balance and stability.
Focus on keeping your chest lifted to avoid rounding your back.
Use a mirror or have a partner check your form to ensure proper alignment.
Start with bodyweight squats before adding weights to master the form.
Breathe in as you lower down and exhale as you push up.
Warm up properly before squatting to prevent injury.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/深蹲开合跳

exercises.description: The squat jack keeps the legs working in a low squat while small hops alternate between a narrow and wide stance. Hold your hands in front of your chest, open and close your feet without standing up, and absorb each landing through bent knees that follow the direction of your toes.
instructions: Lower into a squat with your hands together in front of your chest.
Brace your abdomen and keep your chest lifted.
Make a small hop to bring your feet closer together while staying low.
Hop your feet apart again to return to a wider squat stance.
Land with bent knees that follow the direction of your toes.
Continue opening and closing your stance without standing up between hops.
mistakes: Letting the knees cave inward instead of tracking over the toes.
Rising out of the squat between jumps instead of staying low.
Landing with straight or locked knees.
Landing heavily instead of absorbing the impact softly through the hips and knees.
Allowing the chest to collapse forward and the back to round.
Letting the heels lift off the floor during the squat.
exercises.name: Squat Jack
tips: Exhale on take-off and breathe in as you reset.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest as a position cue.
Use short sets that let you repeat the same movement pattern.
Pick a point in front of you to help maintain your balance.
Use a firm floor with reliable traction when changing the foot spacing.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/平板支撑收腿跳

exercises.description: A bodyweight conditioning exercise in which you jump both feet from a high plank into a deep crouch just behind your hands, then jump them back out to the plank. Your hands stay planted under your shoulders the whole time, so your abs, hip flexors and shoulders work to keep your body stable.
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders, arms straight and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your abs and glutes.
Jump both feet forward together, driving your knees toward your chest.
Land softly in a deep crouch with your feet just behind your hands. Keep your hands flat on the floor.
Without pausing, jump both feet back and land in the high plank with your legs straight.
Repeat for the planned number of reps without lifting your hands off the floor.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag in the plank and arching the lower back
Piking the hips up in the plank instead of holding a straight line
Bringing the feet only partway in, so they land far from the hands
Jumping back too far, so the shoulders end up behind the hands
Bending the elbows on landing
Landing with one foot before the other or one foot ahead
Letting the head drop toward the floor
exercises.name: Squat Thrust
tips: As you jump in, shift your shoulders slightly forward over your hands. This takes weight off your feet and makes the jump easier.
Spread your fingers and push the floor away to keep your upper back firm.
Pull your knees in with your abs. Your hips will rise a little as your feet travel forward.
Land quietly in both the crouch and the plank. A loud landing means you are dropping instead of controlling the jump.
Breathe out as you jump in and breathe in as you jump back.
To make it easier, step one foot in and out at a time instead of jumping.

exercises.description: The Stability Ball Crunch is an effective core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles. By performing this exercise on a stability ball, you engage more muscle fibers and improve balance and coordination. This exercise primarily works the rectus abdominis, with secondary engagement of the obliques and transverse abdominis.
instructions: Sit on a stability ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Walk your feet forward and roll your back onto the ball until your lower back is supported and your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Place your hands behind your head with elbows wide, or cross them over your chest.
Engage your core by pulling your navel towards your spine.
Exhale as you lift your upper body off the ball, curling your shoulders towards your hips.
Pause at the top of the movement for a moment, ensuring maximum contraction of the abs.
Inhale as you slowly lower back down to the starting position, maintaining tension in your core.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Positioning the ball too high under the back, reducing core engagement.
Placing feet too close together, compromising stability.
Pulling on the neck with hands, causing strain.
Using momentum instead of controlled movements.
Allowing hips to sag, disengaging core muscles.
Rising too high, shifting focus away from the abs.
Failing to maintain a neutral spine alignment.
Holding breath instead of breathing steadily.
Not engaging the core before initiating the movement.
exercises.name: Stability Ball Crunch
tips: Ensure that the stability ball is properly inflated to maintain balance and effectiveness.
Keep your feet firmly planted on the ground to prevent slipping during the exercise.
Focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift rather than pulling on your neck or head.
Maintain a slow and controlled motion throughout to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid arching your back excessively; keep it in a natural curve supported by the ball.
Breathe out during the crunch phase and inhale as you return to the starting position.
For increased difficulty, try extending your arms overhead or holding a weight plate across your chest.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/健身球靠墙深蹲

exercises.description: The Stability Ball Wall Squat is an exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and core muscles. It involves using a stability ball placed between your lower back and a wall to perform a squat with added support and balance challenge.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, positioning a stability ball between your lower back and a wall.
Lean back slightly against the ball, ensuring it is secure and stable.
Engage your core muscles and keep your chest up.
Slowly bend your knees and lower your body into a squat position, keeping your knees aligned with your toes.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as comfortable without losing form.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the squat.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, keeping the movement controlled.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Placing the stability ball too high or too low on the back, leading to improper support and balance.
Allowing knees to extend beyond toes, increasing strain on the knee joints.
Failing to maintain a straight line from head to tailbone, resulting in poor posture and reduced core engagement.

exercises.description: Stand with your back to a high pulley, hold a rope at your temples and curl down until your elbows reach your knees: a weighted crunch done on your feet. The six-pack muscle (rectus abdominis) does the work along its whole length, and the bottom of each rep is where it burns most; the obliques at the sides of your waist help a little. All you need is a rope and a high pulley, no mat or bench, so it suits days when kneeling bothers your knees. For heavier loads, switch to the kneeling version facing the stack.
instructions: Clip a triceps rope to the high pulley of a cable column or lat-pulldown station.
Take a rope end in each hand, turn your back to the stack and step forward until the cable hangs just behind your head.
Bring your fists to your temples, palms facing in, with the rope behind your head and your bent elbows pointing forward and down.
Set your feet hip-width apart, toes forward, knees soft. Stand tall with your ribs down; the plates should already be off the stack.
Breathe out and curl from the top: chin in, upper back rounding, ribs pulling toward your pelvis, fists still glued to your temples.
Curl until your elbows reach your knees and your head is about knee height.
On the way, your hips slide back slightly and your knees bend a bit more.
Hold the squeeze for a second, uncurl over about 2 seconds and stop once you're upright. Start the next rep before the plates touch down.
When the set is done, step back toward the column until the weight rests, then let go. Released at your head, the rope whips straight up.
mistakes: Folding at the hips with a flat back: your trunk tips forward in one piece and you feel it in the back of your thighs. Think "ribs to pelvis" and round your upper back first; your hips move back only a little, at the very end.

Pulling the rope down with your arms, so your hands leave your head and your elbows open up like a triceps pushdown. Pin your fists to your temples and keep the elbow angle fixed. If your arms keep taking over, drop the weight.

Letting the stack yank you back up past vertical, so your lower back arches or you step back to catch your balance. Take about 2 seconds to uncurl and stop as soon as you're upright; if you still lose balance, the weight is too heavy.

Standing in the wrong spot. Too far from the column and the cable drags you backward; too close and the rope scrapes your neck while the plates rest on the stack. Stand where the cable hangs just behind your head, usually a foot-length out.
Dipping your knees to push the weight down instead of curling. Keep them soft and nearly still; they bend a little only as your hips move back at the bottom.
Yanking your head down chin-first and straining your neck. Let your head follow your upper back as it rounds, with your hands at your temples and never on your neck.
exercises.name: Standing Cable Ab Crunch
tips: Take 2–4 sets of 10–20 reps close to failure.

Going heavier than 8–12 rarely pays off here, because standing, your balance gives out before your abs do. Pick a range such as 12–15 and add reps at the same weight until you get 15 on every set with a full curl, a one-second squeeze and a 2-second return. Then add one plate (usually 2.5–5 kg) and go back to 12. If that plate pulls you off balance at the top, stay at the old weight and slow the reps down instead.

You should feel the whole front of your stomach working, with a hard burn at the bottom and a little at the sides of your waist. Tired arms or shoulders mean you're pulling the rope; a stretch in the back of your thighs means you're folding at the hips with a flat back. Sharp pain in your lower back, or pain running into a leg, means stop.

Keep turning it into a hip bend? Learn the curl seated first, where the bench pins your hips. Once the standing version gets easy, slow the return to 3–4 seconds and hold the bottom for 2 before you add a plate. Loads differ from one pulley to the next, so only compare weights on the same station.

Substitutes: Kneeling Cable Abs Crunches (same rope and curl, facing the stack, heavier loads), Seated Ab Cable Crunch (no balance needed), Machine Abdominal Crunches (fixed path, small weight jumps) and Band Standing Crunches (the same standing crunch at home or when every cable is taken).

exercises.description: Stand with a dumbbell beside each ear and press both overhead until your elbows lock out: a staple for building bigger, stronger shoulders. Unlike the seated version, there's no backrest, so your glutes and abs have to keep your torso upright. The front and side delts do most of the pressing, and your triceps take over as your arms straighten at the top. Each arm finds its own path, so many lifters find it easier on the wrists and shoulders than a barbell press, and a pair of dumbbells is all you need.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, toes forward or turned out slightly, knees straight but not locked back.
Curl the dumbbells to your shoulders. With heavy ones, rest them on your thighs and kick them up with a knee, one at a time.
Hold them beside your head at ear or jaw height, palms facing forward and handles in one line, each wrist stacked straight over its elbow.
Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs down so your torso stays vertical, eyes straight ahead.
Press both dumbbells up together and slightly inward, keeping your forearms vertical as they rise.
Lock your elbows with the dumbbells almost touching above the crown of your head, upper arms by your ears. Hold for a moment.
Take about 2 seconds to lower back to ear level with your elbows just below your shoulders. Press again without bouncing.
To finish, bring the dumbbells down to your shoulders, then to your thighs, before you put them on the floor.
mistakes: Leaning back and arching your lower back until the press turns into an incline press. Squeeze your glutes and keep your ribs down; if you still lean, the dumbbells are too heavy.
Dipping your knees to drive the last reps up. That's a push press. Keep your legs still and end the set when your arms can't finish a rep on their own.
Letting the dumbbells drift in front of your face with the forearms tilted. Stack each wrist over its elbow and finish above the crown of your head, upper arms beside your ears.
Cutting the range at both ends: turning around at forehead height or stopping short of straight arms. Lower to ear or jaw level and lock out every rep.
exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press
tips: For shoulder size, 3–4 sets of 8–12 reps work well, ending each set 1–3 reps short of failure. Build reps at one weight. Once all sets reach 12 with a full lockout and no lean, move to the next pair, usually 1–2.5 kg heavier per dumbbell, and work up again from 8. With light dumbbells that step can be a 15–20% jump, so do your first set with the new pair and the rest with the old one until it sticks.

You should feel the front and side of your shoulders, most in the bottom half of the press, and the back of your arms near lockout. A tired lower back means you're leaning back, so pick lighter dumbbells. A pinch on top of the shoulder with your arms overhead ends the set; next time bring the elbows a little further forward.
Too wobbly? Sit on an upright bench, or at home use the Band Shoulder Press. Too easy and no heavier pair around? Take 3 seconds to lower and pause for one second at the bottom.

Substitutes: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press, Barbell Overhead Press, Dumbbell Standing Alternate Press, Machine Shoulder Press. Sit down to load the shoulders with the least lower-back work, or press one arm at a time when two heavy dumbbells overhead feel shaky.

Keep a small bend in the standing knee and square your hips forward.
Hinge forward from your hips toward the extended leg, keeping your back long and chest open.
Reach your hands toward your shin, ankle, or foot only as far as you can without rounding your lower back or forcing the stretch.
Hold the stretch while breathing steadily, feeling it along the back of the extended thigh.
Return to standing slowly, then repeat on the other side.

Pushing the front knee into hyperextension rather than keeping the straight leg relaxed.
Letting the hips rotate or shift away from the extended leg.
Bouncing at the bottom of the stretch instead of holding a steady position.
Forcing the range of motion and stretching into sharp pain.
Letting the extended foot turn inward or outward instead of keeping it aligned with the knee.

tips: Keep the front heel on the floor with the toes pointing upward.
Keep most of your body weight on the rear leg.
Use your shin or ankle as a reach target if the toes are out of reach.
Breathe slowly and let the tension ease with each exhale.
Hold for about 20 to 30 seconds, then repeat on the other side.

exercises.description: Hold one dumbbell overhead in both hands, lower it behind your head and straighten your arms again to train your triceps from a deep stretch. All three heads of the triceps work. The long head crosses the shoulder, so with your arms up it is already lengthened at the bottom, and that is where you feel the strongest pull. A single dumbbell and no bench is all it takes, so it suits home workouts. Because you stand, nothing supports your back: keep your abs braced, and move to the seated version once your lower back starts to arch.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, knees straight but not locked. Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your ribs stay down.
Stand the dumbbell on end and cup the top plates from underneath with both palms side by side, thumbs around the handle. The handle hangs between your forearms.
Bring the dumbbell to your chest and press it straight up. At the top your arms are vertical, upper arms by your ears, elbows about shoulder-width apart.
Bend your elbows and take 2–3 seconds to lower the dumbbell behind your head. It stays vertical; only your forearms move.
Keep going until your elbows are fully bent and the lower end of the dumbbell sits near the back of your neck, or stop higher if that depth hurts.
Straighten your arms to a full lockout without snapping into the joint, and hold the squeeze for half a second.
When you finish, bring the dumbbell back over your head to your chest and lower it to your thigh. Never let it drop behind you.
mistakes: Elbows drifting wide as the dumbbell goes behind your head. Point them up and slightly forward, roughly shoulder-width apart, and drop the weight if they won't stay there.
Ribs flaring and lower back arching as your arms straighten. Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs down; if the arch stays, go lighter or sit down.
Upper arms swinging forward and down until the rep turns into a pullover or a press. Pin them beside your head and let only the forearms move.
Reversing the rep with the dumbbell only at the top of your head. The deep stretch is what this exercise is for, so bend your elbows fully on every rep that stays pain-free.
Lacing your fingers around the handle. The dumbbell tilts and can slip; cup the top plates instead and keep it vertical.
Poking your head forward to make room. Eyes forward, head still, and let the dumbbell travel behind it.
exercises.name: Standing One Dumbbell French Press
tips: A good dose is 2–4 sets of 10–15 reps, finishing most sets one or two reps short of failure.

Elbows rarely like very heavy sets in a deep overhead stretch, so stay at 8 reps or more. Add reps first: when you reach 15 in all sets with a full stretch, a full lockout and no back arch, take the next dumbbell, usually 1–2.5 kg heavier, and start again at 10. On a light dumbbell that is a big step, so expect a few sessions at each weight.

At the bottom you should feel a strong pull along the back of your upper arm toward the armpit, and at lockout a hard squeeze. Feeling it in your lower back means your ribs have flared: brace harder or go lighter. Sharp pain at the elbow in the stretch says shorten the bottom; a pinch at the top of the shoulder says skip overhead work today.
Easier: reverse the rep when the dumbbell reaches ear level, or do the seated version with back support. Harder: pause 1–2 seconds in the stretch and take 3 seconds on the way down.
Using an adjustable dumbbell? Tighten the collars before the first set, because the plates pass right behind your head and neck.

Substitutes: Dumbbell Seated Triceps Extension, the same two-hand lift seated with back support, when your lower back arches or you want a heavier dumbbell; One-Arm Overhead Triceps Extension to work each arm on its own; Cable Overhead Triceps Extension, where the cable still pulls at lockout, the point at which the dumbbell goes light; Standing Overhead Barbell Triceps Extension for a fixed grip width.

Not aligning the wrists and elbows properly, leading to instability.

exercises.name: Straight Leg Raise on Dip Bars
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the movement to prevent arching of the lower back.
Avoid swinging or using momentum to lift your legs; focus on controlled movements.
If you find it difficult to keep your legs straight, start with bent knees and gradually progress to straight leg raises as you build strength.
Ensure that your shoulders remain stable and do not shrug up towards your ears during the exercise.
Breathe steadily; exhale as you lift your legs and inhale as you lower them.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/直臂背阔肌下拉

exercises.description: Hinge forward at a high pulley and sweep a short straight bar from above your head to your knees with straight arms, so your lats do the pulling. The work sits along the sides of your back and in the teres major at the back of your armpit, while your lower traps hold the shoulder blades down. Your elbow angle never changes, so your biceps and grip can't give out first. That makes it a good lat warm-up before pull-ups or pulldowns and a finisher after rows. Pick the bar over the rope version when you want both hands fixed on one bar and a steadier, heavier set.
instructions: Clip a short straight bar to the high pulley and pick a light weight to start. A lat bar held shoulder-width also works.
Grip the bar overhand at shoulder width and walk back a long step or two, until the plates stay up with your arms reaching forward.
Feet hip-width and knees soft, push your hips back until your torso is about 30–45° above horizontal. Back flat, head between your arms.
Reach your arms forward and up in line with your torso. Set a small bend in the elbows and keep that angle for the whole set.
Start each rep by pulling your shoulders down, away from your ears, before the bar moves.
Sweep the bar in an arc, moving only at the shoulders, until your arms are near vertical and the bar is in front of your knees.
Hold a second, then let the bar rise over about 2 seconds along the same arc until you feel a stretch under your armpits.
When the set is done, walk toward the tower and let the plates settle on the stack before you let go of the bar.
mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows so the bar gets pushed down like a triceps pushdown. Set a small bend at the top and keep it, moving hands and upper arms as one piece from the shoulders. If you can't, the weight is too heavy.
Standing up out of the hinge or bobbing your torso to get the bar moving. Set your hips back before the first rep and keep the chest angle fixed; if the torso has to move, drop a plate.
Rounding your lower back to get deeper into the hinge. Hips back, knees soft, back flat. Hinge a little less if your back starts to round.

Half reps: the bar stops halfway down, or your arms never come back in line with your torso. Finish with your arms vertical and a one-second hold, and on the way up return to the full stretch without letting the plates touch down.
exercises.name: Straight-Arm Lat Pulldown
tips: Sets of 10–15 reps suit most people. This isn't a lift for heavy singles; around 8–10 clean reps is as heavy as it usually pays to go. Add reps first: when you reach 3 × 15 with the same torso angle and no elbow bend, move the pin down one plate, usually 2.5–5 kg, and work up again from 10. If the stack jumps in 5 kg plates or bigger, use the add-on weight or stay on each weight longer.

Most of the work runs along the sides of your back from the armpit toward your waist, plus a little low between the shoulder blades and in the back of your upper arms. If your triceps or forearms burn more than your back, your elbows are bending and straightening.

Two to four sets do the job as a warm-up before pull-ups or as a finisher after rows. Torso keeps bobbing? Go lighter and stop the bar at your thighs, or switch to the Machine Pullover, where the seat holds you still. To make it harder, take 3 seconds to sweep the bar down and hold it 2 seconds at the bottom.
If the stretched top position pinches the front of your shoulder, stop the bar a little lower on the way up.

Substitutes: Rope Straight-Arm Lat Pulldown (hands can travel past your hips, wrists neutral), One-Arm Straight-Arm Cable Lat Pulldown (evens out left-right differences), Machine Pullover, Dumbbell Pullover (lying on a bench, no cable needed).

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/臀部/相扑硬拉

exercises.description: The Sumo Deadlift is a compound exercise that primarily targets the muscles of the posterior chain, including the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back, while also engaging the quadriceps and adductors. This variation of the deadlift involves a wider stance and a more upright torso compared to the conventional deadlift, which can reduce stress on the lower back and allow for greater emphasis on hip mobility and strength.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Position yourself close to the barbell so that it is over the middle of your feet.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower your body, keeping your chest up and back straight.
Grip the barbell with both hands inside your knees, using a double overhand or mixed grip.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders back before initiating the lift.
Push through your heels and extend your hips and knees to lift the barbell, keeping it close to your body.
Stand fully upright with shoulders back at the top of the lift.
Lower the barbell back to the ground in a controlled manner by bending at the hips and knees.
mistakes: Feet positioned too narrow, reducing stability and power.
Hips set too high, causing excessive strain on the lower back.
Shoulders not aligned over the bar, leading to poor leverage.
Knees caving inward, increasing the risk of knee injury.
Bar drifting away from the shins, compromising balance.
Back rounding excessively, risking spinal injury.
Failing to engage the lats, resulting in a lack of upper body tension.
Pulling with the arms instead of driving with the legs.
Not locking out the hips fully at the top of the lift.
Descending too quickly, losing control of the bar.
Not maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
tips: Focus on keeping your chest up and back straight throughout the movement to prevent injury.
Ensure that your knees track in line with your toes as you lift to maintain proper form.
Engage your core muscles before lifting to stabilize your spine and improve power transfer.
Start with lighter weights to master form before progressing to heavier loads.
Use a mixed grip if necessary to improve grip strength and control over heavier weights.
Maintain a neutral head position by looking forward or slightly down during the lift.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/臀部/相扑硬拉短拉

exercises.description: Lift the barbell from the floor in a wide sumo stance with a narrow overhand grip between your knees. Extend the hips and knees dynamically, then bend the elbows outward to continue the pull, finishing with the bar near the waist as shown before lowering it under control.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width, toes turned slightly out, with the barbell over the middle of your feet.
Bend your knees and hips to grip the bar with a narrow overhand grip, hands inside your knees.
Push through your feet to lift the bar, extending your knees and hips together.
When the bar reaches mid-thigh, drive your hips forward powerfully and rise onto your toes if needed.
Use the leg and hip drive to continue the pull, bending your elbows outward as the bar rises near your waist.
Finish upright with the bar near your waist and the elbows slightly bent, without leaning back.
Lower the bar under control by straightening your arms first, then guide it down your thighs and return it to the floor with a neutral back.
mistakes: Letting the knees collapse inward instead of tracking over the toes.
Rounding the lower back as the bar leaves the floor.
Pulling the bar away from the body, which makes the lift less controlled.
Bending the arms too early instead of driving through the legs and hips first.
Beginning the short finishing pull before fully extending the hips.
Leaning back excessively at the top instead of finishing tall with ribs stacked over the pelvis.
exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift with Short Pull
tips: Set your feet wider than shoulder width with toes turned out slightly, then grip the bar with your hands inside your knees.
Use the bar markings to keep the narrow grip symmetrical.
Reestablish your grip and stance with the bar still on the floor before each repetition.
Lower the bar under control by returning it to your hips first, then bending your knees and hips to place it back on the floor.
Practice the short finishing pull with an empty bar before adding weight.

exercises.description: Perform a Romanian deadlift with a wide, toes-out stance and the bar held inside the legs. Push the hips back with a small knee bend, lowering the bar toward the shins, then extend the hips to stand. This wide-stance hip hinge works the glutes, hamstrings and inner thighs.
instructions: Stand upright holding the bar at your thighs, with feet wider than shoulder width and toes turned out.
Hold the bar with an overhand grip inside your legs and keep your knees slightly bent.
Set your back flat, brace your core, and pull your shoulders down and back. Keep your chest open and your neck neutral.
To lower the bar, keep a slight bend in your knees and push your hips back. Let the bar travel straight down close to your thighs and shins.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings and inner thighs while maintaining a flat back. Do not force the bar lower by rounding your lower back.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing, squeezing your glutes at the top. Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Repeat with controlled tempo. Stop the set if you cannot keep your back neutral or the bar drifts away from your legs.
mistakes: Letting the knees cave inward instead of tracking over the toes.
Rounding the lower or upper back as the weight lowers.
Holding the weight away from the legs instead of keeping it close to the body.
Failing to brace the core before each repetition.
Locking the knees hard or hyperextending them.
Leaning back and overextending the lower back at the top.
Rushing the lowering phase instead of controlling the weight.
exercises.name: Sumo Romanian Deadlift
tips: Choose a stance that leaves room for the hands inside the knees.
Wrap your thumbs around the bar for a secure grip.
Spread pressure across the whole foot throughout the hinge.
Exhale as you approach standing and inhale before the descent.
Focus on the stretch through the back and inside of the thighs as the hips move back.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/相扑深蹲

exercises.description: The Sumo Squat is a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and inner thighs. It involves a wider stance than a traditional squat, which emphasizes the adductor muscles and provides a different angle of engagement for the lower body muscles.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly outward.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core engaged throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if sitting into a chair.
Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not extend past them.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below, depending on flexibility.
Press through your heels to return to the starting position, fully extending your hips and knees.
mistakes: Feet positioned too narrowly, reducing stability and limiting range of motion.
Knees collapsing inward, increasing stress on the joints.
Hips not pushed back enough, leading to excessive forward knee movement.
Torso leaning too far forward, shifting weight away from the heels.
Not maintaining a neutral spine, causing unnecessary strain on the back.
Failing to engage core muscles, reducing overall control and stability.
Descending too quickly, compromising control and muscle engagement.
Not squatting low enough to fully activate glutes and inner thighs.
Allowing heels to lift off the ground, decreasing balance and power.
Rising unevenly, causing an imbalance in muscle activation.
exercises.name: Sumo Squat
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement to avoid lower back strain.
Focus on keeping your weight distributed evenly across your feet, particularly pressing through the heels.
Engage your core to stabilize your torso and prevent leaning forward.
Adjust your stance width based on comfort and flexibility to ensure proper form.
Control the descent and ascent to maximize muscle engagement and reduce injury risk.
Inhale as you lower down and exhale as you push back up to maintain breathing rhythm.

exercises.description: The Sumo Squat off Stepbox is a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and inner thighs. By performing this squat variation on a stepbox, you increase the range of motion and engage stabilizing muscles for improved balance and strength.
instructions: Position a stepbox securely on the floor.
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart on the stepbox, toes pointing slightly outward.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core engaged.
Lower your body by bending at the hips and knees, keeping your back straight.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
mistakes: Feet positioned too close together, reducing stability and range of motion.
Knees collapsing inward, increasing stress on knee joints.
Excessive forward lean, shifting weight onto toes and straining lower back.
Not engaging core, leading to poor balance and control.
Descending too quickly, losing control and risking improper form.
Not reaching full depth, limiting muscle activation in glutes and inner thighs.
Allowing heels to lift off the stepbox, reducing stability and power.
Rounding the back, increasing risk of spinal strain.
Incorrect stepbox height, affecting squat depth and muscle engagement.
Failing to keep chest up, leading to poor posture and reduced effectiveness.
exercises.name: Sumo Squat off Stepbox
tips: Ensure the stepbox is stable before starting the exercise.
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement to prevent injury.
Engage your core to help stabilize your body during the squat.
Focus on pushing through your heels to activate the glutes effectively.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes to avoid unnecessary strain.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/史密斯机相扑深蹲

exercises.description: The Sumo Squat With Smith Machine is a lower body exercise targeting the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and inner thighs. This variation of the squat involves a wider stance and utilizes the Smith machine for stability and control, allowing for a focused engagement of the lower body muscles.
instructions: Position the bar of the Smith machine at shoulder height and set the safety stops just below your lowest squat position.
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and toes slightly pointed outwards.
Place the bar across your upper back, ensuring it rests comfortably on your trapezius muscles.
Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar by straightening your legs and stepping back slightly.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to lower into a squat by bending at the hips and knees.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below, ensuring your knees track over your toes.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, fully extending your hips and knees.
mistakes: Feet positioned too close together, reducing stability and engagement of inner thighs.
Knees caving inward instead of tracking over the toes, leading to improper alignment.
Hips not pushed back far enough, causing excessive forward knee movement.
Barbell placed too high on the neck, increasing strain on the cervical spine.
Lack of core engagement, resulting in a loss of balance and control.
Descending too quickly, which can lead to poor form and reduced muscle activation.
Not squatting to an appropriate depth, limiting the range of motion and effectiveness.
Allowing heels to lift off the ground, decreasing stability and power.
Using arms to push the bar instead of maintaining a stable shoulder position.
Neglecting to keep the chest up, leading to a rounded back and potential lower back strain.
exercises.name: Sumo Squat With Smith
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement to prevent injury.
Focus on keeping your knees aligned with your toes to avoid unnecessary strain on the joints.
Engage your core muscles to stabilize your torso during the squat.
Keep your weight distributed evenly across both feet, with emphasis on pushing through the heels.
Adjust the width of your stance as needed to ensure comfort and proper form.
Use a controlled tempo to maximize muscle engagement and maintain balance.
Start with a lighter weight to perfect your form before progressing to heavier loads.

exercises.description: A classic yoga flow that links a standing reach, a forward fold, plank, upward-facing dog and downward-facing dog, with one breath for each movement. Use it as a warm-up or a mobility routine for the hamstrings, hips, shoulders and spine, repeating several rounds at an even pace.
instructions: Stand at the front of your mat with your feet together or hip-width apart and your palms together at your chest.
Inhale and sweep your arms overhead.
Exhale and fold forward from your hips, bending your knees as needed to place your hands beside your feet.
Inhale and lift your chest halfway with a long spine. Exhale and step or jump back to a high plank.
Lower with control through chaturanga with your elbows close to your ribs, or lower your knees first.
Inhale into upward-facing dog with straight arms and your thighs off the floor, or into cobra.
Exhale, lift your hips up and back into downward-facing dog and hold for about five breaths.
Step or jump your feet to your hands, lift halfway, fold, then inhale and rise with your arms overhead. Exhale and bring your palms back to your chest.
mistakes: Rushing and losing the link between breath and movement.
Letting the hips sag or pike up in plank.
Flaring the elbows and dropping the shoulders below elbow height in chaturanga.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears in plank or upward-facing dog.
Leaving the hips and thighs on the floor in upward-facing dog.
Landing heavily when jumping back, which jars the wrists and shoulders.
exercises.name: Sun Salutation A
tips: Let the breath set the pace: inhale as you open or lift, exhale as you fold or lower.
Spread your fingers and press the whole hand into the mat in plank and downward-facing dog.
If chaturanga is too hard, lower your knees first and choose cobra instead of upward-facing dog.
In downward-facing dog, keep a long spine first. Bend your knees if your back rounds.
In the halfway lift, keep your neck in line with your spine and look slightly forward.

exercises.description: The Superman exercise is a bodyweight movement targeting the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings. It involves lying face down and simultaneously lifting the arms and legs to engage the posterior chain.
instructions: Lie face down on a mat with your arms extended in front of you and legs straight.
Keep your neck in a neutral position by looking at the floor.
Simultaneously lift your arms and legs off the ground, engaging your core and glutes.
Hold the top position for a moment while squeezing your back muscles.
Slowly lower your arms and legs back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Lifting the head too high, causing neck strain.
Arching the lower back excessively, leading to discomfort.
Failing to engage the core, reducing stability.
Raising arms and legs unevenly, causing imbalance.
Holding breath, which can increase tension.
Not fully extending arms and legs, limiting range of motion.
Rushing the movement, sacrificing control.
Allowing shoulders to shrug, reducing effectiveness.
exercises.name: Superman
tips: Focus on controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid arching your neck; keep it aligned with your spine.
Engage your core throughout the exercise to maintain stability.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift and inhaling as you lower.
Start with smaller lifts if you're new to this exercise to build strength gradually.

exercises.description: The Spider Push Up is a dynamic variation of the traditional push-up that engages the core, chest, shoulders, triceps, and obliques. It involves bringing one knee towards the elbow on the same side as you lower your body, adding an element of core stabilization and mobility.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
As you lower your chest towards the ground, simultaneously bring your right knee towards your right elbow.
Push back up to the starting position while returning your right leg to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left knee towards your left elbow.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Failing to engage the core, leading to a sagging lower back.
Incorrect hand placement, causing imbalance and reduced power.
Insufficient arm extension, limiting the range of motion.
Lifting the chest too high, resulting in strain on the lower back.
Poor coordination between arm and leg lift, disrupting the flow of the movement.
Neglecting to maintain a straight body line, causing improper form.
Landing too heavily, increasing the risk of wrist and shoulder strain.
Rushing the movement, leading to loss of control and precision.
exercises.name: Superman Push-Up
tips: Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement to ensure proper form.
Engage your core muscles to help stabilize your body as you perform the exercise.
Focus on controlled movements rather than speed to maximize muscle engagement and reduce injury risk.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you lower down to target the triceps effectively.
Breathe out as you push up and breathe in as you lower down for optimal breathing technique.
