exercises.description: Superman swimmers use alternating lifts of the opposite arm and leg while lying face down with the limbs hovering above the floor. Reach forward with the arms and back with the legs, moving in a small, steady flutter while the pelvis stays supported and the neck remains in line with the trunk.
instructions: Lie face down with straight legs and both arms reaching overhead.
Brace the abdomen and lift the arms and legs slightly from the floor, keeping the pelvis supported.
Look down and keep the head in line with the trunk.
Raise the right arm and left leg slightly higher as the left arm and right leg lower toward the floor.
Switch pairs and continue alternating without resting the limbs on the floor.
Finish by lowering the arms and legs gently to the floor.
mistakes: Lifting the chest too high and overextending the lower back instead of using the upper back and glutes.
Letting the hips or pelvis rock side to side during each repetition.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears instead of keeping the neck long and shoulder blades controlled.
Looking forward and cranking the neck, rather than keeping the head in a neutral position.
Using fast, swinging movements instead of slow alternating lifts with control.
Bending the knees or elbows excessively and shortening the movement.
exercises.name: Superman Swimmers
tips: Reach long through the fingertips and toes.
Use a comfortable width between the arms and between the feet.
Let the movement follow a regular swimming rhythm.
Breathe continuously rather than matching every small flutter.
Use a mat if the contact under the hips is uncomfortable.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/支撑式头倒立（头立式）

exercises.description: Kneel facing a wall or use a spotter. Interlace your fingers, place your forearms on the floor shoulder-width apart, and rest the crown of your head lightly between your hands. Lift your hips, walk your feet closer, then draw your knees toward your chest and slowly extend your legs overhead. Press firmly through your forearms and shoulders to keep weight off the neck, maintaining a long, controlled body line. Lower with control and rest before repeating. Avoid if you have neck, shoulder, eye-pressure, or blood-pressure concerns.
instructions: Practice near a wall with a clear, padded surface, and avoid this exercise if you have neck, shoulder, eye-pressure, blood-pressure, or balance concerns unless cleared by a qualified healthcare professional.
Kneel facing the wall and place your forearms on the floor, interlacing your fingers to create a stable cup for the back of your head.
Set your elbows about shoulder-width apart; keep them from sliding outward by checking that each hand can lightly hold the opposite elbow before interlacing your fingers again.
Place the crown of your head gently on the floor with the back of your head supported by your interlaced hands, keeping pressure light through the neck.
Tuck your toes, lift your knees, and walk your feet toward your torso until your hips are stacked as closely as possible over your shoulders.
Press firmly through your forearms and shoulders, drawing your shoulder blades away from your ears so most of the load is supported by your upper body rather than your head and neck.
Bend one knee and draw it toward your chest, then bring the other knee in to balance in a compact tuck position without kicking off the floor.
When stable, slowly extend both legs upward until your body forms a straight line, keeping your core engaged, legs together, and gaze neutral.
Hold the position while breathing steadily and maintaining active pressure through your forearms; stop immediately if you feel neck pain, tingling, dizziness, or loss of control.
To exit, bend both knees into the tuck position, lower one foot and then the other to the floor with control, and rest briefly in Child’s Pose before standing.
mistakes: Placing too much weight on the head instead of distributing it through the forearms and shoulders
Allowing the elbows to flare wide, reducing the stability of the forearm base
Shrugging the shoulders or collapsing through the upper back instead of actively pressing through the forearms
Using a loose or unstable hand clasp that lets the head shift during the hold
Placing the crown of the head too far forward or backward rather than centered within the forearm base
Kicking up aggressively instead of lifting the legs with controlled core engagement
Arching the lower back and letting the ribs flare instead of stacking the hips over the shoulders
Keeping the hips behind the shoulders, creating a banana-shaped position rather than a vertical line
Bending the knees or separating the legs unintentionally during the hold
Letting the legs drift forward or backward instead of making small controlled balance adjustments
Holding the breath and losing trunk tension
Dropping out of the position without control instead of lowering the legs slowly
exercises.name: Supported Headstand
tips: Warm up the shoulders, upper back, wrists, and neck before practicing, and only attempt the full position if you can comfortably hold a stable dolphin pose.
Set up on a firm, non-slip surface with your forearms shoulder-width apart and elbows directly under the shoulders; interlace the fingers to create a stable cup for the back of the head.
Place the crown of the head lightly on the floor with the back of the head supported by your clasped hands; avoid putting the forehead or the back of the skull directly into the floor.
Press strongly through the forearms and lift the shoulders away from the ears so the neck stays long and does not carry most of your body weight.
Walk the feet in gradually until the hips stack over the shoulders, then draw the knees toward the chest with control before extending the legs upward.
Keep the ribs gently drawn in, engage the abdominals and glutes, and aim to stack ankles, hips, and shoulders in one vertical line rather than arching the lower back.
Use a wall for initial practice, but avoid kicking forcefully into it; build balance by lifting one knee at a time and moving slowly.
Breathe smoothly and keep the jaw, face, and neck relaxed; come down immediately if you feel neck pain, pressure, dizziness, tingling, or loss of control.
Exit with the same control used to enter: bend the knees, bring them toward the chest, lower the feet quietly, and rest in Child’s Pose for several breaths.

Avoid headstands if you have neck or shoulder injuries, uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma or other eye-pressure conditions, recent head injury, or if a qualified professional has advised against inversions.
Practice with a qualified instructor or spotter if you are new to inversions, and prioritize a short, well-aligned hold over trying to stay upside down for a long time.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/悬挂式胸部飞鸟

exercises.description: The Suspension Chest Fly is an upper body exercise that targets the pectoral muscles, utilizing suspension straps to engage stabilizing muscles and enhance core strength. This exercise is effective for developing chest definition and improving shoulder stability.
instructions: Attach suspension straps to an anchor point above head height.
Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding the handles with arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Lean forward slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels, and engage your core.
Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in the elbows.
Lower your body until your chest is in line with your hands, feeling a stretch in your chest muscles.
Reverse the motion by bringing your arms back together in front of you, squeezing your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing the straps to rub against the arms, reducing range of motion and causing discomfort.
Starting with the straps too loose, leading to instability and poor control.
Dropping the hips, which disengages the core and affects balance.
Failing to keep the elbows slightly bent, increasing stress on the shoulder joints.
Letting the hands come too close together at the top, reducing chest engagement.
Not maintaining a straight line from head to heels, compromising posture and core activation.
Allowing the shoulders to hunch forward, reducing chest activation and increasing shoulder strain.
Using momentum to complete the movement, which reduces muscle engagement and control.
Not keeping the wrists neutral, leading to potential wrist strain.
Opening the arms too wide, risking shoulder strain and reducing exercise effectiveness.
exercises.name: Suspension Chest Fly
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the exercise to protect your lower back.
Keep your core engaged to prevent sagging or arching of the lower back.
Adjust your foot position to modify the difficulty; stepping forward increases intensity, while stepping back decreases it.
Focus on controlled movements; avoid using momentum to swing the arms.
Ensure that the straps are taut throughout the exercise for maximum stability and effectiveness.
Breathe out as you bring your arms together and inhale as you open them.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/chest/悬吊式胸部推举

exercises.description: The suspension chest press works the chest and triceps while the trunk stabilises an inclined body against moving handles. Face away from the anchor, lower your chest between the handles by bending your elbows, then press back to straight arms with the straps taut and both feet on the floor.
instructions: Set the suspension straps to mid length and place the handles at chest height. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding one handle in each hand with palms facing down.
Lean forward until the straps are taut, keeping both feet on the floor. Keep your body aligned from head to heels and brace your abdomen and glutes.
Start with your arms straight in front of your chest, hands slightly wider than shoulder width. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Bend your elbows and slowly lower your chest between your hands. Keep your body rigid and allow your elbows to travel at about a 45 degree angle from your torso.
Lower until your hands are beside your chest or until you reach a comfortable depth with control. Do not let your hips sag or your lower back arch.
Press through the handles to straighten your arms and return to the starting position. Keep the straps under tension throughout the movement.
Choose a more upright body angle for less resistance, or a more horizontal angle for greater resistance.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike instead of keeping a straight plank from head to heels.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides instead of keeping them slightly angled back.

Slowly extend your arms to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.description: Face the suspension trainer's anchor and hold both handles with your arms extended, leaning back against the straps. Exhale through the lift and take a fresh breath before the next flip.

exercises.description: Lie on your back with both legs raised vertically and reach toward the toes with straight arms. Lift the shoulders in a short abdominal crunch, then lower them under control while keeping the legs still. The movement works the abdominals without bringing the torso into a full sit-up.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight and raised toward the ceiling. Keep your feet about hip-width apart.
Extend your arms straight up toward your toes, with your palms facing inward.
Press your lower back gently into the floor and brace your abdominal muscles.
Exhale as you lift your shoulders and upper back off the floor, reaching your hands toward your toes.
Keep your legs as still as possible and avoid pulling your head forward with your neck.
Pause briefly at the top when your abs are fully contracted.
Inhale as you lower your shoulders and upper back under control, then repeat.
mistakes: Swinging the arms to create momentum rather than curling the torso up.
Keeping the shoulders on the floor and only reaching with the hands.
Arching the lower back instead of keeping it pressed into the floor.
Letting the legs drift back toward the body or bend excessively.
Rushing the reps and dropping the torso without control.
Holding the breath instead of exhaling as you crunch up.
exercises.name: Toe Touch Crunch
tips: Think of curling the ribs toward the pelvis.
Keep the chin slightly tucked and the neck relaxed.
Look toward the feet as you rise.
Reach with open hands rather than trying to grab the toes.
Pause briefly at the top to feel the abdominal contraction.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/触脚趾运动

exercises.description: Toe Touches are a core exercise targeting the abdominal muscles, specifically the rectus abdominis. This exercise involves lying on your back and reaching your hands towards your toes, engaging the core to lift the shoulders off the ground.
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended straight up towards the ceiling.
Keep your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Engage your core by drawing your belly button towards your spine.
Exhale and lift your shoulders off the mat, reaching your fingertips towards your toes.
Hold the top position briefly, ensuring maximum contraction of the abdominal muscles.
Inhale and slowly lower your shoulders back to the mat, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Bending the knees excessively, reducing hamstring engagement.
Rounding the back instead of hinging at the hips.
Reaching forward with the arms instead of focusing on the torso movement.
Not engaging the core, leading to a lack of stability.
Performing the movement too quickly, sacrificing control.
Failing to maintain a neutral spine, increasing strain on the lower back.
Overextending the arms, causing shoulder strain.
Neglecting to breathe properly, reducing oxygen flow and endurance.
exercises.name: Toe Touches
tips: Keep your lower back pressed against the mat throughout the exercise to prevent strain.
Focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift rather than pulling with your neck or shoulders.
Maintain a steady and controlled movement; avoid using momentum to reach higher.
If you find it difficult to keep legs straight, slightly bend them but ensure they remain elevated.
Breathe out as you reach up and breathe in as you return to the starting position.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/脚趾触杠

exercises.description: Toes To Bar is a dynamic core exercise primarily targeting the abdominal muscles, hip flexors, and grip strength. It involves hanging from a pull-up bar and lifting your toes to touch the bar, requiring coordination, strength, and flexibility.
instructions: Begin by hanging from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Engage your core and initiate the movement by slightly swinging your legs back.
Use your core muscles to lift your legs upward, aiming to bring your toes to touch the bar.
Maintain control throughout the movement, avoiding excessive swinging.
Lower your legs back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Swinging excessively instead of using controlled movement.
Not engaging the core muscles effectively.
Allowing the shoulders to collapse or shrug during the movement.
Failing to maintain a hollow body position throughout the exercise.
Kicking the legs up using momentum rather than controlled muscle engagement.
Not keeping the legs straight during the upward phase.
Bringing the toes to the bar without fully extending the hips.
Dropping too quickly from the top position, risking shoulder strain.
Using a grip that is too loose, leading to loss of control.
Neglecting to activate the lats to stabilize the shoulder girdle.
exercises.name: Toes To Bar
tips: Ensure your grip is firm and secure on the bar to prevent slipping.
Focus on engaging your core muscles throughout the entire movement.
Avoid using momentum; control is key for maximizing effectiveness and safety.
If you struggle to reach the bar with your toes, start by bringing your knees up as high as possible.
Breathe out as you lift your legs and inhale as you lower them back down.
Keep your shoulders engaged and avoid letting them sag during the exercise.

exercises.description: The Trap Bar Deadlift is a compound exercise targeting the lower body, particularly the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and lower back. It utilizes a hexagonal barbell, allowing for a more upright torso position and reducing stress on the lower back compared to a conventional deadlift.
instructions: Stand in the center of the trap bar with feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend at the hips and knees to grip the handles of the trap bar firmly.
Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and spine neutral.
Engage your core and push through your heels to lift the bar by extending your hips and knees.
Stand fully upright with your shoulders back and chest proud at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back to the ground by bending at the hips and knees, maintaining a neutral spine throughout.
mistakes: Starting with hips too low, resembling a squat rather than a deadlift.
Allowing the knees to cave inward during the lift.
Rounding the back instead of maintaining a neutral spine.
Lifting with the arms instead of driving through the legs.
Not engaging the core to stabilize the torso.
Hyperextending the lower back at the top of the lift.
Pulling the bar too quickly off the ground, sacrificing control.
Not keeping the shoulders down and back, leading to shoulder rounding.
Standing too far forward or backward within the trap bar.
Failing to lock out fully at the top of the movement.
Using an incorrect grip width, leading to imbalance.
Not aligning the feet properly under the hips.
exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
tips: Ensure your feet are positioned evenly in the center of the trap bar for balance.
Focus on keeping your chest up and shoulders retracted to maintain a strong back position.
Engage your core muscles throughout the lift to protect your lower back.
Drive through your heels rather than your toes to maximize power and stability.
Control the descent of the bar to prevent injury and maintain form.
Practice with lighter weights to perfect form before increasing load.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/六角杠铃跳跃深蹲

exercises.description: Jump vertically from a squat while holding a trap bar by its side handles with straight arms. The hips, knees and ankles extend together to lift the body and bar, then bend again on landing. This loaded jump trains leg power and requires a light load that allows a controlled landing.
instructions: Stand in the center of the trap bar with your feet about hip-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grasp the handles with a neutral grip, keeping your chest lifted, back flat, and shoulders pulled down.
Lower into a squat with the plates near the floor, keeping your arms straight.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles to jump vertically, allowing the trap bar to travel with your body while keeping your torso stable.
Land softly on the mid-foot with bent knees and hips, absorbing the impact quietly while maintaining a neutral spine and control of the handles.
Reset your position and balance between repetitions, and stop the set if you cannot land safely or maintain an explosive, controlled jump.
mistakes: Starting with the hips too high and turning the movement into a stiff-leg pull
Letting the knees collapse inward during the dip or takeoff
Failing to keep the chest up and the spine neutral throughout the movement
Losing trunk tension while lowering into the squat.
Bending the elbows or pulling with the arms instead of keeping the trap bar stable
Pausing too long between the dip and the jump, which reduces explosiveness
exercises.name: Trap Bar Jump Squat
tips: Choose a light load that allows a clear jump and a stable landing.
Set up inside the trap bar with your feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart and the handles centered over your midfoot.
Start each repetition by driving forcefully through the whole foot, extending your hips, knees, and ankles together.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and then lower the heels under control, absorbing the impact by bending your knees and hips.
Take enough rest between sets to preserve jump height.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/陷阱杠铃耸肩

exercises.description: Trap Bar Shrugs are an exercise targeting the trapezius muscles, performed using a trap bar. This movement emphasizes the upper trapezius and helps improve shoulder stability and posture. The trap bar allows for a neutral grip, which can reduce strain on the wrists and shoulders compared to a straight barbell.
instructions: Stand inside the trap bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and grasp the handles with a neutral grip.
Keep your back straight and chest up as you stand tall with the trap bar.
Engage your core and pull your shoulders up towards your ears in a shrugging motion.
Hold the contraction at the top for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using too much weight, leading to poor form and reduced range of motion.
Failing to keep the core engaged, resulting in a lack of stability.
Allowing the shoulders to roll forward instead of moving straight up and down.
Shrugging too quickly, which reduces muscle engagement and control.
Not fully contracting the traps at the top of the movement.
Bending the elbows, which shifts focus away from the traps.
Leaning forward or backward, compromising balance and form.
Neglecting to keep the neck in a neutral position, leading to strain.
exercises.name: Trap Bar Shrugs
tips: Focus on lifting with your shoulders rather than using momentum.
Keep your elbows slightly bent but fixed throughout the movement.
Avoid rolling your shoulders; lift them straight up and down.
Maintain a neutral spine to prevent lower back strain.
Exhale as you lift your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
Start with a lighter weight to ensure proper form before increasing resistance.

exercises.description: The Trap Y Raise is an isolation exercise targeting the trapezius muscles, particularly the lower and middle fibers, as well as the rear deltoids. It is performed with light weights to focus on muscle activation and improve shoulder stability and posture.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a pair of light dumbbells in each hand.
Bend slightly at the hips and knees, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Let your arms hang down naturally with palms facing each other.
Engage your core and raise your arms in a Y shape until they are in line with your ears.
Pause briefly at the top, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Lifting weights that are too heavy, leading to loss of control and poor form.
Shrugging shoulders instead of keeping them down and retracted.
Arching the lower back excessively, causing strain and reducing effectiveness.
Using momentum to swing the arms instead of controlled, steady movement.
Failing to engage the core, resulting in instability and reduced shoulder isolation.
Allowing the elbows to bend, which shifts focus away from the traps.
Raising arms too high, causing unnecessary shoulder joint stress.
Not maintaining a neutral neck position, leading to potential neck strain.
exercises.name: Trap Y Raise
tips: Use light weights to maintain proper form and focus on muscle activation.
Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders; focus on using your traps and rear delts.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Ensure your core is engaged to support your lower back.
Perform the exercise in front of a mirror to monitor form and alignment.

exercises.description: Treadmill Climbing is a cardiovascular exercise that simulates uphill walking or running. It primarily targets the lower body muscles, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and calves, while also engaging the core for stability. This exercise is effective for improving cardiovascular endurance, burning calories, and enhancing leg strength.
instructions: Begin by setting the treadmill to a low speed and a moderate incline to warm up.
Gradually increase the incline to simulate climbing. Adjust speed as necessary to maintain a steady pace.
Maintain an upright posture with your shoulders back and core engaged.
Use a natural arm swing to help balance and maintain rhythm.
Focus on landing softly on your feet to reduce impact on the joints.
Continue climbing for your desired duration or until you reach your target heart rate.
mistakes: Leaning too far forward, causing strain on the lower back.
Gripping the handrails tightly, reducing the workout's effectiveness.
Using a stride that is too short, limiting range of motion.
Allowing the hips to drop, leading to poor posture and engagement.
Setting the incline too high, causing excessive stress on the knees.
Running instead of walking, which can lead to balance issues.
Failing to engage the core, reducing stability and control.
Overstriding, which can lead to joint discomfort and inefficiency.
Not maintaining a steady pace, resulting in inconsistent effort.
exercises.name: Treadmill Climbing
tips: Start with a gentle incline and gradually increase it as you become more comfortable.
Keep your core tight to support your lower back and improve balance.
Avoid holding onto the treadmill handles unless necessary for balance.
Monitor your heart rate to ensure you are working within your target zone for optimal cardiovascular benefits.
Stay hydrated before, during, and after your workout to maintain performance and recovery.
Incorporate interval training by alternating between different inclines and speeds for added intensity.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/跑步机跑步

exercises.description: The treadmill run is a cardiovascular exercise performed on a treadmill machine, designed to improve aerobic fitness, endurance, and overall cardiovascular health. It allows for controlled speed, incline, and duration settings, making it suitable for various fitness levels.
instructions: Start by standing on the treadmill with your feet on the side rails.
Attach the safety clip to your clothing to ensure the treadmill stops if needed.
Set the treadmill to a low speed to begin and step onto the belt carefully.
Gradually increase the speed to your desired running pace.
Maintain an upright posture with your head up and shoulders relaxed.
Keep your arms bent at a 90-degree angle, swinging naturally with each stride.
Focus on landing softly on the midfoot and rolling through to the toes.
Adjust the incline setting to simulate outdoor running conditions if desired.
Cool down by gradually reducing speed before stepping off the treadmill.
mistakes: Leaning forward excessively, causing strain on the lower back.
Holding onto the handrails, reducing core engagement.
Overstriding, leading to inefficient movement and potential knee stress.
Landing heavily on the heels, increasing impact on joints.
Running with a hunched posture, limiting lung capacity and airflow.
Failing to maintain a consistent pace, affecting workout intensity.
Neglecting to adjust incline, missing out on varied muscle activation.
Allowing the feet to slap the belt, indicating lack of control.
Ignoring arm movement, reducing overall running efficiency.
exercises.name: Treadmill Run
tips: Warm up with a brisk walk or light jog for 5-10 minutes before increasing speed.
Stay hydrated by drinking water before, during, and after your run.
Use proper running shoes to provide adequate support and cushioning.
Listen to music or podcasts to make longer runs more enjoyable.
Monitor your heart rate to ensure you're working within your target zone.
Vary your workouts by changing speed and incline settings regularly.
Focus on breathing deeply and rhythmically to maintain endurance.
Avoid holding onto the handrails as it can disrupt natural running form.

exercises.description: Steady walking on a flat treadmill belt with an upright torso, a natural arm swing and hands off the rails. It is low-impact cardio that works the legs, mainly the quadriceps, glutes and calves, and the set belt speed lets you hold an exact pace for a warm-up, a cool-down or a longer easy session.
instructions: Stand with your feet on the side rails, attach the safety clip to your clothing and start the belt at a slow speed.
Holding a handrail lightly, step onto the belt one foot at a time, then let go once your steps match the belt.
Stand tall with your chest up, shoulders relaxed and eyes looking forward.
Walk in the middle of the belt. Land on your heel just in front of your body and roll through the foot to push off from your toes.
Swing your arms naturally at your sides, opposite to your legs, without touching the handrails.
Raise the speed to a brisk walk you can hold for the planned time, keeping the belt flat.
To finish, lower the speed gradually, stop the belt and step off only once it has stopped completely.
mistakes: Holding the handrails or the console, which takes weight off your legs and changes your gait.
Leaning forward from the hips or rounding the shoulders.
Looking down at your feet or the console, which pulls the head and chest forward.
Overstriding, so the heel lands far in front of the body and brakes every step.
Shuffling with flat feet instead of rolling from heel to toe.
Drifting to the back or the edge of the belt, where it is easy to catch the side rail or slip off.
Setting the speed so high that you break into a jog and lose a steady rhythm.
Stepping off or turning around while the belt is still moving.
exercises.name: Treadmill Walk
tips: Start at a pace where you can still talk in full sentences. As it gets easier, raise the speed or the walking time, one at a time.
Push off through the ball of the foot and the big toe at the end of each step.
Let your arms swing from the shoulders with your elbows slightly bent to keep your rhythm.
Keep your core lightly braced so your pelvis stays level and does not sway from side to side.
Check where the stop button is before you start and keep the safety clip attached for the whole walk.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱三头肌/绳索三头肌后踢

exercises.description: The Tricep Cable Kickback is an isolation exercise targeting the triceps brachii muscle. It involves extending the arm behind the body using a cable machine, which provides constant tension throughout the movement. This exercise helps in building muscle definition and strength in the triceps.
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley cable machine.
Stand facing the machine, holding the handle with one hand, and step back to create tension in the cable.
Bend forward slightly at the hips, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent.
Position your upper arm parallel to your torso, elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Keep your upper arm stationary and extend your forearm backward by straightening your elbow.
Squeeze your tricep at the top of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching arms.
mistakes: Using too much weight, leading to swinging and lack of control.
Allowing the elbow to drift away from the body, reducing triceps engagement.
Failing to fully extend the arm, limiting the range of motion.
Bending the wrist, which can cause strain and reduce effectiveness.
Leaning too far forward, causing instability and improper form.
Not keeping the upper arm parallel to the floor, reducing isolation of the triceps.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement, decreasing muscle activation.
Starting with the cable too high, leading to improper alignment and reduced tension on the triceps.
exercises.name: Triceps Cable Kickback
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the exercise to avoid lower back strain.
Focus on keeping your upper arm still; only your forearm should move during the exercise.
Control the movement to maximize muscle engagement and prevent momentum from taking over.
Exhale as you extend your arm and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Start with a lighter weight to ensure proper form before increasing resistance.

exercises.description: The Triceps Push Up is a bodyweight exercise that targets the triceps brachii muscles, along with engaging the chest, shoulders, and core. It is performed in a plank position, requiring stability and strength to effectively isolate and work the triceps.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core and glutes.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides as you descend.
Continue lowering until your chest is just above the ground.
Push through your palms to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Hands placed too wide, reducing triceps engagement and shifting focus to chest muscles.
Elbows flaring outwards, which decreases triceps activation and increases shoulder strain.
Hips sagging or lifting too high, leading to poor core engagement and potential lower back strain.
Failing to lower the body fully, limiting range of motion and triceps activation.
Not maintaining a straight line from head to heels, causing misalignment and inefficient force distribution.
Rushing through repetitions, reducing control and increasing the risk of improper form.
Allowing shoulders to collapse, which can lead to neck strain and reduced triceps involvement.
Neglecting to engage the core, resulting in instability and decreased overall effectiveness.
exercises.name: Triceps Push-Up
tips: Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout the movement to prevent sagging or arching of the back.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your body to maximize triceps engagement and reduce shoulder strain.
Engage your core and glutes to maintain stability and prevent hip sagging.
Breathe in as you lower down and exhale as you push up.
If you find it difficult to maintain form, perform the exercise on your knees while keeping the same alignment.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱三头肌/v型杆三头肌下压

exercises.description: Facing a high pulley, you push a V-bar from your lower chest down to your thighs by straightening your elbows, which trains your triceps and little else. The angled handles hold your hands about 10 cm apart with the palms turned slightly in, a good fit if a flat overhand grip on a straight bar bothers your wrists or elbows. Unlike a rope, both hands stay fixed on one handle, so you can usually load a bit more. You feel it along the back of your upper arm, mostly the lateral and medial heads, and hardest at lockout, where the stack is still up and pulling.
instructions: Set the pulley at the top of the cable column and clip the V-bar's swivel ring onto the cable.
Take one angled handle in each hand, palms down and turned slightly in, hands about 10 cm apart. Wrap your thumbs and keep your wrists straight.
Stand facing the stack about a forearm's length from the column, feet hip-width or narrower, knees soft, chest up. The cable hangs almost straight down.
Pull the bar to your lower chest and pin your elbows to your ribs, bent about 90 degrees, upper arms vertical. The plates are already lifted.
Push the bar down and slightly back in an arc until your arms are fully straight and your hands reach the front of your thighs. Only the forearms move.
Hold the lockout for half a second and squeeze the back of your arms; the stack is at its highest here and still pulling.
Let the bar rise over 2–3 seconds along the same arc. Stop when your forearms are level with the floor, before your elbows slide forward.
When the set is done, let the bar rise to chest height before letting go. Dropped at the bottom, the cable whips it toward your face.
mistakes: Elbows sliding forward on the way up until the bar reaches your face, so your shoulders start pressing it down. Keep your upper arms vertical and end the return when your forearms are level with the floor.
Leaning over the bar and pushing with your body weight, shoulders rolled forward. Stand tall, step in until the cable hangs straight down, and take a plate off.
Stopping a few degrees short of straight arms, or bouncing out of the bottom. Lock your elbows out on every rep and pause there for half a second.
Elbows flaring out as the bar goes down. Point them straight back; with your hands this close, your forearms should stay close together all the way.
Wrists bending back over the angled handles. Keep your knuckles facing forward and push through the heel of your hand.
exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown V-Bar
tips: Take 2–4 sets of 10–15 reps to one or two reps short of failure. The last set can go all the way, since you can simply stop on a cable.

Add reps before weight. Once you get 15 on all sets with a full lockout and still upper arms, move the pin down one plate and restart at 10. One plate is a big jump on a two-arm triceps move, so expect a few sessions at each weight. Compare numbers only on the same machine, because pulley ratios differ.

Feel it in the front of your shoulders or your chest? Your elbows are drifting forward or you're leaning over the bar. Sharp pain at the tip of the elbow means the weight is too heavy or you're slamming into lockout: go lighter and straighten smoothly.
When a weight gets easy, slow the return to 3 seconds and hold the lockout for a full second. If your elbows won't stay pinned, drop the weight and end the return at navel height until they do.

Substitutes: Cable Triceps Pushdown, with a straight bar at about shoulder width, if you want a wider grip; Rope Triceps Pushdown when your elbows prefer a neutral grip and you like spreading your hands at the bottom; EZ-Bar Tricep Pushdown for a slightly wider angled grip; Band Triceps Pushdown for training at home.

exercises.description: The TRX Biceps Curl is a suspension training exercise that targets the biceps muscles. It utilizes body weight and gravity to provide resistance, enhancing strength and muscle endurance. This exercise is performed using TRX straps, which allow for a range of motion and require core stability.
instructions: Attach the TRX straps to a secure anchor point at an appropriate height.
Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the TRX handles with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Lean back slightly, keeping your body straight and core engaged.
Extend your arms fully in front of you, maintaining tension in the straps.
Pull your body towards the anchor by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Continue curling until your hands are near your shoulders.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Allowing elbows to flare out, shifting focus away from the biceps.
Failing to keep wrists straight, causing strain and reducing effectiveness.
Using momentum to swing the body, decreasing muscle control and engagement.
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom, limiting range of motion.
Pulling with the shoulders instead of isolating the biceps.
Rushing through the movement, sacrificing form for speed.
Not maintaining a stable plank position, affecting core stability and exercise effectiveness.
exercises.name: TRX Biceps Curl
tips: Ensure the TRX straps are securely anchored before starting the exercise.
Keep your elbows close to your body throughout the movement to maximize bicep engagement.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels by engaging your core and glutes.
Control the movement on both the curl and extension phases to enhance muscle activation.
Adjust your foot position to increase or decrease resistance: stepping forward reduces resistance, while stepping back increases it.
Focus on squeezing the biceps at the top of the curl for maximum contraction.
Breathe out as you curl up and inhale as you return to the starting position.

exercises.description: The TRX Single Leg Bird Dog is a compound exercise that targets the core, glutes, and shoulders, enhancing stability and balance. Utilizing the TRX suspension trainer, this exercise requires coordination and control as you extend opposite limbs while maintaining a stable core.
instructions: Attach the TRX straps securely to an anchor point.
Adjust the TRX straps to mid-calf length.
Kneel on the floor with your hands directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Place one foot in the TRX strap loop, keeping your knee bent at 90 degrees.
Engage your core and extend the opposite arm forward while simultaneously extending the leg in the TRX strap backward.
Hold the position for a moment, ensuring your body forms a straight line from hand to foot.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

Arching the lower back instead of maintaining a neutral spine.
Allowing the supporting knee to collapse inward.
Failing to engage the core, leading to instability.
Reaching the arm and leg too high, causing loss of balance.
Not maintaining a straight line from head to heel on the extended side.
Using momentum instead of controlled movements.
Neglecting to keep the shoulders away from the ears.
Letting the TRX straps become slack rather than keeping tension.
Holding the breath instead of breathing steadily.
exercises.name: TRX Single Leg Bird Dog
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement to prevent lower back strain.
Focus on slow and controlled movements to enhance stability and muscle engagement.
Keep your hips level and avoid rotating them as you extend your limbs.
Engage your core by drawing your navel towards your spine to improve balance.
Ensure that your supporting knee is directly under your hip for optimal alignment.
Breathe steadily and consistently throughout the exercise to maintain focus and control.

exercises.description: The Tsunami Overhead Press is a variation of the traditional overhead press, utilizing a flexible barbell known as the Tsunami Bar. This exercise targets the shoulders, triceps, and upper chest while engaging stabilizing muscles due to the bar's oscillating nature. It enhances strength, stability, and coordination.
instructions: Begin by setting up the Tsunami Bar on a squat rack at shoulder height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand grip.
Unrack the bar and step back, keeping your core engaged and feet firmly planted.
Position the bar at shoulder level with your elbows slightly in front of your body.
Press the bar overhead by extending your arms fully, ensuring your head moves slightly forward as the bar passes your face.
Lower the bar back to shoulder level in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using excessive weight, leading to improper form and reduced control.
Failing to engage the core, resulting in an unstable base.
Arching the lower back excessively, increasing risk of lumbar strain.
Allowing elbows to flare out too much, reducing shoulder stability.
Not maintaining a straight wrist position, causing unnecessary wrist strain.
Pressing the bar too far forward, leading to poor shoulder mechanics.
Neglecting to fully extend the arms overhead, limiting range of motion.
Lowering the bar too quickly, compromising control and muscle engagement.
Starting with the bar positioned too low, affecting initial lift mechanics.
Not keeping the head in a neutral position, causing neck strain.
exercises.name: Tsunami Overhead Press
tips: Maintain a tight core throughout the movement to stabilize your spine.
Focus on controlling the bar's oscillations to enhance muscle engagement.
Keep your wrists straight to avoid unnecessary strain.
Ensure your elbows are not flaring out excessively during the press.
Breathe out as you press the bar overhead and inhale as you lower it.
Start with a lighter weight to master form and balance before progressing.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/back/团身前水平悬垂

exercises.description: Hang from a bar with straight arms, then draw your knees to your chest and raise your hips. Lean back until your back is close to horizontal and hold the tucked position with active shoulders. Keep your elbows straight and lower back to the hang under control.
instructions: Set a pull-up bar high enough that your feet cannot touch the floor. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip and hang with straight arms.
Set your shoulders by pulling them down away from your ears and slightly back. Keep your elbows locked and your chest open.
Tighten your abdomen and bring your knees toward your chest. Keep your knees bent and close together.
Lean your torso back while pressing down on the bar with straight arms. Lift your hips until your body is nearly parallel to the floor.
Hold the tuck position with your back rounded slightly, hips lifted, and knees close to your chest. Keep your shoulders depressed and do not let your elbows bend.
To finish, lower your hips under control back to a dead hang, then step down safely.
mistakes: Letting the hips drop below shoulder level instead of holding a horizontal line.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears instead of keeping the scapulae depressed.
Bending the elbows to compensate for insufficient shoulder strength.
Using momentum or swinging into the hold instead of lifting under control.
Letting the knees drift away from the chest and turning the tuck into a longer lever.
Allowing one shoulder or hip to drop lower than the other.
exercises.name: Tuck Front Lever
tips: Use a secure overhand grip about shoulder-width apart on the bar.
Brace your abs, tuck your pelvis under, and keep your ribs pulled down to avoid arching your lower back.
Think about pressing the bar down toward your hips while pulling your body into position.
Keep your neck neutral and look slightly forward or up toward the bar.
Keep holds short, about 5 to 10 seconds, and rest between attempts.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/收腹跳

exercises.description: A bodyweight plyometric jump in which you take off from both feet and pull both knees up toward your chest at the top. A quick dip with an arm swing loads the takeoff, and every rep ends with a soft landing on both feet. It trains leg power, the hip flexors and landing control.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Push your hips back and bend your knees into a quick dip, leaning your torso forward and swinging your arms back.
Swing your arms forward and up and push hard through both feet to jump straight up.
At the top of the jump, pull both knees up toward your chest while keeping your torso upright.
Lower your legs on the way down so your feet are under you before you land.
Land softly on the balls of both feet, then lower your heels and bend your hips and knees to absorb the landing.
Stand up, regain your balance and start the next rep.
mistakes: Letting the knees cave inward in the dip or on the landing.
Landing on straight, stiff legs.
Landing flat-footed or on the heels.
Lifting the knees only a little, so it turns into a plain vertical jump.
Jumping forward instead of straight up.
Landing with the knees still tucked, before the feet are back under the body.
Rounding the back in the dip instead of leaning forward with a flat back.
exercises.name: Tuck Jump
tips: Swing your arms back in the dip and forward and up as you take off. The swing adds height.
Go from the dip straight into the jump without pausing at the bottom.
Bring your knees up to your chest instead of bending your chest down to your knees.
Brace your abs just before takeoff so your torso stays steady in the air.
For power, reset between jumps. For conditioning, rebound into the next jump as soon as you land.
End the set once your landings get loud or unsteady.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/屈膝两头起

exercises.description: Tuck-ups bring the torso and knees together to train the abdominals. Lie with your legs straight and arms overhead, then lift your torso and bend both knees into a seated tuck balanced on your glutes. Reach your hands toward your shins, then lower smoothly and extend your arms and legs again.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms extended overhead.
Brace your abdomen and keep your ribs drawn toward your pelvis.
Lift your torso while bending both knees toward your chest.
Reach both hands toward your shins and balance on your glutes in a compact seated position.
Lower your torso smoothly while extending your legs and returning your arms overhead.
Repeat without using a kick or swinging your arms to start the lift.
mistakes: Using momentum from the arms or upper body.
Letting the lower back arch off the floor at the bottom.
Failing to bring the knees toward the chest during the tuck.
Keeping the arms overhead at the top instead of reaching toward the shins.
Dropping the upper body and feet quickly.
Slamming the feet to the floor between repetitions.
exercises.name: Tuck-Up
tips: Keep both legs together so they act as one balanced lever.
Hold the seated tuck briefly to check your balance before lowering.
Keep your neck relaxed and your chin slightly tucked. Look toward your knees rather than pulling your head forward with your hands.
Exhale as you lift and inhale as you return.
Keep your arms closer to your torso to make the exercise easier.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/土耳其起身

exercises.description: The Turkish Get Up is a full-body exercise that enhances strength, stability, and mobility. It involves transitioning from a lying position to standing while holding a weight overhead, typically a kettlebell. This exercise engages multiple muscle groups including the shoulders, core, hips, and legs.
instructions: Lie on your back with your right leg bent and foot flat on the floor. Extend your left leg straight out.
Hold a kettlebell in your right hand with your arm extended towards the ceiling. Keep your eyes on the kettlebell throughout the movement.
Press through your right foot and roll onto your left hip and forearm.
Push up onto your left hand, keeping the kettlebell stable overhead.
Lift your hips off the ground by pressing through your right foot and left hand.
Sweep your left leg back into a kneeling position under your body.
Align your torso upright by adjusting your kneeling position.
Stand up by driving through your right foot to come to a standing position with the kettlebell overhead.
Reverse the steps to return to the starting position.
mistakes: Rushing through the movement without maintaining control.
Not keeping the wrist straight and aligned with the forearm.
Allowing the shoulder to collapse instead of keeping it packed.
Failing to keep the eyes on the kettlebell throughout the movement.
Not using the non-working arm to assist in the initial roll to elbow.
Letting the knee cave in during the lunge portion.
Raising the hips too high during the transition to the hand.
Not aligning the back knee with the front foot during the lunge.
Neglecting to engage the core throughout the entire exercise.
Using the lower back instead of the hips to drive the movement.
exercises.name: Turkish Get Up
tips: Start with a light weight to master the technique before progressing to heavier weights.
Maintain a strong grip on the kettlebell and keep your wrist straight to ensure stability.
Focus on controlled movements; avoid rushing through each step.
Engage your core throughout the exercise to maintain balance and control.
Keep your eyes on the kettlebell at all times to help maintain alignment and focus.
Practice each segment of the movement separately if you're new to this exercise.
Ensure that each transition is smooth and deliberate, particularly when moving from kneeling to standing.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/仰卧扭转卷腹

exercises.description: A floor crunch with rotation that works the obliques along with the rectus abdominis. Lying on your back with knees bent and hands behind your head, you curl your shoulders up and bring one elbow toward the opposite knee, alternating sides on every rep.
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands behind your head with your elbows out to the sides.
Tighten your abs and press your lower back lightly into the floor.
Exhale and curl your head and shoulders off the floor, rotating your torso to bring one elbow toward the opposite knee.
Pause briefly, then inhale and lower your upper back and head to the floor with control.
Repeat to the other side and keep alternating until you finish the set.
mistakes: Pulling the head forward with the hands instead of lifting with the abs
Moving only the elbow across while the shoulders stay on the floor
Arching the lower back away from the floor
Jerking up with momentum instead of curling up smoothly
Dropping back to the floor without control
Letting the knees fall to the side or the feet lift as you twist
Holding your breath during the set
exercises.name: Twisting Crunch
tips: Think of bringing your ribs toward the opposite hip; the elbow does not need to touch the knee.
Curl up only until your upper back leaves the floor. Sitting all the way up turns it into a sit-up.
Keep a fist-sized space between your chin and chest so your neck stays relaxed.
Hold the top for a moment and squeeze your obliques hard before you lower.
To make it harder, take three seconds to lower or hold the top for two seconds.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/双手地雷管推举

exercises.description: A standing press with both hands clasped around the end of a barbell anchored in a landmine. You push the bar from your chest forward and up along its arc until your arms are straight. It works the upper chest, front delts and triceps, and the angled path is often easier on the shoulders than an overhead press.
instructions: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine and load a plate on the free end.
Stand facing the free end with your feet about hip-width apart and your knees soft.
Clasp both hands around the very end of the bar, one hand over the other, and hold it in front of your chest with your elbows pointing down.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar forward and up along its arc until your arms are fully straight.
Lower the bar under control along the same arc until your hands are back in front of your chest.
Finish the set, then lower the end of the bar to the floor.
mistakes: Arching the lower back and leaning back to force the bar up
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears as the arms straighten
Flaring the elbows wide to the sides at the bottom
Letting the wrists bend back under the weight of the bar
Stopping the press before the arms are fully straight
Dipping the knees and driving with the legs to move the bar
Dropping the bar fast and bouncing it off the chest
Twisting the torso or shifting the weight onto one foot
exercises.name: Two-Arm Landmine Press
tips: Stand far enough from the anchor that the end of the bar sits in front of your upper chest at the start.
Push the bar away from you along its arc instead of trying to drive it straight up.
Lean your whole body slightly toward the bar, keeping a straight line from heels to head.
At the top, reach the bar a little further forward so your shoulder blades slide around your ribs.
Breathe in and brace at the bottom, then breathe out as you press.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肱三头肌/反握三头肌伸展

exercises.description: The Underhand Triceps Extension is an isolation exercise that targets the triceps brachii, specifically emphasizing the medial head. This exercise is performed using a cable machine with an underhand grip, which can help reduce stress on the elbows and enhance muscle engagement.
instructions: Attach a straight or EZ-curl bar to a high pulley on a cable machine.
Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, and grasp the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
Begin with your forearms parallel to the floor, then extend your arms downward by contracting your triceps until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring full contraction of the triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, allowing the forearms to come back to parallel with the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Elbows flaring outwards, reducing triceps engagement.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement, leading to poor muscle activation.
Allowing wrists to bend excessively, causing strain and reducing effectiveness.
Not fully extending the arms, limiting triceps activation.
Leaning forward excessively, shifting focus away from triceps.
Gripping too tightly, causing unnecessary tension in forearms.
Not maintaining a stable core, leading to improper form.
Starting with elbows too far from the body, reducing leverage and control.
exercises.name: Underhand Triceps Extension
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better stability during the exercise.
Focus on keeping your elbows tucked in and stationary to maximize triceps activation.
Avoid using momentum; perform each repetition in a controlled manner to prevent injury and ensure effective muscle engagement.
Exhale as you extend your arms downward and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Start with a lighter weight to perfect your form before progressing to heavier loads.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/前臂/单侧农夫行走

exercises.description: The Unilateral Farmer Walk is a strength and conditioning exercise that targets the core, grip strength, and lower body stability. It involves carrying a heavy weight in one hand while walking a specified distance or for a set time. This exercise challenges balance and coordination, engaging muscles on both sides of the body asymmetrically.
instructions: Select a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell and place it beside you.
Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and engage your core.
Bend at the knees to pick up the weight with one hand, keeping your back straight.
Hold the weight securely at your side with your arm fully extended.
Begin walking forward in a straight line, maintaining an upright posture.
Keep your shoulders level and avoid leaning to one side.
Walk for a set distance or time, then switch hands and repeat.
mistakes: Leaning excessively to one side instead of maintaining an upright posture.
Allowing the weight to swing, losing control and stability.
Failing to engage the core, leading to poor balance and posture.
Taking overly large or small steps, disrupting natural gait and balance.
Holding the weight too far from the body, increasing strain on the shoulder.
Neglecting to keep the shoulder blades retracted, resulting in a rounded back.
Walking too quickly, compromising form and muscle engagement.
Not keeping the head aligned with the spine, leading to neck strain.
Using too heavy a weight, causing compensatory movements and poor form.
exercises.name: Unilateral Farmer Walk
tips: Choose a weight that challenges your grip but allows you to maintain proper form.
Focus on keeping your core tight to prevent your torso from tilting.
Maintain a steady pace and controlled breathing throughout the walk.
Ensure your steps are even and deliberate to enhance balance.
Switch hands regularly to work both sides of the body equally.
Use this exercise as part of a balanced routine to improve overall functional strength.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/上犬式

exercises.description: The Upward Dog, also known as Upward-Facing Dog or Urdhva Mukha Svanasana, is a yoga pose that strengthens the spine, arms, and wrists while stretching the chest, shoulders, and abdomen. It is commonly used in yoga sequences to improve posture and increase flexibility.
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the mat with your legs extended straight back and the tops of your feet resting on the floor.
Place your hands under your shoulders with your elbows close to your body.
Inhale deeply and press firmly into your palms to lift your chest off the ground.
Straighten your arms completely while keeping your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears.
Engage your thighs and lift your knees off the floor, balancing on the tops of your feet.
Hold the pose for several breaths, keeping your gaze forward or slightly upward.
Exhale and slowly lower your body back to the starting position.
mistakes: Allowing shoulders to shrug up towards the ears, causing tension in the neck.
Collapsing the lower back instead of engaging the core to support the spine.
Failing to press the tops of the feet into the ground, reducing leg engagement.
Overextending the elbows, leading to joint strain and reduced control.
Dropping the head back excessively, straining the neck.
Not aligning wrists directly under shoulders, compromising stability.
Letting the thighs touch the floor, which disengages the core and legs.
exercises.name: Upward Dog
tips: Ensure that your hands are aligned directly under your shoulders for optimal support.
Keep your elbows slightly bent if you feel any strain in the lower back.
Engage your core muscles to protect your lower back during the pose.
Focus on lifting through the chest rather than pushing with the arms to maintain proper alignment.
If you experience discomfort in the wrists, try spreading your fingers wide for better weight distribution.
Maintain a steady breath throughout the pose to enhance relaxation and focus.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/v字坐姿卷腹

exercises.description: The V-Sit Crunch is a core exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the rectus abdominis and obliques. It involves balancing on your glutes while lifting your legs and torso to form a 'V' shape, engaging the core throughout the movement.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your arms at your sides.
Lean back slightly, keeping your back straight and engage your core.
Lift your legs off the ground, bending your knees slightly.
Simultaneously lift your torso to form a 'V' shape with your body.
Hold this position briefly, ensuring your core remains engaged.
Lower your torso and legs back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Leaning too far back, losing core engagement.
Rounding the lower back, risking spinal strain.
Using momentum instead of controlled movements.
Feet touching the ground, reducing core activation.
Neck strain from pulling on the head with hands.
Inconsistent breathing, leading to fatigue.
Legs not fully extended, limiting range of motion.
Shoulders hunched, reducing effectiveness.
Rapid movements, compromising form and control.
exercises.name: V-Sit Crunch
tips: Keep your core tight throughout the exercise to maintain balance and stability.
Avoid rounding your back; maintain a straight spine to prevent strain.
Control the movement both when lifting into the 'V' position and when returning to the start.
Focus on breathing steadily; exhale as you lift into the 'V' and inhale as you lower back down.
If you're new to this exercise, start with fewer repetitions and gradually increase as you build strength.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腹肌/v字仰卧起坐

exercises.description: The V-Up is a core strengthening exercise that targets the abdominal muscles, particularly the rectus abdominis and obliques. It involves lifting both the upper and lower body simultaneously to form a 'V' shape, engaging the core throughout the movement.
instructions: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and arms stretched overhead.
Engage your core by pulling your belly button towards your spine.
Simultaneously lift your legs and upper body off the ground, reaching your hands towards your feet.
Keep your legs straight and try to form a 'V' shape with your body at the top of the movement.
Hold the position briefly, ensuring your core remains engaged.
Slowly lower your arms and legs back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Lifting the legs too high, causing the lower back to arch excessively.
Failing to engage the core, leading to a lack of stability and control.
Using momentum by swinging the arms or legs instead of controlled movement.
Not keeping the legs straight, reducing the effectiveness of the exercise.
Failing to reach the arms toward the toes, limiting the range of motion.
Allowing the shoulders to slump forward, reducing core engagement.
Not maintaining a straight line from head to toe at the top of the movement.
Rushing through the movement, compromising form and control.
exercises.name: V-Up
tips: Maintain a slow and controlled motion to maximize core engagement.
Avoid using momentum; focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid straining it by looking up at the ceiling.
If you find it difficult to keep your legs straight, slightly bend your knees as you lift.
Exhale as you lift into the 'V' position and inhale as you lower back down.
Start with fewer repetitions if you're new to this exercise and gradually increase as you build strength.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/垂直腿举

exercises.description: Lying on your back under a plate-loaded sled that runs straight up and down, you lower the platform toward your chest and press it back up until your legs are straight. The quads on the front of your thighs do most of the work, and the glutes help at the bottom of the rep.
instructions: Load the same plates on both sides and set the safety stops just below the lowest point you plan to reach.
Lie on your back on the bench with your hips under the platform and your head, back and hips flat on the pad.
Place your feet flat on the platform about hip-width apart, toes turned slightly out. Hold the handles or rest your hands beside your hips.
Press the platform up slightly to take the load off the safety catches, then release them.
Bend your knees and hips and lower the platform over about 2 seconds, knees tracking over your toes, until your thighs come close to your chest.
Stop before your hips start to lift off the pad, then press through your whole foot to drive the platform straight up.
Straighten your legs at the top without snapping your knees into lockout, then start the next rep.
After the last rep, lock the safety catches with your legs extended before you take your feet off the platform.
mistakes: Lowering so deep that your hips curl off the pad and your lower back rounds under the load.
Letting your knees cave inward as you press.
Snapping your knees into lockout at the top, which leaves the full load resting on locked joints.
Doing shallow half reps with too much weight on the sled.
Pushing through your toes so your heels lift off the platform.
Dropping the platform fast and bouncing out of the bottom.
Pushing on your knees with your hands to finish a rep.
exercises.name: Vertical Leg Press
tips: Start with less weight than you use on a 45-degree leg press. Here the full weight of the plates and sled bears straight down on you.
Feet higher on the platform bend your hips more and bring in more glutes. Feet lower bend your knees more and load the quads harder, but your heels lift sooner.
Sets of 8-15 reps work well. Add plates only when you reach the top of the range with the same depth on every rep.
Expect to feel it mostly in the front of your thighs, plus the glutes near the bottom. Pain at the front of the knee is a sign to shorten the range or move your feet higher.
If you get stuck at the bottom, lower the platform onto the safety stops instead of fighting the weight.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/史密斯机垂直腿举

exercises.description: The Vertical Leg Press on a Smith Machine is a compound lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and calves. This exercise involves lying on your back and pressing the weight upwards using your legs, with the Smith Machine providing stability and safety through its guided bar path.
instructions: Position a flat bench under the Smith Machine bar. Ensure the bench is aligned with the bar path.
Lie on your back on the bench, positioning your feet shoulder-width apart on the bar.
Unlock the Smith Machine bar by rotating it slightly to release it from its locked position.
Lower the bar slowly towards your chest by bending your knees, keeping your feet flat on the bar.
Press the bar back up by extending your legs fully without locking your knees at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully lock the bar back into place.
mistakes: Placing feet too high or too low on the platform, affecting muscle engagement.
Allowing knees to collapse inward, risking knee strain.
Locking knees at the top of the movement, increasing joint stress.
Using excessive weight, compromising form and control.
Failing to maintain a neutral spine, leading to lower back strain.
Descending too quickly, reducing muscle tension and control.
Not lowering the weight sufficiently, limiting range of motion.
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels, reducing glute activation.
Allowing hips to lift off the bench, risking lower back injury.
exercises.name: Vertical Leg Press Smith Machine
tips: Ensure your back remains flat against the bench throughout the movement to prevent strain.
Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and support for your lower back.
Adjust the bench height and foot placement to ensure a comfortable range of motion.
Control the descent of the bar to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Avoid locking out your knees at the top of the movement to maintain tension in your muscles.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/步行有氧运动

exercises.description: Walking Cardio is a low-impact aerobic exercise that involves walking at a steady pace to improve cardiovascular health, endurance, and overall fitness. It can be performed on a treadmill or outdoors and is suitable for all fitness levels.
instructions: Begin with a warm-up by walking at a slow pace for 5-10 minutes to prepare your muscles and joints.
Adjust the treadmill to a comfortable speed or choose a flat, safe path if walking outdoors.
Maintain an upright posture with your shoulders relaxed and your core engaged.
Swing your arms naturally at your sides to help maintain balance and rhythm.
Walk at a brisk pace that elevates your heart rate but still allows you to hold a conversation.
Continue walking for 20-60 minutes depending on your fitness level and goals.
Cool down by gradually slowing your pace for the last 5-10 minutes of your walk.
mistakes: Slouching posture reduces lung capacity and engagement of core muscles.
Overstriding causes unnecessary stress on the knees and hips.
Allowing arms to hang loosely instead of maintaining a 90-degree angle reduces upper body engagement.
Not activating the glutes and hamstrings limits lower body muscle engagement.
Walking with toes pointed outward or inward can lead to imbalanced muscle use.
Failing to maintain a steady pace disrupts cardiovascular benefits.
Holding onto treadmill handles excessively reduces core activation and balance.
Landing heavily on the heels increases impact on joints.
Neglecting to engage the core results in reduced stability and support.
Walking with a stiff, rigid gait limits natural movement and fluidity.
exercises.name: Walking Cardio
tips: Ensure you wear comfortable, supportive footwear to prevent injury.
Keep hydrated by drinking water before, during, and after your walk.
Incorporate intervals by alternating between faster and slower paces to increase intensity.
Use a fitness tracker or pedometer to monitor your steps and progress over time.
Focus on maintaining a consistent pace rather than speed to build endurance.
Listen to music or podcasts to make the exercise more enjoyable and help pass the time.
If walking outdoors, choose routes with varying terrain for added challenge.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/腿部锻炼/行走弓步蹲

exercises.description: Walking lunges are a dynamic lower body exercise targeting the quadriceps, hamstrings, glutes, and calves. This movement involves stepping forward into a lunge position and then alternating legs as you move forward. It enhances balance, coordination, and functional strength.
instructions: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or holding dumbbells by your sides.
Step forward with your right foot, landing on the heel first.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the ground and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
Ensure your front knee is aligned over your ankle and does not extend past your toes.
Push through the heel of your right foot to rise and bring your left foot forward to step into the next lunge.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions or distance.
mistakes: Allowing the front knee to extend beyond the toes, increasing joint strain.
Failing to maintain an upright torso, leading to excessive forward lean.
Stepping too far forward, causing instability and balance issues.
Not engaging the core, resulting in poor balance and control.
Letting the back knee slam into the ground, risking knee injury.
Using momentum instead of muscle engagement to push off.
Not keeping the front foot flat, causing heel lift and instability.
Allowing the back leg to remain too straight, reducing range of motion.
Failing to maintain consistent stride length, leading to uneven muscle activation.
Neglecting to align the hips and shoulders, causing twisting or lateral movement.
exercises.name: Walking Lunges
tips: Maintain an upright torso throughout the movement to engage core muscles effectively.
Focus on a controlled descent to prevent knee strain and maximize muscle engagement.
Keep your gaze forward to help maintain balance and proper posture.
Use a moderate pace to ensure stability and control during each step.
If you're new to this exercise, start without weights to master form before adding resistance.
Ensure each step is long enough so that both knees form approximately 90-degree angles at the bottom of the lunge.

alternates.zh: https://smartworkout.app/zh/健身练习库/肩部/墙天使

exercises.description: The Wall Angel exercise is designed to improve shoulder mobility, posture, and scapular stability. It targets the muscles of the upper back, shoulders, and chest by promoting proper alignment and movement patterns.
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall, feet shoulder-width apart, and heels about 6 inches away from the wall.
Ensure your lower back is flat against the wall by engaging your core and slightly tucking your pelvis.
Raise your arms to shoulder height and bend your elbows at 90 degrees, keeping your upper arms parallel to the floor.
Press your entire arm, from fingertips to elbows, against the wall.
Slowly slide your arms upward along the wall while maintaining contact with the wall. Stop when you feel any discomfort or if your arms lose contact with the wall.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly slide your arms back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on maintaining proper form throughout.
mistakes: Arms not in contact with the wall throughout the movement.
Arching the lower back away from the wall.
Allowing the shoulders to shrug upwards during the exercise.
Failing to keep the head in contact with the wall.
Bending the wrists instead of keeping them straight.
Rushing through the movement without controlled motion.
Not maintaining a 90-degree angle at the elbows.
Letting the elbows drift away from the wall.
Failing to engage the core muscles to stabilize the torso.
Performing the exercise with a limited range of motion due to tightness.
exercises.name: Wall Angel
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to prevent arching of the lower back.
Focus on maintaining full contact of your arms with the wall to ensure proper shoulder movement.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize its effectiveness.
If you experience difficulty keeping your arms against the wall, try adjusting your stance or performing shoulder mobility exercises as a warm-up.
Breathe steadily and avoid holding your breath during the movement.

exercises.description: The wall ball shot combines a squat with an overhead throw. Holding a medicine ball at your chest, squat until your hips drop below your knees, drive up explosively and throw the ball to a target high on the wall. Catch it as it comes down and sink straight into the next squat.
instructions: Stand facing a wall about half a step away, feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned slightly out.
Hold the medicine ball at chest height with both hands on its sides, slightly underneath, and your elbows pointing down.
Brace your core and squat until your hips drop below your knees. Keep your chest up and your heels on the floor.
Drive up explosively through your whole foot and fully extend your hips and knees.
Carry that momentum into your arms and throw the ball to the target on the wall, finishing with your arms extended overhead.
Catch the ball at chest height with bent elbows as it comes down.
As you catch it, sink straight into the next squat and repeat until the set is done.
mistakes: Squatting too shallow, with the hips staying above the knees
Letting the knees cave inward as you stand up
Lifting the heels at the bottom of the squat
Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the squat
Throwing with the arms only, after the legs have already straightened
Standing too far from the wall, so the ball flies forward and rebounds out of reach
Catching the ball with straight arms instead of bending the elbows to absorb it
Pausing upright after the catch instead of riding the ball down into the squat
exercises.name: Wall Ball Shot
tips: Aim at the same spot on every rep. The standard target height is 3 m (10 ft) for men and 2.7 m (9 ft) for women.
Keep the ball tight to your chest in the squat so it does not pull your torso forward.
Look up at the target before you throw, then follow the ball with your eyes as it drops.
Breathe out on the throw and take a quick breath as you catch.
Use a lighter ball than the usual 9 kg for men or 6 kg for women if you cannot hit the target for the whole set.
In long sets, take short planned breaks before your throws start missing the target.
